author: JoeJoeflyn
body:
## Description

Fast pointer motion across folders could fire `leave(A)` after `enter(B)`, so `schedule_close_peek` cancelled `pending_peek` that now belonged to B and `close_peek_visual` took `peek_anchor` before B's open delay elapsed — the destination peek never opened.

Three changes:

- **`schedule_close_peek`** no longer cancels `pending_peek`; only the close timer is (re)armed. A pending peek for a newly entered folder survives a late `leave` from the previous one.
- **`close_peek_visual`** no longer cancels `pending_peek` or takes `peek_anchor`; it only tears down the currently open peek. A pending peek for the next folder is not destroyed when the previous one closes.
- **`pending_peek` open callback** now checks the anchor's `PRELIGHT` state before calling `begin_peek`. If the pointer has left the anchor (leave to empty space), the stale pending peek is dropped — covering the case the old unconditional cancellation handled.
- **`truncate`** explicitly cancels `pending_peek` and takes `peek_anchor` before `close_peek_visual`, since column removal needs a hard cancel that `close_peek_visual` no longer performs.

## Visual evidence

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/11a10a13-cf8a-40b6-a1f8-123d85e5b49d

## How to test

1. In Columns mode, open a folder containing several subfolders.
2. Move the pointer quickly from one folder row to an adjacent folder row and stop.
3. Wait for the peek delay (~180ms).

**Expected result:** The second folder's peek popover opens. Repeat in List and Icons modes; repeat moving across three or more folders in one sweep.

## Related issue

Closes #871

issues.body:
## Bug report

**Strata version:** 0.16.0 (main, commit e598625)

**Installation method:** local build from source

**Environment:** Arch Linux, Wayland/Hyprland

**Reproduction steps:**

1. Open Strata in Columns (or List/Icons) mode in a directory with several subfolders side by side.
2. Move the pointer quickly from one folder row to an adjacent folder row.
3. Stop on the second folder and wait.

**Expected behavior:** The second folder's peek popover opens after the hover delay.

**Actual behavior:** The peek frequently does not open. The pointer has to leave the listing and re-enter the folder, or hover back and forth, to trigger the peek.

**Sanitized logs:** N/A — the peek simply never starts; no error is logged.

## Root cause (investigated)

GTK can fire `enter(B)` before `leave(A)` when the pointer moves fast. `schedule_close_peek` (from `leave(A)`) unconditionally cancelled `pending_peek`, which by then belonged to folder B. `close_peek_visual` (triggered by the close timeout, 80ms < 180ms open delay) also cancelled `pending_peek` and took `peek_anchor`, destroying B's pending peek in both paths.

author: JoeJoeflyn
body:
## Description

When restoring trashed items via undo, `trashed_entries_for_originals` scans every `.trashinfo` file in `~/.local/share/Trash/info/` to find the trash entries for the requested original locations. This scan is O(total trash), not O(items to restore), and had no cancellation support — clicking Cancel during the restore did nothing until the entire scan finished, making the app appear frozen.

Thread the operation's existing `gio::Cancellable` through `trashed_entries_for_originals` and `home_trash_entries_at`:
- `home_trash_entries_at` breaks early from the `.trashinfo` loop when cancelled
- `trashed_entries_for_originals` checks cancellation between the home-trash scan and the GIO `trash:///` enumeration, and at the top of each 64-item batch
- Cancelled lookups emit a proper `OperationEvent::Cancelled` (via the existing `cancelled_event` helper) instead of a generic `Failed`

No new abstractions — all reuses existing helpers (`cancelled_local_operation`, `was_cancelled`, `cancelled_event`) and the same `gio::Cancellable` pattern every other operation already uses.

## Visual evidence

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f7d63ceb-592f-4f48-83a9-ec07bb66fe3a

## How to test

1. Create a directory with many files: `mkdir ~/strata-test && cd ~/strata-test && for i in $(seq 1 500); do echo "x" > "file_$i.txt"; done`
2. Open Strata, navigate to `~/strata-test`
3. Select all files (Ctrl+A) and delete them (Delete key)
4. Click **Cancel** in the progress dialog while deletion is still running
5. Press undo to restore the trashed files
6. Click **Cancel** in the restore progress dialog while it says "Restoring items"

**Expected result:** The restore cancels within one batch (64 files) and shows "Operation cancelled". Before the fix, the Cancel button had no effect until the entire `.trashinfo` scan completed.

## Related issue

Refs #733
title: fix(trash): make restore trash lookup cancellable

author: JoeJoeflyn
body: ## Description `compare_display_names` compared names byte-by-byte, so `File 10` sorted before `File 2` because `'1' < '2'` at the first differing byte. Replace the folded-byte comparator with a natural comparator that walks both names in parallel, extracts digit runs, and compares them by integer value. Non-digit runs keep the casefold-then-raw-byte tie-break for stable case-insensitive ordering. No allocations on the ASCII fast path. ## Visual evidence ## How to test 1. Create a folder with files named `File 1` through `File 12`. 2. Open it in Strata, sort by name ascending. **Expected result:** `File 1, File 2, File 3, ..., File 10, File 11, File 12` ## Related issue Closes #878

issues.body:
## Bug report

**Strata version:** 0.16.0 (main, commit e598625)

**Installation method:** local build from source

**Environment:** Arch Linux, Wayland/Hyprland

**Reproduction steps:**

1. Open Strata in any mode in a directory containing files named `File 1`, `File 2`, ..., `File 10`.
2. Sort by name, ascending.

**Expected behavior:** `File 1, File 2, File 3, ..., File 10`

**Actual behavior:** `File 1, File 10, File 2, File 3, ...` — the `10` sorts before `2` because the comparator compares byte-by-byte (`'1' < '2'`).

**Sanitized logs:** N/A — this is a pure ordering bug with no error logged.

## Root cause

`compare_display_names` in `src/app/navigation.rs` compares names lexicographically. When two names share a non-numeric prefix and differ in a numeric suffix, the shorter number `10` sorts before `2` because `'1' < '2'` at the first differing byte. A natural sort that compares numeric runs by their integer value would order `2` before `10`.

title: fix(navigation): sort numeric suffixes naturally instead of lexicographically

## Bug report

**Strata version:** 0.16.0 (main, commit e598625)

**Installation method:** local build from source

**Environment:** Arch Linux, Wayland/Hyprland

**Reproduction steps:**

1. Open a folder containing `.svg` files in Strata.
2. Switch to Icons mode.

**Expected behavior:** SVG files show a rendered thumbnail.

**Actual behavior:** SVG files show the generic image fallback icon. `thumbnail_kind` does not recognize `svg`, and `thumbnail-image` calls `render_pixbuf` directly, which fails when gdk-pixbuf has no SVG loader installed.

**Sanitized logs:** N/A — no error; the thumbnail path is never attempted.

`thumbnail_kind` in `src/ui/thumbnail.rs` omits `svg` from the `ThumbnailKind::Image` match arm, so SVGs never enter the thumbnail pipeline. The existing `render_raw` fallback chain (pixbuf → ImageMagick → dcraw) already handles this for `preview-image` and `thumbnail-raw`.

issues.body:
## Bug

When an image currently shown in the quick preview pane is deleted, the preview continues displaying the deleted image instead of closing or switching to the newly selected entry.

## Reproduction

1. Click an image file to open it in the quick preview pane
2. Delete the image (Delete key or right-click → Delete)
3. The preview pane continues showing the deleted image

## Expected behavior

The quick preview should close immediately when the previewed file is removed from the model, or switch to the newly selected entry if it supports preview.

## Root cause

`PreviewState` only listens for `FocusChanged`/`SelectionSetChanged` events to update its content. When a file is deleted via an operation, `handle_directory_change` emits `EntriesSpliced` but only emits `FocusChanged` when the new selection is `None`. When a new entry is selected to replace the deleted one, no focus/selection event reaches the preview handler, leaving the stale content rendered.

This is intentional for background monitor changes (which shouldn't grab focus), but it also affects operation-driven deletions.

## Description

Columns mode duplicated the shared `filter_controls()` widget construction from `browser_modes.rs`. Replaced the inline copy with a call to the existing helper so List, Icons, and Columns all build filter controls the same way.

A single capture-phase `GtkGestureClick` on the `ApplicationWindow` dismisses the active column filter when a click lands outside the filter entry/button. This covers empty space, sidebar, header, other columns, and any non-focusable area — the previous focus-leave approach missed clicks on non-focusable widgets like the sidebar because GTK focus stayed in the entry.

Opening a filter in one column now deactivates any other column's active filter via the existing `set_active(false)` path (which clears text and hides the revealer), so only one filter is open at a time.

## Visual evidence

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6d88bb16-7e48-4e2b-ac0b-76212a67b773

## How to test

1. Switch to Columns view and open a directory with subfolders (2+ columns)
2. Press `Ctrl+F` in column 1 — the filter bar opens
3. Click on empty space (no column) — the filter closes
4. Press `Ctrl+F` in column 1 again, then click the sidebar — the filter closes
5. Press `Ctrl+F` in column 1, then `Ctrl+F` in column 2 — column 1's filter closes, only column 2's is open
6. Click the filter entry or toggle button — the filter stays open

**Expected result:** Clicking anywhere outside the filter entry/button closes the active column filter. Only one column filter is open at a time.

In Columns (Miller) view, each column can open its own pane filter. When focus moves away from a filtered column, or when starting a filter in a different column, the previous column’s filter UI can stay open. That leaves stale filter chrome across columns and makes multi-column browsing noisier than it needs to be.

author: ogarza
body:
## Description

- Fill Miller-column free space with a 2× standard-column preferred minimum (600 logical px), prioritizing the focused column. Best-effort 48px peeks reveal/focus neighboring columns without activating hidden contents, adapting #876 by JoeJoeflyn.
- **Appearance → Preview panel** is a window-session toggle with a **Space** hint. Unsupported selections do not disable it; the next supported selection returns automatically.
- **Icons keeps preview space reserved while enabled**, using a quiet placeholder for folders, ZIPs, and empty selections. Cards do not rearrange between supported and unsupported selections. Explicit toggles and window/divider sizing can reflow the grid. Long Icons headings ellipsize instead of forcing sideways panning; Columns and List retain their existing behavior.
- Preserve column positions on explicit close, session-local divider widths, document state, and paused media across narrow-window fallback. Media stays centered within 1280 logical px with at most 2× enlargement; PDF/text viewers remain uncapped. No new saved settings.

Image previews use bounded full renders rather than normalized shared thumbnails, which lack reliable native dimensions; slow RAW loads may show a loading indicator. Validation also exposed two existing archive-test fixture assumptions, fixed in a separate test-only commit without changing archive handling.

## Visual evidence

Icons view, switching from a previewable file to a ZIP in the same enabled session:

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Previously the grid expanded and rearranged](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ogarza/strata/e6d3a61e7d585a8018b778bd40d13cbdeb626b38/docs/evidence/885/icons/before-unsupported.png) | ![Reserved preview space keeps the grid stable](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ogarza/strata/e6d3a61e7d585a8018b778bd40d13cbdeb626b38/docs/evidence/885/icons/after-unsupported.png) |

[All comparisons, including the supported-file layout, Appearance toggle, column peeks, media limits, and narrow-window behavior](https://github.com/ogarza/strata/blob/e6d3a61e7d585a8018b778bd40d13cbdeb626b38/docs/evidence/885/README.md).

## How to test

1. In Icons, enable Preview panel and move quickly between text/images, ZIPs, folders, and empty selection. Navigate into another folder. The grid width and card placement should stay stable; unsupported selections clear stale content and show a placeholder.
2. Turn preview mode off with Space or Appearance: the grid should expand once and stay full-width during selection changes. Narrow/widen the window to check geometry-only fallback.
3. In Columns, navigate deeply, click the exposed strips, and preview a file in an earlier column. Close the preview, resize its divider, and reopen it.
4. Preview small/wide images, GIFs/video, and PDF/text; exercise playback, text size, and temporary hiding/restoration.

**Expected result:** Icons reflows for intentional layout changes, not file-type changes. Preview mode and session width remain consistent; Columns/List behavior, reveal-only peeks, media limits, and document state are preserved.

## Related issue

Closes #885

Adapts #876 (related issue #874); the other PR is not modified.

issues.body:
### Problem or use case

Miller-column previews currently leave unused space between the last directory column and the preview, and use a fixed minimum that does not express a relationship to column width. Wide windows should give previews the remaining viewport, while deep paths should scroll older columns left without sacrificing the focused directory column. Finder on macOS is the interaction reference.

### Proposed solution

- In automatic mode, fill all horizontal space between the last open directory column and the viewport's right edge.
- Use a preferred minimum preview width of the standard directory-column width multiplied by a centralized, adjustable multiplier. Start at **2×** (currently **600 logical pixels**), independent of manually resized directory columns.
- While open, reveal the focused column, including when navigating backward. Its full width, including manual column resizing, takes priority over preview width preferences.
- Adapt the 48-logical-pixel neighbor peeks from PR #876. Use actual neighboring columns, not trailing empty space. Peek clicks reveal/focus only, including double-clicks, and peeks yield before a full focused column or an otherwise usable preview.
- Treat preview mode as a window-session toggle. Appearance has a checked **Preview panel** option with a **Space** shortcut hint. Unsupported files, folders, empty selections, and navigation hide the content without turning the mode off; the next supported selection returns. Explicit close/toggle actions disable it.
- In Icons view, keep the grid's available width stable within each preview-toggle state. While enabled, reserve preview space for supported files, unsupported files, folders, and empty selection; show a quiet placeholder and clear stale content immediately. Turning preview mode off intentionally releases the space. Window/divider/density changes may reflow the grid, and narrow-window fallback depends on geometry rather than file type. Columns/List behavior remains unchanged.
- Closing the preview preserves column positions, leaving empty space on the right rather than shifting columns back. Scrolling and navigation remain usable.
- If there is not enough room for both a full focused column and a usable preview (one standard column / 300 logical pixels), temporarily hide the preview. Restore the latest selection and preferred width when space returns; pause hidden media and preserve existing document state. Explicitly closing a hidden preview cancels restoration.
- Retain a draggable preview divider. A manual width overrides automatic sizing for that window session, survives navigation and closing/reopening the preview, and is not persisted to settings. Constrain it safely on narrow windows without losing the preferred width.
- Center images, GIFs, videos, and their playback controls in a section capped at **1280 logical pixels**. Preserve aspect ratio, fit available width and height without cropping, and upscale media to no more than **2× its original dimensions**. Keep both limits centralized for future tuning.
- Exclude PDF and text viewers from the media cap. Preserve their existing scrolling/zoom behavior and media playback/drag interactions.
- Use logical GTK coordinates so display scaling works naturally; do not introduce a new global UI scaling setting or saved preview preferences in this change.

### Alternatives considered

A fixed preview width wastes wide-window space; shrinking directory columns obscures filenames. An always-automatic divider prevents users from choosing a useful width during a browsing session. Persistent or folder-specific settings can follow later.

### Visual examples

Finder's column-view preview is the reference. Before/after screenshots, including the narrow-window fallback and unchanged column positions on close, are attached to PR #888.

### Strata version

Source baseline: e598625 (main).

### Additional context

The owner confirmed the 2× standard-column default, session-local manual resizing, 2× media upscaling limit, 1280-logical-pixel media cap, and exclusion of PDFs/text. Shared preview media should behave consistently in Columns, Icons, List, and the chooser; column-specific automatic layout applies only to Columns. In follow-up feedback, the owner requested stationary columns on close and last-column priority in small windows, and approved temporarily hiding unusably narrow previews. Subsequent feedback prioritizes the focused column, approves reveal-only neighbor peeks, and requests the session toggle in Appearance. The matching reference is PR #876 (not #867). The owner also approved stable Icons layouts within enabled/disabled preview states, allowing a deliberate reflow when explicitly toggling preview mode.

author: JoeJoeflyn
body:
## Description

Render PDF pages at the preview viewport width instead of a fixed oversized surface, and serialize sandboxed Poppler page renders across previews. This reduces first-content work and prevents rapid scrolling from multiplying renderer CPU and memory pressure. Rendered-page caching remains bounded and size-aware.

## Benchmark

Local engineering sample using the reported 179-page, 17.9 MB optimized PDF (531 × 666 pt pages), a debug build, Poppler 26.08.0, and a warm filesystem cache. The alternating first-page samples ran in one process to reduce startup variance; timings remain machine-specific.

| Metric | Before | After | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Median first-page render | 1,583 ms at 1400 × 1755 | 909 ms at 640 × 802 | 43% faster |
| First-page PNG payload | 938,382 bytes | 246,071 bytes | 74% smaller |
| Peak PDF-helper RSS while paging four visible pages | ~411 MiB across concurrent workers | ~112 MiB with serialized work | 73% lower |

The scheduler intentionally prioritizes first visible content and bounded memory over completing several offscreen page renders simultaneously; later visible pages are queued FIFO and cancelled if they leave the viewport.

Validation note: the owner directed this push before local full checks completed. Targeted PDF, sandbox, provider, and preview tests passed. Formatting and Clippy passed. The full Rust suite reached 1,517 passing tests but reported the pre-existing #613 inline-entry failure and one search test that passed on isolated rerun. The canonical E2E run was interrupted twice; the second attempt displayed early failures before interruption, so local E2E is not reported as passed and GitHub CI remains required.

## Visual evidence

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/770e5eb9-807d-410e-892b-da098d186bf4

## How to test

1. Open quick preview for a large, complex, multi-page PDF.
2. Confirm the first page appears, then scroll rapidly through many pages and reopen the preview.

**Expected result:**

The first page appears sooner; page rendering remains responsive and bounded without a freeze or crash, and revisited rendered pages use the cache.

## Related issue

Closes #815

issues.body:
### Strata version

### What happened?

Opening a PDF in quick preview and scrolling down causes Strata to hang and then crash. The PDF viewer is a `GtkListView` that lazy-loads each page on `factory.connect_bind`, firing a preview load per page (`src/ui/preview.rs`, `render_pdf_viewer`). Scrolling rapidly binds/unbinds many pages and starts many concurrent preview loads, after which the window freezes and exits.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Select a multi-page PDF in a browser pane.
2. Open quick preview (space).
3. Scroll down through several pages.
4. Observe the window hangs and then crashes.

### Expected behavior

Scrolling a PDF preview should page in rendered pages smoothly without freezing or crashing, cancelling/skipping loads for pages that scroll out of view.

### Screenshots or video

N/A

### Relevant logs

No sanitized logs captured yet. If reproducible, collect with:

```shell
coredumpctl list strata
coredumpctl info strata
journalctl --user _COMM=strata --since "30 minutes ago"
```

### Additional context

Reporter environment: Arch Linux, Hyprland 0.56.2, built from source. Likely related to unbounded concurrent page loads and load cancellation on unbind (`factory.connect_unbind` removes the load handle but may not cancel in-flight rendering). Worth checking whether page loads are throttled and whether in-flight loads are cancelled when a page unbinds.

comments.body:
## Repro update

**Verdict: PARTIALLY REPRODUCED** on `wmfeht/strata` `main` at `4eb018fb59d7883374cb8a6cdba449a626fd5bf5` (Strata 0.15.0 debug binary). Rapid scrolling a 40-page PDF in Space preview did **not** hang or crash the process on this X11/XFCE VM, but it did break PDF page rendering (blank preview + “Unable to render this PDF page”) while spawning an unbounded burst of sandbox helpers. Hang/crash as reported on Arch/Hyprland/Wayland was **not** observed here.

### Environment

- Checkout: `wmfeht/strata` `main` @ `4eb018f` (`4eb018fb59d7883374cb8a6cdba449a626fd5bf5`)
- Binary: `cargo build --bin strata` → debug `target/debug/strata` (no product-code changes)
- GTK 4.14.5, Poppler 24.02.0, `bwrap` present, rustc 1.98.1
- Display: TigerVNC X11 `DISPLAY=:1`, XFCE, `GDK_BACKEND=x11`, `GSK_RENDERER=cairo`, `LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1` (llvmpipe). Not Wayland/Hyprland.
- Isolated XDG/HOME fixture: `/tmp/strata-repro-815/{home,config,data,cache,state}`
- Fixture file: `/tmp/strata-repro-815/files/multipage-preview.pdf` (40 letter-size pages, ~13.3 kB). Same pages render fine in isolation via `strata --preview-helper preview-pdf` (pages 0, 1, 2, 9, 20, 39 all returned valid PNGs).
- List mode, `type_to_search = false`, portal offer pre-dismissed.

### What happened

1. Built the debug binary from the SHA above and launched Strata on the isolated fixture directory (`GDK_BACKEND=x11`).
2. Selected `multipage-preview.pdf` and pressed Space. Quick preview opened and **page 1 rendered correctly** (“PAGE 1 OF 40”).
3. Focused the preview pane and scrolled down rapidly (mouse wheel bursts + dragging the preview scrollbar toward the bottom), then continued with more up/down bursts for ~1 minute.
4. After the first fast scroll (~5s after preview opened), the preview went blank (theme background, no page image). Hovering the pane showed **“Unable to render this PDF page”**. Further scrolling never showed later page numbers. The window stayed mapped and the pointer kept moving.
5. Process `strata` PID stayed alive the whole time (`Ssl`, never a coredump). RSS ~166 MiB idle → ~235 MiB after the burst; VSZ peaked ~2.9 GiB.
6. A 0.4s sampler during the scroll burst counted in-flight `--preview-helper` / `bwrap` processes climbing in a few seconds: helpers 0 → 3 → 42 → 83 → **117**, bwrap 0 → 2 → 28 → 56 → **78**, UI threads 14 → **53** (09:53:30–09:53:42). Counts include helper children; even so this is many concurrent PDF sandbox renders for a 40-page document. Helpers dropped back to 0 by 09:53:47; the preview stayed blank.
7. Isolated helper renders of later pages succeeded, so the blank preview is not a corrupt fixture. This host is Ubuntu 24.04 XFCE/X11, not the reporter’s Arch Linux Hyprland 0.56.2 / Wayland session.

### Evidence

Cloud Agent run: https://cursor.com/agents/bc-c65819c2-da9a-4832-b555-9be6a11ae025

- `pdf_preview_rapid_scroll_repro.mp4` — Space opens page 1, rapid scroll, preview goes blank, app stays up (~1m15s)
- `pdf_preview_page1_opened.png` — first page rendered
- `pdf_preview_after_rapid_scroll.png` — blank preview immediately after the fast scroll
- `pdf_preview_error_persists.png` — still blank after continued scrolling
- `pdf_preview_monitor_scroll_burst.log` / `pdf_preview_process_monitor.log` — helper/bwrap/RSS samples

### Likely code area (observation only; no fix)

Matches the report’s pointer: `GtkListView` PDF viewer in `src/ui/preview.rs` (`render_pdf_viewer`). `factory.connect_bind` starts a `PreviewPdf` sandbox load per visible row with no concurrency cap. `connect_unbind` drops the `LoadHandle`, which cancels the token and aborts the glib task, but `gio::spawn_blocking` / `sandbox::parse` children keep running until `wait_for_renderer` notices cancel. Rapid recycling therefore overlaps many live `bwrap` helpers. Failed loads set the overlay tooltip to “Unable to render this PDF page”. Thumbnail PDF helpers also use the same sandbox path (`MAX_PREVIEW_CACHE_ENTRIES` is 64 and is a cache, not a run queue). Whether that burst hangs or crashes may depend on compositor/GPU (Hyprland/Wayland vs this software X11 session).

issues.body:
## Description

When deleting multiple files, the dissolve animation (560ms) and the progress popup appear at the same time, which looks awkward. The animation should play after the progress popup completes (or be skipped for large batches).

Currently:
- The dissolve animation plays immediately when the user confirms the delete dialog.
- The progress popup appears after `DeletionStarted`, which fires inside the animation's `on_done` callback (so after the animation for large batches ≥16).
- For small batches (<16), the popup's 350ms delay can land mid-animation, causing visual overlap.

## Expected behavior

The dissolve animation should play after the progress popup completes, or be gated to only play for small batches where no progress popup is shown.

## Constraint

Files are removed from the model incrementally during `DeletionProgress`, so by the time the animation plays, fragment positions may be stale. For full-batch deletes this is fine; for partial views, fragments may briefly overlay surviving items.

## How to test

1. Select 20+ files
2. Press Delete
3. Confirm the dialog
4. Observe the dissolve animation and progress popup overlapping

## Related context

Discord discussion (l0gicgate, Gio, fadilasif):
- l0gicgate suggested showing the animation only for smaller batches with no progress
- Files disappear as they get deleted, so delaying row removal is not straightforward

author: pdwaldrop
body:
## Description

Trash Restore resolves a destination by canonicalizing the closest existing ancestor of the original path, which silently follows a symlink if that ancestor has been replaced by one. The existing volume-identity and mount-point checks only catch an escape that *leaves* the volume (`symlink_parent_that_leaves_the_volume_is_rejected`), so a same-volume symlink parent -- e.g. a directory swapped for a symlink into a sibling folder on the same disk -- passed through untouched and wrote the restored file into the symlink's target instead of its real original location.

`canonical_restore_destination` now checks the destination's immediate parent with `symlink_metadata` (which does not follow the final component) before any canonicalization happens, and refuses outright if it's a symlink rather than a real directory.

## Visual evidence

N/A -- this is a backend safety check in the trash-restore path with no UI change.

## How to test

1. Trash `documents/nested/inner.txt`.
2. Replace `nested` with a symlink to another folder on the *same* volume (e.g. `pictures/`).
3. Try to restore the trashed file.
4. Before this fix, the restore silently succeeds and writes the file into `pictures/inner.txt`. After, it's refused with "The original location's parent is a symlink and cannot be restored."

Added `symlink_parent_that_stays_on_the_volume_is_still_rejected` alongside the existing leaves-the-volume test, confirmed it fails against the pre-fix code and passes after.

## Related issue

Closes #862

author: pdwaldrop
body:
## Description

`Dispatcher::handle_key` runs `window_commands` before `inline_editing` in its chain, so window-level chords (Ctrl+1/2/3 view-mode switching, Ctrl+K global search) were handled unconditionally, before inline editing or location editing ever got a chance to claim the key for its own field. Pressing Ctrl+2 mid-F2-rename switched view mode and committed the half-typed name; Ctrl+K while renaming or editing the location bar (Ctrl+L) opened global search over the field instead of reaching it.

`window_commands` now returns early when a text field currently has focus (`KeyEvent::text_has_focus`, the same signal `inline_editing`'s catch-all `Propagation::Proceed` and `text_input`'s location-edit handling already rely on), letting the key fall through to whichever field owns it.

## Visual evidence

N/A -- this is a keyboard-dispatch ordering fix with no visual change.

## How to test

1. Select a file, press F2, and start typing a new name.
2. Press Ctrl+2. Before this fix, the view switches to Icons and the half-typed name is committed. After, the keystroke reaches the rename field and editing continues.
3. Press Escape, then Ctrl+L to edit the location bar, then press Ctrl+K. Before this fix, global search opens over the field. After, the key reaches the location entry.

Updated `inline_editing_owns_filter_keys_but_not_global_search` (renamed `inline_editing_and_location_edit_own_filter_and_global_search_keys`) to cover both the rename and location-edit cases for Ctrl+K and Ctrl+2/mode-switch; confirmed it fails against the pre-fix code and passes after.

## Related issue

Closes #861

### Installation method

### Linux distribution and desktop environment

Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS, XFCE (Cursor Cloud QA on private Xvfb; not William's desktop)

## Description

`Dispatcher::handle_key` has an early fallthrough that returns `Propagation::Proceed` for any key whenever a search/filter result is selected and no text field has focus, so that search rows keep ownership of their own navigation instead of directory commands acting on a hidden (filtered-out) selection. That fallthrough runs before `dismissal`, which is what handles Delete -> Move to Trash, so it swallowed Delete too: pressing Delete on a selected Ctrl+F filter result left the file in place.

Excluded `Key::Delete` from that fallthrough so it still reaches `dismissal`, which already resolves the current selection correctly regardless of whether it came from a filter result or a plain directory listing.

## Description

`Browser::select_all` selected every position in a column's raw `entries` list, which always includes hidden entries (each tagged `is_hidden`) regardless of the show-hidden preference -- only the GTK filter model excludes them from the visible listing. With hidden files off, Ctrl+A therefore selected `.hidden.txt` even though it was never shown, and a multiple-select file chooser returned its URI in the result.

Added `select_all_excludes_hidden_entries_unless_shown`, confirmed it fails against the pre-fix code (selects 2 instead of 1) and passes after; also confirms toggling hidden files back on selects both.

## Description

`strata --version` was treated as an ordinary application launch, so packaging checks and scripts had no way to print the installed version without starting the GUI. `docs/packaging.md` already documents this flag as the post-install verification step.

Recognize `--version` in the existing first-argument launch-mode dispatch, print `strata <installed-version>` from `build_info::installed_version()`, and exit successfully without starting GTK. Document the flag next to the other launch examples in the README.

## Visual evidence

N/A — this is a CLI-only launch-mode change with no GUI.

## How to test

1. Build Strata from this branch.
2. Run `strata --version`.
3. Run `strata --version ~/Documents` as well, then `strata ~/Documents --version`.

**Expected result:** the first two print a single line `strata <installed-version>` (matching Settings / the updater, including prerelease identity) and exit without opening a window. The third still launches the application, because only the first argument is a launch mode.

## Related issue

Closes #917

issues.body:
### Problem or use case

Packaging checks, support, and scripts need a way to print the installed Strata version without launching the GUI. `docs/packaging.md` already documents `strata --version` as the post-install verification step, but the binary treated that flag as an ordinary application launch.

### Proposed solution

Recognize `--version` as a launch mode, the same way `--portal` and `--preview-helper` already are, and print a single line:

```
strata <installed-version>
```

then exit successfully without starting GTK. Use `build_info::installed_version()` so the printed identity matches Settings and the updater, including prerelease tags.

Document the flag next to the other launch examples in the README.

### Alternatives considered

Printing only `CARGO_PKG_VERSION` would miss prerelease identity carried in `STRATA_RELEASE_TAG`. Adding a long `--help` parser is more than this needs; the existing first-argument launch-mode dispatch is enough.

### Additional context

This is a CLI-only change. No GUI is involved.

body: ## Description Give hidden and cut items distinct visual treatments across Columns, Icons, and List views. Hidden items now display their icon or thumbnail and name at 65% opacity. Cut items replace their icon or thumbnail with the existing scissors icon without reducing the item's opacity. When both states apply, the scissors and name use the hidden-item opacity. Selection backgrounds and focus outlines remain fully opaque. This change affects presentation only and preserves the existing clipboard behavior. ## Visual evidence ### Before Hidden files and folders are visually indistinguishable from normal items and Cut items are indicated only by reduced opacity: ### After ## How to test 1. Open a directory containing normal and hidden files or folders. 2. Press `Ctrl+H` or `Ctrl+.` to show hidden items. 3. Compare normal and hidden items in Columns, Icons, and List views. 4. Select a normal item and press `Ctrl+X`. 5. Repeat with a hidden item and with a file that has a thumbnail. 6. Press `Ctrl+C` on another item or complete the paste operation to clear the cut state. **Expected result:** Hidden items display their icon or thumbnail and name at 65% opacity. Cut items display the scissors icon at full opacity, including when replacing a thumbnail. Hidden-and-cut items display the scissors and name at 65% opacity. Selection and focus styling remain fully opaque, and clearing the cut state immediately restores the original icon or thumbnail. ## Related issue Closes #926

issues.body: ## Problem or use case Strata currently communicates the cut state by reducing the opacity of the entire item. This becomes ambiguous when hidden files and folders also need a visually subdued presentation, since both states would rely on the same signal. Applying opacity to the whole item also attenuates selection and focus styling, making the current state harder to read. Hidden and cut should remain independent and immediately recognizable: - opacity should communicate that an item is hidden; - a scissors icon should communicate that an item is cut. ## Proposed solution Use the following visual states consistently in Columns, Icons, and List views: | State | Icon or thumbnail | Label | | --- | --- | --- | | Normal | Original presentation | 100% | | Hidden | Original presentation at 65% | 65% | | Cut | Scissors replacing the icon or thumbnail at 100% | 100% | | Hidden and cut | Scissors replacing the icon or thumbnail at 65% | 65% | Additional behavior: - Replace the complete thumbnail with the existing Lucide scissors icon while an item is cut. - Restore the original icon or thumbnail when the cut state ends. - Keep selection backgrounds and focus outlines at full opacity. - Update the presentation immediately when the cut state changes, without requiring a manual refresh. - Preserve each view's existing normal icon opacity instead of normalizing every icon to 100%. ## Alternatives considered - **Opacity for cut items:** rejected because it would be visually ambiguous with hidden items and also attenuates selection/focus styling. - **Scissors badge over thumbnails:** rejected because the badge becomes too small to read in compact views. - **Dashed border around the scissors:** tested, but rejected because it competes with the scissors and becomes illegible at the 17–18 px sizes used by Columns and List. - **`square-bottom-dashed-scissors` Lucide icon:** tested, but rejected for the same small-scale legibility issue. ## Visual examples ### Before Hidden files and folders are visually indistinguishable from normal items: Cut items are indicated only by reduced opacity: ### Proposed Hidden, cut, and hidden + cut: ## Strata version v0.16.0 ## Additional context Requested as an enhancement, not a bug. To exercise: enable hidden files, then compare normal, hidden, cut, and hidden-and-cut items in Columns, Icons, and List views. The expected result is: - hidden items display their icon or thumbnail and label at 65% opacity; - cut items replace their icon or thumbnail with the existing scissors icon at full opacity; - hidden-and-cut items display the scissors icon and label at 65% opacity; - selection backgrounds and focus outlines remain at full opacity; - clearing the cut state immediately restores the original icon or thumbnail. This is a presentation-only change. Existing clipboard ownership, transfer, paste, and cancellation behavior should remain unchanged.

author: pdwaldrop
body:
## Description

Revealing a specific entry by name or location (`select_entries_by_name_at` / `select_entries_by_location_at`) finds the matching entry's position in the column's raw entry list and applies it through the UI's raw-position-to-view-position translation (`ColumnView`'s `ViewMap`). A hidden entry has no view position while hidden files are off -- the filtered view simply doesn't contain it -- so the translation silently drops it and nothing gets selected. `ShowItems` on a hidden file therefore opened its parent directory but left the selection empty, contrary to the README's promise that named items are selected.

`select_entries_matching_at` now checks whether any matching entry is hidden and, if hidden files are currently off, turns them on first (via the same path the Toggle Hidden action uses) before resolving positions -- so the row actually exists in the view by the time selection is applied.

This is shared by `ShowItems` and the CLI file-argument reveal path (`open_argument.rs`), which route through the same selection helper, so both get the fix.

## Visual evidence

## Description

Keep encrypted devices visible in the Devices sidebar, add themed Lock/Unlock controls and a shared context menu, and keep device controls clear of the overlay scrollbar. Strata-owned mounts retain the themed authentication overlay; competing mount jobs are waited on without cancelling them. Unlock completion refreshes the current mount or navigates when requested, unless its progress was hidden.

Successor matching uses exact GIO object identity and the LUKS UUID rather than accepting another encrypted partition on the same physical drive. Mounted GVfs crypto volumes lock through unmount; unsupported unmounted locks report an error before touching saved passwords. Supported cached credentials require confirmation before deletion. Password-manager deletion prompts that Strata cannot display remain an explicit limitation.

**Still unverified:** the live Wayland/automounter prompt-ownership acceptance for #537. The existing [reproduction limitation](https://github.com/lgse/strata/issues/537#issuecomment-5611464811) is not closed by isolated GTK tests. This PR does not disable or configure desktop automounters.

## Visual evidence

**Pending owner upload through the GitHub editor.** Current private-Xvfb captures show production device controls with explicitly synthetic device rows and the unsupported-lock error. They are not live LUKS evidence. No supported authenticated attachment uploader is available in this review session.

## How to test

1. With a disposable LUKS volume, unlock from its Devices row, lock icon, and context menu. Check quiet Cancel, wrong-password retry, and successful unlock/mount/navigation without another file manager.
2. Hide the unlocking progress and change folders; completion must not steal navigation. When already inside the mount, its contents should refresh without F5.
3. Lock a mounted encrypted volume. When its password is saved, Cancel the forget-password confirmation, then confirm it. Verify both lock state and credential removal. An unlocked but unmounted volume without a supported lock operation must show an error without deleting its password.
4. With enough sidebar content to scroll, verify Lock/Eject remain reachable. Non-encrypted devices must have no lock control, and devices without eject capability must not offer Eject. Change the theme and check live recoloring.
5. On the target Wayland desktop, record the owners and request sequence of prompts with the automounter present and absent. Keep this live verification separate from the synthetic/isolated captures.

**Expected result:** device rows survive lock/unlock; Strata's operations use its themed prompt, errors remain actionable, and unsupported operations never claim success. Live competing-prompt ownership remains pending until step 5 is verified.

## Related issue

Refs #537 — live prompt-ownership acceptance remains open.
Closes #954

## Description

Add a saved **Keep arrows in file list** switch under Settings → General → Browsing, off by default. When enabled, arrow keys no longer move focus out of the file list into the pane header, sidebar, or top navigation bar — fast arrowing stays scoped to content. Tab and the mouse still reach those controls. A live **Ctrl+\\** shortcut toggles the mode mid-session, and the file chooser respects the same preference.

This is an opt-out for the arrow-escape behavior introduced in #291, defaulting off to preserve existing keyboard-only and accessibility workflows.

## Visual evidence

Review-update screenshots (Columns focus and settings search) are captured locally; GitHub attachment upload is pending owner action. See the review follow-up comment.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/39eb4417-5fef-4fa3-bceb-709790743eb5

## How to test

1. In List or Icons, focus the file list and hold Up to the first row. With the toggle off, focus escapes into the pane header (unchanged).
2. Turn **Keep arrows in file list** on (or press **Ctrl+\\**). Hold Up from the first row again; focus stays in the file list.
3. With it on, press Left at the left edge; focus stays in the file view instead of entering the sidebar.
4. Press **Ctrl+\\** again to toggle off; confirm the Settings switch reflects the change, and that Tab and mouse still reach the header, sidebar, and top-bar controls.
5. Open the file chooser and repeat; it respects the same preference.

**Expected result:** With the toggle on, arrow keys never leave the file list. Tab and mouse remain the way to reach the chrome. The choice persists across restarts and applies to the file chooser.

## Related issue

Closes #939

issues.body:
### Problem or use case

When navigating files fast with arrow keys (or h/j/k/l) in List or Icons mode, focus can escape the file list and land in the UI layer. Once selection reaches the first row, the next Up moves focus into the pane header (sort/view-mode buttons); from there Left/Right traverse header controls, and further Up can leak into the sidebar and the top navigation bar. The same happens at the left edge in Icons, where Left enters the sidebar.

This is the documented behavior from #291, but when moving quickly it stumbles: the user expects to keep arrowing through files and instead ends up tabbing around chrome, losing their place in the content. There is no way to opt out of arrows reaching the UI layer.

### Proposed solution

Add a saved preference (off by default, to preserve current keyboard-only/accessibility behavior) that keeps arrow navigation scoped to the file list. When enabled:

- Up from the first row stays on the first row (or stops) instead of focusing the header.
- Left at the edge stays in the file view instead of entering the sidebar.
- The header, sidebar, and top-bar controls remain reachable by Tab and mouse click, just not by arrows.

Surface the toggle in Settings → Keybindings, next to "Show keybinding hints", since both govern keyboard behavior. Follow `docs/preferences.md` for live updates across open windows.

Additionally, bind a keyboard shortcut to toggle this preference live, so power users can flip the mode mid-session without opening Settings (e.g. when they do want to arrow through the toolbar for a moment).

### Alternatives considered

- Hard-disable arrow escape into chrome: rejected, breaks keyboard-only and accessibility workflows that rely on full arrow traversal.
- Settings toggle only (no shortcut): simpler, but slower to flip contextually.

author: JoeJoeflyn
body:
## Description

Replaces coarse `EntryKind` sorting with filename-based MIME description ordering across Columns, Icons, and List views.

- Resolves MIME content types strictly from filename via `gio::content_type_guess(name, None)` with bounded thread-local filename caching to ensure zero disk I/O and no heap overhead per `FileEntry`.
- In Ascending order: Known MIME types are sorted A–Z, with unrecognized ("Other") entries placed last, and identical types tie-broken A–Z by filename.
- In Descending order: "Other" entries are placed first, known MIME types are sorted Z–A, and identical types remain tie-broken A–Z by filename.
- Respects the *Folders first* preference: folders lead the listing A–Z when enabled, or participate alphabetically as `"Folder"` among known MIME types when disabled.
- Updates List view's Type column and *Group by Type* sections to display and group by MIME descriptions instead of generic file tags.

## Visual evidence

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/86496cd4-c73e-45d9-a31c-11664bd673f2

## How to test

1. Open a directory containing different file types (e.g. `.pdf`, `.py`, `.json`, `.txt`, folders, and unrecognized files).
2. Switch sort key to **Type** and toggle between **Ascending** and **Descending**.
3. In List view (`Ctrl+2`), observe the **Type** column displaying human-readable MIME descriptions (e.g. "JSON document", "PDF document", "Folder", "Other").
4. Enable **Group by Type** in List view and verify the section headers.

**Expected result:**
Entries sort by their human-readable MIME descriptions in A–Z / Z–A order, "Other" files remain at the boundary (last in ascending, first in descending), filenames inside each type tie-break A–Z, and List view displays MIME descriptions.

## Related issue

Closes #508

issues.body: ### Problem or use case **Type** sort is wired up in Columns, Icons, and List, but it only compares coarse filesystem kind (`Folder` / `File` / link / other). Every ordinary file is the same key, so with Folders first on (the default) Type ascending and Type descending look like Name ascending. Toggling Type does nothing useful in a mixed folder. A file manager should cluster by what the file *is* — JSON with JSON, PDFs with PDFs — not by inode kind. List **Group by type** already shows shared-MIME descriptions (`JSON document`, `Python script`, …). Type *sort* should use that same notion. ### Proposed solution When the pane sort key is **Type**, order by filename MIME **description**. Guess the type from the **name only** (`content_type_guess(name, None)`), the same path Group by type already uses. Do not sort by `EntryKind`. Do not sniff file bytes, stat for emptiness, or query `standard::content-type` during enumerate. **Extensions only, not Dolphin-style sniffing.** Dolphin (and GIO `standard::content-type` on the inode) inspects contents. A 0-byte `z.txt` becomes `application/x-zerosize` / empty and shows as **Other**; a `.txt` with bytes shows as **Text**. Strata will not do that. `.txt` is always the OS description for `text/plain` (e.g. Plain text document), empty or not. Same ceiling as Group by type: wrong extensions and extensionless files follow the name, not the bytes. Matching Dolphin would mean I/O on every file and fights streaming / incremental sort. **Ascending** 1. Known MIME descriptions A–Z 2. **Other** last (unrecognized / `application/octet-stream` / empty description) 3. Within each type, names always A–Z **Descending** 1. **Other** first 2. Known MIME descriptions Z–A 3. Within each type, names still A–Z (do not reverse names) **Folders first** (when enabled) - Folders come before known types and before Other - Folders themselves are always A–Z, including when Type is descending - Then apply the Type order above to everything else When Folders first is off, folders take part in the Type order like any other known type (e.g. “Folder” among A–Z / Z–A). Other is a special bucket: last in ascending, first in descending — not sorted as the word “Other” in the alphabet. Example with Folders first on: - Ascending: `alpha/` `zeta/` → Markdown… → JSON… → PDF… → Other (`archive-index`, `blob.qqqqq`) - Descending: `alpha/` `zeta/` → Other → PDF… → JSON… → Markdown… Names inside each type stay A–Z in both directions. This is the shared pane sort, so Columns, Icons, and List all follow it. If List **Group by type** is on while sorting by Type, section order should match so headings and rows agree. The List Type column should show the same MIME description (and Other) the sort uses, not `File`/`Folder` kind labels. Keep it on the cheap path: suffix-cached labels, no extra `String` on every `FileEntry`, no Size/Modified-style metadata fill or second sort. ### Alternatives considered - Keep sorting by `EntryKind`: already implemented, and it is a no-op for ordinary files. - Treat Other as a normal A–Z label: would bury unknowns in the O’s instead of parking them at the end (or start, when descending). - Reverse names when Type is descending: worse for scanning a type alphabetically. - Sniff contents like Dolphin (empty `.txt` → Other, non-empty `.txt` → Text): more accurate for zerosize and misnamed files, but real I/O on every entry. Out of scope; filename MIME is the Type sort. ### Visual examples ### Strata version `main` ### Additional context Lift the existing MIME description helper and suffix cache out of List Group by type so `compare_entries` can use it. Type sort already runs once per listing; Columns, Icons, and List all render that order. Object kind (`EntryKind`) stays an internal tag for directories, links, and capabilities; it is not the Type sort key. Labels still come from the OS shared MIME database (e.g. `text/plain` → “Plain text document”). Strata does not invent those strings. It only maps suffix → MIME id → description, with Other as the unknown bucket.

### Problem or use case

Enabling **Settings → General → System file chooser** does not make other applications use Strata for **Show in File Explorer** / **Reveal in File Manager** / **Open containing folder**.

That control is currently the only Desktop Integration action in Settings. Users who skip the installer flags (or who assume “file chooser” means “file manager”) enable it and still get another file manager — or none — for reveal.

The FileChooser portal and the default file manager are separate XDG mechanisms:

- Portal `org.freedesktop.impl.portal.FileChooser` → Open/Save dialogs in portal-aware apps.
- `inode/directory` / `xdg-open` on a folder → open the folder in the default file manager.
- `org.freedesktop.FileManager1` `ShowItems` / `ShowFolders` → what browsers and many GTK/GNOME editors call for reveal, independent of `mimeapps.list`.

Settings only configures the first. Reveal needs the other two. Related closed work: #299 (Omarchy default file manager / installer; not a Settings FileChooser gap), #290 (FileManager1 is implemented, but still opt-in via `--with-file-manager` / the per-user `.service` file), #120 (chooser portal itself).

### Proposed solution

Add a Settings → General desktop-integration control for the default file manager / “Open file location” path, alongside the existing chooser row, using the same installer semantics:

- Set `io.github.lgse.Strata.desktop` as the `inode/directory` handler (GIO, not hand-edited mimeapps).
- Install the per-user `org.freedesktop.FileManager1` activation service, with the existing conflict check against another per-user provider.
- Show current status (`xdg-mime query default inode/directory` and who owns FileManager1) and allow restore.
- Keep FileChooser and default-FM actions independent, matching `--with-file-chooser` vs `--with-file-manager` / `--with-folder-association`.

If a second Settings control is out of scope, at least surface that Reveal is a separate opt-in and point at the README steps, so the only Desktop Integration row is not the dead end for this workflow.

### Alternatives considered

- Treat this as a chooser bug: the Settings copy already says Open/Save only and “This is separate from your default file manager.” `docs/portal-file-chooser.md` says the same. The chooser write path is doing what it documents.
- Rely on the interactive installer only (#299 was closed for that reason). That does not help a running install whose only in-app control is the chooser.
- Set `inode/directory` from the chooser action: would surprise users who want Strata dialogs but not Strata as the folder handler, and still would not cover FileManager1 reveal.

### Visual examples

Settings row (verbatim):

> **System file chooser**
> Use Strata for Open and Save dialogs in portal-aware apps, or restore your previous chooser. This is separate from your default file manager.
> `Configure…`

Configure dialog (verbatim):

> Only apps using the desktop FileChooser portal are affected. … Your default file manager and other portals are unchanged.

### Strata version

0.13.0, built from source (`c62354f` on `main`; chooser Settings copy unchanged on later `main`).

### Additional context

**Reproduction (Settings `Configure…` → Use Strata, same code path as `strata --install-portal` / `portal_setup::install`):**

1. Note baseline: `xdg-mime query default inode/directory` → `thunar.desktop`; no `~/.config/mimeapps.list`; FileManager1 owned by Thunar (`/usr/share/dbus-1/services/org.xfce.Thunar.FileManager1.service`, `Exec=/usr/bin/Thunar --gapplication-service`).
2. Open Settings → General → DESKTOP INTEGRATION → System file chooser → Configure… → Use Strata.
3. Success: “Installed Strata as the per-user file chooser.”

**What the setting writes:**

```
~/.config/xdg-desktop-portal/portals.conf
  [preferred]
  org.freedesktop.impl.portal.FileChooser=strata;*;

~/.local/share/xdg-desktop-portal/portals/strata.portal
  Interfaces=org.freedesktop.impl.portal.FileChooser;

~/.local/share/dbus-1/services/org.freedesktop.impl.portal.desktop.strata.service
  Name=org.freedesktop.impl.portal.desktop.strata
  Exec=…/strata --portal
```

**What it does not write:** `mimeapps.list`, `inode/directory`, or `io.github.lgse.Strata.FileManager1.service` (`Name=org.freedesktop.FileManager1`).

After enable: `xdg-mime query default inode/directory` still `thunar.desktop`. Calling `FileManager1.ShowItems` on `file:///tmp/reveal-demo/notes.txt` still opened **reveal-demo - Thunar**; the running Strata window stayed on its existing Documents folder.

Environment: Ubuntu 24.04, XFCE. Installation method: built from source.

Code: `src/ui/portal_preferences.rs` (Settings row + dialog), `src/portal_setup.rs` (writes only the FileChooser portal), `src/adapters/file_manager1.rs` (Reveal implementation; requires the separate service to be the activatable owner).

author: JoeJoeflyn
body:
## Description

Add a keyboard-first folder jump palette backed by Strata's own navigation history. Successful native folder visits are persisted locally and ranked using fuzzy relevance, frequency, and recency without requiring zoxide or changing pinned folders.

## Visual evidence

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/72e9ab67-3950-413b-878e-d8a99b79426b

## How to test

1. Launch Strata and browse into several folders, revisiting one of them a few times.
2. Press `Ctrl+Shift+K`, type part of a visited folder's name or path, use the arrow keys, and press Enter.

**Expected result:**

The palette initially lists visited folders by frecency, filters to folder-only matches as you type, and immediately navigates to the selected folder. `Ctrl+K` continues to open global file search.

## Related issue

Closes #276

issues.body:
### Problem or use case

Strata's pins work well for a small, manually curated set of locations, but there is no keyboard-first way to jump back to folders discovered during everyday browsing. Recursive search can find a known path, but it does not prioritize locations based on how recently or frequently they were visited.

Users want a quick folder-only search, similar to Yazi's zoxide-powered jump workflow, that learns from navigation and makes commonly used or recently visited directories easy to reopen.

### Proposed solution

Add a quick folder-jump palette that reuses Strata's existing search interaction where practical:

- Search directories only by folder name and path.
- Rank matches using navigation history, taking both frequency and recency into account.
- Record folders visited while browsing in Strata so results improve over time.
- Open the selected folder immediately and support keyboard navigation throughout the palette.
- Keep this distinct from pinned folders: pins remain explicit favorites, while quick jump is learned automatically.

The implementation could either maintain Strata's own ranking data or optionally integrate with zoxide. If zoxide is used, the feature should degrade gracefully when it is not installed and should make the data-sharing behavior clear.

### Alternatives considered

- **Pinned folders:** useful for permanent favorites, but require manual maintenance and do not adapt to browsing habits.
- **Recursive search (`Ctrl+K`):** searches the current tree rather than a learned set of previously visited folders.
- **Location entry (`Ctrl+L`):** fast when the exact path is already known.
- **Direct zoxide integration only:** provides an established frecency database, but would introduce an external dependency and may mix terminal and Strata navigation history in ways users do not expect.

### Visual examples

N/A — the requested interaction is comparable to Strata's current search palette, but restricted to folders and ordered by recency/frequency. Yazi's zoxide jump workflow is a behavioral reference.

### Strata version

N/A

### Additional context

The request specifically referenced Yazi and suggested that its behavior may be backed by zoxide. The desired outcome is a ranked, recent/frequent folder search; zoxide compatibility is an implementation option rather than a requirement.

author: davidkodar
body:
## Description

Quick preview and Print were decided from the file name alone (`gio::content_type_guess(name, None)`), so text files without a recognized extension were rejected before the preview loader ran, even though the loader already resolves uncertain guesses from the file's content type.

When the name-based guess is uncertain, `entry_supports_quick_preview()` and `entry_supports_printing()` now let the file through and the loader decides: text opens in the text preview, images and media use the existing sandboxed paths, and anything else shows "No visual preview". For Print, the deferral only applies when the guessed type is otherwise unsupported, because GLib also reports some recognized names such as `photo.png` as uncertain.

Printing content the loader cannot handle now shows "This file type cannot be printed." instead of silently doing nothing, since Print is offered for extensionless files.

Directory listing, sorting, and grouping remain name-only.

## Visual evidence

After: `some notes` (no extension) opens in the text preview, identified as `text/plain`, with the Print action available in the preview header. Before screenshots are in #964.

![Quick preview of the extensionless text file some notes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/davidkodar/strata/issue-media-extensionless-preview/after-quick-preview-some-notes.png)

## How to test

1. `printf 'hello\nworld\n' > ~/Documents/"some notes"`
2. Select `some notes` in Strata and press Space.
3. Right-click `some notes` and choose Print.
4. `head -c 64 /dev/urandom > ~/Documents/"some data"`, select it and press Space, then right-click it and choose Print.

**Expected result:** `some notes` opens in the text preview and its context menu offers Quick preview and Print, which opens the print dialog. `some data` shows "No visual preview", and Print reports "This file type cannot be printed."

## Related issue

Closes #964

issues.body:
### Strata version

0.17.0 (commit b82ac8e)

### Installation method

Built from source

### Linux distribution and desktop environment

Arch Linux / Omarchy 4.0.3, Hyprland 0.56.2, GTK 4.22.4, GLib 2.88.3, shared-mime-info 2.5.1

### What happened?

Plain text files without an extension cannot be previewed or printed. Pressing Space does nothing, single-click previews do nothing, and the context menu has neither the Quick preview nor the Print item. Enter still opens the file in the default editor, and the Properties dialog correctly shows it as "Plain text document".

Extensionless files are common on Linux (notes, `LICENSE`-style files, exported data), so these files are currently impossible to preview.

The cause appears to be that `entry_supports_quick_preview()` (`src/ui/preview.rs`) decides using only `gio::content_type_guess(name, None)`. For names like `notes` or `todo`, GLib returns `application/octet-stream` with `uncertain = true`, so the file is rejected before the preview loader runs. `entry_supports_printing()` (`src/ui/browser/entry.rs`) uses the same name-only guess, which is why Print is missing too. The loader in `src/adapters/local_preview.rs` already handles uncertain guesses by querying `standard::content-type`, which returns `text/plain` for these files. The gate never lets them reach it.

### Steps to reproduce

1. `printf 'hello\nworld\n' > ~/Documents/"some notes"`
2. Open Strata and select `some notes`.
3. Press Space (or single-click it with single-click file previews enabled).
4. Observe: no preview opens. Right-click the file and observe that there is no Quick preview or Print item.
5. Open Properties for the same file and observe that it is identified as "Plain text document".
6. Copy it to `some notes.txt` (identical contents) and repeat: Space previews it, and the context menu shows Quick preview and Print.

### Expected behavior

The file opens in the existing text preview, like `some notes.txt` does.

When the name-based guess is uncertain, the quick preview gate could let the selected file through and let the loader decide from its content type. Files that turn out not to be previewable would show the existing "No visual preview" message, the same as a `.zip` file today. I checked GIO content types for extensionless test files:

| File (no extension) | `standard::content-type` | Resulting preview |
| --- | --- | --- |
| text | `text/plain` | text preview |
| random binary | `application/octet-stream` | No visual preview |
| empty | `application/x-zerosize` | No visual preview |
| executable | `application/x-executable` | No visual preview |
| zip | `application/zip` | No visual preview |
| PNG | `image/png` | sandboxed image preview |
| MP4 | `video/mp4` | sandboxed media preview |

Directory listing, sorting, and grouping could stay name-only as described in #508. Content would only be queried asynchronously for the single file being previewed.

### Screenshots or video

1. Properties for `some notes`: Strata identifies it as "Plain text document" and opens it with Neovim.

![Properties dialog for some notes showing Plain text document](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/davidkodar/strata/issue-media-extensionless-preview/properties-some-notes.png)

2. Context menu for `some notes.txt`: Quick preview (Space) and Print are available.

![Context menu for some notes.txt with Quick preview and Print](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/davidkodar/strata/issue-media-extensionless-preview/menu-some-notes-txt.png)

3. Context menu for `some notes` (same contents, no extension): Quick preview and Print are missing.

![Context menu for some notes without Quick preview or Print](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/davidkodar/strata/issue-media-extensionless-preview/menu-some-notes.png)

### Relevant logs

N/A — no error is logged; the file is silently filtered out before the preview loader runs.

### Additional context

Related: #223 / #224 added a fallback for extensionless dotfiles only, so ordinary extensionless files are still excluded.

Behavior change to confirm: an extensionless binary file would open the preview pane with "No visual preview" instead of doing nothing, and the Quick preview context-menu item would appear for extensionless files. Print could follow the same content-type result.

Possibly separate: the #224 dotfile fallback treats any non-executable extensionless dotfile as text, even when GIO identifies it as `application/octet-stream`, so a binary dotfile renders as garbled text.

I'd like to work on this fix if it can be assigned to me.
issues.title: fix(preview): quick preview ignores text files without a recognized extension

title: fix(preview): defer uncertain file types to the preview loader

## Description

HEIC, HEIF, AVIF, and JPEG XL images showed a generic file icon instead of a thumbnail. `thumbnail_kind()` only accepts a fixed extension list, and these formats were missing, so thumbnail generation was never attempted even though the sandboxed image helper already renders them through gdk-pixbuf/glycin with the ImageMagick fallback.

This adds `heic`, `heif`, `avif`, and `jxl` to the thumbnail extension list, and `heic`, `heif`, and `jxl` to the picture icon mapping, which already had `avif`. While a thumbnail loads, or when no decoder is installed, these files now show the picture icon instead of the generic document icon.

## Visual evidence

Before (from #968): `sample.heic` shows a generic icon next to `sample.jpg` with a thumbnail.

![Before: sample.heic without a thumbnail](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/davidkodar/strata/issue-media-extensionless-preview/thumbnails-heic-vs-jpg.png)

After: both files show the thumbnail.

![After: sample.heic and sample.jpg both show thumbnails](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/davidkodar/strata/issue-media-extensionless-preview/thumbnails-heic-vs-jpg-after.png)

## How to test

1. Put a `.heic` photo in a folder, along with a copy converted to JPEG (`magick photo.heic photo.jpg`).
2. Open the folder in Strata and switch to Icons view (Ctrl+2).
3. Optionally repeat with `.heif`, `.avif`, and `.jxl` files, for example `magick photo.jpg photo.avif`.

**Expected result:** the `.heic` file shows the same thumbnail as the `.jpg` copy. AVIF, HEIF, and JPEG XL files get thumbnails as well, provided the system has a decoder for them.

## Related issue

Closes #968

### Strata version

0.17.0 (commit b82ac8e)

### Installation method

Built from source

### Linux distribution and desktop environment

Arch Linux / Omarchy 4.0.3, Hyprland 0.56.2, GTK 4.22.4, GLib 2.88.3, gdk-pixbuf2 2.44.7, glycin 2.1.5, libheif 1.23.4, ImageMagick 7.1.2.31

### What happened?

HEIC photos show a generic file icon instead of a thumbnail. HEIC is the default photo format on iPhones, so photos copied from an iPhone to Linux are affected in bulk. HEIF, AVIF, and JPEG XL images are affected the same way.

Thumbnail generation is never attempted for these files. `thumbnail_kind()` in `src/ui/thumbnail.rs` only accepts a fixed extension list:

```rust
"png" | "jpg" | "jpeg" | "webp" | "gif" | "bmp" | "tif" | "tiff" | "svg" => Some(ThumbnailKind::Image)
```

`heic`, `heif`, `avif`, and `jxl` are not in the list, so these files fall through to `None`.

The rest of the pipeline already supports them. GIO identifies the files as `image/heif`, `image/avif`, and `image/jxl`, and the sandboxed helper renders them. Running `strata --preview-helper thumbnail-image <file> <output> 256 software` inside the same bubblewrap sandbox as the app:

| Input | Result |
| --- | --- |
| iPhone `.heic` photo | 192x256 PNG, correct orientation |
| generated `.avif` | 256x192 PNG |
| generated `.jxl` | 256x192 PNG |

Quick preview already works for these files: selecting a `.heic` photo shows the full image in the preview pane, because preview classifies by content type (`image/*`) rather than this extension list. Only the thumbnail is missing.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Copy a `.heic` photo from an iPhone into a folder.
2. Open the folder in Strata in Icons view.
3. Observe: the file shows a generic icon instead of a thumbnail.
4. Convert the same photo to `.jpg` (for example `magick photo.heic photo.jpg`) and observe that the JPEG gets a thumbnail.

### Expected behavior

HEIC, HEIF, AVIF, and JPEG XL images get thumbnails like other image formats, through the existing `ThumbnailKind::Image` path and its gdk-pixbuf/ImageMagick fallback chain. When the system lacks a decoder, the file keeps its normal icon, as for any failed thumbnail today.

### Screenshots or video

Icons view with the same image saved as `sample.heic` (generic icon) and `sample.jpg` (thumbnail):

![sample.heic shows a generic icon while sample.jpg shows a thumbnail](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/davidkodar/strata/issue-media-extensionless-preview/thumbnails-heic-vs-jpg.png)

### Relevant logs

N/A: no error is logged; thumbnail generation is never attempted.

### Additional context

Same class of issue as #880, where `svg` was missing from the list and #881 added it with a `thumbnail_kind` test in `src/ui/thumbnail/tests.rs`.

I'd like to work on this fix if it can be assigned to me.

author: l0gicgate
body:
## Description

One combined archive update, replacing #973 and #977:

- Reserve a fresh folder for each activation (`archive`, `archive (1)`, …), preserving existing contents.
- Show Preparing… immediately and retain an activity spinner while encoding/finalizing.
- Stop cancelled encoding cooperatively inside members; wait for worker exit before cleanup and the cancellation summary.
- Avoid unnecessary recompression according to each container's capabilities:

| Format | Policy |
| --- | --- |
| ZIP | Store known already-compressed files; DEFLATE others. Raw TAR/BMP/WAV/AVI/ISO inputs retain compression. |
| 7Z | Copy known already-compressed files; streaming LZMA2 for others, with a member-sized dictionary. Preserve AES payload and header encryption. |
| TAR | Uncompressed, retaining sparse-file and symlink handling. |
| TAR.GZ | One valid gzip stream: stored DEFLATE blocks for all-compressed payloads, default gzip for mixed/unknown payloads. Small size overhead is the CPU tradeoff. |
| RAR | Extraction only; no creation added. |

Classification is a filename heuristic, not payload sampling. Mixed TAR.GZ still compresses the entire TAR stream. See [archive behavior and limitations](docs/archives.md).

## Visual evidence

Pending owner upload through the GitHub editor. Sanitized collision before/after and preparation captures are retained locally; exact paths and captions are in the handoff comment. No attachments are claimed yet.

## How to test

1. Double-click `archive.tar.gz` three times. Edit a file in the first extracted folder before repeating. Expect separate `archive`, `archive (1)`, and `archive (2)` folders with the edit preserved.
2. Create ZIP, 7Z, TAR, and TAR.GZ archives from compressed media, then from a mix of media and text. Open/extract each and compare contents. Try password-protected ZIP and 7Z too.
3. Start 7Z or TAR.GZ creation on a large unknown-extension file. Expect immediate Preparing… feedback; cancel during encoding and wait for the cancellation summary. Close it and create another archive.

**Expected result:** Existing extractions stay untouched; supported containers avoid wasteful recompression without changing format or losing encryption. Progress remains visibly active. Cancellation leaves no published partial archive or staging file, and subsequent operations work.

## Related issue

Closes #972
Closes #974
Closes #978
Closes #413

issues.body:
### Strata version

0.11.1, source commit `a96c4a097f99d9183bd41c9976695b250858a0bb` (debug build).

### Installation method

Built from source.

### Linux distribution and desktop environment

Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS, XFCE on X11 (Cursor Cloud VM). Isolated temp HOME/XDG. This is not Omarchy / Hyprland / Wayland.

### What happened?

Compressing a large directory and clicking **Cancel** dismisses the archive progress overlay immediately, but the blocking compression worker keeps running. Staging is unlinked from the destination directory, so the listing looks idle and no zip appears, while Strata continues to burn CPU for tens of seconds writing into the unlinked file.

This is the compression counterpart of extraction-cancel [#403](https://github.com/lgse/strata/issues/403). Extraction is addressed (unmerged) in [PR #410](https://github.com/lgse/strata/pull/410). On current `main`, compression has the same abort-and-detach worker pattern.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open a writable listing that contains one large directory (this run used `payload-dir`: 160 × 2 MiB unique-random files, ~321 MiB).
2. Right-click the directory → **Compress…**. Leave ZIP, no password. Click **Compress**.
3. Wait until the **Working** overlay is clearly in progress (both trials were past 50 / 160 files).
4. Click **Cancel** once.
5. Observe the overlay, the listing, CPU, and any `.strata-compression-*` sibling of the destination.

### Expected behavior

Cancel should stop further compression promptly. The progress UI should stay up until the worker has actually stopped. Incomplete staging should be cleaned up, and a published archive should not appear after a mid-run cancel.

### Screenshots or video

Recordings and logs from this Cursor Cloud run: https://cursor.com/artifacts/v/art-6494cafd-082d-4b79-b674-bbf9dda4ee81

- Trial 1: Cancel at **53 / 160 files**; overlay gone immediately.
- Trial 2: Cancel at **56–69 / 160 files**; overlay gone immediately; window stayed up (post-cancel screenshot of the listing with only `payload-dir`, no zip).

Recording trailers may show a desktop/session overlay after the capture ends. The Strata process (pid 3178) stayed alive across both trials; it did not crash.

### Relevant logs

```text
CLK_TCK=100

Trial 1
  staging .strata-compression-8wzu6S grew to 111 MiB
  Cancel unlinked staging at t=111.7s (ticks 2174, 17 threads)
  worker continued: ticks 2174 → 5183 by t=156.2s (Δ 30.1s CPU)
  threads 17 → 15 only after the worker finished
  published zip: never

Trial 2
  staging .strata-compression-iNmosS grew to 140 MiB
  Cancel unlinked staging at t=536.8s (ticks 7799, 17 threads)
  worker continued: ticks 7799 → 10315 over the next 33s (Δ 25.2s CPU)
  published zip: never
```

Directory reload (ArchiveCompleted) is logged at the Cancel instant, while CPU is still climbing:

```text
2026-09-06T02:13:18Z  directory load finished entries=1   # trial 1 cancel → listing refresh
2026-09-06T02:20:23Z  directory load finished entries=1   # trial 2 cancel → listing refresh
```

### Additional context

## Repro update

**Verdict: REPRODUCED** on `main` @ `a96c4a0` (v0.11.1 debug build, X11). Isolated temp HOME/XDG. Synthetic names only (`payload-dir`, `batch-NN`, `item-NNN.bin`). Cancel failed consistently (2/2): overlay dismissed immediately; worker kept running; no zip published.

### Trigger

ZIP-compress a directory large enough that **Working** shows `N / total files`, then Cancel while the count is still moving. Both trials used the same 160-file random payload. Format left at ZIP, no password.

### What Cancel actually does (observed)

- Progress overlay (**Working** / **This may take a moment** / **Cancel**) disappears at once.
- Destination listing reloads; `.strata-compression-*` is unlinked so nothing looks in progress.
- No error dialog, no cancellation summary.
- `payload-dir.zip` was not published in either trial (persist never ran).
- Strata CPU stays near one core for ~30s after Cancel, writing into the unlinked staging fd, until the encoder finishes and the extra worker thread drops.

The UI therefore looks cancelled. The operation is not.

### Likely code area (observation only; no fix)

On `main`, `LocalOperationProvider::compress` in `src/adapters/local_operations.rs` sets an `AtomicBool` and aborts the supervising `glib` task. Only `archive_progress_timer` reads that flag. Encoding runs in `gio::spawn_blocking` inside `write_staged_archive`; `compress_zip` / `compress_tar` / `compress_7z` never check cancel. Dropping the blocking handle detaches the worker.

`Browser::cancel_file_operation` treats archives as non-transfer/delete/restore and immediately emits `ArchiveCompleted`, which is why the overlay dismisses before the worker stops.

The unit test `cancelling_staged_compression_unlinks_the_partial_output` already aborts the glib task, asserts the stage name is gone, then **waits for the worker to finish** — it documents continued work after unlink.

[PR #410](https://github.com/lgse/strata/pull/410) (`cursor/fix-archive-staging-and-cancel-32c5`) is extraction + staging-permissions. That branch also threads the cancel flag into the compression loops and stops aborting the compress glib task (LoadHandle only stores the flag). It is not merged; `main` still has the abort-and-detach compression path. This report is about current `main` compression UX, not extraction.

**Labels suggestion:** `bug`, `UX`
