author: spandan11106
body:
## Description

Quick preview renders RTF and Word (DOCX) documents instead of showing raw source or nothing at all. Both feed the paragraph/block document model and virtualized rich-text view already used for Markdown, HTML, CSV/TSV and workbooks, so they inherit its theming, selection, copy, sorting and bounded-parsing behaviour.

- **RTF** is converted in process to the bounded HTML subset the rendered view already parses: paragraphs, line breaks, bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, Windows-1252 `\'hh` escapes and `\uN` escapes with their `\ucN` fallback characters. Font tables, stylesheets, pictures, headers, footers and other non-body destination groups are discarded. It keeps its **Source** view like Markdown and HTML.
- **DOCX** is read with `docx-rs` inside the existing preview sandbox, under the same 20 MiB input limit as workbooks, and returns bounded JSON that the application reparses with the existing HTML parser. Headings, `Title`/`Subtitle`, quote styles, inline formatting, tabs, breaks, bulleted and numbered lists with nesting, and tables all render; the first table row becomes the sortable column titles. Being a ZIP container, it has no Source view — the same as XLSX/ODS.
- Underline (`u`, `ins`) is now part of the supported HTML subset. The Pango layer already had the span style but the parser dropped it, so underlined text lost its formatting and raised a misleading "unsupported or active HTML content was omitted" notice.
- `PreviewContent::Workbook` is renamed to `Rendered`, since spreadsheets and Word documents now share it.

The RTF converter is hand written rather than using `rtf-parser` as the issue proposed. That crate (0.4.3) drops `\par` entirely, so every paragraph runs together; decodes `\'93` to U+0093 instead of a curly quote; and turns `舒?` into an unrelated CJK character while leaving the `?` fallback in place. DOCX uses `docx-rs` as planned.

Known limits, documented in `docs/document-previews.md`: DOCX drops images, hyperlink targets, headers, footers, footnotes and comments, joins each cell's paragraphs into one value, and flattens nested tables into their containing cell; RTF renders paragraphs and inline formatting only, so list markers and table cells become plain text, code pages other than Windows-1252 can mis-decode `\'hh`, and files over the 1 MiB preview limit fall back to Source.

## Visual evidence

Pending — a short video of both previews will be attached in a follow-up comment below.

## How to test

1. Create a folder with a `.docx` containing headings, bold/italic/underlined text, a bulleted list, a numbered list and a table, plus a `.rtf` with several paragraphs, styled runs, curly quotes and an em dash. Any Word or WordPad/LibreOffice export works.
2. Browse to that folder in Strata, select the `.docx` and press <kbd>Space</kbd>.
3. Click a column title in the table to sort it, then drag across a few cells and press <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>C</kbd>.
4. Select the `.rtf` and press <kbd>Space</kbd>, then use **View source** in the preview header and switch back to the rendered view.
5. Switch theme while both previews are open.

**Expected result:** the DOCX preview shows a styled document — headings, inline formatting, nested bullets, numbered items and a sortable table whose first row is the column titles — with no **View source** control and no omission notice; the copied cells arrive tab separated. The RTF preview shows one block per paragraph with its bold, italic, underlined and struck runs, curly quotes and dashes intact, and toggles between **Rendered** and **Source**. Both follow the active theme live. Files that cannot be parsed fall back to the source view or "Preview unavailable" rather than failing the pane.

## Related issue

Closes #730

issues.body:
### Problem or use case

Strata's quick preview shows RTF and DOCX files as raw/source text, which is not meaningful for DOCX (a ZIP-based binary format) and loses all formatting for RTF. Part of the broader tabular/office preview work tracked in #244; this issue scopes the RTF/DOCX portion of it.

### Proposed solution

Both formats are rich-text documents (paragraphs, headings, emphasis, lists, tables, images) rather than tabular data, so they don't fit the table-grid preview already shipped for CSV/TSV/Excel/ODS (#723). Instead, they share a rendering shape with each other: parse into a structured paragraph/block document model and render through a rich-text document view.

- Parse RTF with `rtf-parser` (MIT, mature, zero external dependencies).
- Parse DOCX with `docx-rs` (MIT, mature, structured read path covering paragraphs, runs/formatting, tables, images, and styles).
- Render both through the same native rich-document view — paragraphs, headings, emphasis, lists, tables, and images with Strata's theme tokens applied — reusing the paragraph/block document model and virtualized rich-text view PR #187 is building for Markdown/HTML previews (issue #89), rather than building a separate one-off renderer.

**This issue depends on #187 merging first**, since it introduces the document model and view that RTF/DOCX parsing would feed into.

### Alternatives considered

- Continue showing RTF/DOCX as plain text or no preview (status quo).
- Building a standalone renderer instead of reusing #187's document model — rejected, would duplicate a large amount of already-reviewed rendering infrastructure.

### Visual examples

N/A — follows the rendered-document styling introduced by #187 once that lands.

### Strata version

Current `main`

### Additional context

PPTX/PPT/ODP (presentations) and ODT are intentionally excluded here: presentation formats need a slide-based view rather than a document view, the PPTX/ODP Rust library (`pptx-to-md`) is under 1.5 years old and unproven, legacy PPT/DOC have no viable pure-Rust reader, and ODT has no structured-reader library at all. These remain tracked under the parent epic #244 without a concrete plan yet.

DOCX has substantially richer feature coverage than RTF (images, complex tables, styles), so even under one issue, implementation will likely land as separate commits/PRs per format.

## Description

Add Archive Quick Look support for ZIP, 7z, TAR, and TAR.GZ/TGZ archives. Archives can be previewed as a directory tree without extraction, with password handling, malformed-archive detection, sandboxed listing, cancellation, and resource limits for hostile archive names/nesting.

author: JoeJoeflyn
body:
## Description

Copying a folder onto an existing folder with the same name previously offered only Replace, Keep Both, or Skip, and Replace permanently deletes destination-only contents. This PR adds Finder/Nautilus-style folder merging with safe undo, plus a small Columns-view fix bundled in the same branch.

This PR:

- offers a **Merge** action in the conflict dialog for folder-to-folder copy conflicts, combining the incoming tree into the destination while preserving destination-only entries;
- overwrites same-named leaf items with the incoming copies, after staging each overwritten original in Trash so nothing is lost;
- reports the merge plan through a new `Merged` operation event and records an `UndoEntry::Merge`, so **Ctrl+Z** removes what the merge created, deletes the incoming copies at overwritten paths, and restores the staged originals through the existing Trash restore pipeline;
- does not offer Merge for file conflicts or for moves, where a merged undo cannot safely restore the consumed source;
- fixes Ctrl+C/Ctrl+X (and duplicate) doing nothing on an opened folder in Columns view: the actions now fall back to the entered folder when the focused column selected nothing, reusing the `deletion_entries` fallback from #90;
- keeps delete behavior in Columns unchanged, per #358.

## Visual evidence

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/425f52a4-8fd5-4866-82be-48cf23c24388

- the conflict dialog showing the **Merge** button between Keep Both and Replace;
- the merged destination after Merge, then after Ctrl+Z (incoming file gone, overwritten file restored to its original contents, destination-only file untouched).

## How to test

1. Create `source/folder` containing `incoming.txt` and `shared.txt`, and `archive/folder` containing `stays.txt` and a different `shared.txt`.
2. Copy `source/folder`, paste it into `archive`, and choose **Merge** in the conflict dialog.
3. Confirm `archive/folder` now holds `incoming.txt`, `stays.txt`, and `shared.txt` with the incoming contents, and that the source folder is unchanged.
4. Press Ctrl+Z and confirm `incoming.txt` is removed, `shared.txt` is restored to its original contents, and `stays.txt` and `folder` itself are untouched.
5. Copy a file onto a same-named file, or cut a folder onto a same-named folder, and confirm Merge is not offered.
6. In Columns view, click a folder so its contents open in the next column while it stays highlighted, press Ctrl+C, then paste elsewhere and confirm the folder is copied.

**Expected result:** Folder contents merge with incoming-wins overwrites, Ctrl+Z fully reverts the merge via Trash staging, and copy/cut operate on the entered folder in Columns view.

## Related issue

Closes #1091

issues.body:
### Problem or use case

Copying a folder onto an existing folder with the same name offers only Replace, Keep Both, or Skip. Replace is a staged whole-directory swap that permanently deletes destination-only contents, so there is no way to combine two directories the way Finder's Merge or Nautilus/Explorer folder merging does.

### Proposed solution

Offer a Merge action on folder-to-folder copy conflicts: the incoming folder's contents are unioned into the destination, destination-only entries are preserved, and same-named leaf items are overwritten by the incoming copies. Overwritten originals are staged in Trash first so the merge is undoable: Ctrl+Z removes what the merge created and restores the staged originals. Merge is not offered for file conflicts or for moves.

### Alternatives considered

- Keep Both: creates a numbered sibling copy instead of combining contents.
- Replace: loses destination-only files permanently.
- Per-file conflict prompts inside the merge, or newer-wins resolution like Finder: possible follow-ups, but incoming-wins with Trash staging keeps v1 predictable and undoable.

### Strata version

main @ 0.18.0 development build

## Description

Enable smooth horizontal edge autoscrolling when dragging files near the viewport edges in Columns view, matching expected multi-column file manager behaviors.

Key changes:
- Track file drag motion over the column scroller and dynamically autoscroll horizontally (and vertically inside listings) when dragging near strip edges.
- Disable automatic `scroll-to-focus` on the columns scroller viewport so drop operations and background filesystem notifications do not cause unwanted scroll jumps back to the original source column.
- Verify drag threshold in `install_column_peek_targets` so dragged items released over peeked columns are not mistakenly treated as peek reveal clicks.
- Clear pending pointer activations immediately upon drag initiation to prevent unintended click activation on drag release.

## Visual evidence

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7e440894-e4cd-41ba-a313-52ea8dca71f2

## How to test

1. Open Strata in Columns mode.
2. Resize the window narrow enough so only 1–2 columns fit horizontally.

author: JoeJoeflyn
body:
## Description

Adds folder-merge support and undo coverage for create, replace, restore, and compress. This PR now targets `main` and includes the merge/merge-undo machinery from #1092.

- **Create** — undo trashes the new file/folder.
- **Copy Replace** — preserve the original in Trash and restore it on undo. Publication refuses concurrent arrivals; if publication fails, the original remains recoverable in Trash. The existing non-undoable atomic-exchange fallback remains when Trash is unsupported.
- **Restore** — undo re-trashes the actual restored destinations.
- **Compress** — undo trashes a newly created/Keep Both archive, or restores the identity-matched original after Replace, even when Trash contains same-path entries with identical timestamps. Archive replacement fails safely if the original cannot be preserved in Trash.

Permanent delete remains non-undoable by design.

## Visual evidence

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8e014f71-ca9e-46f6-bdd3-fc295ad64845

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e4cb184b-ac63-435c-acbd-d64a49da9338

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0a86577c-b9a1-483e-b89f-85d2c8ac604a

## How to test

1. Create a folder → Ctrl+Z → it lands in Trash.
2. Copy a file over a same-named file → Replace → Ctrl+Z → the original is restored.
3. Restore an item from Trash → Ctrl+Z → it returns to Trash.
4. Compress with a name collision → Keep Both → Ctrl+Z → only the new numbered archive is trashed.
5. Compress with a name collision → Replace → Ctrl+Z → the previous archive contents return.
6. Merge two same-named folders → destination-only files survive, shared files are replaced → Ctrl+Z after a copy merge restores the destination originals.
7. Shift+Delete still cannot be undone.

## Issue

Part of #1091
title: feat(operations): make create, replace, restore, and compress undoable

## Problem or use case

The Modified column always renders relative buckets ("5m ago", "Yesterday, 14:30", weekday/dated fallbacks). There is no way to see a stable absolute timestamp like `2026-09-17 14:30`. The bucketing also uses calendar days rather than elapsed time, so a file saved at 23:59 flips to "Yesterday, 23:59" the moment the clock passes 00:00, even though it is seconds old. Slightly-future mtimes (clock skew on network mounts, `cp -p` races) render as a raw ISO timestamp instead of "just now".

## Proposed solution

Add a **Modified date format** preference under Settings → Appearance → Date & time with three choices, each showing a live rendered example: Relative (default), ISO 8601 (`2026-09-17 14:30`), and Long (`September 17, 2026, 14:30`). Persist as `date_format` in preferences; open labels re-render live when it changes. Sub-hour recency uses elapsed time so it survives midnight, and timestamps within a minute of now (either direction) read "just now".

## Alternatives considered

Keep relative-only rendering (status quo), or follow the system locale's date format automatically — both give users no explicit control.

main (dev build)

body: ## Description Video, audio, and GIF previews always called `play()` as soon as they opened — no way to just browse a folder of media without playback and sound starting immediately, and no saved way to keep the pane paused until pressing play, matching the request in the issue. ## Description

`ui::theme::ThemeManager` was the single application-wide settings store, even though most of its call sites were not about themes. This separates the two responsibilities:

- `ui::preferences::PreferenceManager` now owns the `Preferences` schema, load/save/repair, change notification, widget bindings, and every preference getter/setter. `TextSize`, the binding registry, and the preference tests and fixtures move with it.
- `ui::theme::ThemeManager` owns the theme catalog, token/CSS application, custom-theme editing and previews, and Omarchy following. It reads preferences through `PreferenceManager` and applies shared CSS when theme selection, Omarchy following, text size, or element glow change. Theme-derived bindings use the new `ThemeManager::bind_theme_preference`.

The theme singleton is now held for the process lifetime so its appearance observer survives; previously the manager applied CSS directly from its own setters. `settings.toml` is unchanged, and no behavior or settings UI changes.

## Visual evidence

1. Change **Settings → Appearance → Text** size and **Element glow**, or use **Ctrl++/Ctrl+−/Ctrl+0**.
2. Change prefs from a second window and from a browser context menu (theme, density, sorting, hidden files).
3. Switch **Follow Omarchy** on and off while an Omarchy theme is available.

issues.body:
## Problem or use case

`ui::theme::ThemeManager` is the single application-wide settings store: it owns the serialized `Preferences` schema, persistence, change notifications, browser/sidebar/media preferences, and folder customization. Only a minority of its 400+ call sites are actually about themes. The historical name makes every non-theme settings consumer depend on a theme module, and the module mixes two responsibilities:

- preference storage, persistence, and change notification
- theme catalog, CSS/token application, custom themes, and Omarchy following

## Proposed solution

Split the two responsibilities and rename the general-purpose store:

- `ui::preferences::PreferenceManager` owns the `Preferences` schema, load/save/repair, change notifications, widget bindings, and all preference getters/setters.
- `ui::theme::ThemeManager` owns the theme catalog, token/CSS application, custom theme editing, previews, and Omarchy following. It reads preferences through the `PreferenceManager` and re-applies shared CSS when appearance preferences (theme selection, Omarchy following, text size, element glow) change.
- Move `TextSize`, the preferences binding registry, and the preference tests to the preferences module.
- Update `docs/preferences.md`.

This is a behavior-preserving refactor; no settings.toml schema change.

### Alternatives considered

- Rename only, without separating responsibilities: leaves the theme module owning browser and persistence behavior.
- Keep `element_glow`/`text_size` setters on `ThemeManager`: keeps two writers of the preferences file instead of one.

### Additional context

Follow-up to the discussion that the store is not theme-specific. All work lands in one PR.

author: JoeJoeflyn
body:
## Description

Double-clicking a List-view column resize handle was a no-op: `register_list_column_cell` applies the column's fixed `width_request` to every registered cell, so `measure()` inside `max_child_natural_width` echoed the current width back, and all row/heading labels cap natural width at one character via `max_width_chars(1)`. The autofit could therefore never change the width.

This measures each registered cell with both constraints lifted (`list_cell_content_width` clears the cell's `width_request` and descendant labels' `max_width_chars`, measures, then restores them), so double-click now expands the column to fit its widest content — matching the Miller-columns behavior added in #114. The same code path serves the FileChooser dialog, which is fixed identically.

Also includes a separate `style:` commit applying rustfmt to files that drifted on main.

## Visual evidence

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cb3e8a9d-6094-46a7-8c98-0d966db24448

**Pending — needs owner upload.** `gh` cannot attach images; please drag these into the editor:

- `target/pr-captures/autofit-before.png` — Name column manually narrowed, long filename ellipsized
- `target/pr-captures/autofit-after.png` — after double-click on the resize handle: column expanded, full filename visible

## How to test

1. Switch to List view (Ctrl+3) in a folder containing a file with a long name
2. Drag the Name column's resize handle left to narrow it (or leave at default with a long name)
3. Double-click the resize strip at the right edge of the column header

**Expected result:** the column expands to fit its widest entry. Works the same in the FileChooser dialog's list view.

## Related issue

Closes #1115

### Strata version

0.17.0 (source build at cb49684c)

### Installation method

Built from source

### Linux distribution and desktop environment

Arch Linux, Hyprland (Wayland)

### What happened?

In List view, double-clicking a column's resize handle is supposed to autofit the column to its contents (feature added in #114), but nothing happens: the column keeps its current width and long filenames stay truncated. This affects both the main window and the FileChooser dialog, which share the same list-view code.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Switch to List view (Ctrl+3 or Appearance → List)
2. Open a folder containing a file whose name is wider than the Name column
3. Double-click the resize strip at the right edge of the Name column header
4. Observe the column width does not change

### Expected behavior

The column expands to fit its widest content, matching Finder/Explorer autofit behavior, as the Miller-columns mode already does.

### Root cause

`register_list_column_cell` applies `set_width_request()` with the current column width to every registered cell, so `measure()` inside `max_child_natural_width()` echoes the existing width back. Additionally every row and heading label sets `max_width_chars(1)`, capping measured natural width at one character. The autofit can therefore never change the width — it is a no-op that at best clamps to `LIST_COLUMN_MIN_WIDTHS`.

## Description

Fixes several misleading or missing trash/restore visuals reported in #1118:

- **Restore icon:** Restore context-menu items and the restore confirmation dialog showed a folder glyph identical to "Move to…". Both now use a bundled Lucide `undo-2` icon.
- **Trash fill level:** The sidebar Trash icon was static. It now reflects the probed item count — outline (empty/unknown), low fill (1–4), half fill with a crest (5–14), solid bin with mound (15+). Count is enumerated capped at 32 items.
- **Lid animation:** The sidebar trash lid flips open during delete and restore flights and closes when they finish, with an open variant per fill level.

- **Release animation:** Restoring while viewing Trash animated icons out of the sidebar button toward disappearing rows — backwards. Restored items now lift off their rows and launch upward (coil, banked launch, shockwave/beam/spark burst) since the destination folder is not visible. The trash-to-row flight still plays when restored rows materialize in a normal folder, including the Ctrl+Z path which now animates via a post-restore retry.
- **Ordering:** The restore animation played before the confirmation modal. It now runs only after the modal is accepted; cancelling animates nothing.

author: JoeJoeflyn
body:
## Description

Adds Finder-style redo for every undoable file operation. Undo keeps a process-wide history stack shared across windows; this adds a parallel redo stack fed by completed undos, so **Ctrl+Shift+Z** (and **Ctrl+Y**) re-applies what was just reverted:

- **Trash** → re-trashes the restored locations
- **Move** → replays the transfer with swapped endpoints, through the same collision dialog as undo
- **Copy** → restores the trashed copies from Trash
- **Rename** → replays the rename with swapped endpoints
- **Put Back** → rides on the `UndoEntry::Copy` entries restore already records, so undoing a Put Back (re-trash) can itself be redone

Two correctness rules:

- **Invalidation** — any new forward operation clears the redo stack (`push_pending_undo`), matching Finder.
- **Partial replay** — undo/redo can half-complete on conflicts. A `completed` bucket on each pending entry accumulates only items that actually applied, so a partial undo offers a redo for just the reverted portion, and a partial redo regenerates the matching undo subset. Failed operations push nothing — a failed rename undo, for example, offers no redo.

Undo and redo share one replay core (`replay_move`, `replay_rename`, `replay_entry_locations`, `resolve_replay_collisions`, `finish_claimed_replay`) parameterized by direction rather than duplicated per direction. Replays reuse the existing provider operations (`undo_move`, `undo_rename`, `undo_copy`, `restore`) — no new provider API.

Merge/copy-overwrite undos deliberately offer no redo: a merge undo mixes deletions and restores that no single replay operation can re-apply.

## Visual evidence

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9890f0ed-2ffa-4f43-85d5-25b43210c507

- `target/pr-captures/redo-1-restored.png` — after Ctrl+Z: `todo.txt` put back in the listing
- `target/pr-captures/redo-2-retrashed.png` — after Ctrl+Shift+Z: `todo.txt` re-trashed, listing back to four items

## How to test

1. Trash a file (Delete), press **Ctrl+Z** — the file is put back; press **Ctrl+Shift+Z** — it is trashed again
2. Cut+paste a file to another folder, Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+Shift+Z — moves back, then forward again
3. Copy+paste, Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+Shift+Z — copy trashed, then restored
4. Rename (F2), Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+Shift+Z — old name, then new name again
5. Trash, Ctrl+Z, then **rename any other file**, Ctrl+Shift+Z — nothing happens: the new operation invalidated redo
6. Multi-select → cut+paste → Ctrl+Z → **Skip** on a conflict → Ctrl+Shift+Z redoes only the files that actually reverted

## Related issue

Closes #1117

issues.body:
### Problem or use case

Ctrl+Z undoes the latest reversible file operation (trash, move, copy, rename), but once an operation is undone there is no way to re-apply it. Finder and other file managers pair every undo with a redo (Cmd+Shift+Z), so users who undo a move or rename by mistake — or who undo to inspect state and want their operation back — currently have to redo the work manually.

### Proposed solution

Add a redo history mirroring the existing undo history:

- Ctrl+Shift+Z (and Ctrl+Y) re-applies the most recently undone operation.
- Redoable operations mirror the existing undoable set:
  - Redo Move — move items to the destination again.
  - Redo Rename — re-apply the new name.
  - Redo Trash — re-trash items at the location restore placed them.
  - Redo Copy — re-copy the originals to the destination.
- Restoring items from trash (Put Back) becomes undoable/redoable: undoing a Put Back re-trashes the items, and redoing re-restores them.
- Standard redo semantics: performing any new operation clears the redo stack, and a partially-completed undo only makes the completed portion redoable.

### Alternatives considered

- Re-doing the operation manually (re-drag, re-rename): works but loses the batch and destination context the undo entry already holds.
- A persistent action journal instead of a redo stack: unnecessary complexity for parity with platform conventions.

### Additional context

Builds on the undo machinery from #298, #390, and #1059.
issues.title: feat(operations): redo undone file operations with Ctrl+Shift+Z

title: feat(browser): redo file operations with Ctrl+Shift+Z

author: pdwaldrop
body:
## Description

Copying a directory onto a FAT/exFAT/vFAT destination (a USB stick, most commonly) failed outright with "Invalid filename" as soon as any nested entry's name contained a character those drivers reject (`" * / : < > ? \ |`, or a control character) — and since the transfer stages into a temporary sibling directory first, the whole staged copy was discarded on that one failure, even after a large amount had already been written. Pasting a single file with such a name failed the same way.

Mirrors GNOME Files' behavior: when the destination reports a FAT-family filesystem type (checked once per transfer against the parsed mount table, not per file), rejected characters are replaced with `_` and trailing dots/spaces are trimmed (the drivers strip these anyway). Sibling names that collapse to the same result after sanitizing get a numbered suffix (`name (1).ext`) instead of one silently overwriting the other. This applies to the top-level paste target and every nested copy path: the recursive copy itself, move's cross-filesystem `WouldRecurse` fallback, replace, and merge.

Non-FAT destinations are completely unaffected — verified with a dedicated regression test.

## Visual evidence

N/A — this only changes filename handling during file transfers; there is no UI-visible change.

## How to test

1. Create a folder containing a file with a FAT-invalid name, e.g. `mkdir demo && touch 'demo/a?b:c.txt' demo/ok.txt`.
2. Mount an exFAT (or vfat) test volume, e.g. `truncate -s 256M fat.img && mkfs.exfat fat.img && udisksctl loop-setup -f fat.img`.
3. In Strata, copy `demo` and paste it onto the mounted volume.

**Expected result:** the folder is copied in full; `a?b:c.txt` lands as `a_b_c.txt` instead of the whole transfer failing and being discarded. Pasting a single file with an invalid name onto the same volume also succeeds, sanitized the same way.

*Local validation note: this machine has no docker/podman set up, so the pinned `./scripts/quality.sh` container runner wasn't available — used plain host `cargo fmt --all --check` / `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` instead (both clean), plus `./scripts/test-headless.py` for the full `adapters::local_operations::` and `adapters::volume::` suites (all passing; two pre-existing, unrelated archive-compression test failures were confirmed present on unmodified `main` too, via `git stash`, before ruling them out as caused by this change).*

## Related issue

Closes #1123

issues.body:
### Strata version

0.18.0

### Installation method

Other

### Linux distribution and desktop environment

Omarchy 4.0.4 (Arch Linux), Hyprland 0.56.2

### What happened?

Copying a folder to an exFAT USB stick fails with **"Invalid filename"** when any file inside it has a name containing a character FAT/exFAT does not allow (`" * / : < > ? \ |` or a control character). Nothing is left on the stick: Strata writes the whole tree into a staged `.strata-replacement-*` directory first, then discards it all when the one bad name fails. In my case ~300 MB were written and then removed because of one file deep inside the tree, a LibreOffice icon cache entry named `sc_macroorganizer?tabid:short=1.png`.

GNOME Files copies the same folder to the same stick without errors, because it replaces the rejected characters with `_` when the destination is a FAT-family filesystem.

Pasting a single file whose name contains one of these characters also fails.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a folder containing a file with a FAT-invalid name, e.g. `mkdir demo && touch 'demo/a?b:c.txt' demo/ok.txt`.
2. Mount an exFAT (or vfat) formatted USB stick. No hardware needed: `truncate -s 256M fat.img && mkfs.exfat fat.img && udisksctl loop-setup -f fat.img`.
3. In Strata, copy `demo` and paste it onto the stick.
4. Observe: "Invalid filename", and `demo` does not exist on the stick.

### Expected behavior

The folder is copied, and names the destination filesystem cannot store are adjusted (e.g. `a?b:c.txt` → `a_b_c.txt`), matching GNOME Files. At minimum, one unrepresentable name should not discard everything that was already copied successfully.

### Screenshots or video

_No response_

### Relevant logs

```shell
$ cp 'a?b:c.png' /run/media/$USER/USB/
cp: cannot create regular file '/run/media/$USER/USB/a?b:c.png': Invalid argument
```

### Additional context

Root cause: in `src/adapters/local_operations.rs`, `copy_recursively_local` and `copy_recursively_with_progress` create every child with `target.child(&child_name)`, using the source name verbatim, and the paste loop does the same for top-level items. The vfat/exfat kernel drivers reject those names with `EINVAL`, and `copy_new_recursively_with_progress` then discards the staged directory.

A possible fix, mirroring GNOME Files: query `filesystem::type` of the destination once per transfer (GIO reports `msdos`/`vfat`/`exfat`). When it is FAT-family, map each child name by replacing rejected characters with `_` and dropping trailing dots and spaces, which the drivers strip anyway. A mapped name that collides with a sibling in the same source directory should get a numbered suffix, so that one entry never silently overwrites another in the staged copy. `WouldRecurse` moves go through the same copy path, so they get the fix too.

The diagnosis was done with help from an AI coding assistant.

issues.body:
### Problem or use case

Strata always hides GTK title buttons (`HeaderBar::set_show_title_buttons(false)`) and always shows a custom close control in the in-app header. There is no minimize or maximize control, and close cannot be turned off.

That mix does not fit both tiling window managers and ordinary stacking desktops:

- On a TWM (i3, Sway, Hyprland, and similar), window management is the compositor's job. In-app close/minimize/maximize are redundant or wrong (minimize/maximize especially).
- On a normal window manager (GNOME, KDE, XFCE, and similar), users expect close, minimize, and maximize to be available on the window.

Visibility of those three buttons should be a user choice, not a single hard-coded layout.

### Proposed solution

Add a saved preference that controls whether the close, minimize, and maximize buttons are shown. Apply it at window construction and live, through the existing preference-binding path; Settings should only edit the preference.

Tiling WM users should be able to hide some or all of the buttons. Stacking WM users should be able to show the conventional three. Keep today's close-only header as the default unless a better default is chosen in implementation.

This is about button visibility on Strata's header, not the outer window frame.

### Alternatives considered

- Leave the current close-only header: works on some TWMs, but stacking desktops never get minimize/maximize and cannot hide close.
- Always restore GTK title buttons: better for some stacking WMs, worse for TWMs that already decorate or keybind those actions.
- Detect the window manager and pick a layout automatically: brittle, and still needs an override for mixed setups.
- Fold this into #1098: that ticket is the outer border/chrome, and it explicitly keeps the in-app header and close control.

### Visual examples

N/A — no mockup; compare a TWM session (often no in-app window buttons) with a stacking desktop that expects close/minimize/maximize.

### Strata version

N/A — current main header construction (custom `HeaderBar` plus always-on close). Recheck against current main before implementation.

### Additional context

Searched open and closed lgse/strata issues for close button, minimize, maximize, window controls, titlebar buttons, CSD buttons, TWM, window manager decorations, and hide window buttons. No existing ticket asks to configure those three buttons' visibility.

Related but distinct:

- #1098: drop outer window borders/chrome on non-Hyprland desktops; keep Strata's header and close control.
- #156: close-button padding, not visibility.
- #469 / #497: XFCE toolbar and pane icon scale.
- #577 / #579: compact the in-app top bar height.

Filed from the feature-request form. No P-band; triage can band it later.

issues.body:
### Problem or use case

Selecting several files and folders and opening Properties should answer two questions that the listing itself does not: how many nested items those folders contain, and how much disk the whole selection occupies.

Today Properties is single-item only (Alt+Enter uses the focused entry; the multi-item context menu has no Properties action). Single-folder Properties already shows recursive SIZE and CONTAINS. The footer reports a selection breakdown such as `1 folder, 2 files selected (6 B)`, but that size is files only — folder contents are not counted. There is no one place to inspect a mixed selection's nested item count and total size.

### Proposed solution

When two or more items are selected, Properties (Alt+Enter and the context menu) should open for the whole selection and at least show:

- Nested item count: selected files plus recursive contents of selected folders (files and folders), with a calculating state for large trees
- Total size: selected file sizes plus recursive folder contents, using the same bounded directory summary Properties already uses for a single folder, including a lower-bound / truncated indicator when the walk stops early

A compact summary is enough for a first version (for example `3 items selected` plus CONTAINS and SIZE). Permissions, rename, and media metadata can stay single-item-only.

### Alternatives considered

- Footer counts from #1033: already show how many files and folders are selected, but they exclude nested folder contents and are not a Properties inspect.
- Preview-pane multi-select summary (#940): closed as superseded by the footer; it was a different surface and never shipped as Properties.
- Open Properties on each selected folder: slow, and it does not produce one combined total.
- Files-only size on the selection: cheaper, but it understates folders the same way the footer already does.

### Visual examples

N/A — no mockup; single-item folder Properties (SIZE + CONTAINS) is the reference layout.

### Strata version

0.18.0 (current `main` source). Confirmed by inspection: `show_focused_properties` takes one focused entry; the multi-item context menu omits Properties; footer tooltip states folder contents are not counted.

### Additional context

Related but not the same:

- #604 / #556 — CONTAINS and recursive SIZE for a **single** folder
- #1033 — footer item/selection counts (files-only size)
- #940 — preview auto-summary for multi-select (closed; superseded by #1034)
- #900 — recursive count and size on permanent-delete / Empty Trash confirms, not Properties
- #937 — optional checkboxes to **make** a multi-selection, not inspect one

Feature request only; no implementation in this filing.

N/A — no crash or terminal error.

`src/ui/browser.rs` builds `location_entry` with placeholder `Enter an absolute path` and tooltip `Location (Ctrl+L)`, and the icon-only confirm/cancel with tooltips `Navigate (Enter)` and `Cancel (Escape)`. issues.body:
## Description

The **thumbnail size slider** in **Icons view** (drag the "px" control in the Icons toolbar) is not remembered across app restarts. Setting it to e.g. 95 px works for the session, but relaunching Strata resets the grid to the default 64 px.

## Expected behavior

Once set, the thumbnail size stays at the chosen value across restarts (and ideally is stored per-preference along with the other persisted browser/view settings).

## Actual behavior

Every launch begins at the hardcoded default of 64 px; the slider change is only session-local.

## Root cause (from a quick look at the source)

In `src/ui/browser_modes.rs`, the value lives purely in memory and is never written to a saved setting:

- `const DEFAULT_ICONS_THUMBNAIL_SIZE: i32 = 64;`
- `icons_thumbnail_size: Rc<Cell<i32>>` is seeded to `DEFAULT_ICONS_THUMBNAIL_SIZE` when the browser is built;
- the Icons controls write it back with `thumbnail_size_for_change.set(size)` (slider `value-changed`);
- nothing persists it — no key exists in the saved settings/settings.toml, and the thumbnail-generation path (`src/ui/thumbnail.rs`) always keys the shared cache at `CANONICAL_MAX_EDGE` (256 px), so the cache is unaffected.

Because the size is not one of the persisted browser preferences, the grid re-renders at 64 px on each new session.

## Suggested approach

Persist the Icons thumbnail size the same way other per-view settings are saved (e.g. alongside the existing persisted per-view state / settings plumbing), and restore it when the browser window is rebuilt. A small clamp on load (e.g. 16–256) would mirror the runtime `clamp(16, 256)` already used by the thumbnail request code.

## Notes

- The feature request is independent of thumbnail *cache* behavior — the shared freedesktop thumbnail cache (`~/.cache/thumbnails/large`, canonical 256 px, mtime-validated) already works correctly and is display-size-agnostic; changing the slider does not invalidate it.
- Related prior work: #888 deliberately made several Preview/sizing values "session-local" with "no new saved settings"; this request is specifically about the Icons thumbnail/zoom control crossing to persisted state.

Permanent delete and Empty Trash cannot be undone. Before confirming, it should be obvious how many files will be destroyed and how much disk they occupy. author: JoeJoeflyn
body:
## Description

Opening an archive extracts it into a new subfolder named after the archive. That folder is reserved with `create_dir` before the operation is dispatched, so the extractor's failure cleanup — which only removes destinations it created itself — never applied to it. When extraction then fails (for example because the archive is malformed), an empty `<archive-name>/` folder was left behind. Latest `main` sanitizes `../` members rather than failing on them; they are no longer a valid failure fixture.

`ExtractRequest` now carries `created_destination`, letting a caller that already reserved the destination mark it operation-created so the existing empty-folder cleanup applies. Only the extract-to-subfolder path sets the flag: "Extract here", "Extract to…", and password retries keep their behavior, a folder that already existed is still never removed, and a folder containing extracted content is kept since the cleanup only removes empty destinations.

## Visual evidence

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/141f060c-33de-470e-bf4c-ef7d7f49265c

## How to test

1. Create a malformed archive: `printf "not an archive" > broken.zip`.
2. Open/activate `broken.zip` in the browser — an extraction error appears.
3. Dismiss the error and inspect the folder.

**Expected result:** no empty `broken/` folder remains beside the archive. A normal archive still extracts into its subfolder, and an archive that wrote files before failing keeps its folder with the partial content.

## Related issue

Closes #1135

issues.body:
## Strata version
v0.19.0 (reproduced on current main, source build)

## Installation method
Source build; not install-method specific (logic is in the archive operation path)

## Environment
Linux, GTK — platform-independent

## Steps to reproduce
1. Create a ZIP containing a member with an unsafe path, e.g. `../outside` (zip slip)
2. Activate the archive in the browser (open/double-click), which extracts to a new subfolder named after the archive
3. The extraction correctly fails: a popup reports the archive is unsafe ("Refusing unsafe archive path")

## Expected behavior
The destination folder created for the extraction is removed when nothing was extracted, matching the cleanup added in #827 for extractor-created destinations.

## Actual behavior
An empty folder named after the archive (e.g. `unsafe/`) is left behind next to the archive.

## Root cause
`extract_entry_to_subfolder` reserves the destination with `fs::create_dir` before dispatching (`src/ui/browser/archive.rs`), so `local_operations::archive::extract` sees `dest_dir.exists()` and clears `created_dest`. The failure/cancel cleanup only runs for destinations the extractor itself created, so the caller-created empty folder survives.

## Notes
- "Extract here" and "Extract to…" are unaffected: their destinations either pre-exist or are created by the extractor itself.
- Fix: let `ExtractRequest` declare the destination was created for the operation so the existing empty-folder cleanup applies.

issues.body:
### Strata version

v0.19.0 (main @ 984706cd)

### Installation method

GitHub release archive

### Linux distribution and desktop environment

Arch Linux, Hyprland (Omarchy) — Strata configured as the `org.freedesktop.impl.portal.FileChooser` backend

### What happened?

When the Strata chooser opens for a SaveFile/SaveFiles portal request, the file list auto-selects the first entry on load (the "load cursor" used for keyboard focus). That implicit selection is treated as an explicit folder selection, so accepting the dialog writes the file into `<shown directory>/<first sorted subfolder>/` instead of the shown directory.

The calling application then records the returned directory (e.g. Chromium's `savefile.default_directory`), so every subsequent save dialog opens inside the wrong folder. Observed behavior: downloads land in a seemingly random folder inside Downloads, and each new save dialog opens at that folder, drifting further on repeat saves.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Configure Strata as the FileChooser portal backend and keep the default `folders_first` sorting.
2. Ensure the save dialog's initial directory contains at least one folder (e.g. `~/Downloads`).
3. From a portal-aware app (e.g. Brave/Chromium: right-click a link → "Save link as…"), open the save dialog.
4. Accept immediately without selecting anything.

### Expected behavior

The file is saved into the directory currently displayed by the dialog. Only an explicit user selection should redirect the destination. (Compare the Open-directory path and `paste_destination`, which both exclude the load cursor.)

### Screenshots or video

N/A — behavioral defect; reproducible via the steps above and the included regression test.

### Relevant logs

### Additional context

Root cause: `Browser::navigate` calls `select_first_on_load(0)`; when the listing finishes, the first visible entry is auto-selected and flagged `load_cursor` (`src/app/navigation.rs`). `ChooserState::selected_folder()` reads `selected_entries()` without the `selection_is_load_cursor()` guard, so the save destination silently becomes the first sorted folder. With `folders_first` (default on) any directory containing a folder is affected.

author: JoeJoeflyn
body:
## Description

The window-level Ctrl+wheel text zoom controller (from #1069) runs in capture phase with `EventControllerScrollFlags::DISCRETE`. GTK's discrete mode masks the horizontal axis and reports sub-threshold smooth deltas as handled while accumulating toward a step — so every touchpad scroll event was consumed at the window before descendant scrolled windows could see it. Two-finger horizontal scrolling in the browser columns never reached the column-strip controller added in #1125, and vertical touchpad scrolling was degraded to discrete chunks.

This drops `DISCRETE` and accumulates deltas manually in a `TextZoomScroll` helper, gated on Ctrl zoom actually being applicable (Ctrl held, no Alt/Super, non-zero delta, pointer outside PDF scroll containers). Pending state resets on modifier loss, direction reversal, or unit change. Ordinary smooth input returns `Propagation::Proceed` and flows to descendants; Ctrl+wheel still zooms text size in whole steps.

## Visual evidence

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ed7a5d12-79b5-41ed-8151-c43f00877e75

## How to test

1. Open a deep path so the Miller columns overflow horizontally
2. Two-finger swipe horizontally over the columns

**Expected result:** the column strip scrolls horizontally. Vertical touchpad scrolling remains smooth, and Ctrl+wheel still steps text size.

## Related issue

Fixes #1124

author: ogarza
body:
## Description

Reserve a font-sized metadata line in Icons cards before details arrive, and truncate long details within the existing caption width. File sizes, dimensions and durations no longer change cell measurements.

Retry admission after the final scroll allocation, and reserve metadata-queue capacity for the current viewport. Fast scrolling previously filled the 1,024-entry backlog with old requests, silently dropping visible files even though their cached thumbnails displayed. Visible requests now displace queued offscreen work without cancelling active jobs or increasing the limit.

Covers final-allocation wake-up, saturated admission, a 5,000-image fling with warm thumbnails, and source dimensions across multiple disk-cache batches. Separate renderer/compositor trails remain unverified.

Icons now shares the List/Columns rename-completion reveal path: focus the renamed file or folder, reveal it after sorting if necessary, and preserve the viewport when it remains visible. Deliberate scrolling still cancels automatic reveal. Renaming an unchanged file also retains its loaded thumbnail and metadata instead of decoding them again; changed size, modification time, or extension still invalidates reuse.

Large scrollbar jumps and Page Up/Down no longer scan every tracked icon for each recycled cell. Live thumbnail/icon slots use direct lookups and release their tracking on disposal, preserving customization and rename reuse.

## Visual evidence

**Pending owner upload:** sanitized before/after Icons captures are retained locally; no authenticated attachment-upload route is available here. Upload them through GitHub's editor and embed the resulting attachment URLs. The captures show the preserved settled appearance, not metadata-arrival timing; paths and captions are in the validation handoff on #1146.

Rename follow-up: isolated before/after captures are ready, pending owner upload (paths and captions in the follow-up comment). They show the preserved thumbnail and dimensions; the brief old fallback flash was not caught by the screenshot sampling.

## How to test

1. Open a large directory of images/audio/video in Icons view. Watch details fill at normal and enlarged text sizes; try compact and airy density.
2. Reopen it with thumbnails cached, flick rapidly through several thousand entries, then stop without another input. Check dimensions on every visible row, not just the first batch. Also try inline rename after details have filled.

3. In Icons, rename a visible file or folder without changing its sort position, then rename it so it sorts offscreen. For an image with loaded dimensions, rename only its basename and check that its thumbnail and details remain present.

4. In an Icons directory with 100,000 images, drag the scrollbar thumb rapidly and repeat Page Up/Down. Check that the destination fills and live icon customizations still follow recycled cells.

**Expected result:** details fill without moving the grid; newly visible thumbnails and metadata resume on their own. Renamed items keep keyboard focus and scroll into view only when needed.

## Related issue

Closes #1146

author: l0gicgate
body:
## Description

Move the shared quality/E2E environment from Ubuntu GTK 4.14 to a signed, dated Arch snapshot with GTK 4.22.5. Build a matching-source, test-image-only GTK accessibility-coordinate patch and verify its loaded path, checksum, and rendered bounds during image construction.

Repair the GTK 4.22 menu lifecycle, keyboard anchoring, focus restoration, modified-drag behavior, and submenu Left/Right navigation exposed by the upgraded toolkit. Re-enable the five ignored Rust menu tests and all 256 quarantined E2E cases, remove the quarantine machinery, and refresh the reviewed GTK 4.22 visual baselines. Auto worker selection now also respects cgroup task limits so Arch toolkit/media threads cannot exhaust the container.

Keep initial keyboard focus on the first available context-menu action as MIME lookup completes, without letting a stationary pointer take ownership. Replace the overlapping submenu return handlers with native navigation that clears GTK's open-submenu state, so Left followed by Up/Down stays in the parent menu.

Keep inline rename/create text aligned to its presentation: centered in Icons, left-aligned in List and Miller Columns, and mode-aware in filtered results and chooser views. Filtered Properties → Rename now edits the displayed result inline instead of opening a rename dialog. Shared modal viewports constrain oversized dialogs to the available window, with responsive Properties actions at large text scales. Use the canonical Lucide trash icon everywhere, removing the fill-level and open-lid variants and their count-based switching logic.

Replace the separate single-pane filtered-results view with a stable shared collection configurable for row or icon presentation, single or multiple selection, activation, focus, and selection callbacks. Icons now filters into an icon grid, List uses rows, Columns retains its native collection, and file choosers consume the same result behavior. Progressive updates preserve result identity, selection, focus, thumbnails, inline rename, drag/drop, quick preview, and real recursive locations for actions such as Open file location.

Resolve the eight guided-test findings: hide files in folder-only choosers, keep recursive queries/results consistent with file-type filters, retain matching renamed results (including shared searches and undo), remove redundant filename banners and option tooltips, contain keyboard background menus within their window, and scale dialog bezels with the text while filling the heading height. Retry thumbnail admission after newly mapped slots are allocated, so renamed image results render without a manual refresh.

## Visual evidence

Pending owner upload through the GitHub editor. Additional guided-fix before/after captures and exact paths are listed in the [consolidated results](https://github.com/lgse/strata/pull/1155#issuecomment-5755238870); they are not attached yet. The [focused retest and final bezel/thumbnail follow-up](https://github.com/lgse/strata/pull/1155#issuecomment-5755998449) contains the newer before/after capture inventory and supersedes the earlier center-only bezel evidence. Sanitized captures are retained locally at:

- `target/issue-1154-gtk-4.14-baselines.png` — before, Ubuntu/GTK 4.14 baseline contact sheet.
- `target/issue-1154-gtk-4.22-baselines.png` — after, Arch/GTK 4.22 baseline contact sheet.
- `target/pr-1155-evidence/centered-filtered-rename.png` — centered inline rename in filtered Icons results.
- `target/pr-1155-evidence/list-filtered-rename-left.png` — left-aligned inline rename in filtered List results.
- `target/pr-1155-evidence/scaled-properties-dialog.png` — 24 px text (about 1.85×) in a 520×420 window.
- `target/pr-1155-evidence/default-lucide-trash.png` — canonical Lucide trash icon in the sidebar.
- `target/pr-1155-menu-focus-evidence/before-initial-focus.png` / `after-initial-focus.png` — Shift+F10 with two files: Actions incorrectly focused before; Open focused after.
- `target/pr-1155-menu-focus-evidence/before-parent-navigation.png` / `after-parent-navigation.png` — Right, Down, Left, Down: focus escapes to the window before; Cut in the parent menu is focused after.

## How to test

1. Build the deliberate environment update with `STRATA_CONTAINER_ENGINE=podman python3 scripts/e2e_base.py build`.
2. With submenu actions installed, select multiple files sharing a default application and press Shift+F10. Confirm Open receives initial focus. Navigate to Actions, press Right, move down inside it, then press Left and Down: Cut should receive focus in the parent. Reopen with Right, Space, and Enter; verify both keyboard activation and pointer hovering still work in Columns, Icons, and List.
3. Filter for a nested result in Columns, Icons, and List. Confirm each mode keeps its normal presentation and navigation, Quick Preview targets the result, and its menu offers Open file location.
4. Repeat filtering in an open/save chooser and confirm selection, filename, preview, and acceptance follow the displayed result.
5. Open Properties for a filtered result, choose Rename, and confirm the mode-aligned inline editor appears on that result.
6. Exercise rename/create in Columns, Icons, List, and a file chooser; increase text size to 1.6× or above and open Properties in a small window.
7. Add and remove Trash contents and confirm the sidebar keeps the same canonical Lucide trash icon.

8. In single- and multiple-folder choosers, confirm regular files are hidden in normal and recursive listings. Switch Text→Images→Text while a query is active in each view; the query should remain and only eligible files should be returned.
9. Rename a nested matching result to another matching name, then use Open file location. Confirm the renamed file remains searchable at its real parent and unrelated duplicates are unchanged. For images, verify the thumbnail renders again without refreshing in all three views.
10. With no files selected, press Shift+F10 in each view and verify the menu stays inside the window. At 24px text, inspect and cancel a permanent-delete confirmation; its bezel should be at least as tall as the title/subtitle block, with proportional space around its icon.

**Expected result:**

The image reports GTK 4.22.5 and rejects an unexpected GTK path/checksum or incorrect accessible coordinates. Native menus retain focus and dispatch correctly; filtering preserves each mode's presentation and shared interactions across the browser and chooser; recursive actions target the real file location; inline editors use the appropriate alignment without modal rename fallbacks; dialogs remain reachable within the window at large text scales; and Trash always uses one Lucide icon.

## Related issue

Closes #1154

issues.body:
### Strata version
PR #1085, v0.19.0, source commit `0c8eeaa312ca67b085494ccb3c370f6afbb7b49c`.

### Installation method
Built from source.

### Linux distribution and desktop environment
Canonical Ubuntu 24.04 container; GTK 4.14.5; Rust 1.98.1; private Xvfb and D-Bus/AT-SPI. No desktop session required. Separate experimental Arch/GTK 4.24.0 / GLib 2.90.0 runs are not the restored CI baseline.

### What happened?
The native GtkPopoverMenu migration in #1085 regressed menu lifecycle, focus and action dispatch. CI run [35483970576](https://github.com/lgse/strata/actions/runs/35483970576) reports three failed Rust cases and 104 failed parameterized E2E cases across the three shards. Symptoms include timeouts after menu actions, incorrect keyboard focus, and actual GTK popup-layout crashes. These are not all accessibility-coordinate errors.

The owner explicitly requested restoring the previous image/CI configuration, temporarily disabling confirmed failing tests, and tracking repairs here so the large feature PR can proceed. Native GTK submenus remain; skips do not establish that the behavior is safe or fixed. Host GTK/GLib upgrades are not reverted. The separate newer-GTK accessibility-coordinate investigation is preserved separately from these baseline failures.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Check out the failing source revision above.
2. Run the canonical pinned container with a private display/bus:
   `STRATA_CONTAINER_ENGINE=podman ./scripts/e2e.sh tests/e2e/scenarios/test_dialogs_and_menus.py -k 'file_properties or enter_submits_compress_and_extract_to_dialogs or enter_submits_the_copy_to_dialog' -n 0`.
3. Compress a file from its context menu, submit with Enter, then open the generated archive's context menu. Also exercise Properties, Copy to, repeated menu replacement/dismissal, and keyboard menu focus.
4. For each listed Rust case, use `./scripts/test-headless.py <fully-qualified-test-name>` on this revision. After quarantine lands, add `--ignored` to exercise an ignored Rust case; E2E will provide `--run-quarantined` for opt-in reproduction.

### Expected behavior
Native menus preserve selection/focus, dispatch exactly once, close cleanly, reopen on other entries, and do not crash or block subsequent dialogs/input. All quarantined regressions are restored to the normal required suites once fixed.

### Screenshots or video
N/A for the quarantine itself (test configuration only). Failure artifacts are attached to the linked CI run; retain sanitized diagnostic text rather than requesting core dumps.

### Relevant logs
- Rust focus assertion: expected GtkListItemWidget, actual GtkModelButton after Escape.
- Rust Open file location fixture: timed out waiting for filtered results.
- GTK 4.14 crash signature observed during local reproductions: `gdk_surface_request_motion(NULL)` from `gtk_popover_native_layout` / `maybe_request_motion_event`.
- CI E2E shard results: 35 failed/229 passed; 32 failed/226 passed; 37 failed/221 passed.

### Additional context
Repair in scoped groups rather than repeatedly running the whole suite. Do not weaken assertions or remove the native-menu requirement. Re-enable exact cases when their original behavior is verified. Full required CI must eventually pass with these quarantines removed.

- `ui::browser::context_menu::tests::keyboard::context_menus_preserve_filtered_grouped_and_chooser_selections`

comments.body:
## GTK accessibility-coordinate investigation — patch handoff

**This is a separate problem from the GTK 4.14 popup crashes. It is not an explanation for every quarantined test.** The merged PR restored the original GTK 4.14.5 CI image. The newer-GTK investigation below used upstream GTK 4.24.0 / GLib 2.90.0, including signed Arch packages `gtk4 1:4.24.0-1` and `glib2 2.90.0-1`.

### Confirmed minimal reproduction

A GTK window contains a `GtkBox` with CSS `padding: 22px`, containing a `GtkEntry`. No Strata code is needed.

On GTK 4.24.0:

```text
GtkEntry accessible bounds relative to parent: x=0, y=0, width=456, height=34
GtkBox accessible bounds:                    x=0, y=0, width=500, height=300
Summed accessible origin:                    (0, 0)
Actual entry border bounds in the window:    (22, 22), 456 × 34
Actual entry content origin in the window:   (31, 23)
```

The border/content distinction matters: the extra `(9, 1)` is the entry's own CSS inset. The accessibility calculation loses the ancestor box's padding. The same reproduction on GTK 4.14.5 reports entry `(9, 1)` plus box `(22, 22)`, summing to `(31, 23)`—the content origin, rather than the new erroneous `(0, 0)`.

In Strata's action editor, the harness reported Description at `(219, 277)` while its rendered border began around `(242, 301)`. Clicking the reported center missed the field; subsequent typing remained in Name. Ordinary mouse use at the rendered position need not fail. Accessibility consumers relying on these coordinates can be affected too; this is not exclusively a test-harness bug.

### Relevant upstream code/change

- [GTK commit `17f244335092407e615b6ddca7cccd3f184b5118`](https://github.com/GNOME/gtk/commit/17f244335092407e615b6ddca7cccd3f184b5118), dated 2024-04-10: **“a11y: Simplify GtkWidget's GtkAccessible.get_bounds implementation.”** It replaced origins computed with `gtk_widget_compute_point()` with origins taken from `gtk_widget_compute_bounds()`.
- [`gtk_widget_accessible_get_bounds()` in GTK 4.24.0](https://github.com/GNOME/gtk/blob/4.24.0/gtk/gtkwidget.c).
- [`gtk_at_spi_translate_coordinates_from_accessible()`](https://github.com/GNOME/gtk/blob/4.24.0/gtk/a11y/gtkatspiutils.c) computes WINDOW coordinates by summing accessible-parent bounds.
- [`GetExtents` / `GetPosition` handlers](https://github.com/GNOME/gtk/blob/4.24.0/gtk/a11y/gtkatspicomponent.c) use that translation.

The mismatch is that child border bounds relative to a parent's **content** coordinates are summed as though each were relative to the parent's **border** origin. This loses padding/border translations across the ancestor chain. The source change and A/B reproduction strongly implicate this calculation; this was not a complete upstream bisection.

Source inspection found the same implementation in **4.16.13, 4.18.6, 4.20.4, and 4.22.4**. Those versions were not all runtime-tested, so they must not be advertised as tested good/bad baselines. There is no verified unaffected stable version between 4.14 and 4.24 from this investigation.

### Self-contained diagnostic

Save this as `coordinate_probe.py` on a machine/container with Python GI and GTK 4:

```python
import gi

gi.require_version("Gtk", "4.0")
from gi.repository import Gdk, GLib, Gtk

Gtk.init()
css = Gtk.CssProvider()
css.load_from_string(".padded { padding: 22px; }")
Gtk.StyleContext.add_provider_for_display(
    Gdk.Display.get_default(), css, Gtk.STYLE_PROVIDER_PRIORITY_APPLICATION
)
window = Gtk.Window(default_width=500, default_height=300)
box = Gtk.Box(orientation=Gtk.Orientation.VERTICAL)
box.add_css_class("padded")
entry = Gtk.Entry()
box.append(entry)
window.set_child(box)
loop = GLib.MainLoop()


def inspect():
    node = entry
    x = y = 0
    while node is not None:
        valid, nx, ny, width, height = Gtk.Accessible.get_bounds(node)
        print(type(node).__name__, valid, nx, ny, width, height)
        if valid:
            x += nx
            y += ny
        node = node.get_accessible_parent()
    valid, rect = entry.compute_bounds(window)
    print("summed accessibility origin:", x, y)
    print("actual window border bounds:", valid,
          rect.get_x(), rect.get_y(), rect.get_width(), rect.get_height())
    window.destroy()
    loop.quit()
    return GLib.SOURCE_REMOVE


window.present()
# A one-shot delay lets this diagnostic's window allocate; not a production fix.
GLib.timeout_add(100, inspect)
loop.run()
```

Run only on a private display/bus:

```bash
env -u DISPLAY -u WAYLAND_DISPLAY -u DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS -u AT_SPI_BUS_ADDRESS \
  GTK_A11Y=none NO_AT_BRIDGE=1 GIO_USE_VFS=local \
  GDK_BACKEND=x11 GSK_RENDERER=cairo \
  timeout 15s dbus-run-session -- xvfb-run -a python3 coordinate_probe.py
```

`GTK_A11Y=none` here intentionally avoids external accessibility services while directly inspecting the GTK Accessible bounds API used by AT-SPI. It is **not** an E2E setting or proposed accessibility-disabling workaround. A final fix must also be verified with a real private AT-SPI bus and pointer input.

### Candidate correction tested — not a validated package fix

A diagnostic-only GTK 4.24.0 build adjusted the successful `gtk_widget_accessible_get_bounds()` result before converting to integer coordinates:

```c
if (parent != NULL)
  {
    graphene_rect_t parent_bounds;
    if (gtk_widget_compute_bounds (parent, parent, &parent_bounds))
      {
        bounds.origin.x -= parent_bounds.origin.x;
        bounds.origin.y -= parent_bounds.origin.y;
      }
  }
```

This translates the child border bounds into the parent's border-origin coordinate system. **It changed the minimal reproduction's summed origin to `(22, 22)`, matching the actual border bounds.** That is the only established positive result. It is a candidate for review, not a recommendation to install this exact patch unchanged. Review nested padding/borders, CSS transforms, scrolling, fractional scaling/rounding, virtual/non-widget accessible parents, and popovers/native surfaces. The diagnostic build also disabled Vulkan, so it is not an equivalent replacement for the official full-featured Arch package.

**Important correction to the earlier experimental E2E result:** an attempted patched-library run reported 4 failed / 3 passed, but it passed the library through `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`. Strata's E2E `harness/environment.py::process_environment()` deliberately inherits only PATH; `Application.start()` builds the child's environment from that allowlist. Thus the patched-library override was not forwarded to the Strata child. Those results do **not** establish whether the candidate fixes the application tests. They must not be cited as a valid patched/unpatched comparison.

For the next attempt, install the candidate package **inside a disposable test image**, preserving the normal harness environment isolation. Verify `/proc/<strata-pid>/maps` and the loaded library's build ID/checksum before accepting any result. First rerun the action-editor click failure and the minimal AT-SPI reproduction; only then expand to affected cases. Do not compensate with hard-coded coordinate offsets, remove assertions, or pass desktop environment variables through the harness.

### Distinct popup-crash investigation

The older pinned GTK 4.14.5 failures included a real crash signature at `gdk_surface_request_motion(NULL)` from `gtk_popover_native_layout()` / `maybe_request_motion_event()`. That path uses the pointer-focused widget's native surface during popup layout. It is a lifecycle/surface issue, **not proven to be caused by the coordinate bug above**. Earlier experiments alternating retention, unparenting and unrealizing popovers did not produce a reliable fix. Keep that investigation separate and use an independent minimal popup lifecycle reproduction.

### Packaging and evidence

- The host currently has the **official, unpatched** GTK 4.24.0 / GLib 2.90.0 packages. No candidate accessibility patch was installed on the host.
- The merged CI image remains GTK 4.14.5; this newer-toolkit experiment was reverted from the PR.
- Any promoted fix should use reviewed, versioned packages and identical binaries in the chosen test image/host, with a recorded rollback. Obtain owner approval before replacing the host's official GTK with a custom patched build.
- Existing media-runtime patch obligations are separate; an accessibility fix does not establish that GTK/GStreamer resource-lifetime issues are fixed.
- Local diagnostic sources/logs are under `/home/l0gicgate/.cache/pi-tmp/pr1085-gtk-latest/` (`coordinate_probe.py`, `coordinate-probe.log`, `bounds-change.json`, `patched-probe.log`, `patched-scoped.log`). This scratch location is temporary; the reproduction and candidate snippet above are the durable handoff. No core dumps or private user data are attached.

author: JoeJoeflyn
body:
## Description

Deleting a file left it visible in an already-open Recent view until the view was manually reloaded. Recent entries resolve to their real target paths during enumeration, but deletion updates only spliced removed entries from the column showing the deleted file's parent directory — a `recent:///` column never matched that parent.

- `remove_deleted_locations` now also matches open `recent:///` columns when splicing deletions (covers deleting from the Recent view itself) and includes `recent:///` in the bulk-deletion refresh set.
- `handle_directory_change` fans the removal side of `Remove`/`Move` changes out to other open Recent columns, so monitor-driven removals and moves retire stale targets too. Only the removal side fans out: a moved target's new location is not a Recent member.

## Visual evidence

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e115e7ae-7db6-4984-a48a-c6989855f879

## How to test

1. Open the Recent view.
2. Select a listed file and press Del (or Shift+Del and confirm permanent deletion).
3. Observe the list.

**Expected result:** the entry disappears from Recent immediately; previously it stayed visible until navigating away and back. Deleting a file in a normal folder while Recent stays open also drops it from Recent.

## Related issue

Closes #1156

0.19.0 (built from source, commit 984706cd)

### Installation method

Built from source

### Linux distribution and desktop environment

Omarchy, Hyprland (Wayland)

### What happened?

After deleting a file, it remains visible in an already-open Recent view until the view is manually reloaded. The file itself is correctly moved to Trash (or permanently deleted); only the Recent listing goes stale.

The Recent view resolves each bookmark to its real target path when enumerating `recent:///`, but the deletion update path only splices removed entries from the column showing the deleted file's parent directory. A `recent:///` column never matches that parent, so it is never told to drop the entry. The same applies to files moved elsewhere and to removals reported by the filesystem monitor.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open the Recent view.
2. Select a listed file and press Del (or Shift+Del and confirm).
3. Observe that the entry is still shown in Recent even though the file is gone.
4. Navigate away and back to Recent: the entry is finally gone.

### Expected behavior

Deleting (or moving away) a file should remove its entry from an open Recent view immediately, matching the next reload.

author: JoeJoeflyn
body:
## Description

Extracting a multi-root archive now behaves like Finder: contents are written into the destination, then bundled into a fresh `<archive stem>/` folder only when more than one top-level entry landed. Single-root archives — one loose file or one top-level directory — extract as-is.

This replaces the previous split behavior where "Extract here" spilled loose files into the current folder and archive activation always wrapped (producing `foo/foo/` for tidy archives). All three entry points — "Extract here", double-click/Enter, and "Extract to…" — now share the same outcome, and password retry re-runs the same path.

Implementation: `ExtractionSession` reports the distinct resolved top-level paths it wrote; the worker reserves `stem`/`stem (n)` and moves the roots in with same-directory renames after a successful decode. No archive pre-scan, so `.tar.gz` is not decompressed twice, and cancellation/conflict-rename handling is unchanged.

## Visual evidence

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/de3194de-1474-401c-8b92-83c8929751a6

## How to test

- Right-click → **Extract here** on a zip containing multiple top-level entries → contents land in `<archive name>/`, selected afterward.
- Same on a zip containing a single top-level folder (e.g. `foo.zip` with `foo/` inside) → folder extracts as-is, no `foo/foo/` double-wrap.
- Same on a zip containing one loose file → file lands loose, no wrapper.
- Double-click an archive → same smart behavior as Extract here.
- Extract the same multi-root archive twice → second run produces `name (1)/`, first stays intact.
- `./scripts/test-headless.py adapters::local_operations::archive` — covers zip, tar, tar.gz bundling, verbatim single-root, and name-collision suffixing.

## Related issue

Closes #1159

issues.body:
### Problem or use case

Extracting an archive that contains several top-level entries ("Extract here", double-click, or "Extract to…") drops every entry loose into the destination folder. A zip of fifty loose photos spills fifty files into the current directory, mixing them with whatever already lives there.

The opposite wart also exists: activating an archive always wraps its contents in a folder named after the archive, so `foo.zip` that already contains a single `foo/` directory extracts to `foo/foo/`.

### Proposed solution

Match Finder / Archive Utility: extract an archive's contents into the destination, and when more than one top-level entry was written, bundle them into a fresh folder named after the archive (`photos.zip` → `photos/`). A single-root archive — one loose file or one top-level directory — extracts as-is, never double-wrapped.

### Alternatives considered

- Keep "Extract here" verbatim and "Extract to…" for wrapped extraction (status quo): both ends are wrong — spill for multi-root archives, double-wrap for tidy single-folder archives.
- Always create the wrapper folder before extraction (previous activation behavior): cannot know whether the wrapper is needed without inspecting the archive, and produces `foo/foo/`.

### Visual examples

N/A

### Strata version

main @ 528b1ab0

### Additional context

Implemented by bundling after decode: the extraction session reports the distinct resolved top-level paths it wrote, and the worker moves them into a reserved `stem`/`stem (n)` folder when there is more than one. Same-directory renames only, no archive pre-scan, cancellation and conflict naming unchanged.

## Description

Home, Trash, Network and Recent join the XDG folders in the saved `sidebar_order`, so any of them can be dragged into a custom position — Recent can now sit at the top. They render as one block (the separator that used to split specials from folders is gone, since the two sets now mix). An order saved before this change lists only the five XDG ids; the missing special ids are slotted back beside their default neighbours instead of being appended, so existing sidebars look unchanged after the upgrade.

Drag a sidebar row in the usual way: press, move it over another row, and release. A plain click still navigates. This applies to pinned rows too, since they share the same drag plumbing.

## How to test

1. Start Strata and look at the sidebar: Home, Trash, Network (and Recent, where the backend is available) sit in the same block as Documents/Downloads/etc.
2. Click Recent (or Home) — it navigates, no drag.
3. Drag a row above Home and release. No hold delay is needed.
4. Restart Strata.

issues.body:
## Problem or use case

Recent is a useful sidebar destination, but it sits in a fixed position with the other special places (Home, Trash, Network). I want **Recent at the top** of the sidebar so it is the first place I click.

XDG folders (Desktop, Documents, Downloads, Pictures, Videos) and pins can already be drag-reordered. Special destinations cannot, so there is no way to put Recent first without a code change.

## Proposed solution

Let users drag special sidebar destinations into a custom order, using the same interaction as the existing XDG folder reorder, and persist that order across restarts.

At minimum, Recent should be movable so it can sit at the top. Ideally Home, Trash, Network, and Recent all participate in that shared order (or can be mixed with the reorderable XDG folders).

Pins and Devices can stay in their own sections.

## Alternatives considered

- Pinning a folder as a stand-in for Recent does not work: Recent is a virtual list of recently used files, not a folder.
- Hiding other places (#1024) can reduce clutter but does not move Recent to the top.
- A setting that only pins Recent first would cover my case, but full reorder of special destinations is more consistent with the current XDG/pin drag behavior.

## Visual examples

N/A — same drag-and-drop as Documents / Downloads / pins.

## Strata version

0.19.0

## Additional context

Related (not duplicates):

- #1082 added the Recent destination but did not make it reorderable
- #184 / #214 cover pin reorder only
- #1024 covers show/hide of default places

`sidebar_order` today only stores the XDG place ids (`desktop`, `documents`, `downloads`, `pictures`, `videos`). Recent is appended as a fixed `recent:///` row.
