author: ogarza
body:
## Description

Marquee selection in large folders no longer rescans the whole folder on every selection change, in Columns, Icons and List. The work per change now depends on the selection, not on the folder size.

- **Selected positions are remembered.** A column remembers the listing positions of its selection, so reading the selection no longer hashes every path in the folder. Any change to the selection drops them, and so does any change to the listing (load batches, monitor events, removals, re-sorts). The next read then scans once. The exception is a lone selected cursor: a batch that adds no other row for its location only moves its row. This removes the three full-folder scans per change: the footer's two (positions and entries) and the read-back that Icons/List and Columns do after `set_selection`.
- **Positions are trusted only when each location is listed once.** A provider can list one location on several rows. Positions taken from the view, and the one-item cursor shortcut, are kept without a scan only while the column knows that it lists each location once. Learning that costs one pass over the listing, the first time a selection needs it after a provider load. Monitor events and re-sorts keep it. A listing that repeats a location scans once per change, as on `main`.
- **A drag changes the selection by difference.** When the previous positions are known, `set_selection` adds and removes only the items whose state changed, instead of rebuilding a set of every selected path. A select-all becomes an explicit selection on its first change, as on `main`, so folder-monitor events keep their current semantics; later changes are by difference.
- **Icons and List map selections without GTK lookups.** Each view keeps a view→source position array, built from the identity maps it already maintains and rebuilt only after either model changes. Mapping a selection no longer calls `GtkFilterListModel` for each item, which made each change take 0.1–4 s over a large selection. The selection handler now maps only the focus candidates, not the whole selection twice.

Measured with the method from #1567: a 90,000-file folder, a release build with frame pointers, a private Xvfb display with software rendering, XTest drags, and `perf` main-thread samples grouped per marquee refresh. Before is `main` at 5bb2e347; after is this branch, built with the same flags.

| Scenario | Before: main thread per selection change | After: slowest marquee refresh |
|---|---|---|
| List, small band | 23.6 ms median, 33.8 ms max | 0.8 ms |
| Columns, small band | 24.3 ms median, 49.8 ms max | 0.7 ms |
| Icons, small band | 25.3 ms median, 30.2 ms max | 0.8 ms |
| List, edge auto-scroll with more than 64 selected | 19.0 ms median, 32.0 ms max | 1.6 ms |
| List, Ctrl+A then Ctrl+Alt marquee (about 90,000 selected) | 114 ms to 2.35 s | 12.7 ms for the first change, which converts the select-all; under 3 ms after (1.4 ms p90) |

Apart from that first select-all change, no refresh took 3 ms or more, and the footer fell from 21–54% of main-thread samples, depending on the mode, to under 0.5%. Rendering is now most of the remaining time. These measurements predate the repeated-location fix (69e9bac6). That fix adds one pass over the listing to the first selection that needs it after a load.

## Visual evidence

N/A. This is a CPU-time fix with no visual change; the measurements above replace screenshots.

## How to test

1. Open a local folder with about 90,000 files (`scripts/generate-fixture.sh` creates a 100,000-entry folder in `target/fixtures/100000`).
2. In each view mode, press in blank space and drag a marquee up and down across a few rows, then against the bottom edge so it auto-scrolls.
3. In Icons or List, press Ctrl+A, then hold Ctrl+Alt and drag a marquee across some rows. Release, and check the footer count.
4. In a small folder, select a few files with a marquee, then Ctrl-marquee over part of them and copy with Ctrl+C; paste into an empty folder.

**Expected result:**

1. The folder loads as before.
2. The band and the selection highlight follow the pointer without lagging, and auto-scroll runs at the same speed as in a small folder.
3. The window stays responsive; the dragged rows are deselected and the footer counts the remaining items.
4. Exactly the files still selected are pasted.

## Related issue

Closes #1567

issues.body:
### Strata version

0.21.0, commit 5bb2e347 (`main`)

### Installation method

Built from source

### Linux distribution and desktop environment

Arch Linux (Omarchy), Hyprland 0.56.2. Measurements below were taken on a private Xvfb display (X11, cairo renderer) with a private D-Bus session.

### What happened?

Marquee (rubber-band) selection stutters badly in large folders, in Columns, Icons, and List. Every time the band crosses an item boundary, Strata rescans the **entire folder** up to three times on the main thread, hashing every entry's path. In a 90,000-entry folder one full scan costs ~9 ms. A single selection change costs ~25 ms, which exceeds the 16.7 ms frame budget at 60 Hz and is several frames at 144 Hz. The band and the selection lag the pointer, and edge auto-scroll slows down.

When the drag runs over a large existing selection, for example Ctrl+A followed by a Ctrl-marquee, Icons and List also map every selected position through `GtkFilterListModel` one item at a time. Each selection change then takes **115 ms to 4 s**, and the window freezes.

The cost scales with folder size and selection size, not with how much the selection actually changed.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open a local folder containing ~90,000 files. Measured with 90,000 JPEGs. `scripts/generate-fixture.sh` creates `target/fixtures/100000`, a comparable 100,000-entry folder, but that fixture was not used for these numbers.
2. In any view mode, press in blank space and drag a marquee up and down across a few rows.
3. Observe the band and the selection highlight lagging the pointer. Dragging against the bottom edge auto-scrolls noticeably slower than in a small folder.
4. Press Ctrl+A, then hold Ctrl+Alt and drag a marquee in Icons or List. Alt is needed because every row is selected, so there is no blank space to start in. The window freezes for 0.1–4 s per selection change.

### Expected behavior

The work done per selection change should be proportional to the items that changed, or at worst to the selection size, never to the folder size. The marquee should keep up with the display refresh rate regardless of how many entries the folder holds.

### Screenshots or video

N/A. This is a CPU-time problem; the measurements and profiles are below.

### Relevant logs

```shell
# perf report --no-children --comm strata (List mode, small band, release build)
26.93%  <core::hash::sip::Hasher<Sip13Rounds> as Hasher>::write
17.07%  <std::path::Path as Hash>::hash
 6.35%  <RandomState as BuildHasher>::hash_one::<&strata::model::Location>
 2.04%  NavigationState::selected_positions::{closure#0}
 1.04%  Vec<FileEntry>::from_iter (NavigationState::selected_entries)

# perf report --children --comm strata (same run)
57.32%  marquee after-paint refresh (MarqueeState::begin closure → apply_selection)
55.78%  browser_modes::sync_browser_selection
40.42%  shortcut_footer::update_item_count        (SelectionSynced observer)
36.07%  NavigationState::selected_positions        (footer + sync read-back)
19.30%  NavigationState::selected_entries          (footer)
11.93%  gsk_renderer_render

# perf report --no-children (List, Ctrl+A then Ctrl+Alt marquee, ~90k selected)
76.91%  browser_modes::selected_source_positions   (inclusive)
17.12%  gtk_bitset_get_nth                         (self)
~45%    unsymbolized libgtk-4 code at addresses next to gtk_bitset_get_nth
 4.79%  g_object_unref
```

### Additional context

#### Method

- Release build of 5bb2e347 with LTO off, frame pointers, and line tables only, so `perf` can unwind through inlined Rust frames.
- Strata ran on a private Xvfb display with a private D-Bus session and isolated XDG directories, seeded with the E2E harness's default preferences.
- XTest (`tests/e2e/harness/xtest.py`) synthesized drags of ~245 motion events/s for 5–8 s, sweeping the band across rows.
- Recorded with `perf record -F 1999 --call-graph fp -p <pid>`.
- "Per change" is the length of each contiguous main-thread sample burst under the marquee's after-paint refresh.
- Rendering was software (cairo), so its share will differ on a GPU session. The Strata-side costs below don't depend on the renderer.

#### Measurements

| Scenario | Main-thread cost per selection change | Dominant cost |
|---|---|---|
| List, small band (≤64 selected) | ~25 ms median, 31 ms max | 3 full-folder path-hash scans |
| Columns, small band | ~26 ms median, 33 ms max | same |
| Icons, small band | ~39 ms median, 51 ms max | same, plus rendering |
| List, edge auto-scroll with >64 selected | ~10.5 ms median | 1 full scan (the footer skips its scans above 64) |
| List, Ctrl+A then Ctrl+Alt marquee (~90k selected) | 115 ms – 4 s | per-item `GtkFilterListModel` lookups |

During the auto-scroll run the view covered ~135 rows in 4 s. The configured step of 24 px per 16 ms should cover ~210 rows in that time, so the refresh cost also slows auto-scroll.

Frames in which the band doesn't cross an item boundary are cheap (~0.5 ms bursts). The marquee itself is not the problem.

#### Call chain for one selection change

1. `MarqueeState::apply_selection` (`src/ui/marquee.rs:727`) calls `gtk::MultiSelection::set_selection`, which emits `selection-changed` only when the selection actually differs.
2. A handler reacts to `selection-changed`:
   - Icons/List: the `connect_selection` handler (`src/ui/browser_modes.rs:4485`) calls `sync_browser_selection` (`:5274`).
   - Columns: the selection closure in `append_column` (`src/ui/browser/columns.rs:1327`).
3. That handler calls `Browser::set_selection` (`src/app/browser.rs:2281`), which calls `NavigationState::set_selection` (`src/app/navigation.rs:1583`).
   - The marquee calls `commit_selection()` first, so the "unchanged selection" early return is skipped. `set_selection` builds a new `HashSet<Location>` of the k selected paths and emits `BrowserEvent::SelectionSynced`.
4. `SelectionSynced` observers run synchronously:
   - `ShortcutFooter::observe_browser` (`src/ui/shortcut_footer.rs:982`) calls `refresh_filter`, which calls `update_item_count` (`:1844`). This observer runs on **every** browser event, not just selection events.
   - The preview ignores `SelectionSynced` while the marquee is updating (`src/ui/preview.rs:604`).
   - `ViewState::handle` returns early (`src/ui/browser/events.rs:61`).
5. Back in the handler from step 2, it reads the selection back with `browser.selected_positions(depth)` to verify it (`src/ui/browser_modes.rs:5297`, `src/ui/browser/columns.rs:1388`).

#### Hotspot 1: full-folder path-hash scans (all modes)

`NavigationState` stores a column's selection as `HashSet<Location>`, where `Location` wraps `Native(Arc<Path>)`. Both `selected_positions` (`src/app/navigation.rs:1783`) and `selected_entries` (`:1816`) walk **every** entry in the column and probe the set. Each call therefore SipHash-es every path in the folder: ~9 ms for 90,000 entries, plus cache misses walking `FileEntry`s.

| Caller | Full scans per change | When |
|---|---|---|
| Footer `update_item_count`: `selected_positions` (`src/ui/shortcut_footer.rs:1865`), used to request size fills | 1 | 1–64 selected |
| Footer `update_item_count`: `selected_entries` (`:1898`), used for the "N files selected (size)" text | 1 | 1–64 selected, not the whole folder |
| Read-back verification of the selection (step 5 above) | 1 | always |

The "1–64 selected" condition is the common marquee case. In the List profile, hashing alone was ~50% of all samples, and the footer accounted for 40% inclusive.

#### Hotspot 2: per-item filter-model lookups for large selections (Icons and List)

`selected_source_positions` (`src/ui/browser_modes.rs:5259`) maps each selected view position separately. It calls `view_model.item(p)`, which goes through `GtkSortListModel` to `GtkFilterListModel`, then looks the item up in `SourceIndexMap`'s `HashMap<glib::Object, usize>`.

`GtkFilterListModel` resolves each position with `gtk_bitset_get_nth` on its match bitset, which scans linearly, so mapping k positions costs roughly O(k·N). Two things make it worse:

- The mapping runs twice per change: once in the handler (`src/ui/browser_modes.rs:4513`) and once per section in `sync_browser_selection`.
- `bitset_positions` materializes the selection into a `Vec` twice.

With ~90k selected this took 77% of samples inclusive, and each change took 115 ms – 4 s. Grouped views run all of this once per section.

Columns already avoids this: `ViewMap::source_position` (`src/ui/browser/collection.rs:668`) uses a cached forward/reverse position map, so each lookup is O(1). Columns large-selection drags were not profiled separately. They still pay Hotspot 1 and the O(k) `HashSet<Location>` rebuild.

#### Ruled out

- **Updating every frame:** the marquee coalesces motion into one after-paint refresh per frame and only hit-tests bound (visible) rows. Selection signals fire only on real changes.
- **Hover handlers** (Icons content hover, name tooltips, folder peek): the drag gesture holds an implicit pointer grab, so row motion controllers don't receive events. Capture-phase ancestors (input ownership, column resize-edge hints) measured ≤0.6%.
- **Metadata / file size fetching:** sizes come from the listing. The footer's `request_metadata_fill` calls are deduplicated and deferred to idle, so no I/O happens per change.
- **Band placement:** setting the band's margins and size request plus `queue_draw` is constant-time.
- **Rendering:** 9–25% of samples under software cairo. It contributes, but it doesn't scale with folder size.

#### Suggested fix directions

1. **Make selected positions O(k).** `NavigationState::set_selection` already receives the positions. Keep a sorted position list (or bitset) alongside `selected_locations`, and invalidate it on entry insert/splice/replace, re-sort, reload, hidden-file toggles, and other selection mutations. Alternatively, keep a `Location → position` index per column. Either way, `selected_positions` and `selected_entries` become proportional to the selection.
2. **Footer:** fetch the (at most 64) selected entries by position instead of scanning. Coalesce `refresh_filter` to once per frame or idle instead of running synchronously on every `BrowserEvent`.
3. **Drop the read-back scan:** have `set_selection` return the positions it adopted (or whether they differ from the input) instead of re-deriving them with `selected_positions`.
4. **Icons/List position mapping:** compute view→source positions once per signal, in a single ordered pass or incrementally from the `(position, count)` range in `selection-changed`, instead of calling `view_model.item(p)` per selected item twice. Columns' cached position map is a working model.
5. **Secondary:** a faster hasher for `Location` sets would cut the constant factor but would not fix the scaling.

Expected outcome: small-band selection changes drop from ~25 ms to well under 1 ms. Large-selection changes become proportional to the changed range rather than taking 0.1–4 s.

body:
## Description Triage batch 6 (#1556). It covers eleven groups from the 2026-10-04 triage. The triage issues were closed earlier as housekeeping, so this PR refers to them with "Refs". Two new F1 reference strings are localized in the ten supported languages; the translations were written for this PR and haven't been reviewed by native speakers. **Columns click on a multi-selected item (#1446)** - A plain click on an item that is part of a multi-selection collapsed the selection but didn't open the folder or show the preview. It now applies the normal click behaviour. Pressing a member and dragging still drags the whole selection. **`..` in typed paths (#1445)** - Absolute and `~/` paths typed in the location bar or 10xer's go prompt now resolve `.` and `..` as text, the way GIO already treats command-line paths. Before, a crumb could read `…/documents/..`, and Alt+Up from there moved down instead of up. - Typing a file path through `..` now selects the file in place when its folder is already open. **Clicking empty preview space (#1450)** - A click on a preview that shows something (content or its placeholder) keeps the browser selection. A click on the blank reserved preview slot clears it, like the space beside the columns. Dragging from the preview still draws a selection rectangle. - A disabled button (for example video Next) no longer counts as empty space, and the preview header's drag handle gaps drag the file again instead of starting a selection rectangle. The file chooser behaves the same. **Media keys (#1451)** - The volume slider now steps (0.1 per arrow, 0.2 per Page; Home mutes, End is full volume) and lands exactly on mute. - A focused timeline and 10xer's Media surface accept, besides ←/→ (±5 s): - Page Up/Down and Shift+←/→ (±30 s) - Home and `0` (start), End and `G` (last frame) - `+` / `=` / `-` (volume) - The key set follows cliamp and other terminal players. No new Ctrl+Alt shortcuts. - The seek slider for media that's neither audio nor video gets the same steps. **Column widths (#1448)** - Columns autofit and dragging stop at the visible browser area (the window minus the preview divider and the sidebar at full width). Autofit still saves its width, as #1539 documents, now capped. - A saved width wider than the window is narrowed when a window opens and after a text-size change. A text-size round trip restores the dragged width. Resizing the window doesn't narrow open columns. **Custom theme names without ASCII letters or digits (#1458)** - Names like `日本語` or `!!!` now save as `custom-theme.toml` (then `-2`, `-3`) instead of failing with "Enter a theme name". **Material Lighter body text (#1459)** - Text and dim text are darker (1.79:1 → 6.94:1 on the background). Material Vivid's text is lifted from 4.37:1 to 6.01:1. - A catalog test keeps body text at ≥ 4.5:1 on the background and ≥ 3:1 on the surface. Other weak pairs are listed in #1566. **Archive preview hover (#1555, split from #1294)** - Hovering a row in the archive Quick Look tree selected it and moved the keyboard cursor. Rows now select on click and open folders on release, as the browser views and Ctrl+F results do (#1291). Ctrl/Shift+click acts like a plain click (the list is single-selection). - Double-click opens exactly one level. - Row padding moved inside the row, so the hover fill and keyboard outline reach the row edge. **Color dialog theming (#1460)** - The native color dialog's Cancel and Select buttons, its custom-color editor (hex entry, sliders, value popups) and the folder-color "+" swatch now use the theme, including live theme changes. CSS only. **HTML comments in release notes (#1464)** - Comments are hidden in release notes only. Markdown file previews still show them escaped. - Notes that contain only a comment show "No release notes were provided". **Launcher zombies (#1465)** - Open in Terminal, Run, and the AUR/Omarchy update launchers now reap their process on a background thread, so no `` children remain. **Not in this PR:** - #1468 was already fixed by #1519. - #1469 is deferred. Its GTK-CRITICAL comes from GTK's submenu timer on an item-menu button Strata has already freed, not from the sidebar rebuild the plan assumed. ### What happened?

In the archive Quick Look tree, hovering a member row selects it. The hover-selected row also becomes the keyboard cursor, so Up, Down, Right and Enter then act on the row under the pointer instead of the one the keyboard was on.

The list still uses GTK's single-click-activate mode (`src/ui/preview/archive.rs`), which in GTK4 also selects whatever the pointer enters. #1291 fixed the same problem for the Ctrl+F results (#1294), but the archive tree was not part of that change.

In Columns with single-click previews on, arrowing onto `bundle.zip` shows no highlighted member; moving the pointer across the preview highlights one.

### Expected behavior

Hovering never changes the highlighted member. A single click highlights a row (and opens a folder), as in the browser views and the Ctrl+F results. Keyboard navigation continues from the clicked or keyboard-selected row, not the hovered one.

author: JoeJoeflyn
body:
## Description

Eliminates main-thread freezes when initiating drag and drop and validating drop destinations in folders with large item counts (such as 50k–100k items):
- Avoids allocating and cloning the entire `selected_entries()` vector in List, Columns, and Icons drag preparation by performing an $O(1)$ bitset membership lookup via `is_position_selected`.
- Caches active drag locations during internal file drags, avoiding redundant GFile URI reconstruction on hover events.
- Caches volume mountpoint queries and optimizes common parent path checks in `transferable_drop_sources` to avoid repeated synchronous filesystem queries during pointer motion.
- Cleans up active drag locations on drag completion.

## Visual evidence

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f57acb42-8e45-471a-a552-cd3d7aa4fa8f

## How to test

1. Open a folder containing a large number of items (e.g., 50,000+ files).
2. Select multiple items and start dragging them in List, Columns, or Icons view.
3. Drag over destination folders to preview the drop action.

**Expected result:**
Drag initiation starts immediately without freezing the UI thread, and hovering over destinations updates drag actions smoothly without lag.

## Related issue

Closes #1573

issues.body:
### Strata version
commit a3050d95

### Installation method
Built from source

### Linux distribution and desktop environment
Linux, Wayland / X11

### What happened?
When selecting and dragging files in directories with large item counts (e.g. 50,000+ items), the interface freezes noticeably on drag start and during hover over drop targets.

During drag preparation in List, Icons, and Columns views, `browser.selected_entries()` clones and iterates over the entire selection vector just to determine if the clicked row is included in the selection. Additionally, repeated volume mountpoint queries and URI resolution on motion events stall the main thread during hover validation.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Open a directory containing a large number of items (e.g. 50,000+ files).
2. Select multiple items.
3. Click and drag an item to initiate a drag-and-drop operation.
4. Hover over destination targets.
5. Observe noticeable UI freeze on drag start and hover.

### Expected behavior
Drag start should be instantaneous via O(1) bitset selection checks without cloning the entire selected entries list, and hover target validation should cache volume and path lookups to prevent main-thread stalls.

body:
## Description

Configured the `GridView` and `ListView` in `src/ui/inline_search/collection.rs` to use `gtk::ListTabBehavior::Item`. When search results in List or Icons modes are focused, pressing Tab now leaves the results view in a single press rather than stepping through every item in the view. Shift+Tab returns focus to the previously focused result item.

## Visual evidence

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1dfcb2d8-9c7b-4ebf-b88c-979430869137

## How to test

1. Open a directory with multiple files.
2. Press `Ctrl+F` and search for a term matching multiple items in List or Icons view.
3. Press `Down` to navigate focus into the filter results.
4. Press `Tab`.

**Expected result:** Focus immediately exits the search results container on the first Tab press, instead of tabbing through each matching item one by one. Pressing `Shift+Tab` returns focus directly back to the active result item.

## Related issue

Closes #1550

### What happened?
Since #1533, each listing is a single Tab stop in List, Icons and Columns. The pane filter's result views in List and Icons were not changed. They still use GTK's default `ListTabBehavior::All`, so Tab from a focused result walks through every result before it leaves the results. Reported in the #1533 review as a follow-up. Confirmed by reading the code.
### Steps to reproduce
1. In List or Icons, open a folder with many files.
2. Press Ctrl+F and type a query that matches many files.

Expected per the code: each Tab moves to the next result rather than leaving the results.

The results are one Tab stop, like the listing. Tab leaves them in one press, and Tab into them lands on the cursor result (#1431).
### Additional context
- `src/ui/inline_search/collection.rs:672-690` builds the results `GridView`/`ListView` without `set_tab_behavior(gtk::ListTabBehavior::Item)`. The main views set it at `src/ui/browser_modes.rs:2625` and `:3272`.
- The triage plan for #1431 included this ("Check the search-result and peek lists as well"); #1533 left it out.

author: ogarza
body: ## Description Shortcuts broke whenever a key's character wasn't the exact Latin letter a handler compared against (#1538): - with a Russian (or any non-Latin) layout active, Ctrl+C/V/X/A and every other letter shortcut did nothing; - with Caps Lock on, Ctrl+C/V failed on a plain US layout (the key arrives as `C`); - Ctrl+Shift+1–0 was matched against US shifted symbols, so it failed on German, Russian and others, and Ctrl+1/2/3 could not work on French AZERTY; - the F1 reference and hints were hand-typed strings, separate from the matching code, in mixed spellings and with English key names in every language. What changed ([`docs/keyboard-shortcuts.md`](https://github.com/lgse/strata/blob/fix/1538-layout-independent-shortcuts/docs/keyboard-shortcuts.md) is the spec): - `ui::keys` turns each key event into a `KeyPress` once: GDK's `KeyEvent::match_()`, then, for a key outside ASCII, the Latin key on the same physical key from another configured layout (`Display::map_keycode`) or a built-in US-QWERTY table. The digit row counts by position. Keypad keys act as the main keys. The ASCII path costs one `match_()` call and a range check: no allocation, no keymap query. - Every key handler installs through `keys::on_press` / `keys::on_release` and matches named constants in the binding catalog `ui::keys::bindings`. `clippy.toml` bans `connect_key_pressed`, `connect_key_released` and `set_accels_for_action` outside `ui::keys`. - Ctrl+K, Ctrl+Shift+K, Ctrl+Alt+T, F5 and Ctrl+\\ are dispatcher bindings that activate the same guarded `win.*` actions; `DEFAULT_ACCELS` and the per-window accelerator rewriting are gone. - In a focused text field, an editing key recognized only through the fallback runs the field's own action (cut, copy, paste, select all, undo, redo). A focused document-table cell does the same for copy and select all. - F1, footer hints and panels, context menus, tooltips, accessible names and Settings render shortcuts from the catalog through one formatter, with key names translated in all ten languages (German Strg, Entf, Bild auf; French Suppr; Spanish Supr). F1 search matches key names in English and in the interface language. - E2E: a fixture switches layouts on the harness's private Xvfb (`setxkbmap -display` plus an XKB group lock) and always restores US. ### Decisions (owner-approved) | Question | Decision | | --- | --- | | Letter shortcuts | Key label first; for non-ASCII characters, the Latin character of the same physical key from another configured layout. Caps Lock ignored. | | No Latin layout configured | Built-in US-QWERTY table by keycode. | | Digit row | By physical position on every layout (Ctrl+1/2/3, Ctrl+Shift+1–0, 10xer digits). | | Plain-letter commands (10xer, chords, h/j/k/l) | Same fallback; typing consumers always get the real character. | | Architecture | One `ui::keys` adapter computes a `KeyPress` once per event; Clippy `disallowed-methods` bans raw key handlers elsewhere. Dispatch stays in the handlers. | | Displayed shortcuts | F1, Settings, context menus and footer hints render from the same constants the handlers match, kept in one binding catalog (`ui::keys::bindings`). No free-text key labels. | | Label characters | Always the Latin key (Ctrl+C with Russian active, Ctrl+1 on AZERTY); labels don't track layout switches. | | Key names | Translated per interface language in all ten catalogs; one notation everywhere. | | Modifiers | GTK accelerator form (`KeyEvent::match_()`), exact matching over Ctrl/Alt/Shift/Super through one `Binding` type. | | Modifier tolerance | Letter, symbol and digit shortcuts match exactly; navigation and dismiss keys keep each site's tolerance through `Binding::ignoring`. | | Keypad | Keypad keys act as the main keys; Num Lock digits stay digits. | | PDF Ctrl+0 | The dead PDF zoom-reset handler is removed. | | GTK accelerators (Ctrl+K, Ctrl+Shift+K, Ctrl+Alt+T, F5, Ctrl+\\) | Become dispatcher bindings that activate the same guarded `win.*` actions. | | Text fields | Editing shortcuts resolved only through the fallback activate the widget's own GTK action. | | Tests | Table-driven normalizer unit tests plus E2E layout scenarios. | Refinements recorded in the spec: - The fallback reads the level Shift selects, because Caps Lock raises the event's level for letters. - Where a top-row key types `+` or `−`, Ctrl shortcuts and `g` read it as that symbol, as before: Swiss German Ctrl++ (Shift+1) is not tab 1, and AZERTY `g −` still unpins. `t` and `;` have no `+`/`−` step, so they count the key's position: AZERTY `t` then the `−` key is tab 6, Czech `t` then the `+` key is tab 1. - A chord's digit step (`t 1`, `g 1`, `; 1`) also accepts the Shift AZERTY types digits with. - A digit typed off the digit row counts, such as the Hungarian 0 left of 1. - Above level 1 (AltGr), the top row counts only a digit it types, so AltGr symbols there stay symbols and Ctrl+\\ works on German, Swiss, Swedish and Norwegian Mac layouts. - `0` in media also accepts Shift, as #1570 intended for AZERTY. - Rust tests that emit `key-pressed` without a GDK event read as US-QWERTY presses. ### Implementation checklist - [x] `ui::keys` normalizer, `KeyPress`, `Binding`, `on_press`/`on_release`, US-QWERTY table, digit row, keypad folding; table-driven tests for us, us+ru, ru-only, uk, el, he, fr AZERTY, de QWERTZ, Dvorak and Caps Lock. - [x] Binding catalog, `Keys` row model, `keys::label` formatter, `keys.name.*` in all ten catalogs; catalog completeness test (each listed binding has its own F1 row in each map its block names). - [x] F1 rows, footer hints and panels, context-menu hints, tooltips and Settings strings on catalog constants; label-to-accelerator parsing deleted; menu rows show the formatter's text. - [x] `clippy.toml` ban; one `#[expect(clippy::disallowed_methods)]` in `ui::keys`. - [x] Every handler migrated; typing paths use `text()`; ordinal shortcuts match digits by position (tabs, view modes, text size, 10xer `t` and `;` digits, `g` pin digits). - [x] `DEFAULT_ACCELS`, `TENXER_SUPPRESSED_ACCELS`, `install_mode_accelerators` and the per-window accelerator bindings removed; window actions run after the dispatcher yields; chooser policy and rename/modal gating unchanged. - [x] Text-field routing for fallback editing keys (browser windows and the file chooser). - [x] Shortcut predicate tests moved onto bindings, driven through the real handlers. - [x] E2E layout fixture and cases: Ctrl+C/V on us,ru and with Caps Lock, Ctrl+1/2/3 on fr, Ctrl+Shift+2 on de, 10xer `j` on us,ru, Ctrl+K and rename-field Ctrl+A/X/V on ru-only. - [x] Docs: spec in sync, architecture keyboard routing, layout links from keyboard navigation and 10xer mode, the layout fixture in e2e-testing, and an AGENTS.md rule. - [x] Mutation patches regenerated (clipboard, filter-results, view-switching, quick-preview); all four are detected again. - [x] Guardrails: no new dependency; the ASCII path neither allocates nor queries the keymap; every US difference is listed below. ### Intentional differences on a US layout - **Accidental extra modifiers on letter, symbol and digit shortcuts no longer match.** Examples: Ctrl+Super+Z (undo), Ctrl+Alt/Super+V/C/X/D/A (file clipboard verbs), Ctrl+Super+1/2/3, Ctrl+Alt/Super+, (Settings), Ctrl+Alt/Super+L and the chooser's Ctrl+Shift+L (location), Ctrl+Alt+Shift+N, Ctrl+Super+F, Ctrl+Super+H, Super or Alt with h/j/k/l, Shift+Y / Shift+P (copy path, pin), Ctrl+Shift/Alt/Super+C on a table, and Ctrl+Shift/Alt/Super+A in Settings search (Ctrl+Shift+A is GTK's unselect again). - **Chord digits accept Shift**, so `g` and `;` followed by Shift+digit now act as the digit, as `t` already did. - **Hyper and Meta are not shortcut modifiers.** Menu or Shift+F10 with them held now opens the context menu, and tab chords and the search palette's Alt+Enter ignore them. - **Keypad keys act as the main keys** wherever the main key works: keypad Enter, arrows, Home/End, Page Up/Down, Delete, Tab and Space. Keypad `/` opens an empty filter like `/`. Ctrl+Shift+keypad `+`/`−` no longer changes the text size, and Shift+keypad `+`/`−` after `g` no longer pins, because Shift is not part of those keys. - **Caps Lock never changes a shortcut.** Ctrl+C/V/X/A and h/j/k/l work with Caps Lock on, and Caps Lock+letter acts as the plain letter: Caps Lock+g is `g`, not `G` (10xer last item, media seek to the end). - **PDF previews:** Ctrl+Alt+0 and Ctrl+Super+0 no longer reset PDF zoom; plain Ctrl+0 still resets the text size, as before. - **Media:** Shift+0 also seeks to the start (the binding accepts the Shift AZERTY needs). - **Text:** one notation everywhere (Escape, Page Up, Enter, Alt+←, Ctrl++ / − / 0, 1–9 / 0) with translated key names. Menu rows read Enter, Ctrl+Shift+N, lowercase 10xer letters and "F2 / Ctrl+R"; Properties shows Alt+Enter. The sidebar toggle tooltip says Ctrl+N and the preview close tooltip says i while 10xer mode is on. The file chooser's `g` panel leaves out the steps it refuses, and the preview's `g` panel lists `m`. - **Tab numbers** show exactly while Ctrl+Shift is held. - **F1 search:** Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+Y and Ctrl+Shift+Z undo and redo in the reference's search field; the open reference used to swallow them. A typed `-` also finds the `–` of digit ranges, so `1-9` finds Ctrl+Shift+1–9 / 0. Typing is unchanged everywhere. In 10xer mode the Russian Ё key types Ё in text fields instead of toggling F1. Not changed here, for a follow-up decision (all predate this PR): - In 10xer mode Ctrl+Alt+T still opens a terminal from the file list (and Ctrl+Shift+K from a non-menu popover), although `docs/10xer-mode.md` lists them as unbound. - A US `~` typed into the location bar in 10xer mode toggles F1. - `scripts/e2e-mutation-check.sh` does not detect the `rename-caret` mutation, on this branch or on `main` (85663d55); the long-rename scenario passes with it applied. ## Visual evidence Pending upload by the owner (captures taken on a private Xvfb, not attached yet): 1. F1 reference in English, before / after 2. F1 reference in German, before / after (Rücktaste and Strg+B instead of Backspace and Ctrl+B) 3. A file's context menu in English, before / after (Enter, F2 / Ctrl+R, Alt+Enter) 4. A file's context menu in German, before / after (Eingabe, Strg+C, Entf, Umschalt+Entf instead of Return, Ctrl+C, Delete) ## How to test 1. On Hyprland, run `hyprctl eval 'hl.config({ input = { kb_layout = "us,ru" } })'`, then `hyprctl switchxkblayout all next` to activate Russian. With a `hyprland.conf` instead of a Lua config, the first command is `hyprctl keyword input:kb_layout us,ru`. 2. Select a file, press Ctrl+C, open another folder, press Ctrl+V. Press Ctrl+A, then Ctrl+K and type a few Cyrillic letters into the search. 3. Rename a file (F2), then press Ctrl+A, Ctrl+X and Ctrl+V in the name field. 4. With two or more tabs open, press Ctrl+Shift+2. Turn on 10xer mode (Ctrl+Shift+M) and press the keys labelled J/K (о/л). 6. Switch back to US with Caps Lock on and repeat step 2. 7. Run `hyprctl eval 'hl.config({ input = { kb_layout = "fr" } })'` and press Ctrl+& (the 1 key), then Ctrl+é (the 2 key). 8. Restore your layout with `hyprctl reload`. 9. Open F1 and a file's context menu in English, then with the interface language set to German. Search F1 for `strg+c` and for `ctrl+c`. **Expected result:** every shortcut behaves as on a US layout: the file is copied, everything is selected, search opens, the name field cuts and pastes, tab 2 is selected, the 10xer cursor moves, and Ctrl+& / Ctrl+é switch to Columns / Icons. Typing in search, filters and the name field still produces Cyrillic characters. F1 and the context menu show the same labels in one notation (German: Strg+C, Entf), each listed shortcut works, and both searches find Copy. ## Related issue Closes #1538

comments.author: ogarza
comments.body:
Reproduced on `main` (a3050d95) with a `us,ru` layout. With the Russian layout active, Ctrl+C and Ctrl+V on a file do nothing. The same steps with the US layout copy the file. Shortcuts registered through GTK's accelerator system (Ctrl+K, F5) still work with the Russian layout active.

Cause: Strata's own key handlers compare the character a key produces with Latin letters. With the Russian layout active, the C key produces `с` (`Cyrillic_es`), so Ctrl+C never matches. GTK's built-in shortcut matching falls back to the physical key, which is why its accelerators are unaffected.

Thanks for the clear report. The fix will make shortcut matching independent of the active layout rather than special-casing Cyrillic; a PR will be linked here.

author: l0gicgate
body:
## Description

Every successful file-provider action opened a blocking "File availability" dialog, even when the service opens its own window (Dropbox's Share).

- Activation replies may now set `feedback`: `dialog` (default), `notice` (a brief non-blocking notice with the provider name and message, shown in the window's bottom-right progress dock), or `none`. Strata honors it only for fully accepted outcomes. Rejected, partial and unknown outcomes, message-only replies, and disconnects always show the dialog. Unrecognized values fall back to the dialog, and older hosts ignore the field.
- Manifests may set `icon` to a declared icon id, drawn before the provider's context-menu group heading. GTK section titles can't hold images, so the heading becomes a custom row styled like a section title. Providers without an icon keep the native title.
- The Send-to success notice is now a shared `ui::notice` helper. It also moves from the top of the browser to the progress dock, so transfer feedback appears in one place.
- `docs/file-providers.md` documents both fields.

## Visual evidence

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5456f3ec-4e47-47f9-9c04-062eb1c2ba2d


## How to test

1. Install a provider under `~/.config/strata/providers/<id>/` whose `provider.json` declares `"icon": "<declared icon id>"`, and whose activation replies include `"outcome": {"status": "accepted"}` with `"feedback": "notice"` for one action and `"none"` for another.
2. Restart Strata, right-click a file the provider handles, and run each action.
3. Make the provider return `"status": "rejected"` with `"feedback": "notice"` and run the action again.

**Expected result:** the menu heading shows the icon before the provider name. The `notice` action shows a non-blocking notice in the bottom-right progress dock for about four seconds, and the `none` action shows nothing. The rejected action still opens the result dialog.

issues.body:
### Problem or use case

Every successful file-provider action opens a blocking "File availability" dialog, for example "dropbox: Accepted (1/1) — Sent “Share...” to Dropbox." For actions that open their own UI (Dropbox's Share window) or need no confirmation, the user must dismiss an extra modal each time. The "File availability" title is also misleading for actions unrelated to availability.

### Proposed solution

Add an optional `feedback` field to protocol 1 `activate` replies so the provider chooses, per action, how a successful result is presented:

- `"dialog"` (default, current behavior for existing providers)
- `"notice"`: a brief non-blocking banner, like the Send-to success notice
- `"none"`: no host feedback

Rejected, partial and unknown outcomes and disconnects always use the dialog, whatever the provider requests, so problems are never hidden. The field is additive and ignored by older hosts.

### Alternatives considered

A Settings preference was considered, but it applies to every action alike and can't tell "Share..." (opens its own window) from "Copy link" (deserves a notice).

author: ogarza
body: ## Description **Simplified Chinese.** Adds zh-CN (**简体中文**, Standard Mandarin as written in mainland China and Singapore) as the eleventh interface language. Every catalog is translated: interface strings, messages and shortcut descriptions, counts, dates, Settings search keywords, and the desktop entry. The text reads like Chinese desktop software, using the terms of File Explorer, Finder and GNOME Files in zh_CN (文件夹, 回收站, 打开方式, 重命名, 标签页, 主文件夹), not English sentence structure. The process was: - an agreed glossary; - six translators; - a native copy-edit of every string; - a cross-catalog consistency pass. Auto-detect maps every Chinese locale to zh-CN, Traditional ones (`zh_TW`, `zh_HK`) included, just as every Portuguese locale maps to Brazilian Portuguese. The language uses the existing pieces: the `Language` enum and locale tables (invariant plurals, `.` decimals with `,` grouping), the catalogs, and the `i18n` helpers. Two shared helpers were extended rather than given zh-only paths: - **`i18n::join_sentences`** replaces an archive-only `。` special case. Wherever two translated sentences are joined, Chinese and Japanese no longer get a space after a full stop, and a bare system error that ends without a stop gets the language's own. The FAT32 copy-failure message now joins its reason this way instead of embedding it in the template. - **Settings search** now matches a Han or kana query of two or more characters inside a title, and against a title's words joined together. Chinese titles have no spaces between words but do have spaces around Latin words, so before this change 隐藏 could not find 显示隐藏文件, and Omarchy主题变体 could not find Omarchy 主题变体. **Chinese keyboard layouts.** - **Plain `cn` (pinyin input methods run on it):** GDK reports exactly the US keymap, so every shortcut is the US one. - **`cn(altgr-pinyin)`:** its AltGr tone dead keys on the digit row are text input, never digits. **Ctrl+1** and **t 1** keep working. The normalizer tests and a new E2E layout option (the harness now loads XKB variants) cover this. **Input-method fix (Chinese, Japanese, Korean, dead keys, Compose).** GTK passes a key to the focused field's input method only after every capture-phase handler has run. With an input method loaded into the app (X11, or `GTK_IM_MODULE=fcitx`/`ibus`), or with GTK's own dead keys and Compose, Strata took the keys of an unfinished composition: - Escape cancelled a rename, or closed the filter, location bar, footer prompt, global search or F1 reference. - Space opened quick preview from the filter. Space is the pinyin candidate key. - Enter ran a 10xer rename prompt with the partial text. `keys::on_press` now forwards each key to the composing field first, as GtkSearchEntry's key capture does, and runs Strata's handler only if the input method passes the key back. Korean input methods such as fcitx5-hangul commit the current syllable and pass back Escape, arrows and Ctrl shortcuts, so one press both commits and runs the command. The release of a key the input method took is forwarded too. Global search and the 10xer footer prompt also submit from their field's `activate` signal, which is how Enter arrives after an input method passes it back. No other handler changes; with nothing composing, the cost is one empty-list check per key. On Wayland the input method runs in the compositor, so the keys it uses never reached Strata there. **Dependency.** `rust-i18n` goes from 3.1.5 to 4.2.4, because cargo-deny now rejects `unsafe-libyaml` (RUSTSEC-2024-0449), which 3.x pulled in through `serde_yaml`. 4.2.1 and later parse YAML with `serde-saphyr`. The catalog backend follows the 4.0 `Backend` trait. The compiled catalog tables are unchanged. **Known limitations** (documented in `docs/internationalization.md` and `docs/keyboard-shortcuts.md`): - Han glyph forms follow the process locale or `PANGO_LANGUAGE`, not Strata's language setting. Choosing 简体中文 manually on, for example, an `en_US` system can show another region's glyph forms; `PANGO_LANGUAGE=zh-cn` fixes it. - Type-to-search started from the file list begins without the input method. Open the filter first (**Ctrl+F**) to type pinyin. - Filenames sort by code point, not pinyin. ## Visual evidence Both binaries run on a `zh_CN.UTF-8` locale with Language set to Auto-detect, the tokyo-night theme, and 1600×900 on a private Xvfb. Before is `main` at 3dd59999; after is this branch. Captures are in `target/pr-1582-captures/`: | Before (`main`) | After | |---|---| | `before-context-menu.png` — English menus under a Chinese locale | `after-context-menu.png` — file context menu and status bar in Chinese | | `before-settings-language.png` — no Chinese in the language list | `after-settings-language.png` — Settings → 常规, with 简体中文 in the language list | | `before-shortcuts.png` — English F1 reference | `after-shortcuts.png` — F1 reference in Chinese; key names stay as printed (Ctrl+C, Shift+Delete) | ## How to test 1. Install a CJK font with Simplified Chinese glyphs (`noto-fonts-cjk` / `fonts-noto-cjk`). Start Strata with `LANG=zh_CN.UTF-8` and Language on Auto-detect, then do the same with `LANG=zh_TW.UTF-8`. **Expected:** the interface is in Simplified Chinese both times. 2. Open Settings → 常规 → 语言 on a non-Chinese locale, choose 简体中文, and restart. **Expected:** the interface switches to Chinese. 3. Browse the menus, the context menu, Properties, the F1 reference (F1), the status bar and dates. **Expected:** Chinese copy, “…” quotes around names, `3 个项目`, `2026年9月7日 14:30`, and key names such as `Ctrl+C`. In Settings search, typing 隐藏 finds 显示隐藏文件. 4. Without an input-method daemon, run `setxkbmap -layout cn -variant altgr-pinyin`, start renaming a file, press AltGr+1 and then Escape. **Expected:** the rename stays open, and AltGr+1 followed by `a` types ā. With fcitx5 + pinyin under `GTK_IM_MODULE=fcitx` (or on X11), type `wenjian` in the rename field or the filter, then press Escape or Space. **Expected:** only the composition is cancelled or a candidate is picked; the rename stays open, and quick preview does not open. With a Korean input method, type 보고 in a rename and press Escape once. **Expected:** the syllable commits and the rename is cancelled. 5. On `cn(altgr-pinyin)`, press **Ctrl+1** and then **t 1**. **Expected:** both select tab 1. AltGr+1 does not. The interface language and the keyboard layout are independent, as for every other language. Steps 4 and 5 don't depend on the language, so also run them under `LANG=en_US.UTF-8`. **Expected result:** Chinese users get a complete, natural Simplified Chinese interface automatically, and pinyin or dead-key composition is never interrupted by Strata's shortcuts. Every other language and the US layout behave as before. ## Related issue Closes #1582

issues.body:
### Problem or use case

Strata ships ten interface languages, but not Chinese. Standard Mandarin (Putonghua), written in Simplified characters, is the most widely used form of Chinese. Chinese users currently get English even when their desktop runs a `zh_*` locale.

Chinese users also type differently from the layouts covered in #1576. They use the `cn` XKB layout (identical to US) with a pinyin input method such as fcitx5 or IBus, or the `cn(altgr-pinyin)` variant, whose AltGr digit-row keys are dead tone marks. Shortcuts should behave on these setups exactly as `docs/keyboard-shortcuts.md` promises, and tests should cover them.

### Proposed solution

**Language**
- Add Simplified Chinese (`zh-CN`, shown as **简体中文**) to Settings → General → Language.
- Auto-detect maps every Chinese locale (`zh_CN`, `zh_SG`, `zh_TW`, `zh_HK`, `zh_MO`, `zh-Hans`, `zh-Hant`) to `zh-CN`, the same way every Portuguese locale maps to Brazilian Portuguese.
- Translate every catalog: interface strings, messages and shortcut descriptions, counts, dates, Settings search keywords, and the desktop entry.
- Write the translation as native Chinese software copy, not literal English. Use the terms Chinese users know from Windows File Explorer, macOS Finder and GNOME Files, full-width punctuation, and “…” quotation marks for names.
- Apply Chinese number, list, plural (invariant), and date conventions.

**Keyboard layout**
- Cover `cn` and `cn(altgr-pinyin)` in the shortcut normalizer tests and in the end-to-end layout options.
- Make sure shortcuts, digit-row bindings and typing behave as documented on these layouts.
- Document how pinyin input methods interact with shortcuts and type-to-search.

**Docs and rules**
- Update `docs/internationalization.md`, `docs/preferences.md`, `docs/keyboard-shortcuts.md`, and the AGENTS.md rule that every string ships in all supported languages (now eleven).

### Alternatives considered

- **Traditional Chinese (`zh-TW`) instead of, or as well as, Simplified.** Taiwan's Standard Mandarin uses Traditional characters and different vocabulary. It would need a separate catalog and can follow later. Until then, Traditional locales get Simplified Chinese.
- **Falling back to English for Traditional locales.** Rejected by the owner in favour of one Chinese catalog for every Chinese locale.

### Visual examples

_No response_

### Strata version

main at 3dd59999

### Additional context

Japanese and Korean already depend on system CJK fonts. Simplified Chinese needs a CJK font with Simplified Chinese glyphs, such as Noto Sans CJK SC.

author: itsmunzir
body:
## Description

The folder Trash-support probe queried the first listed entry with the default flags. For a symlink, the query returned the target's information. A symlink to a location without Trash (for example a file on tmpfs such as `/dev/shm`) can make the whole folder report "no Trash". Delete then shows the permanent-deletion confirmation for every item, and Move to Trash is hidden.

An entry is trashed as itself, so a symlink must not take the Trash support of its target. The probe now uses `NOFOLLOW_SYMLINKS`, and the comment states the intent. The probe stays on the first entry, so a folder that cannot itself be removed still describes the entries it contains. Regular entries keep their result.

Verification: the final diff passes `cargo fmt --check`, and the change reuses the `NOFOLLOW_SYMLINKS` flag that `query_file_entry` already uses. This host cannot run `cargo check` (Windows without GTK pkg-config), so the build and test gate is CI.

## Visual evidence

N/A — the change affects a capability probe, not the interface layout, and no GTK runtime is available in the development environment for a capture.

## How to test

1. On a filesystem with Trash (for example under `~`), make the first entry that the folder enumerator returns a symlink to a file on a filesystem without Trash (for example `/dev/shm`).
2. Open the folder.
3. Select a regular file and press Delete, or open the context menu.

**Expected result:** Delete offers Move to Trash, and the context menu shows Move to Trash. The permanent-deletion confirmation does not appear.

## Related issue

Closes #1551

### Strata version
main @ aee71335
### Installation method

### What happened?

Delete then opens the "This location doesn't support Trash. These items will be permanently deleted." confirmation for every item in the folder, not a trash attempt. The dialog still confirms first, so nothing is deleted without consent. Reported in the #1533 review; confirmed by reading the code.

The probe describes the folder's own entries. A symlink is trashed as a link, so it should not take its target's Trash support. Query with `NOFOLLOW_SYMLINKS`, or probe a non-symlink entry.

author: Rizmi
body:
## Description

Extracting archives containing directories on filesystems lacking `RENAME_NOREPLACE` (such as NTFS mounted via FUSE/ntfs-3g) previously failed during destination publication because directory publication unconditionally returned `OPNOTSUPP`. This left extracted members trapped inside hidden `.strata-extraction-<uuid>` staging folders and reported an unexpected system error.

This adds a safe, exclusive directory publication fallback when atomic `RENAME_NOREPLACE` is unavailable:
- Exclusively reserve the candidate destination name with descriptor-relative `mkdirat`, preserving existing collision detection and candidate suffixing (`stem (1)`, `stem (2)`).
- Recursively migrate directory entries: child files via `linkat`, child symlinks via `symlinkat` (falling back from `linkat`), and nested directories via recursive `mkdirat` descriptor migration.
- Apply directory permissions and timestamps to newly created directory descriptors.
- On any migration failure, remove the partially created destination tree and preserve staging intact.
- Upon successful migration, remove the source directory tree.

## Visual evidence
https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a4ac8e42-2779-47f3-ba70-82fed470214e

## How to test

1. On a filesystem lacking `RENAME_NOREPLACE` (e.g. an NTFS partition mounted via FUSE/ntfs-3g), extract an archive containing directory members or a single root folder.
2. Extract the same archive again to test collision avoidance.

**Expected result:** The archive extracts and publishes into the destination directory without error. On collision, an incremented suffix (`name (1)`) is created without clobbering existing directories.

## Related issue

Closes #1585

issues.body:
### Strata version
0.21.0 / commit 3dd59999 (current main)

### Installation method
Built from source

### Linux distribution and desktop environment
Arch Linux, Hyprland

### What happened?
When extracting an archive (such as a `.zip` file) on a filesystem that does not support `RENAME_NOREPLACE` (e.g. an NTFS partition mounted via FUSE / `ntfs-3g`), extraction extracts all entries into the hidden staging folder `.strata-extraction-<uuid>`, but fails when attempting to publish the final folder, presenting an error dialog:

> **Unable to complete operation**
> Could not publish “<name>”: An unexpected system error occurred. Extracted entries remain in “.strata-extraction-<uuid>”.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Mount a partition lacking `RENAME_NOREPLACE` support (e.g. an NTFS partition mounted at `/mnt/Data`).
2. Place an archive containing multiple entries or a directory on the partition (e.g. `archive.zip`).
3. Right-click and extract the archive.
4. Observe the operation fails with "Could not publish ... An unexpected system error occurred".
5. Observe the un-published staging folder `.strata-extraction-...` remains behind in the directory.

### Expected behavior
Strata should safely publish extracted directories on filesystems lacking `RENAME_NOREPLACE`:
- Exclusively create the candidate destination directory via `mkdirat` (which fails atomically with `EEXIST` if the path already exists, safely triggering candidate numbering like `<name> (1)` without overwriting).
- Move entries from the staging directory into the destination directory descriptor.
- Remove the empty staging directory upon completion.
- On failure, clean up only the destination entries created by the operation and leave staging intact.

### Relevant logs
```shell
Could not publish “debug-b4-prod”: An unexpected system error occurred. Extracted entries remain in “.strata-extraction-8ca8c950-15f3-4d39-8e38-6d84c79013a4”.
```

### Evidence
https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/13cb85b8-6f7f-4dc8-8607-b98087242960

### Additional context
In `src/adapters/local_operations/archive/destination.rs` (`move_without_replacing`), `rename_no_replace` fails with `EINVAL` on NTFS and falls back to `move_by_link`. For directories, `move_by_link` explicitly returns `Err(rustix::io::Errno::OPNOTSUPP)` because directories cannot be hardlinked, causing the publish operation to fail unconditionally for any directory.

Code, language, and config files now use the [Catppuccin VSCode icon set](https://github.com/catppuccin/vscode-icons) (v1.26.0, MIT) instead of the monochrome Simple Icons and Devicons glyphs. author: l0gicgate
body:
## Description

At some device pixel sizes (15px JetBrains Mono, reached here as 10px × 1.1818 text scaling × 1.25 monitor scale) the GL and Vulkan renderers drop the top pixel row of glyphs, so `Trash` reads as `Irash`. GTK's `automatic` font rendering rasterizes with slight hinting but hint metrics off: Pango reports unhinted ink extents while FreeType's light hinter draws the top bar one row higher, and GSK sizes the glyph atlas slot from the extents, so the top row falls into undrawn padding (GNOME/gtk#8395, same mismatch as GNOME/gtk#8340).

`ThemeManager::load` now pins `gtk-font-rendering` to `manual` for Strata's process. Manual mode hints metrics as well, so the extents match the raster, and it follows the desktop's hint style and antialiasing. Application-set GtkSettings values outrank the settings portal, so the desktop's `automatic` does not override it. The property is looked up by name and skipped on GTK older than 4.16, keeping the 4.12 floor. The Cairo renderer preference is unchanged. `docs/preferences.md` documents the behavior.

## Visual evidence

Pending owner upload: before/after capture of the file list and sidebar under `GSK_RENDERER=gl` (llvmpipe, 15px) is at `scratchpad/app/shots/compare.png` in the session scratch directory; before shows `Irash`/`IBEAM`, after shows `Trash`/`TBEAM`. The owner also confirmed the fix on the real 1.25x Wayland display.

## How to test

1. On Omarchy, set `omarchy display text size 14`, a monitor at 1.25x scale, font rendering left at `automatic`.
2. Fully quit Strata, then run `GSK_RENDERER=gl ./target/debug/strata <folder with files starting with T>` and set text size to 10.
3. Compare with the previous build under the same command.

**Expected result:** With this change every `T`, `E`, and `I` keeps its top pixel row in the sidebar and file lists; the previous build renders `Iabs Showcase.mp4` and `Irash`.

## Related issue

Closes #1600

issues.body:
### Strata version

main at 6662d8d4 (source build)

### Installation method

Built from source

### Linux distribution and desktop environment

Omarchy (Arch Linux), Hyprland on Wayland, GTK 4.24.0, Omarchy text size 14px (GNOME `text-scaling-factor` 1.1818), font hinting `slight`, display DP-3 at 1.25x scale, JetBrains Mono Nerd Font.

### What happened?

With Strata text size 10px, the GL renderer drops the top pixel row of glyphs: `Tabs Showcase.mp4` renders as `Iabs Showcase.mp4`, `Theme variants.mp4` as `Iheme variants.mp4`, and `Trash` in the sidebar as `Irash`. `GSK_RENDERER=cairo` renders correctly.

Same symptom as #442 and #1310 reached through a different combination: 10px × 1.1818 text scaling snaps to 12 logical px, and 12 × 1.25 monitor scale is exactly 15 device px.

### Steps to reproduce

1. `omarchy display text size 14` (text-scaling-factor 1.1818), monitor scale 1.25, font rendering left at the default `automatic`.
2. Start Strata without `GSK_RENDERER`, set text size to 10.
3. Open a folder containing files starting with `T`.

### Expected behavior

Glyphs render whole at every text size, text-scaling factor, and monitor scale.

### Screenshots or video

Attached by the reporter on the PR.

### Relevant logs

_No response_

### Additional context

Root cause (GTK 4.24.0 source, confirmed with a Pango probe): GTK's `automatic` font rendering rasterizes with slight hinting but hint metrics off. Pango then reports unhinted ink extents (the `T` top edge at 29.05px) while FreeType's light hinter draws the top bar one row higher (row 28). GSK's GPU glyph cache sizes each atlas slot from the reported extents, so the hinted top row lands in the one-pixel padding that the drawn quad never samples. Cairo draws glyphs directly and is unaffected. Upstream: GNOME/gtk#8395 (symptom, no root cause yet) and GNOME/gtk#8340 (same extents-versus-raster mismatch seen as stale speckles).

Reproduces headlessly without a compositor: a GTK label at 15px under Xvfb with `GSK_RENDERER=gl LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1` loses the top row; Cairo keeps it; `gtk-font-rendering=manual` (hint metrics on) makes both renderers pixel-identical.

## Description Three small fixes where the UI acted on a location the user had left or never opened. **Sidebar highlight after a failed place (#860)** - A sidebar place is highlighted when clicked, before its location is validated. If validation was rejected (for example Network with no GVfs backend), the clicked row stayed highlighted while the pane stayed on the previous location. - The sidebar now resyncs its highlight on `LocationNavigationRejected`, so the open location's row is highlighted again. During a mount-then-open (NotMounted/Mountable), the highlight stays on the open location until the mounted place opens. A failed or cancelled mount no longer leaves the wrong row highlighted. **Abandoned Extract to (#864)** - A failed Extract to (for example a read-only destination) left `pending_navigate` set. The next foreground Extract here then navigated into the abandoned folder. - `OperationFailed` now takes `pending_navigate` right away and passes it only to the password-retry dialog. #808/#827 still work: a retried Extract to still opens its destination. - `OperationCancelled` also drops it. This covers a cancelled foreground Move to, which leaked the same cell. Cancelling an archive extraction already used the value in the `ArchiveCompleted` it emits first, so that path is unchanged. **Columns terminal folder (#867)** - Clicking a folder in Columns opens it as the active column, but the pointer stays over the parent column, which owns the fallback directory. Ctrl+Alt+T then opened the terminal in the parent listing rather than the clicked folder. - In Columns, when the pointer's column has exactly one selected folder and that folder is open as the active column, the terminal now opens there. Otherwise the fallback is unchanged: - hovering an ancestor column further up still uses that column's own directory - List, Icons, keyboard navigation, and context-menu Open in Terminal are unchanged - `docs/keyboard-navigation.md` describes the rule. ## Visual evidence Captured in an isolated E2E session (private Xvfb and D-Bus, `GIO_USE_VFS=local`, test fixtures). | Issue | Scenario | Before | After | |---|---|---|---| | #860 | Click Home, then Network (no GVfs backend), close the error |
Network stays highlighted while Home is open |
Home highlighted again (the Network outline is keyboard focus after Escape) | | #864 | Extract to a read-only `locked` folder fails; then Extract here `later.zip` |
navigates into the empty `locked` folder |
stays put with `later.txt` selected | #867 state when Ctrl+Alt+T is pressed (identical before and after): The stub `xdg-terminal-exec` launch log for #867: | | Before | After | |---|---|---| | Columns: click `documents`, pointer over its parent, Ctrl+Alt+T | `--dir=` | `--dir=/documents` | ## How to test 1. **Sidebar (#860).** Start Strata with `GIO_USE_VFS=local`. Click **Home**, then **Network**, and close the "Unable to open location" dialog. **Expected:** Home is highlighted, and the Network row is not. 2. **Extract to (#864).** Make a folder with `chmod 555`. Right-click a `.zip` → **Extract to…** → choose that folder; close the permission error. Then right-click another archive → **Extract here**. **Expected:** the pane stays in the original folder, with the extracted file selected there. 3. **Terminal (#867).** In Columns, click a folder so its column opens, keep the pointer over the parent column, and press **Ctrl+Alt+T**. **Expected:** the terminal opens in the clicked folder. With the pointer over an ancestor column further up, it opens in that column's directory as before. **Expected result:** as stated under each step. ## Related issue Closes #860 Closes #864 Closes #867

comments.author: wmfeht
comments.body:
Still reproducible on `main` at `0a086aa` (v1.0.0).

A failed place click still highlights the row before navigation is accepted, and nothing puts the highlight back on the location that stayed open.

`SidebarState::bind_place_row` in `src/ui/window/sidebar.rs` calls `select_sidebar_row` and then `Browser::navigate_location`. Network is built with `append_place`, which uses `PlaceNavigation::Validate`, so `navigate_location` (`src/app/browser.rs`) takes `navigate_validated_inner`. When `network://` has no backend, `validate_location_async` returns `LocationValidationError::BackendUnavailable` and the browser emits `LocationNavigationRejected`. The handler in `src/ui/browser/events.rs` shows “Unable to open location” and does not change the sidebar.

`sync_active_place` in `src/ui/window.rs` is the path that matches the highlight to `active_location()`. It runs for `Reset`, `ColumnAdded`, `ColumnsTruncated`, `ColumnsRelocated`, and `FocusChanged`, and after a sidebar rebuild. A rejected navigation emits none of those and leaves `active_location()` unchanged, so the clicked row stays `active` while the pane stays on the previous place.

No pull request references this issue. The sidebar feature note in wmfeht/strata-feature-map (`features/browser/sidebar/index.md`) still lists this as a known gap, and commits on `main` after that note do not change this path. Checked against current `main` sources; there is no test for a rejected place click.

Still reproducible on `main` (`0a086aa`).

`Ctrl+T` no longer opens a terminal. #1484 uses it for a new tab (`TAB_NEW` in `src/ui/keys/bindings/window.rs`). The terminal shortcut is now **Ctrl+Alt+T** (`TERMINAL` in the same file). The directory it receives is unchanged, and no pull request is set to close this issue.

author: l0gicgate
body:
## Description

The sidebar's icon rail was decided in four places with two different thresholds: the window-only rule (`preferred sidebar + one column`) in the layout tick, the header toggle, and the preview's rail release, and the preview's own rule (`sidebar + navigated columns + preview minimum`, with hysteresis) in its split sync. Showing the sidebar in a window where only the preview rule wanted the rail opened it at full width and then snapped it back to the rail. Rail rows also kept a hard-coded 24 px minimum from CSS while the header toggle scales with the text size, so below 100 % the rail icons drifted off the toggle's axis. And the rail was purely automatic: no way to see the full sidebar in a narrow window, or to keep the rail in a wide one.

- One fit rule. `PreviewDrawer::sidebar_fit` applies the preview rule whenever a preview, placeholder, or reserved Columns slot is present and the window rule otherwise; the preview tick, the header toggle, and the chooser all ask it. The separate layout tick and `release_sidebar_rail` are gone.
- `RailPolicy` turns fit observations into an edge-triggered automatic rail: a change in fit compacts an expanded sidebar once, space that returns releases only what it compacted, and an explicit choice overrides either way. It is pure and unit-tested.
- Rail rows, the update row, and the rail width take the scaled header-control size from code; the CSS minimums are gone.
- The header toggle steps the sidebar through its three modes: full, then the icon rail, then hidden, then full again. `Ctrl+B` (and `Ctrl+N` in 10xer mode) take the same step, and the tooltip names the next one. The rail step persists as the new `sidebar_compact` preference, which existing windows bind to live; stepping from hidden to full asks for the full sidebar even where space railed it automatically, so all three modes are reachable at any width. The chooser keeps its steps for the dialog only.
- The toggle tooltips (show, compact, hide) are localized in all eleven catalogs.

## Visual evidence

Pending owner upload. Local captures (private Xvfb, Cairo renderer):

| Capture | Caption |
| --- | --- |
| `evidence/before-rail-text-sizes-9-11-13-16.png` | Before: rail icons versus header toggle at text sizes 9, 11, 13, 16 (misaligned at 9 and 11) |
| `evidence/after-rail-text-sizes-9-11-13-16.png` | After: same four sizes, icons on the toggle's axis |
| `evidence/after-toggle-steps-720px.png` | After: 720 px window; automatic rail, then Ctrl+B steps hidden, full, compact, hidden |
| `evidence/after-toggle-steps-1200px.png` | After: 1200 px window; Ctrl+B steps full, compact, hidden, full |

## How to test

1. Open Strata in Columns and narrow the window until the sidebar rails (about 740 px at the default text size).
2. Press `Ctrl+B` (or click the header toggle) four times. The sidebar hides, comes back at full width and stays there, compacts to the rail, then hides again; the toggle's tooltip names the next step each time.
3. Widen the window with the rail showing: a rail you chose stays, an automatic one releases.
4. In a wide window press `Ctrl+B` once, then open a second window: both show the rail, and `sidebar_compact = true` is in `settings.toml`. Press it twice more in either window: both hide, then both expand.
5. Settings → Appearance: lower the text size to 9 and 11 with the sidebar railed. The rail icons sit under the header toggle.

**Expected result:** the sidebar never expands and snaps back; rail icons align with the toggle at every text size; one toggle reaches open, compact, and closed, and the compact step follows every window like the expanded one.

## Related issue

Closes #1602

issues.body:
### Strata version

0.21.0 (built from source, commit 6662d8d4)

### Installation method

Built from source

### Linux distribution and desktop environment

Arch Linux, Hyprland

### What happened?

At window widths where the sidebar collapses to its icon rail, three things go wrong:

1. **The rail flickers open.** Clicking a rail place such as Home while browsing a deep path in Columns animates the sidebar to full width, then it snaps back to the rail about a second later. The window rule (`preferred sidebar + one column`), the toggle handler, and the preview's own fit rule (`sidebar + navigated columns + preview minimum`, with hysteresis) each decide the rail independently with different thresholds, so a navigation that changes the column count makes them disagree.
2. **The rail drifts out of alignment at smaller text sizes.** The rail rows keep a hard-coded 24 px minimum from CSS while the header's sidebar toggle shrinks with the interface scale, so below 100 % the rail icons no longer sit under the toggle and the rail content is wider than the rail itself.
3. **The full sidebar cannot be shown at small widths.** The rail is purely automatic; there is no way to ask for the full sidebar while the window is narrow, and no way to choose the compact rail on a wide window.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open Strata in Columns at about 1250 px wide and navigate three levels deep so the sidebar rails.
2. Click **Home** in the rail. The sidebar expands fully, then collapses back to the rail.
3. Lower the text size in Settings → Appearance a few steps and compare the rail icons with the header toggle.
4. Try to show the full sidebar while railed: the toggle only hides and re-rails it.

### Expected behavior

- One rule decides whether the full sidebar fits, so toggling, navigating, and the preview never fight over the rail.
- Rail rows and rail width follow the same scaled size as the header toggle so the icons stay aligned at every text size.
- The sidebar has three explicit states: open, compact (rail), and closed. Automatic compaction still happens when space runs out, but the user can expand the sidebar anyway, choose compact on a wide window, or close it, and the choice persists like the existing expanded state.

### Screenshots or video

Screen recording available from the reporter.

### Relevant logs

_No response_

### Additional context

Regression surfaced after the Catppuccin icon work and the text-size scaling of header controls; the rail sizing in `src/style.css` was never scaled.

body: ## Description **Open Omarchy Update** ran `omarchy update` in a bare terminal (`xdg-terminal-exec -- omarchy update`). The window tiled beside the user's windows and closed as soon as the update ended, including on failure, so the output (and Omarchy's "review the output above" error) could not be read. Strata now runs `omarchy-launch-floating-terminal-with-presentation omarchy-update`, the command Omarchy's own menu uses (Update → Omarchy). That gives a floating, centred window that waits for a key after the update. When the launcher isn't on `PATH` or fails to start, Strata falls back to the current terminal launch, so nothing changes outside Omarchy. Both paths launch through `terminal::spawn_reaped`, so neither leaves a defunct child behind. If you'd rather fix this differently or in your own style, feel free to close this. No hard feelings. ## Visual evidence Before: Strata's command opens a tiled terminal (right). After: Strata uses Omarchy's launcher, the floating window in the centre. (It reads "already running" only because the tiled one held the update lock.) ## How to test 1. On Omarchy, install a Strata build with this change while the Omarchy repository has a newer `strata`, so Settings → Updates offers **Open Omarchy Update**. 2. Click **Open Omarchy Update**. 3. Without a pending release, run the two commands directly to compare: `xdg-terminal-exec -- omarchy update` (before) and `omarchy-launch-floating-terminal-with-presentation omarchy-update` (after). **Expected result:** the updater opens in Omarchy's floating, centred window with the Omarchy logo, leaves tiled windows alone, and after the update shows "Done! When an update is available, **Settings → Updates → Open Omarchy Update** runs `omarchy update` in a bare terminal. That causes two problems: 1. **The window closes as soon as the update ends, even when it fails.** The only exception is an update that needs a reboot, because Omarchy asks about that before it exits. Otherwise there's no chance to read what was updated or what went wrong. On failure, Omarchy prints "Something went wrong during the update! Omarchy's own menu (Update → Omarchy) avoids both. Its launcher opens a floating, centred window, shows the Omarchy logo, and after the update runs `omarchy-show-done` ("Done! Press any key to close..."), so the output stays until the user dismisses it. The button runs `xdg-terminal-exec -- omarchy update` (`omarchy_update_command` in `src/ui/settings.rs`). Omarchy's menu runs `omarchy-launch-floating-terminal-with-presentation omarchy-update` (`/usr/share/omarchy/default/omarchy/omarchy-menu.jsonc`, `update.omarchy`). ## Steps to reproduce 1. On Omarchy, with an older Strata installed from the Omarchy repository and a newer `strata` available there, open **Settings → Updates**. 2. Click **Open Omarchy Update**. 3. Without waiting for a release, the two commands can be compared directly: ``` xdg-terminal-exec -- omarchy update # what Strata runs: tiled, closes when done omarchy-launch-floating-terminal-with-presentation omarchy-update # what Omarchy runs: floating, waits for a key ``` ## Expected behavior Strata opens the updater the same way Omarchy does: a floating, centred window that stays open after the update finishes or fails, until the user presses a key, and leaves the user's tiled windows alone. ## Screenshots or video Left: an existing terminal.
