author: wmfeht
body: ## Description Two fixes: returning focus to filter results (#1549) and the GLib-CRITICAL logged by every item-menu action (#1569). **Return focus to the results' cursor hit (#1549)** - `focus_active` is the "return focus to the listing" path used by dialogs, Tab-in and filter/search dismissal. It now lands on the hit under the results' cursor when filter or search results replace the listing, and it leaves their selection unchanged. - Columns: with recursive hits, `ListView::grab_focus` returned to the row GTK last focused. When the cursor had moved without focus (Find and 10xer prompts step it that way), that row was an older hit. - List and Icons (sibling fix, same root cause; noted in #1533 but never filed): focus went to an unmapped row of the hidden directory listing behind the results. After cancelling a dialog opened from a hit, nothing visible had focus, and the next arrow key jumped to the sidebar or the filter field. - The cursor rule: over a 10xer fill, keep GTK's row (the cursor may rest on an unselected hit). Otherwise keep GTK's row if it is selected, or else move focus to the selected hit. Focus moves only; the selection is never rewritten. - A rename of a hit keeps its field focused, as a listing rename already did. - Returning from Quick Look onto results uses the same rule. **Item-menu actions log a GLib-CRITICAL (#1569)** - When the closed item menu is unparented, GTK reports every action the menu observes as removed while it iterates them. Menu items are `hidden-when=action-missing`. Hiding the "Open in…" submenu item (added in #1543) removed its submenu page, which freed the page's items while GTK was still iterating them. - The submenu item now sits alone in a nested section (nested sections draw no separator). Strata adds or removes it there instead of letting GTK hide it. Its entries and every other row keep `hidden-when`. - Clearing the menu model before unparenting did not help: GTK's rebuild takes the same path. **Known limits, not fixed here:** - In Columns, `focus_rebuilt_active_column` (the modal focus fallback, view switches, hiding the preview with the mouse) still focuses GTK's last row on recursive hits. It is a separate entry point with many callers. - In List and Icons, a `SelectionSetChanged` that takes focus while results show still targets the hidden listing. **Owner decisions:** - #1566 was dropped from this PR. - The List/Icons variant of #1549 is included. ## Visual evidence | Case (#1549) | Before | After | |---|---|---| | List: Ctrl+F `txt`, second hit focused, Shift+Delete, Escape | | | | List: then Up | | | | Icons: same steps, then Left | | | The fill on a hit is the selection, and the outline is the keyboard focus ring. In Icons the selected label fill marks the cursor. #1569 is log-only (N/A for screenshots). Before the fix, choosing Copy on a folder logged `GLib-CRITICAL: g_hash_table_iter_next: assertion 'ri->version == ri->hash_table->version' failed` twice; after the fix, the log has none. ## How to test **#1549 (List or Icons)** 1. Open a folder that has a few `.txt` files, some of them in subfolders. Press Ctrl+F with Include subfolders on and type `txt`. 2. Press Down to enter the results, then Down (Right in Icons) to reach the second hit. 3. Press Shift+Delete, then Escape to cancel the dialog. 4. Press Up (Left in Icons). **Expected result:** after the cancel, the second hit has the focus ring, and Up/Left moves to the first hit. Before, nothing had focus and the key went to the filter field or the sidebar. **#1569** 1. Run Strata from a terminal. 2. Right-click a folder in List view and choose Copy, Properties or Pin to sidebar. 3. Right-click the folder again (the menu still shows "Open in…"), then right-click a file (no "Open in…"). **Expected result:** no `GLib-CRITICAL` or `Gtk-CRITICAL` is logged. ## Related issue Closes #1549 Closes #1569

body: ## Description With word wrap off, rendered documents (Markdown and the other rendered formats) clipped long lines at the pane edge with no way to scroll to them. Source rows already widen to their text width when unwrapped. Rendered document rows only got a height, so they stayed as wide as the pane. - **Unwrapped rows widen to their longest line,** so the list grows past the viewport and the existing horizontal scrollbar works. - **Rows start at the left edge while unwrapped.** `ContentColumn` centred each row in the list's full width, so once one row widened the list, shorter rows were centred far to the right and disappeared. Wrapped previews are unchanged. While unwrapped, content in panes wider than 1280px now starts at the left instead of being centred. - **Live wrap toggles resize rows after GTK has re-laid them out.** Measuring right after `set_wrap_mode` returned the previous mode's height, which left blank gaps when turning wrap off and one-line rows when turning it back on. There's no new test: the repository's guidelines exclude layout and clipping tests, so this was checked with the screenshots below. If you'd rather fix this differently or in your own style, feel free to close this. No hard feelings. ## Visual evidence | | Before | After | |---|---|---| | Wrap off: long lines are clipped, nothing scrolls. After: scrolled sideways to the end of the lines. | | | | Wrap turned on while open: each paragraph is cut to one line. After: the text reflows. | | | | Wrap turned off again while open: blank gaps between rows. After: no gaps, rows sit at their unwrapped height, no gaps. | | | ## How to test 1. Turn on **Render documents by default** and preview a Markdown file with lines longer than the pane (prose, a list item and a code block). 2. Turn word wrap off and scroll sideways (touchpad, Shift+wheel or the scrollbar). 3. Toggle wrap on and off a few times with the preview open, then reopen the preview. **Expected result:** with wrap off, every line can be scrolled into view and all rows share the same left edge. With wrap on, the preview wraps and centres as before. Toggling never leaves blank gaps or one-line rows. ## Related issue Closes #1610

issues.body: ## Strata version 1.0.0 (official release tarball); first seen on 0.21.0 (Omarchy repository package `strata` 0.21.0-2) ## Installation method Other: Omarchy package repository (`pacman -S strata`) ## Linux distribution and desktop environment Omarchy 4.0.4 (Arch Linux), Hyprland 0.56.2, Wayland ## What happened? With word wrap off, a rendered Markdown preview cuts long lines at the pane's right edge, and there is no way to reach the rest. No horizontal scrollbar appears, and neither a sideways touchpad swipe nor Shift+wheel moves the text. Source previews scroll sideways as expected, and so did Markdown when the wrap toggle was added in #903. Toggling wrap while the preview is open has a second problem: paragraphs keep the height from the previous mode. Turning wrap on leaves each paragraph one line tall, so the rest of its text is hidden; turning it off leaves large blank gaps between paragraphs. Reopening the preview fixes both. ## Steps to reproduce 1. Turn on **Render documents by default**. 2. Preview a Markdown file with lines longer than the preview pane. 3. Turn word wrap off in the preview header. 4. Try to scroll sideways (touchpad swipe, Shift+wheel, or look for a horizontal scrollbar). ## Expected behavior With wrap off, long lines can be scrolled horizontally, as in source previews. Toggling wrap while the preview is open lays the paragraphs out at their new height. ## Screenshots or video First: wrap off, lines cut at the edge, nothing to scroll. Second: wrap turned on while open, each paragraph cut to one line. Third: wrap turned off again, blank gaps between the paragraph and the list items. ## Relevant logs None. ## Additional context In `src/ui/virtual_preview.rs`, source rows widen to their measured text width when unwrapped (`apply_source_view_wrap`), so the list grows and the horizontal scrollbar has something to scroll. Rendered document rows only get a height (`size_document_text_view`), so they stay as wide as the pane and their text is clipped.

author: wmfeht
body: ## Description Consistent Trash handling on FUSE mounts, implementing the "Consistent Trash handling on FUSE mounts" proposal. GIO decides that a FUSE mount supports Trash when its root is writable, so sshfs, rclone, s3fs, mergerfs and cloud mounts usually report `access::can-trash = TRUE`. The trash attempt then fails partway, and the error depends on which step failed. Before this change, Delete on such a mount showed the raw GIO error (for example `g_rename() failed: Operation not permitted`) in a dialog with only **Close**. It offered no way to delete, failed the same way on every Delete, and left an empty `.Trash-$uid/{info,files}` on the remote. Shift+Delete also promised "permanently deleted… cannot be undone" on cloud mounts whose provider keeps deleted items (#1571). **Trash failures (new `adapters::trash_support`)** - One classifier for every trash call site. `NOT_SUPPORTED` still means "Trash unsupported" everywhere. On a FUSE mount, `PERMISSION_DENIED`, `FAILED`, `INVALID_ARGUMENT` and `G_FILE_ERROR` codes (GLib writes `.trashinfo` with `g_file_set_contents`) count as unsupported only after a quick check that creates nothing and runs off the main thread. The check requires that the item isn't on the home device, is still in place, the mount root answers `stat`, and the folder's owner, mode and sticky bit let the user remove it. `access()` alone isn't trusted, because sshfs answers it with success. A disconnected sshfs or a genuine permission problem keeps the raw error. Local disks keep today's narrow mapping. - A confirmed refusal is remembered in memory for that mount, keyed by kernel mount ID, device and mount point, so a remount starts fresh. The folder probe then reports no Trash, so the existing #1425 Cancel-first dialog opens up front and **Move to Trash** is hidden, as on tmpfs. After the failure, the affected columns reload so this applies to the next Delete. **Reload** (F5) forgets every recorded mount without touching any of them, so a fixed mount can try Trash again. - After a failed batch, empty trash folders that the attempt created are removed. Removal never recurses, never touches a folder that existed before or holds anything, and refuses symlinks. - Other call sites: - Replace on such a mount keeps today's atomic permanent replace, which already stays out of undo. The conflict dialog now says replaced items will be deleted. - Merge still aborts, with an explanation instead of the raw error. - Undo of created items still deletes permanently. - Undo of a grouping removes the group folder only if it is empty, instead of failing. - Per-item messages: "This location doesn't support Trash." (the retry button offers the deletion), "This location is read-only.", "Not enough space to move to Trash." **Wording by location (#1571)** - Local disks, including `fuseblk` drives such as ntfs-3g and exfat-fuse and local FUSE layers such as mergerfs and gocryptfs, keep "Permanently delete… This action cannot be undone." - Network and cloud locations (FUSE mounts other than `fuseblk`, NFS, SMB, GVfs URIs) now get: - the title "Delete N items without Trash?" and the button "Delete N items"; - the size line "… will be deleted"; - the text "Strata can't undo this; whether it can be recovered depends on the storage provider"; - a **Delete without Trash** context-menu item, retry button and operation label. - A mixed selection uses the local wording. - The Trash-unavailable dialog is now made of separate paragraphs: "This location doesn't support Trash.", then "Trash isn't available on ()." when a refusal was recorded, then the wording for the location. 13 messages and 2 labels were added in all 11 languages, and the 3 combined messages were retired. The translations were written for this PR and haven't been reviewed by native speakers. **Not in this PR / deviations from the proposal** - No production debug hook for E2E. The CI container has no FUSE, so the cache-to-dialog flow is covered by GTK tests with a test-only mount table. The existing `/dev/shm` E2E scenario still covers the Cancel-first dialog. - Compress with Replace still moves the old archive to Trash in its synchronous publish step, so it keeps the raw error there. - Folders opened through a symlink: the classifier, cleanup and folder probe resolve the real mount off the main thread. The dialog's mount sentence and the remote wording look only at the path as shown, so the main thread never touches a possibly hung mount. Through a symlink alias they fall back to the generic, local wording. - Persistent or per-mount "Use Trash" settings (D2, D5) and provider-declared recovery (D6) are left for follow-ups, as the proposal recommends. ## Visual evidence Captured on a private Xvfb display through the E2E harness. The fixture's "Cloud Drive" folder is a real FUSE mount (`fuse.clouddrive`): a small loopback filesystem that refuses renames into `.Trash-*`, which is how many cloud and sshfs mounts fail. "Before" is upstream `main` @ e7e43f2a. | Before | After | |---|---| | | | | **Delete:** the raw `g_rename()` error and only **Close**. `.Trash-1000/{info,files}` is left on the mount. | **Delete:** a Cancel-first confirmation that names the mount and its type, with the cloud wording. No `.Trash-1000` is left behind. | | | | | **Delete again:** the same failure. | **Delete again:** the same confirmation opens up front, without another trash attempt. | | | | | **Context menu after the failure:** **Move to Trash** is still offered. | **Context menu after the failure:** only **Delete without Trash**. The highlighted first row is the menu's initial keyboard focus, not a selection. | | | | | **Shift+Delete on the cloud mount:** "permanently deleted… cannot be undone". | **Shift+Delete on the cloud mount:** "deleted without using Trash… depends on the storage provider". Shift+Delete keeps its confirm focus. | | | | | | **Shift+Delete on a local disk:** unchanged, "Permanently delete… cannot be undone". | ## How to test Use a FUSE mount that refuses the trash rename, for example sshfs to a folder whose server rejects renames into `.Trash-$uid`, or an rclone remote without VFS cache. 1. Open a folder on the mount. Right-click a file: **Move to Trash** and **Delete without Trash** are offered. 2. Press Delete. The dialog reads "Delete 1 item without Trash?" with Cancel focused, "This location doesn't support Trash.", "Trash isn't available on (fuse.).", and the provider sentence. Press Enter: nothing is deleted. 3. Check the mount root: no `.Trash-$uid` folder was left behind. 4. Press Delete again. The same dialog opens immediately, without another trash attempt. Right-click: **Move to Trash** is hidden. 5. Press F5, then Delete. Strata tries Trash again. 6. Disconnect the server (`kill` the sshfs process without unmounting) and press Delete: the raw I/O error appears, not "doesn't support Trash". 7. On a local disk, Shift+Delete still reads "Permanently delete 1 item?… This action cannot be undone." **Expected result:** On FUSE mounts without working Trash, Delete always confirms, with Cancel focused, before deleting. It explains why, leaves nothing on the remote, and stops retrying Trash until Reload. Cloud and network deletions no longer promise permanence, and local disks keep the strong warning. ## Related issue Closes #1571 Refs #66, #1425, #1590 This takes the location-dependent approach to #1571 instead of the draft #1572, which changes the wording everywhere, including local disks.

### Strata version
Source build 48187c24 (external file providers, merged in #1385).

### Installation method
Built from source.

### Environment
Arch Linux, Hyprland; Cirrove 0.2.0-canary.2 FUSE cloud mount.

### What happened?
Shift+Delete and the fallback after local Trash is unavailable promise permanent deletion with no recovery. GIO's delete operation bypasses the local Trash, but a cloud filesystem can map it to the provider's recoverable deletion. Cirrove does so, making the confirmation misleading.

### Steps to reproduce

2. Press Shift+Delete, or choose the direct delete action after local Trash is unavailable.
3. Read the confirmation and delete an explicitly disposable fixture.
4. The cloud provider retains the item in its recovery area despite Strata's promise.

### Expected behavior
Describe bypassing the local Trash, preserve the warning about irreversible deletion on local drives, and explain that cloud recovery depends on the provider. Keep the same confirmation, cancellation and keyboard safety behavior.

### Evidence and logs
No private filenames, credentials or provider bodies are required to reproduce this wording issue. Visual evidence will accompany the fix.

author: ogarza
body:
## Description

Strata's no-clobber file operations relied on `renameat2` flags (`RENAME_NOREPLACE`, `RENAME_EXCHANGE`), and native copies went through GIO. Many mounts reject those flags with `EINVAL`, among them NFS, sshfs, ntfs-3g and other libfuse2 daemons, 9p, ceph and older ZFS.
- **Moves:** in v0.21.0, moves on those mounts failed (#1530). Main has #1515's fallback, so they work but write every byte twice.
- **Replace:** it fails there wherever Trash is unavailable.
- **GIO copies:**
  - they lose folder modes and times, and `user.*` xattrs on read-only items;
  - merges overwrite;
  - a move that has to copy deletes everything inside its source after checking only the top item.
- **Names:** a name the destination can't store (`a:b`, `CON`, too long) fails copies on most mounts or changes silently on FAT, and symlinks fail copies onto FAT and SMB.

This PR makes these operations work on such mounts. It never overwrites a destination that appeared meanwhile, and never deletes a source the copy doesn't hold. It delivers steps 1–3 of umbrella #1590, each as its own group of commits.

**Step 1: placement, Replace/Merge, rename, Trash**
- **One placement ladder for every site:** move, staged copy publish, restore, archive extract/compress publish, symlink copy, undo and rename. It tries these in order:
  1. `renameat2(NOREPLACE)`.
  2. For files, `linkat`. The link counts only once the new name reports the source's identity; the old name is then unlinked after an identity check.
  3. For folders, an exclusive empty placeholder that is renamed over.
  4. On mounts with neither `NOREPLACE` nor usable hard links (sshfs, vboxsf, rclone, s3fs), an exclusive empty placeholder that is checked and then renamed over.
  5. A copy, only across devices or where no step can place the item.

  `EEXIST` stays authoritative, and the ladder tells apart the three meanings of `EINVAL`: flag unsupported, invalid name, and folder into itself.
- **The reserved-name step has a narrow window.**
  - The placed item and any existing destination are never at risk. Only a program that overwrites that exact name between the check and the rename loses its write.
  - GLib, and so Nautilus, checks and then renames with no placeholder. So there, even a program that creates the name exclusively in between is overwritten.
- **sshfs and other libfuse daemons without `use_ino`** give each hard link its own inode number. Strata learns this from a probe on its own names and never uses those links to prove a placement.
- **Capabilities are learned per mount** and cached by mount ID. The cache is dropped when the mount table changes.
- **Replace and Merge work without Trash or `EXCHANGE`.**
  - The original is moved aside to a hidden name, the new item is published, and the aside copy is then deleted by identity, with rollback on failure.
  - `EXCHANGE` is used only on in-kernel local filesystems, never FUSE. exfat-fuse reports success for it but simply overwrites, which on main destroyed the original when Trash was unavailable.
  - A same-filesystem move with Replace renames instead of copying.
- **Rename (F2) and undo rename go through the ladder.** Case-only renames (`foo` → `Foo`) work on vfat, exFAT, SMB, casefold ext4 and exfat-fuse. GVfs locations keep GIO.
- **Trash results are verified.** Some FUSE mounts report success without moving anything (GLib #4060).
- **Identity checks** compare file type and birth time as well as device and inode, because ext4, NFS, CIFS and ntfs3 reuse inode numbers immediately.
- **Archives:**
  - ntfs3 reports zero blocks for small files, and the tar crate used to write zeros for them. TAR now stores members in full.
  - Extraction no longer sets symlink times on FUSE, where sshfs applies them to the link's target.

**Step 2: the copy engine**
- **One descriptor-based engine** replaces GIO wherever both ends are native paths:
  - pastes, Duplicate and Keep Both;
  - cross-filesystem moves;
  - Replace stages and merges;
  - Trash restores.

  It runs on worker threads, opens everything beneath pinned folders, and never replaces an entry. GVfs locations keep GIO.
- **Only complete copies appear.**
  - On local POSIX filesystems a file is written to an `O_TMPFILE` and linked to its name when done.
  - Elsewhere the copy is built in a hidden `.strata-copy-*` stage, which is safe to delete, and published through the step 1 ladder.
  - Keep Both picks its number when the copy is placed, so a name taken meanwhile gets the next one.
- **Data:**
  - Each file is copied with `FICLONE`, then chunked `copy_file_range`, then read/write. Network `copy_file_range` is gated on the kernel releases with the NFS, FUSE and SMB fixes, and NFS requests are capped at 2 MiB.
  - Every native file reports byte progress.
  - Sparse files from local disks keep their holes, except onto FAT, exFAT and NTFS (kernel or FUSE), which would zero-fill each skipped hole in one uncancellable call.
- **Metadata:**
  - Order: owner, then xattrs (ACLs last), then mode, then times. `user.*` xattrs survive on read-only items.
  - Folders keep their mode, times, owner and xattrs. Read-only folders get their exact mode in a last pass.
  - Copies into a setgid folder keep its group.
  - Special bits are dropped when the owner can't be kept.
- **Names:**
  - Two source names the destination can't tell apart (`Makefile` and `makefile` on FAT, exFAT, SMB or casefold) are saved as `makefile (1)` and reported. Undoing the move gives the name back.
  - Entries left by lost NFS replies are adopted.
- **Hard links** stay linked within one copied item where the destination keeps them.
- **Special files:** named pipes are recreated, while sockets and devices are left out and reported.
- **Merges never overwrite.**
  - Incoming items are built in a stage inside each merged folder and renamed in.
  - A name taken meanwhile gets the next number and is reported.
  - A stopped merge leaves nothing partial.
- **Moves that copy** delete a source entry only if it still matches what was copied:
  - The comparison uses type, size and times, plus inode, change time and link count where those are stable.
  - Hard-linked names the move removes itself are accounted for.
  - On coarse-timestamp mounts (FAT, exFAT, sshfs), a file modified within one tick of being copied is compared by content first.
  - A file written during its copy is copied again, and kept if it changes again.
  - Kept entries are reported and left out of Undo.
- **Durability:** nothing that only the copy holds is deleted before the destination is flushed. That covers move sources, Replace originals, merge set-asides, archive originals and restored Trash copies.
  - Each filesystem is flushed the way the lab measured that it reaches the device. The design assumed `syncfs`; vfat and exFAT also need a folder `fsync`, and SMB and other FUSE mounts sync each file.
  - ntfs-3g and exfat-fuse, recognised through udev, get one folder sync per batch, which flushes the whole device.
  - Deletions are batched: 256 items, 1 GiB or 5 s.
  - More than eight cross-disk file moves run in parallel.
- **Trash restore** copies through the engine where nothing can place the item.
  - Metadata is best-effort.
  - The copy is flushed, then the Trash copy is deleted entry by entry.
  - Anything left behind keeps its `.trashinfo` and is reported.
  - A restore cancelled mid-copy ends as a cancel, and its partial copy is removed. If the removal can't be proven, the item is reported as failed.
  - Merge undo restores an original only over a path it could check.
- **Undo of a merge or Replace keeps later edits.**
  - When a merge or a Replace puts an item over an original that went to the Trash, Strata records what it placed (up to 100,000 entries per operation).
  - Undo deletes the item only if it is unchanged, using the same checks as moves.
  - Otherwise the whole item stays, its original stays in the Trash with its `.trashinfo`, and the dialog says so.
  - On main, undo permanently deleted whatever was at that path, edits included.
  - Where the Trash is unavailable, undo also deleted the items a merge created, silently. Now it deletes only those it recorded and finds unchanged, and reports the rest. Where the Trash works, they still go to the Trash.
- **Completion report:** one event carries renamed, left-out and left-behind items.
  - One short renamed line shows as a notice; more show in an information dialog.
  - Anything left out or left behind shows a warning.
  - A cancelled or failed transfer, and a restore or merge undo that completes with errors, shows one dialog: its outcome, then the report.
  - In a cancel's summary, an item the cancel cut off and rolled back counts as not attempted, not failed. This applies to local transfers, Trash deletes, restores and merge undos.
- **Responsiveness:**
  - Paste, restore and delete planning run off the main thread.
  - Folder monitors ignore the phantom events of unnamed temporary files, and query each linked-in file once.
- **Docs and lab:**
  - `docs/filesystem-compatibility.md` gains a "Copying" section and the residual limits; the lab's flush and claim measurements are in a comment on this PR.
  - `scripts/fslab` now counts device cache flushes per mount.
  - The full unit suite was rerun on all 14 lab mounts. Every failure left is a test portability issue or a fixture limit of the mount.
- **Speed on the lab** (2,000 × 1 KiB, debug build): vfat with `flush`, 26 s against GIO's 208 s; sshfs, 2–12 s against about 100 s; the rest on par. On exfat-fuse and ntfs-3g, a 300-file move went from about 300 device flushes to 2.

**Decisions taken with the owner during step 2:**
- batched flushes with parallel moves;
- hard links kept within one item;
- pipes recreated, everything else skipped and reported;
- setgid group kept;
- one flush per batch on ntfs-3g and exfat-fuse;
- content recheck of recently modified files on coarse-timestamp mounts;
- SMB opens refused during the client's deferred close are retried, for at most 10 s;
- one dialog per outcome, never a stacked report;
- items a cancel rolled back count as not attempted;
- a cancel never reports the transfer as finished, as decided in #1193.

**Decided by the lead along the way:**
- holes kept as with `cp --sparse=auto`;
- a name taken during a merge is numbered and reported;
- undo gives alias-numbered names back;
- leftovers are not auto-deleted (step 8).

**Step 3: mount profile and names**
- **One name profile per mount**, read off the main thread from the mount behind the destination, through symlinks and nested mounts: mountinfo, udev's format for `fuseblk`, and `statfs`'s name length. It is cached with the mount's capabilities and kept for a whole operation. GVfs locations, and their folders under `/run/user/$UID/gvfs`, get rules by address.
- **Names brought from another filesystem are fixed before anything is created**, and reported:
  - FAT, exFAT, NTFS, SMB without POSIX extensions and MTP: `< > : " \ | ? *` and control characters become `_`, trailing dots and spaces are dropped, malformed UTF-8 becomes `_`.
  - `CON` becomes `CON_` wherever Windows rules apply. `aux.c` and `con.txt` keep their names on FAT, exFAT and ntfs3 (the Windows 11 rule), and get `_` on ntfs-3g, ntfs3 with `windows_names` and SMB without POSIX.
  - Length counts the destination's unit: bytes on POSIX, NFS, SMB and SFTP; UTF-16 units on FAT, exFAT and NTFS; Samba folders 213 bytes, MTP 254 units. A cut keeps the extension and whole grapheme clusters, and every number Strata adds fits.
  - A name that needs no change keeps it. Duplicates, restores and moves within one filesystem keep every name.
- **Names within one paste:** top-level items from two folders that share a name are numbered before copying on every destination, and reported as taken. FAT, exFAT and SMB without POSIX extensions number case pairs before copying; casefolded folders look a later spelling up once first. An item that meets a duplicate's original is asked about as before, and planned items are copied before duplicates and resolved conflicts, so every item lands.
- **Undo gives fixed names back**, deepest first, also between native and GVfs locations; redo fixes them again.
- **A name the mount still refuses** is retried under stricter Windows rules, alone and then together, and the first accepted is used and reported. Only mounts whose type hides their rules (sshfs and other FUSE daemons, unidentified `fuseblk`, unknown types) remember what worked. If none works, the error reads "The name isn't valid at this location" or "The name is too long", naming the item.
- **Symbolic links the destination can't hold are left out and reported**, and the paste goes on: on FAT and exFAT without asking, on SMB without POSIX extensions after its first refusal, on NTFS per refused target, and, wherever names must be UTF-8, for a target that isn't. A move keeps those links at the source, and Undo leaves those items out, naming them.
- **Archive extraction** fixes member names and the archive's folder name, keeps members whose names became one apart (`10_00 (2)/`), retries refused names, leaves out links and hard links to them, reports, and finishes.
- **The conflict prompt sees the name the paste will use**, worked out off the main thread; the paste's UI-thread conflict check is gone.
  - "“a:b” will be saved as “a_b” in this location." opens the prompt where that name is taken, instead of failing.
  - Replace, Merge and Keep Both act on that name, a merge prompt says fixed names overwrite, and Keep Both is offered for moves.
  - A slow destination shows "Preparing items…" with Cancel, in a copy's docked row or a move's dialog. Closing the view dismisses it, and the transfer copies nothing.
- **Typed names** (rename, new file or folder, archive name) that the location would store as another are refused before anything changes, naming the characters (by code point where invisible), the trailing space or period, the reserved name or the length. 10xer prompts stay open.
- **Renaming a GVfs address no backend serves** (`smb://` without GVfs) fails with the backend message, where GLib ended the process (no UI route to it was found).
- **Moves that copy check more:**
  - A file whose copy's reads ended away from its size is copied again.
  - Without multigrain timestamps (Linux before 6.13, or other than ext4, XFS, btrfs and tmpfs), files modified within 100 ms of the read are compared by content.
  - The copy must keep the size and time it was left with, so a file put in its place, even on its freed inode within one tick (ntfs3), keeps the source.
  - Where inode numbers aren't stable (FAT, FUSE, vboxsf, `noserverino`), type, birth time, size and time identify the copy. Kernel exFAT moves a folder's birth time at each rename into it, so there folders count by type.
  - Moves from SMB force each stat they record, so moving or undoing right after a paste or a read there no longer keeps unchanged entries.
  - A selected link that sshfs makes again counts as its copy if it points where the original did.
- **ntfs-3g long names:** renaming over an entry, ntfs-3g cuts a name of 237 UTF-16 units or more and leaves a stray. Strata never does that there or on an unidentified `fuseblk`: files are linked, folders renamed once the name is found free, so nothing is copied.
- **Completion report:** new sections for names not allowed, names too long, links left out, and names Undo couldn't give back.
- **CI:** the Rust test container gets a tmpfs `/tmp`, so copy tests get `O_TMPFILE`; tests that force the named stage cover the fallback. Its kernel is 6.6, so the seam links unnamed files as Linux 6.10 does on every host, and rows that replace a fresh copy wait for a later birth tick.
- **Review:** a collaborator's review was merged in: operations split into subsystems, and published identities kept through moves and undo.
- **Docs and lab:**
  - `docs/filesystem-compatibility.md` gains a "Names" section; the lab's name measurements are in a comment on this PR.
  - A corpus of lab names, 258–768-byte names, links and a tar archive was copied, moved, undone and extracted on all 14 lab mounts plus ntfs3 with `windows_names`: every name landed as planned, servers listed what the client sent, and exfat-fuse got no malformed, forbidden or overlong name. Its gaps are fixed above and were rechecked there.
  - `local_operations::` was rerun on all 14 mounts. Every failure left is a fixture or preset the mount can't hold, or a known limit.

**Decisions taken with the owner during step 3:**
- device names: the Windows 11 rule where they are stored, the full rule where refused or mangled;
- a fixed name in a merge overwrites like any same name, and the prompt says so;
- typed names are refused with the reason, never fixed;
- GVfs rules by address, `/run/user/…/gvfs` included;
- archives fix names, keep folders apart, leave out links, retry refused names, report and finish;
- Undo leaves out items whose links stayed behind, naming them;
- a merged folder re-reads name rules only on another device;
- the `smb://` rename crash is fixed here;
- same-tick checks: reads that end away from the size, and content checks where timestamps aren't multigrain;
- copies on unstable inode numbers accepted by type, birth time, size and time; kernel exFAT folders by type;
- every stat a move records from SMB forced; SMB without POSIX extensions planned as case-folding;
- ntfs-3g folders of 237 units or more renamed once their name is found free;
- identical top-level names numbered everywhere; an item meeting a duplicate's original prompts as before;
- non-UTF-8 link targets left out where names must be UTF-8;
- selected links moved onto sshfs accepted by target;
- a tmpfs `/tmp` for CI's test container.

**Decided by the lead along the way:**
- malformed UTF-8 becomes `_`, not U+FFFD; `CON_`, not `__CON`;
- NTFS case pairs are not numbered;
- only mounts whose rules can't be read learn, and only what a refused name needed;
- Keep Both is offered for moves; links left out make it "Completed with errors";
- extraction keeps `name (2)`; a broken link at the target counts as a conflict;
- an unidentified `fuseblk` mount gets the ntfs-3g long-name rule;
- a later spelling is looked up before copying, never copied twice;
- "Preparing items…" instead of "0/0" in a copy's docked row;
- planned items go before duplicates and resolved conflicts; a prompted name keeps the prompt's reason.

**Steps 4–8** continue in the follow-up PR #1729, tracked in #1590.

**Known limits:**
- **SMB:**
  - On SMB2/3, `NOREPLACE` is enforced only on the client.
  - After this machine writes a file on a share, the client refuses to open another hard-linked name of it until its deferred close ends (`closetimeo`, 1 s by default). Strata retries for that plus 0.5 s, at most 10 s; a writer that keeps the file open still fails the copy.
  - A move from a share takes one more round trip per entry, and a share set to compare case still gets `(1)` for case pairs.
- **Lost replies** (`EIO`, `ETIMEDOUT`) to the rename over a placeholder: on sshfs and vboxsf, where an inode number can't tell the placeholder from the moved item, the empty placeholder can remain and the item is reported as unconfirmed rather than guessed; on NFS and other mounts with stable inode numbers, a placeholder still in place proves the rename failed, so it is removed and the error reported.
- **SFTP without `posix-rename@openssh.com`:** nothing can be renamed over a placeholder. Moves and copies fall back to copying, as before; file renames, archive publication and setting a file aside are refused.
- **Identity and timestamps:**
  - Mounts without birth time (NFSv3, ntfs-3g, exfat-fuse, sshfs) can't tell a recreated item of the same type, size and times from the original. On kernel exFAT and vfat, neither can a move tell a copy replaced so within its 10 ms birth tick.
  - A server or FUSE daemon clock more than 100 ms behind ours (2 s on sshfs) can hide a same-size rewrite.
  - A move from kernel exFAT keeps a whole source folder that another program renamed something into. Onto exFAT, a merged folder renamed away and replaced passes; its copies stay in the renamed folder.
- **Waiting out the tick:** a move of a just-saved file takes up to 2 s longer on FAT and exFAT (3 s on sshfs), and up to 100 ms longer elsewhere without multigrain timestamps.
- **ntfs-3g long folder names:** an empty folder made at the name between the check and the rename is replaced, and ntfs-3g leaves a cut entry beside it.
- **Hard links** are kept within one copied item and one merged folder, never from plain SMB shares or sshfs.
- **GVfs destinations** get no flush and no content check, rules by address only, and no retry of a refused name.
- **Names:**
  - Only names are checked, not paths: SMB and sshfs refuse paths of about 4 KB, and Windows' `MAX_PATH` is not predicted.
  - Inside copied folders, only FAT, exFAT and SMB without POSIX extensions plan case aliases; elsewhere the destination's "exists" decides. NTFS keeps `Makefile` and `makefile` apart.
  - Windows 10 cannot open `aux.c` or `con.txt`, which FAT, exFAT and ntfs3 keep.
  - Unsupported: vfat with a legacy `iocharset` and without `utf8`, exFAT or cifs with a non-UTF-8 code page, and msdos. udisks never mounts these.
  - Link targets are never rewritten, so a link to a renamed entry dangles. A link is judged by its first refusal.
- **Archives:** the folder named after the archive is not retried under stricter rules; where a mount with unknown rules refuses it, the output stays in the hidden staging folder. A member path component such as `c:notes` is refused as a drive prefix.
- **Leftovers:** a `.strata-copy-*` stage left by a crash or an unplug stays until it is deleted (step 8).
- **Not tested on real mounts:**
  - The batch limits were measured on loop devices in RAM, so real USB flush latency is unmeasured.
  - Restoring from Trash still matches by device and inode (step 6).
  - vboxsf, rclone, s3fs, ZFS, 9p, ceph and libfuse2 builds of exfat-fuse were never tried. Their behaviour is taken from their sources and tested through the seam.
  - Name rules on real `smb://` and `mtp://`, a Windows SFTP server's refusals, and extraction into a 237-unit folder name on ntfs-3g.
- **Not reproduced:** in one of four NFSv4.2 lab runs, a merge undo kept an untouched placed file.

| `:` and other Windows characters; malformed UTF-8 | "No such file or folder"; an overlong `/` or a surrogate broke the listing or crashed the daemon | Fixed before the daemon sees them, and reported |
| Symlinks | Copy failed (`ENOSYS`) | Left out and reported |

</details>

<details><summary><b>ntfs-3g</b></summary>

| Edge case | Before (main) | After (this PR) |
|---|---|---|
| Move within one volume | Copied twice, then the source deleted | Renamed: files linked, folders over a placeholder |
| Move or copy onto it from another disk (#1530) | Staged copy, then a second full copy | One copy, linked or renamed into place |
| Replace or Merge without Trash | Replace failed after the full copy; Merge refused | Original set aside |
| Restore | Folders copied; Trash copy deleted unflushed | Placed without copying |
| Flush before deleting | Removable `syncfs`, which flushed nothing | Recognised by udev: `syncfs` plus one folder `fsync` per batch; otherwise per file |
| Windows characters, trailing dots and spaces, device names (udisks sets `windows_names`) | Copy failed: "…: Invalid argument" | Fixed (`con.txt` saved as `con_.txt`) and reported |
| Folder named with 237 UTF-16 units or more (or a `fuseblk` mount udev can't name) | A move within copied it twice; F2 and extraction worked | Renamed (moves, F2, extraction) once the name is found free, not over a placeholder (ntfs-3g would cut the name); an empty folder made there in that instant is replaced |

</details>

<details><summary><b>ntfs3</b></summary>

| Edge case | Before (main) | After (this PR) |
|---|---|---|
| TAR and TAR.GZ of small files | Stored as zeros: silent data loss | Stored in full |
| Replace without Trash | Failed after the full copy (no `EXCHANGE`) | Original set aside |
| Restore by copying (rarely needed: restores rename) | Failed on ntfs3's `$LX*` attributes | `$LX*` never copied; restore copies pass |
| Item recreated with a reused inode number | Passed as the original | Told apart by birth time |
| Flush before deleting a moved source | Removable drives only | `syncfs`, which flushes the device |
| Windows characters and device names | Stored, though Windows can't open them; with `windows_names`, copy failed | Saved with `_`; `CON` as `CON_`, `aux.c` kept; with `windows_names`, every device name fixed |
| Malformed or overlong link targets (malformed on ntfs-3g too) | Copy failed | That link left out and reported |

</details>

<details><summary><b>vfat</b></summary>

| Edge case | Before (main) | After (this PR) |
|---|---|---|
| Replace without Trash | `EXCHANGE`, the original deleted at once | `EXCHANGE`; the original deleted only after the flush |
| Case aliases, including 8.3 short names | Numbered silently by an uppercase key | Numbered before copying by folded names when brought from another filesystem, else on the drive's own "exists"; reported; undo gives names back |
| FAT-invalid characters | Replaced silently, even renumbering a sibling that already had the name; malformed UTF-8 failed | Fixed by the Windows rules (malformed UTF-8 and `CON` too), reported, given back by undo; names needing no change kept |
| Symlinks | Copy failed | Left out without asking, and reported |
| Case-only rename | Refused: "already exists" | Works |
| Flush before deleting | `syncfs`, which flushed nothing | `syncfs` then a folder `fsync`, which flushes the drive |
| Same-size rewrite within the 2 s tick (no change time) | Deleted (no check at all) | Files modified within 2 s of the read are compared by content first; moving a just-saved file takes up to 2 s longer |
| Inode numbers reassigned after eviction | Compared (effect not measured) | Deletion compares type and birth time instead |

</details>

<details><summary><b>exFAT (kernel)</b></summary>

| Edge case | Before (main) | After (this PR) |
|---|---|---|
| Replace without Trash | Failed after the full copy (no `EXCHANGE`) | Original set aside |
| Case aliases, case-only rename | As vfat: numbered silently; renames refused | As vfat: numbered and reported; renames work |
| Windows characters, symlinks | As vfat | As vfat |
| Flush before deleting | `syncfs`, which flushed nothing | `syncfs` then a folder `fsync` |
| Same-size rewrite within a tick | Deleted (no check at all) | Compared by content within FAT's 2 s window. A source folder that had an entry renamed into or within it stays whole (exFAT moves its birth time) |

</details>

<details><summary><b>ext4</b></summary>

| Edge case | Before (main) | After (this PR) |
|---|---|---|
| New file copy | Hidden stage, then GIO's own temp file and an `fsync` per top-level file | Unnamed `O_TMPFILE`, linked when complete: a crash leaves nothing; no `fsync` for plain copies |
| Replace without Trash | `EXCHANGE`, the original deleted at once | `EXCHANGE`; the original deleted only after the flush |
| Item recreated with a reused inode number | Passed as the original | Told apart by birth time |
| Sparse files | Holes filled | Holes kept |
| Flush before deleting a moved source (internal disk) | None | `syncfs` |

</details>

<details><summary><b>Casefolded ext4</b></summary>

| Edge case | Before (main) | After (this PR) |
|---|---|---|
| Case aliases inside a copy | Later name overwrote the earlier; a move deleted both sources | Numbered and reported (casefold flag read per folder) |
| Case-only rename | Refused: "already exists" | Works |

</details>

<details><summary><b>btrfs and XFS</b></summary>

| Edge case | Before (main) | After (this PR) |
|---|---|---|
| Move across btrfs subvolumes or mounts | Copy (reflinked) plus delete; folder metadata lost | Reflinked copy keeping folder metadata; sources deleted entry by entry after `syncfs` |
| Replace or Merge on `subvol=` mounts (no Trash) | Replace exchanged and deleted at once; Merge refused | Exchange with the delete after the flush; Merge sets aside |
| Sparse files across filesystems | Holes filled | Holes kept |

</details>

<details><summary><b>tmpfs</b></summary>

| Edge case | Before (main) | After (this PR) |
|---|---|---|
| Replace (no Trash) | `EXCHANGE`, the original deleted at once | `EXCHANGE`; the original deleted after the flush |
| Merge (no Trash) | Refused when a file would be overwritten | Originals set aside, removed after success |
| Sparse files | Holes filled | Holes kept |

</details>

<details><summary><b>ZFS</b></summary>

| Edge case | Before (main) | After (this PR) |
|---|---|---|
| OpenZFS 2.1 and earlier: move within a dataset | Copied twice, then the source deleted | Renamed: files linked, folders over a placeholder |
| Replace without Trash | 2.2+: exchanged and deleted at once; 2.1: failed after the copy | 2.2+: exchanged, deleted after the flush; 2.1: set aside |
| Case-insensitive datasets | Aliases overwritten; case-only renames refused | Aliases numbered and reported; case-only renames work |
| Sparse files from ZFS | Holes filled | Unchanged on purpose (some releases report holes over unsynced data) |

</details>

<details><summary><b>overlayfs</b></summary>

| Edge case | Before (main) | After (this PR) |
|---|---|---|
| Replace and Merge (no Trash) | Replace exchanged and deleted at once; Merge refused | Original set aside instead (no exchange on overlayfs), deleted after the flush; Merge sets aside |
| Moving a lower-layer folder (no `redirect_dir`) | Copy plus delete; folder metadata lost | Copy keeping folder metadata; sources deleted entry by entry after `syncfs` |

</details>

<details><summary><b>vboxsf, rclone, s3fs</b></summary>

| Edge case | Before (main) | After (this PR) |
|---|---|---|
| Move within one share | Copied twice, then the source deleted | Renamed over a checked placeholder (files; vboxsf folders too) |
| Copies, Replace without Trash, archives | Copies written twice; the others failed | Placed through the same step |
| Restore | Copied with strict metadata | Placed without copying |
| Rename (F2) | Only GIO's check protected the target | Renamed over an exclusively created, checked placeholder |
| Inode numbers, which vboxsf keeps for a name through renames | Compared, as everywhere | Never trusted: a moved copy is known by type, birth time, size and time, and a lost reply to the rename over a placeholder is reported unconfirmed |
| Flush before deleting a moved source | None | rclone, s3fs: `fdatasync` per file plus the folder; vboxsf: per file plus `syncfs` |

</details>

<details><summary><b>9p, ceph</b></summary>

| Edge case | Before (main) | After (this PR) |
|---|---|---|
| Move within one mount | Copied twice, then the source deleted | Renamed: files linked, folders over a placeholder |
| Replace without Trash | Failed after the full copy | Original set aside |
| Restore | Folders copied | Placed without copying |
| Flush before deleting a moved source | None | `fdatasync` per file plus `syncfs` |

</details>

<details><summary><b>GVfs locations (`smb://`, `sftp://`, `mtp://`)</b></summary>

| Edge case | Before (main) | After (this PR) |
|---|---|---|
| Native item moved there | GIO moved files unchecked; folders: top item checked only | Recorded before GIO copies it; each source entry deleted only if unchanged. No flush or content check; a torn copy stays there |
| GVfs item moved to SMB or FUSE | Copy not synced before the source was deleted | Files synced one by one before the source is deleted |
| Keep Both | Exists probes block the UI thread | Probed without blocking the UI thread; retries on "exists" |
| Paste conflict check | Synchronous on the UI thread | Off the UI thread; a slow location shows "Preparing items…" with Cancel |
| Names onto `smb://` and `mtp://` | Sent as they were: GIO failed on refused names; MTP sent an empty name past 254 units | Windows rules by address (MTP: 254 units), reported; undo gives them back |
| Symlinks onto `smb://` and `mtp://` | Copy failed | Left out after the first refusal in each item; reported |
| Item moved from a GVfs location | GIO copies it, then deletes it unchecked | Unchanged |

</details>

## Visual evidence

Pending upload: none of these captures, taken on a private headless display, is attached yet.

**Step 2** (end of step 2; step 1 changed no layout):
1. **Before** (end of step 1): copying `Makefile` and `makefile` onto a case-insensitive folder fails with "An item with that name already exists".
   **After:** a notice says the destination can't tell these names apart and `makefile` was saved as `makefile (1)`.

5. **Before:** moving that folder to another disk is refused.

6. **After:** one dialog after a cancelled move and after a failed copy, with the outcome first and then the report. The cut-off file counts as not attempted.
7. **After:** "Writing to device…" during the final flush of a move to an internal disk.
8. **After:** one "Completed with errors" dialog for a restore that failed one item and left parts of another in the Trash.
9. **After:** 1, 3 and 5 in a light Omarchy theme.

**Step 3** (After only). The "stick" is a RAM folder that a capture-only patch, not in this PR, reads as vfat, so it shows Strata's own planning:

10. A copy onto the stick: "The destination doesn’t allow these names", six names with their new ones.
11. The same with `Agenda.md` beside `agenda.md`: "Names changed for different reasons", adding "The destination can’t tell these names apart".
12. Long Japanese names copied to a home folder: "These names were too long for the destination", each cut, extension kept.
13. A move onto the stick: two symbolic links left behind, and "Undo can’t move these items back…" naming their folders.

16. The folder prompt, ending "Items whose names change to suit this location overwrite items with the new name."

18. The move: a dialog with "Preparing items…" and Cancel.
19. F2 on the stick refused: "Names in this location can’t contain “:”, “?”".
20. 10 and 16 in a light Omarchy theme.

## How to test

**Step 1**
1. Mount an NFS export or an sshfs share; `scripts/fslab/fslab.sh up` provides both inside a container. On that mount, move a large file and a folder into another folder.
   **Expected:** the moves finish instantly without copying.
2. Paste the same names again and choose **Replace**, once with Trash available and once without (for example on a root-owned NFS export).
   **Expected:** the item is swapped, with no "unexpected system error" and no second copy pass.
3. On a vfat or SMB mount, rename `notes.txt` to `Notes.txt` with F2, then undo.
   **Expected:** both succeed.

**Step 2**

4. Build a test folder on a local disk:
   ```sh
   mkdir -p ~/t/src/ro && cd ~/t/src
   echo a > a && ln a b && mkfifo pipe && truncate -s 1G sparse.img
   python3 -c 'import socket; socket.socket(socket.AF_UNIX).bind("sock")'
   setfattr -n user.note -v hi ro && chmod 0555 ro && touch -d 2001-01-01 ro
   ```
   Copy `src` to another folder on the same disk, then to another disk.
   **Expected:**
   - `ro` keeps mode 555, its 2001 time and `user.note`.
   - `a` and `b` share one inode wherever the destination keeps links.
   - `pipe` is a FIFO.
   - `sparse.img` takes almost no space on ext4, btrfs or tmpfs.
   - A warning lists `sock` as left out.
5. Copy a folder holding `Makefile` and `makefile` to a vfat or exFAT stick.
   **Expected:** `makefile (1)` appears on the stick, with a notice. If you move the folder there instead and then undo, both names come back.
6. Run `while :; do date >> ~/t/live/log.txt; sleep 0.2; done`, then move `~/t/live` and a few other files to another disk.
   **Expected:** everything else moves. `log.txt` stays, with a warning that it changed during the move.
7. Move 300 small files, selected individually, to another disk.
   **Expected:** they copy in parallel, "Writing to device…" shows at the end, and every file arrives.
8. Cancel a large folder copy halfway, and cancel a Merge halfway.
   **Expected:** no partial or truncated item under a real name.
9. Optional: `scripts/fslab/fslab.sh test local_operations::` repeats the unit tests on every lab mount.

**Step 3** (a throwaway USB stick, or the lab's mounts)

10. Build a folder of awkward names on a local disk:
    ```sh
    mkdir -p ~/t/names/inner && cd ~/t/names
    touch 10:00 'notes.' CON aux.c 'report?.txt' "$(printf 'caf\xe9.txt')"
    ln -s 10:00 link && ln -s missing inner/dangling
    ```
    Copy `names` to a vfat or exFAT stick.
    **Expected:** the stick holds `10_00`, `notes`, `CON_`, `aux.c`, `report_.txt` and `caf_.txt`. "Completed with errors" lists each fixed name with its new one, and `link` and `dangling` as symbolic links left out.
11. Copy `~/t/names/10:00` into the stick's `names` folder.
    **Expected:** the prompt opens with "“10:00” will be saved as “10_00” in this location." Keep Both adds `10_00 (1)`. Cut and paste the same file: Keep Both is offered for the move, and Ctrl+Z moves it back.
12. Copy the whole `~/t/names` folder onto the stick again.
    **Expected:** the merge prompt ends with "Items whose names change to suit this location overwrite items with the new name." Merging puts the old `10_00` in the Trash, and Undo restores it.
13. On the stick, rename a file to `x:y`, then to `notes.`, then create a folder named `CON` (F2 and New Folder, then **r** and **a** in 10xer mode).
    **Expected:** each is refused with "Names in this location can’t contain “:”", "Names in this location can’t end with a space or a period", or "“CON” is a reserved name in this location". Nothing changes, and the 10xer prompts stay open. The same names are accepted on ext4.
14. On the stick, create a file with a 100-character CJK name (`python3 -c 'open("中"*100 + ".txt", "w")'` in the stick's folder), then copy it to your home folder.
    **Expected:** it arrives as 83 characters plus `.txt`, listed under "These names were too long for the destination".
15. `tar -cf ~/t/names.tar -C ~/t names`, then **Extract to…** the stick.
    **Expected:** a numbered `names` folder whose members have the names step 10 gave them; the links are left out, the report lists both, and the extraction completes.
16. Delete the `names` folders from the stick and the two links from `~/t/names`. Move `~/t/names` to the stick, then undo.
    **Expected:** every original name (`10:00`, `notes.`, `CON`, `report?.txt`, `caf\xe9.txt`) is back in `~/t/names`, and nothing is left on the stick.
17. Recreate the link (`ln -s 10:00 ~/t/names/link`) and move `~/t/names` to the stick again.
    **Expected:** `link` and its `names` folder stay in `~/t`, reported as left behind, and the report says “Undo can’t move these items back…”, naming `names`.
18. Select `notes.txt` in two folders `a` and `b` (for example in search results), copy both to a third folder, then into `a`.
    **Expected:** the third folder gets `notes.txt` and `notes (1).txt`, with a notice under "These names were already taken". In `a`, only `b`'s file prompts; Keep Both adds `notes (1).txt` (the duplicate) and `notes (2).txt` (`b`'s).
19. Optional, with other media:
    - ntfs3: `aux.c` stays, `CON` becomes `CON_`, links are copied. ntfs-3g: `aux.c` becomes `aux_.c`; a folder of 240 `d` characters moves within the drive and takes an F2 rename at once, with no stray entry.
    - Samba without POSIX extensions: `aux.c` becomes `aux_.c`, links are left out, a 220-byte folder name is cut to 213, and `Makefile` and `makefile` from two folders become `Makefile` and `makefile (1)`. Move a folder there, open it and undo at once: all of it comes back.
    - sshfs: a selected symbolic link moved there lands, and its source is removed.
20. Optional: paste into a sshfs folder whose `sftp-server` you have paused with `kill -STOP`.
    **Expected:** a copy's docked row soon shows "Preparing items…" with Cancel and no count (a move shows a dialog), and Cancel abandons the paste without a prompt.

comments.body:
I’m seeing this with **Strata 0.21.0 on Linux**, moving a roughly 7–8 GB file using cut and paste:

Source: Home downloads folder
Destination: /mnt/storage/
Source filesystem: Btrfs
Destination filesystem: NTFS, mounted through ntfs-3g (fuseblk)
Error: Invalid argument (os error 22)

A separate test using a four-byte temporary file reproduced a filesystem compatibility problem:

|Operation|Btrfs|NTFS / ntfs-3g|
|---|---|---|
|renameat2(..., RENAME_NOREPLACE)|Succeeds|Fails with EINVAL (22)|
|Ordinary rename|Succeeds|Succeeds|

Strata’s v0.21.0 implementation uses RENAME_NOREPLACE when publishing a staged copy at its final destination. The initial move attempt handles EINVAL by falling back to copying, but the subsequent staged-copy publication returns an error if that rename fails. Relevant implementation (https://github.com/lgse/strata/blob/v0.21.0/src/adapters/local_operations.rs)https://github.com/lgse/strata/blob/v0.21.0/src/adapters/local_operations.rs

This suggests unsupported RENAME_NOREPLACE on the destination filesystem is the cause, rather than file size. The syscall incompatibility is confirmed; the exact failing syscall during the original Strata transfer has not been traced.

author: KIDult2226
body:
## Description

Custom themes are only discovered at startup, so a theme file that is rewritten while Strata is running never reaches an open window. That defeats dynamic theme generators: a [matugen](https://github.com/InioX/matugen) template that follows the wallpaper and writes `~/.config/strata/themes/matugen.toml` on every change only shows up after a restart.

This watches the custom theme directory and re-reads it when its `.toml` files change (75 ms debounce, the same pattern the Omarchy state watcher uses). If the theme that is currently selected resolves to different colors, it is re-applied through the existing Settings path — CSS provider, icon colors, preview palettes, listeners — so every open window follows.

A file caught mid-write, invalid, or deleted keeps the current appearance until a read produces valid colors, so a generator rewriting in place cannot flash or reset the theme. `save_custom_theme` re-arms the watch as well, because the save may be what creates the directory.

Verified here with a headless run: with the theme selected, rewriting its `accent` repaints the window within a moment (no restart), and writing a broken file leaves it untouched.

## Visual evidence

Pending: before/after captures of one window with the theme file rewritten while Strata runs are ready locally, but the GitHub CLI cannot upload images for a non-collaborator account. Happy to attach them on request, or they can be dragged into this description.

## How to test

1. Select a custom theme (Settings → Appearance → **Your themes**, or `theme = "live"` with `~/.config/strata/themes/live.toml`) and keep the window visible.
2. Rewrite that `.toml` file on disk while Strata is running — for example change `accent`.
3. Also try writing a broken file, then a valid one again.

**Expected result:**

- Step 2 repaints the window with the new colors within a moment, without restarting.
- The broken file changes nothing; the next valid write applies.

`cargo test --all-targets --all-features` covers this with `rewriting_the_selected_custom_theme_applies_without_a_restart` (run it with a display, e.g. `./scripts/test-headless.py`, to execute the GTK test rather than skip it).

## Related issue

Closes #1619

issues.body:
### Problem or use case

Custom themes are only discovered at startup, so a theme file that is rewritten while Strata is running never shows up in the window. The common case is a dynamic theme generator: a [matugen](https://github.com/InioX/matugen) template can write `~/.config/strata/themes/matugen.toml` on every wallpaper change, but the running window keeps yesterday's palette until Strata is restarted (or the theme is re-saved in Settings → Appearance), which defeats the point of a dynamic theme.

Concretely: with a custom theme selected, rewriting its `.toml` file on disk changes nothing in the open window. `docs/themes.md` ("Custom theme files") documents discovery "on startup".

### Proposed solution

Watch the custom theme directory (`~/.config/strata/themes`) for `.toml` changes and re-read it when they happen. If the theme that is currently selected resolves to different colors afterwards, re-apply it live through the same path Settings uses (CSS provider, icon colors, preview palettes, listeners). If the file is momentarily invalid or missing — a generator caught mid-write — keep the current appearance instead of flashing or resetting the theme; the next event that yields valid colors applies them.

Discovery/refresh stays debounced (a short timeout, like the existing Omarchy state watcher) so a generator writing several files in a row only triggers one re-read.

### Alternatives considered

- Restart Strata after every wallpaper change (what users do today); loses session state and is not "dynamic".
- Re-save or re-select the theme in Settings → Appearance: manual and easy to forget.
- Re-reading theme files on every window focus: heavier, and still delayed until focus changes.
- A built-in matugen integration (running matugen from Strata): too opinionated; one template in the user's matugen config plus this reload is enough.

### Visual examples

Before/after screenshots of one window with the theme file rewritten while Strata runs can be attached to the pull request.

### Strata version

1.0.0 (GitHub release archive)

### Additional context

Current behavior, reproducible in a minute:

1. Put any custom theme in `~/.config/strata/themes/live.toml` and select it (Settings → Appearance, or `theme = "live"` in `settings.toml`).
2. With Strata open, rewrite the file (e.g. change `accent`).
3. Nothing changes until Strata restarts.

A matugen template that feeds this (`~/.config/matugen/templates/strata-theme.toml`, mapped to the nine semantic tokens plus the five syntax colors) works today except for the reload; a pull request implementing the watch follows.

author: KIDult2226
body:
## Description

On a quick right click the browser opens its context menu on the secondary *press* while the button is still down, so the release that follows can end up inside the freshly opened popover, where GTK's `GtkModelButton` activates on an *unpaired release*: `gtkgestureclick.c` emits `unpaired-release` for any button and `gtkmodelbutton.c` emits `clicked` whenever the pointer is inside the row. Near the bottom of the window the menu folds upward over the click point, so that release lands on a row — in the worst case on **Move to Trash** or **Delete Permanently**, which then runs at once.

Whether the release reaches the popover is up to the compositor (thanks @wmfeht for the analysis in #1618): with **niri** the xdg_popup grab takes over at the press, so the release is delivered to the popup; **Hyprland / wlroots / X11** keep pointer focus on the window that saw the press, so the release stays there. This is compositor-specific rather than Wayland-wide, and the previous revision of this PR described it wrong.

Fix, following the suggestion in #1618: the menu tracks whether a button press has reached it since it was shown and drops any button release that arrives before one — such a release can only be the end of the click that opened the menu. The flag is cleared in `ActionMenuSection::show`, so nothing can stay armed across presentations, both the file-row and the folder-background menus are covered in one place, and the trigger call sites are untouched. Because the guard is not button-specific, a menu opened by any other button is covered too.

Deliberate trade-off: press-hold-move-release onto a row no longer activates it; menus now want a normal click, like other desktop menus.

## Verification

- `cargo fmt --check`, `clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`, the `ui::browser::context_menu` tests, and a headless X11 regression all pass: a quick right click leaves the menu open, a paired click still runs a row (properties dialog on the last row), Escape closes, and a click outside dismisses.
- **niri, this fix**: the opening release *is* delivered into the popover on niri and is then dropped by the guard — the menu stays open with the row under the cursor only hovered, nothing runs. `WAYLAND_DEBUG=1` trace of the click:

```
wl_pointer#37.button(4921492, 164800476, 273, 1)              # right press on the toplevel
 -> xdg_surface#89.get_popup(new id xdg_popup#122, xdg_surface#71, positioner#110)
 -> xdg_popup#122.grab(wl_seat#3, 4921492)                    # grab with the press's serial
xdg_popup#122.configure(144, 31, 312, 528)                    # menu mapped …
 -> xdg_popup#122.reposition(...)  ; xdg_popup#122.configure(144, 31, 312, 605)   # … and folded up
wl_pointer#37.leave(4921496, wl_surface#50)                   # pointer leaves the toplevel
wl_pointer#37.enter(4921496, wl_surface#124, 176.00, 539.00)  # enters the POPUP, on a row near its bottom
wl_pointer#37.button(4921497, 164800726, 273, 0)              # the opening click's release, delivered to the popup
```
(Nothing after the release: the pointer stays inside the popup, i.e. the menu is still open.)

- **niri, pristine 1.0.0**: the same click (same coordinates, same 250 ms hold) logs the same shape and then `leave(popup)` immediately after the release — the row under the pointer ran: the properties dialog opened by itself.

Screenshots of both runs (menu open vs. properties dialog) are available on request; the GitHub CLI cannot upload images for a non-collaborator account.

## How to test

1. On niri, right click a file near the bottom edge of the window and release quickly (or hold ~250 ms before releasing, so the popover is mapped before the release).
   - Before: the menu opens and the row under the pointer runs at once.
   - After: the menu stays open; left-clicking a row runs it normally, Escape closes, right-clicking elsewhere retargets as before.
2. Repeat in the middle of a tall file list, where the menu folds upward over the pointer.
3. On Hyprland/X11 a click released on a menu row must behave exactly as before (the release never reaches the popover there).

## Related issue

Closes #1618

### What happened?

A quick right click (press and release without moving) in the browser opens the context menu, and the release immediately activates the row under the pointer. When the menu flips upward (right click near the bottom of the window), the pointer ends up somewhere inside the menu, so the file is operated on at once — in the worst case the pointer lands on "Move to Trash" or "Delete Permanently" and the file is deleted.

Workaround: hold the secondary button, move onto the wanted row, then release.

2. Right click a file near the bottom edge of the window, pressing and releasing quickly without moving the pointer.
3. Observe: the menu opens and the row under the pointer (e.g. "Delete Permanently") runs immediately.

### Expected behavior

A quick right click opens the context menu and leaves it open. Only a following click on a row should run an action. (Press-hold-move-release is arguably fine as a second gesture, but a plain click must not activate anything.)

### Screenshots or video

Pending; a screenshot of the flipped-up menu with the pointer resting on "Delete Permanently" can be attached to the pull request.

### Relevant logs

None.

### Additional context

- Wayland only. Under X11 (Xvfb) the same quick right click behaves correctly: the release does not reach the popover there.
- Mechanism: the menu opens on the secondary *press* (the gesture is claimed) while the button is still down. The xdg_popup grab then routes the following release into the new popover, and GTK's `GtkModelButton` activates on an *unpaired release*: `gtkgestureclick.c` emits `unpaired-release` for any button, and `gtkmodelbutton.c`'s handler ignores the button number and emits `clicked` when the pointer is inside the row. So the release of the click that opened the menu runs the row under the pointer.
- Reproduced on GTK 4.24.1; the unpaired-release handling in `GtkModelButton` is not new.

## Description

Keep PDF zoom independent of interface text size. Ctrl+wheel now identifies the widget beneath the seat pointer because GTK scroll events carry no position. Ctrl+0 resets the focused PDF through a local action, including in the file chooser and 10xer mode.

## How to test

1. Set interface text size to 21 px and open a PDF preview.
2. Hold Ctrl and scroll over the page. The PDF zooms while interface text stays at 21 px.
3. Click the PDF and press Ctrl+0. The page returns to its fitted zoom and interface text stays at 21 px.
4. Scroll with Ctrl over the file listing, then focus the listing and press Ctrl+0. These still change and reset interface text size. Repeat PDF reset in the file chooser and with 10xer enabled.

**Expected result:** PDF zoom and reset leave the saved text-size preference alone; interface zoom still works outside the PDF.

## Related issue

Closes #1596

body:
## Description

In `BrowserView::create_new_folder_for_selection`, querying `command_targets()` fell back to the keyboard cursor row via `command_entries()` when no items were selected or when only a load cursor was present. This caused <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>Alt</kbd>+<kbd>N</kbd> (*New Folder with Selection*) to move unselected items under the cursor into the new folder.

Distinguished committed selections from the cursor fallback by introducing `filled_entries()` on `NavigationState` and `Browser`. `create_new_folder_for_selection` now uses `filled_entries()`, returning `false` when no items are selected so the action handler falls back to creating a plain empty new folder.

## Visual evidence
Before:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/822af41a-1427-4fc2-acfb-b1c1a8da48f8

After:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dc896b74-ba92-47c8-864e-fae270e67726

## How to test

1. Open a folder containing multiple files (e.g., `a.txt`, `b.txt`, `c.txt`).
2. Press <kbd>Escape</kbd> or click the pane background so nothing is selected (cursor focus ring remains on an item, footer reports "3 items").
3. Press <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>Alt</kbd>+<kbd>N</kbd>.
4. Check the contents of the newly created folder and the current directory.
5. In a newly opened directory where only a load cursor sits on row 0, press <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>Alt</kbd>+<kbd>N</kbd>.

**Expected result:**

An empty `new folder` is created in rename mode, and existing items (`a.txt`, etc.) remain in place in the current directory. When files are explicitly selected, <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>Alt</kbd>+<kbd>N</kbd> continues to group the selected files into the new folder.

## Related issue

Closes #1591

## Description

A native speaker reviewed the Simplified Chinese translation and found a few strings that were ambiguous or read like word-for-word translations. This PR changes only zh-CN values. Keys and placeholders are unchanged.

- **`Compact sidebar (%{keys})`:** 收起侧边栏 → 紧凑显示侧边栏. Chinese readers take 收起 to mean "hide", which made this step look the same as the next one, 隐藏侧边栏.
- **`Tasks` folder icon:** 清单 → 任务.
- **`Danger` theme color:** 危险 → 危险色, matching 强调色 and 柔和色.
- **Password storage choices:** 不记住 / 直到注销 / 永久 → 不保存 / 保存至注销 / 永久保存, so they use the same verb as the label 保存密码.

Validation: `./scripts/test-headless.py i18n::` was **not run**. It was prepared on macOS, where GTK, Xvfb, and the container engine aren't available. Instead, a script checked both zh-CN catalogs against the same rules as `catalogs_cover_all_languages_and_preserve_interpolation`: same keys in the same order as `en`, no empty values, and the same placeholders. All 2201 messages pass. `git diff --check` is clean.

## Visual evidence

N/A. Only translated text changes, with no layout or styling changes. Screenshots aren't available because the change wasn't run on Linux (see above).

## How to test

1. Choose 简体中文 under Settings → Language and restart Strata.
2. With the sidebar fully shown, hover the sidebar toggle in the top bar.
3. Right-click a folder, choose Customize…, and hover the checklist icon.
4. Open the custom theme editor in Settings.
5. Connect to a location that asks for a password and can save it.

**Expected result:**

1. The tooltip reads 紧凑显示侧边栏（…）, and the next step reads 隐藏侧边栏（…）.
2. The icon is named 任务.
3. The theme color is named 危险色.
4. The password choices are 不保存 / 保存至注销 / 永久保存.

Closes #1624

body:
## Description

In `src/ui/browser/clipboard.rs`, `shell_escape_path` converted paths via `path.to_string_lossy()`, replacing invalid UTF-8 bytes with U+FFFD (). Copied paths containing non-UTF-8 bytes therefore named nonexistent files when pasted into a shell.

Native paths with non-UTF-8 bytes are now deconstructed into components, with non-UTF-8 components formatted using POSIX / ANSI-C quoting syntax (`$'...'`) and hexadecimal byte escapes (`\xHH`). Valid UTF-8 paths retain existing escaping behavior without changes.

## Visual evidence

## How to test

1. Create a file with a non-UTF-8 byte: `touch $'bad\xff.txt'`.
2. In Strata, select the file and use **Copy path** (or press <kbd>y</kbd> in 10xer mode).
3. Paste the clipboard into a shell with `ls -l <paste>`.

**Expected result:**

The clipboard contains `/path/to/$'bad\xff.txt'`, and pasting into a shell successfully resolves and accesses the file.

## Related issue

Closes #1594

body: ## Description When confirming permanent deletion for a symlink pointing to a folder, the confirmation dialog previously recurse-counted the target folder's items and total size, and labeled the entry as "Folder", even though confirming deletion only removes the symbolic link while preserving the target directory and its contents intact. This change: - Updates `aggregate_directory_summary` to only recurse into actual directories (`EntryKind::Directory`), treating symlinks (including `DirectorySymbolicLink`) as single items of 0 bytes without traversing into the target. - Updates `entry_kind_summary` to only count true directories as folders. - Labels directory symlink rows in the delete confirmation list as "Folder link" instead of "Folder". - Ensures single-entry queries like `query_file_entry` resolve directory symlinks to `EntryKind::DirectorySymbolicLink`. ## Visual evidence ## How to test 1. Create a directory `realdir` containing several files. 2. Create a symbolic link pointing to that directory: `ln -s realdir 0dirlink`. 3. In Strata, select `0dirlink` and press Shift+Delete to open the permanent deletion confirmation dialog. 4. Confirm deletion. **Expected result:** The dialog shows "Folder link" next to `0dirlink` and reports "1 item · 0 B will be permanently deleted" without counting the contents of `realdir`. After confirming deletion, `0dirlink` is deleted and `realdir` with its contents remains completely intact. ## Related issue Closes #1592

author: JoeJoeflyn
body:
## Description

When a focused filter result was deleted in List or Icons view, the underlying `GtkListItemWidget` became unmapped and detached from the collection view. Because focus remained referencing the detached unmapped widget, `ResultCollection::update` failed to detect that focus had belonged to the collection, leaving the window with lost keyboard focus and no visible focus ring.

Now:
- `ResultCollection::update` recognizes when the current window focus is an unmapped `GtkListItemWidget` or a bound item from the collection.
- When results remain, focus moves cleanly to the next result (`selected.minimum()`).
- If all results are deleted, focus cleanly returns to the filter text input (`gtk::Entry`) when visible, or stays on the view.

## Visual evidence

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/51ef5263-5876-4551-bfb4-82a859db29f0

## How to test

1. Open a directory with several files and switch to List view (Ctrl+3) or Icons view (Ctrl+2).
2. Press Ctrl+F and type a search query matching multiple items.
3. Press Down arrow to focus the first result.
4. Press Delete (or Shift+Delete) and confirm deletion if prompted.
5. Delete the remaining results until the list is empty.

**Expected result:**

author: JoeJoeflyn
body: ## Description The shared MIME database maps many extensions to several unrelated types. `*.ts` is TypeScript, Qt Linguist, or an MPEG transport stream depending on which database version is installed, and `*.tsx` is a Tiled tileset. A confident name match skipped content sniffing entirely, so Strata mounted a video player for TypeScript source. Special-casing TypeScript only patched one collision. This change makes the loader read the first 8 KiB of every local file before choosing a renderer and lets the bytes override the name: - Text is never handed to a media, image, PDF, archive, or document decoder. - Binary data is never shown as text. - Visual families survive only when the bytes carry their signature, or for XML-based images such as SVG whose source is legitimately text. - A text name still yields to a certain PDF or image signature. - UTF-16 files with a byte-order mark decode as text. Metadata probes verify the bytes the same way, so source files that share a media extension are never probed by GStreamer, and entries whose probe found no media drop out of video stepping. The name-only gates for quick preview, printing, context menus, and the chooser are unchanged; the loader resolves the final family. The highlighting language is still chosen from the filename by GtkSourceView, so TypeScript and TSX keep their highlighting regardless of the MIME database. ## Visual evidence Before (TypeScript opened as a video player): After (syntax-highlighted source): ## How to test 1. Create `app.ts`, `Component.tsx`, and `module.mts` with TypeScript source, and `notes.png` and `movie.mp4` containing plain text. 2. Create `photo.txt` containing PNG bytes and `paper.txt` containing a PDF. 3. Record a real transport stream: `ffmpeg -f lavfi -i testsrc2=duration=3 -f mpegts recording.ts`. 4. Select each file and press `Space`. **Expected result:** The TypeScript files and the text named `.png` or `.mp4` preview as source text. `photo.txt` previews as an image and `paper.txt` as a PDF. `recording.ts` previews as a video. Binary files named `.json` or `.md` show "No visual preview" instead of garbage text. ## Related issue Closes #1631
