author: adamcbrewer
body: ## Description Adds four on-demand camera views to rendered STL and single-part 3MF previews. Previous and next controls move an animated camera dot around the model indicator. Badges show the mesh format and triangle count, and the main preview dims behind a spinner while another view renders. I try to borrow as much from the video and audio player interface as possible. So the play button has become just a central dot to indicate the model's location and the dot that spins around the outside or the circumference is the camera angle looking down from above.Previous and next behave as previous camera position and next camera position. I also included some details around the file name and the X of Y number within the directory of the models they're looking at. There is a modal overlay of the number of meshes required to calculate the next rendering when a camera position is changed so that we don't end up with a blank view, so it still persists the previous view while the new one is being rendered. View selection survives theme changes and resets when opening another file. In terms of performance, on-demand keeps the cost contained. We have four views total, rather than rendering a 3D mesh world which is only useful if interacted with. Opening a model: renders one angle. - First visit to another angle: rereads and parses the mesh, then performs a full CPU render. Dense meshes can still take noticeable time. - Revisiting an angle: uses the cached PNG while that entry remains valid; only image decoding/display work remains. - Memory: cached images share the existing 128 MiB preview cache. Only one heavy preview job runs at a time, so visiting four angles doesn’t multiply peak rendering memory by four. - The main remaining inefficiency is reparsing geometry for each uncached angle. I’d keep this approach unless real-model measurements show that cost warrants retaining parsed meshes. ## Visual evidence ## How to test 1. Open Quick Preview for an STL file or a single-part 3MF without an embedded thumbnail. Use previous and next to cycle through all four views. 2. Make the window taller. Check that the model and controls remain centred together, with the filename and folder position above the format and triangle-count badges. 3. Change the theme, then preview another model. Enable Reduce motion to check that the camera indicator changes without animation. **Expected result:** Rendered meshes change view with stable centring and scale. The centred preview shows the current file and its position among model files. The spinner clearly indicates rendering, the indicator follows the selected camera, and the badges show the mesh details. Thumbnail previews keep their saved image without camera controls. ## Related issue Closes #1633 Follow-up UI refactor: [#1659](https://github.com/lgse/strata/issues/1659). Start only after this PR is merged into `main`.

### Problem or use case

Quick Preview renders STL and some 3MF models from a fixed camera angle, so the other sides are difficult to inspect.

### Proposed solution

Add four camera views looking down from the upper corners of a box around the model. Use compact controls that fit the existing audio and video previews, and cache each view as it is rendered.

Show the controls only when Strata actually renders mesh geometry. Keep existing 3MF and FreeCAD embedded thumbnails as they are.

### Alternatives considered

Continuous mouse rotation would need frequent software renders or a new interactive renderer. A preset view selector keeps this prototype within the current sandboxed renderer.

### Visual examples

Use the current audio and video preview controls as the visual reference.

### Strata version

Source checkout from main.

### Additional context

Keep the camera selection while changing themes. Switching files should start from the default view. The prototype should retain the existing file drag interaction and model limits.

The CI dependency-audit follow-up updates Rustls to 0.23.46 without weakening policy checks. author: jing2uo
body: ## Description On Debian-family systems `/usr/bin/magick` and `/usr/bin/convert` are `update-alternatives` links into `/etc/alternatives`, which the preview sandbox does not mount, so the ImageMagick fallback failed with ENOENT even when ImageMagick was installed. The sandbox now binds just those two links, following the BLAS/LAPACK alternatives already exposed for FFmpeg (#984), rather than the whole alternatives directory. Unlike the BLAS links, they are bound for image operations as well as media ones. On Debian testing/unstable, GDK Pixbuf 2.44 hands every raster format to glycin, which cannot start inside the preview sandbox, so every image relies on this fallback, and even JPEG previews were empty. On Debian 13 only formats GDK Pixbuf cannot decode, such as HEIC, were affected. ## Visual evidence **Before:** JPEG preview on Debian unstable is empty. **After:** the same JPEG renders. ## How to test 1. On Debian testing/unstable, run `sudo apt install imagemagick` and confirm `readlink /usr/bin/magick` prints `/etc/alternatives/magick`. 2. Open a folder containing a `.jpg` image and select it with the preview panel open. On Debian 13, use a `.heic` image instead, since its GDK Pixbuf has no HEIC loader. **Expected result:** The image shows a preview and a thumbnail instead of an empty preview. ## Related issue Closes #1656

issues.body: ### Strata version 1.0.0 ### Installation method Built from source ### Linux distribution and desktop environment Debian forky/sid, Hyprland (Wayland) ### What happened? On Debian-family systems, previews and thumbnails that need the ImageMagick fallback stay empty even when ImageMagick is installed. Debian installs `/usr/bin/magick` and `/usr/bin/convert` as `update-alternatives` links (`/usr/bin/magick -> /etc/alternatives/magick -> /usr/bin/magick-im7.q16`). The preview sandbox binds `/usr` but only selected files under `/etc`, so inside the sandbox both commands are dangling links and fail with ENOENT. Formats that GDK Pixbuf cannot decode (for example HEIC on Debian 13) therefore never render. The sandbox already exposes the individual BLAS/LAPACK alternatives links that FFmpeg needs on Debian-family systems (#984); the ImageMagick links need the same treatment. ### Steps to reproduce 1. On Debian 13 (or testing/unstable), install ImageMagick: `sudo apt install imagemagick`. 2. Check that the command goes through the alternatives directory: `readlink /usr/bin/magick` prints `/etc/alternatives/magick`. 3. Open a folder that contains a `.heic` image in Strata and select it with the preview panel open. ### Expected behavior The HEIC image shows a preview and a thumbnail, decoded through the installed ImageMagick, as it does on distributions where `/usr/bin/magick` is a regular file. ### Screenshots or video ### Relevant logs _No response_ ### Additional context Pointing `/usr/bin/magick` and `/usr/bin/convert` straight at `magick-im7.q16` works around it, but `update-alternatives` restores the links on the next ImageMagick upgrade.

comments.author: jing2uo
comments.body:
On Debian testing/unstable the impact is wider than HEIC: ordinary JPEG and PNG previews are empty as well.

GDK Pixbuf 2.44 there (2.44.8 with glycin 2.2.2) hands every raster format to glycin, and glycin's loader sandbox cannot start inside the preview sandbox. Every image therefore falls back to ImageMagick, which hits the dangling `/etc/alternatives` links described above. Debian 13 and Ubuntu 25.10 still ship GDK Pixbuf 2.42 with built-in PNG/JPEG decoding, so there only formats GDK Pixbuf cannot decode, such as HEIC, are affected.

Binding `/etc/alternatives/magick` and `/etc/alternatives/convert` into the sandbox restores JPEG previews on Debian unstable.

author: l0gicgate
body:
## Description

Global search (Ctrl+K) and recursive pane filters walked the tree with a fixed budget of 10 seconds and 200,000 entries. On slow mounts such as rclone drives, every directory listing is a network round trip, so the walk ran out of time long before the tree was listed and search found only some files (reported on Discord).

This adds two saved preferences under **Settings → General → Search & filtering**:

- **Search time limit**: 10 s (default), 30 s, 1 min, 5 min, 15 min, No limit.
- **Search entry limit**: 200,000 (default), 500,000, 1,000,000, 5,000,000, No limit.

Global search, pane filters, 10xer path search, and folder pickers read the current limits when they start a query, including before Settings opens. A changed limit restarts the next query's index walk, and filesystem rescans keep the limits their index was opened with instead of falling back to the constants. Unlisted saved values round up to the next choice; 0 means no limit. The limits are part of the shared-index key, so searches with different limits never share a snapshot. The entry limit still bounds index memory, and its description says so.

The **Partial results** hint in the search dialog now has a tooltip listing why results are partial and, when a time or entry limit stopped the walk, "Raise the limits in Settings → General → Search & filtering." The inline search status text and the hint's accessible description carry the same sentence. Note: the tooltip policy in AGENTS.md reserves tooltips for icon-only buttons; the owner explicitly requested a tooltip on this warning icon, so this is a deliberate exception.

Strings are localized in all eleven catalogs, and `docs/preferences.md` and the README describe the new settings.

## Visual evidence

Pending upload by the owner. Captures (before/after of the Search & filtering group, Tokyo Night, 1360×760, headless Xvfb) are at:

- `/tmp/claude-1000/-home-l0gicgate-Documents-github-strata/61eafbf2-a788-4be0-85c1-cef9409bf14c/scratchpad/before-search-filtering.png` — the group with only the three switches and exclusions.
- `/tmp/claude-1000/-home-l0gicgate-Documents-github-strata/61eafbf2-a788-4be0-85c1-cef9409bf14c/scratchpad/after-search-filtering.png` — the two new choice rows between **Open search results directly** and **Global search exclusions**.

The tooltip was not captured: it only appears after a walk hits a limit, which needs a tree larger than 200,000 entries or slower than 10 seconds.

## How to test

1. Open **Settings → General** and scroll to **Search & filtering**. Set **Search time limit** to **No limit** and **Search entry limit** to **No limit**.
2. Open a second window and its Settings page: both menus show the same choices.
3. Press Ctrl+K and search a large or slow tree (for example an rclone mount under your home folder). The walk no longer stops after 10 s and the **Partial results** hint does not appear for time or entry limits.
4. Set the limits back to **10 s** and **200,000**, then search the same tree again: the hint reappears once a limit is reached. Hover it: the tooltip names the reason and ends with "Raise the limits in Settings → General → Search & filtering."
5. Edit `~/.config/strata/settings.toml` to `search_time_limit = 45` and `search_entry_limit = 300000`, restart Strata: the menus show **1 min** and **500,000**.

**Expected result:** Searches honor the selected limits on the next query in every window, choices synchronize across windows, hand-edited values round up to the next menu choice, and the partial-results tooltip tells the user where to raise the limits.

## Related issue

Closes #1665

issues.body:
### Problem or use case

Global search (Ctrl+K) and recursive pane filters walk the tree live with fixed limits: 10 seconds of indexing time and 200,000 entries. On slow mounts such as rclone FUSE mounts for Google Drive or OneDrive, every directory listing is a network round trip, so the walk runs out of time long before the cloud tree is enumerated and search finds only some files. A user reported exactly this on Discord: searching for a file they could see in the folder returned nothing, even when searching inside that folder.

The defaults are reasonable for local SSDs, but users with large trees or slow mounts should be able to decide how long a search may walk and how many entries it may hold.

### Proposed solution

Add two saved preferences under **Settings → General → Search & filtering**:

- **Search time limit**: 10 s (default), 30 s, 1 min, 5 min, 15 min, No limit.
- **Search entry limit**: 200,000 (default), 500,000, 1,000,000, 5,000,000, No limit.

Global search and recursive pane filters read the current choice at dispatch. The "Partial results" hint keeps reporting when a limit is reached.

### Alternatives considered

- Warming rclone's directory cache (`--dir-cache-time`, `rclone rc vfs/refresh recursive=true`) helps but does not fix large local trees and asks users to work around the limit.
- Global search exclusions can only shrink the scope, not extend the budget.

### Additional context

Limits live in `src/services/search.rs` (`INDEX_TIME_BUDGET`, `MAX_INDEX_ENTRIES`). The entry limit bounds index memory, so the setting description should mention memory use.
issues.title: Make search indexing time and entry limits configurable

title: feat(search): make the indexing time and entry limits configurable

author: ogarza
body:
## Description

Adds `scripts/benchmark-scroll.py`, a scroll benchmark for the Columns, List, and Icons modes. It drives each binary on a private Xvfb display and session bus, scrolls generated folders with the mouse wheel or the arrow keys, and reports:

- main-thread CPU per wheel notch or key press
- frame times, read from GTK's own sysprof marks, so older releases can be measured unchanged
- idle wakeups

Optional flags compare builds side by side, limit Strata's CPU to approximate slower machines, and record perf call graphs.

This is how the regressions in #1671 were found and bisected. The later pull requests in that series will use it for their before and after numbers. `docs/performance-baseline.md` documents the procedure and how to read the results.

## Visual evidence

N/A: benchmark tooling and documentation only; Strata itself is unchanged.

## How to test

1. Install Xvfb, `at-spi2-core`, and `sysprof`.
2. Build a release binary with symbols:
   ```bash
   CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_LTO=false CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_CODEGEN_UNITS=16 \
   CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_DEBUG=line-tables-only RUSTFLAGS="-C force-frame-pointers=yes" \
   CARGO_TARGET_DIR=target/scroll-bench/target-main cargo build --locked --release --bin strata
   ```
3. Run `./scripts/benchmark-scroll.py --binary main=target/scroll-bench/target-main/release/strata --modes columns,list --fixtures mixed --rounds 1`.
4. Optionally add `--input keys`, `--cpu-quota 25`, or a second `--binary` to compare builds.

**Expected result:** The run prints one line per configuration and ends with a Markdown table. Both are also saved under `target/scroll-bench/results/`. On `main`, List shows several times the CPU per step of Columns. That is the regression tracked in #1671.

## Related issue

Refs #1671
title: test(bench): add a scroll benchmark for the browser modes

author: ogarza
body:
## Description

Since #1081 (v0.19.0), List and Icons have run their deferred row refresh one frame after each scroll event instead of after scrolling stops. During a continuous scroll, every visible row was refreshed about every other frame. The scroller's `list-fast-scroll` class also flipped about once per frame, which restyled every visible row.

This restores a quiet-period settle. The refresh now runs once scrolling has been still for 25 ms, and never sooner than two frames, so a slow machine does not settle between frames of a single scroll. `list-fast-scroll` and its CSS rule are removed: the rule only disabled row transitions that scrolling does not trigger.

Measured with `scripts/benchmark-scroll.py` from #1672, on `main` and this branch. Main-thread CPU per wheel notch, fastest of three rounds, under Xvfb with the Cairo renderer:

| | `main` | This branch |
|---|---:|---:|
| List, mixed folder | 22.7 ms | 3.9 ms |
| List, image folder | 24.0 ms | 6.9 ms |
| Icons, mixed folder | 7.9 ms | 8.0 ms |
| Icons, image folder | 12.8 ms | 12.1 ms |

With Strata limited to 25% of one CPU, roughly a four-times-slower machine:

| | `main` | This branch |
|---|---:|---:|
| List: frame p50 | 19.7 ms | 1.1 ms |
| List: frame p95 | 50.6 ms | 8.6 ms |
| List: frames over 16.7 ms | 136 | 11 |
| List: frames per second | 28 | 70 |

Icons is unchanged here. Its costs are elsewhere and are handled by a later pull request in the series.

## Visual evidence

N/A: nothing changes visually. Cut styling and dates refresh within about two frames of scrolling stopping, rather than during the scroll.

## How to test

1. Run `./scripts/generate-fixture.sh target/fixtures` and open `target/fixtures/10000` in List.
2. Cut a few files with Ctrl+X.
3. Scroll continuously with the mouse wheel past them and back. Repeat in Icons.

**Expected result:** Scrolling stays smooth. Cut rows show their dimmed style as soon as scrolling stops, and dates and hidden-file styling are correct after every scroll.

## Related issue

Refs #1671
title: perf(browser): settle List and Icons scrolling after a quiet period

author: ogarza
body:
## Description

Fixes two costs in Columns found in #1671.

**Size badges.** Since #1564 turned size badges on by default, every badge faded over 120 ms whenever its row was hovered, selected, or on the open path. Moving the selection with the arrow keys kept several fades running, and GTK repainted each of them on every frame. Arrow-key navigation cost 40–80% more per key press than in v0.21.0.

Now a badge fades in only when the pointer enters its row. Selection, the open path, and leaving a row show or hide the badge at once.

I also tried suppressing the hover fade while a column scrolls, by adding a class to the column during the scroll. Toggling that class restyled the whole column, which caused 50–70 ms frames at the start and end of each scroll on a CPU-limited run. So the fade still plays when the pointer enters a row while the wheel scrolls.

**Clipboard marks.** Every Columns row bind cloned the full copy and cut lists, then compared each entry against the row through two `GFile`s. The marks are now indexed whenever the clipboard changes, so each row needs a single lookup. `file://` URIs are keyed by their native path, so GIO-equivalent locations still match.

Measured with `scripts/benchmark-scroll.py` from #1672, `main` against this branch. Main-thread CPU per step, fastest round, under Xvfb with the Cairo renderer:

| Columns | `main` | This branch |
|---|---:|---:|
| Arrow keys, mixed folder | 4.58 ms | 3.33 ms |
| Arrow keys, folder counts | 4.67 ms | 3.75 ms |
| Wheel, after copying 1,000 files | 5.55 ms | 4.35 ms |
| Wheel, mixed folder | 3.45 ms | 3.40 ms |

With Strata limited to 25% of one CPU:

| Columns | `main` | This branch |
|---|---:|---:|
| Arrow keys: frame p95 | 8.0 ms | 3.0 ms |
| Arrow keys: longest frame | 14.2 ms | 8.6 ms |
| Wheel: frame p95 | 7.7 ms | 6.9 ms |
| Wheel: longest frame | 24.1 ms | 20.5 ms |

## Visual evidence

Pending upload: a recording of arrow-key navigation in Columns, slowed three times, with `main` on the left and this branch on the right. On `main`, the previous row's badge fades out after the selection moves. On this branch, it disappears immediately. The local file is `target/scroll-bench/evidence/pr3/before-vs-after-slow.mp4`.

## How to test

1. Run `./scripts/generate-fixture.sh target/fixtures` and open `target/fixtures/1000` in Columns.
2. Hold the Down arrow through the folders at the top.
3. Move the mouse over a few rows, then away from them.
4. Copy several hundred files from another folder, return, and scroll with the wheel.
5. Cut one file with Ctrl+X and scroll it out of view and back.

**Expected result:** While the arrow keys move the selection, the badge moves with it at once, with no fade. Hovering a row fades its badge in, and leaving the row hides the badge at once. Scrolling stays smooth with files on the clipboard. The cut file keeps its cut styling after scrolling.

## Related issue

Refs #1671
title: perf(columns): fade size badges only on hover and index clipboard marks

author: ogarza
body:
## Description

Cuts repeated per-row and per-card work found in #1671.

- **Rename editor lookup:** every bind and unbind scanned all bound rows, upgrading weak references, to find the row's rename editor. In an Icons scroll profile this took 5% of main-thread time. It is now looked up directly by list item.
- **Fallback icon height:** when a reused card switched icons, Icons downloaded and scanned the whole icon texture (up to 768 × 768 px). That cost 4% of main-thread time. The height is now measured once per texture.
- **Icons captions:** each rebound card built two or three Pango layouts across measure and allocate. The measured size is now reused between the two, and the reserved two-line height is kept while the font and text attributes are unchanged.
- **Icon textures:** each bind loaded the icon's SVG and rewrote it before checking the texture cache. Catppuccin icons needed up to 16 string replacements. The cache is now checked first.
- **Stylesheet:** each window added another copy of the full stylesheet to the display, and none were removed. It is now installed once per display.

Measured with `scripts/benchmark-scroll.py` from #1672, `main` against this branch. Main-thread CPU per wheel notch, fastest of three rounds:

| Icons | `main` | This branch |
|---|---:|---:|
| Mixed folder | 8.60 ms | 7.75 ms |
| Image folder | 13.10 ms | 12.40 ms |

With Strata limited to 25% of one CPU:

| Icons | `main` | This branch |
|---|---:|---:|
| Frames per second | 18 | 54 |
| Frame p95 | 40.6 ms | 28.9 ms |

Columns and List do not change beyond noise.

The date-label registry listed in #1671 is left out. After #1673 its refresh runs once per scroll instead of every frame, so it no longer matters.

## Visual evidence

N/A: rendering is unchanged.

## How to test

1. Run `./scripts/generate-fixture.sh target/fixtures` and open `target/fixtures/1000` in Icons. It mixes folders with several file types.
2. Scroll quickly down and back up, rename a file with F2, and change Settings → Text size.
3. Open a folder in a new window with Shift+Enter.

**Expected result:** Cards keep their icons and two-line captions while scrolling, renaming works in place, captions resize with the text size, and the new window is styled the same as the first.

## Related issue

Refs #1671
title: perf(browser): cut per-card work in Icons and other repeated costs

author: ogarza
body:
## Description

A debug build of Strata scrolls and loads noticeably slower than a release build. Nothing showed which build was running, so performance reports from source builds could not be told apart from release builds (see #1671).

Debug builds now add `+debug` to the version shown by `strata --version`, by Settings → About, and in the copied version info. Release builds are unchanged. The update checks still use the plain version.

The README's build-from-source commands now list the optimized `mise run install-local` first. They also note that `start-dev`, `dev`, and `chooser-dev` make debug builds.

## Visual evidence

N/A: release builds look the same. In a debug build, the About Version row reads, for example, `1.0.0+debug`.

## How to test

1. Build both profiles with `cargo build` and `cargo build --release`.
2. Run `target/debug/strata --version`, then `target/release/strata --version`.
3. In the debug build, open Settings → About and copy the version info.

**Expected result:** The debug build prints `strata 1.0.0+debug` and shows `1.0.0+debug` in About and in the copied text. The release build prints `strata 1.0.0` with no suffix.

author: ogarza
body:
## Description

Three tick callbacks always returned `Continue`, so an idle Strata window kept GTK's frame clock running. It drew about 60 frames a second and woke the main thread about 200 times a second while nothing changed, which also costs laptop battery.

- **Column reveal buttons and tab indicator:** they now update after each GTK layout pass, from the frame clock's `layout` signal, which does not keep the clock running. The indicator animates in a tick only while it moves.
- **Preview split sync:** it keeps its per-frame tick, which its suspend, resume and focus handling depend on. The tick now runs only for a second after a layout pass or an input event in the split.
- **File-provider timer:** the hub timer ran every 100 ms. It now stops once discovery finds no providers.

Measured with `scripts/benchmark-scroll.py` from #1672, `main` against this branch. These are the 8 seconds of idle that follow a scroll:

| | `main` | This branch |
|---|---:|---:|
| Main-thread wakeups per second | ~205 | ~35 |
| Frames per second | 60 | 0 once settled |
| Idle main-thread CPU | ~1% | ~0.3% |

This branch averages 7.6 frames per second over that window. All of them come from the first second after the scroll: the scrollbar fading out and the preview sync's grace period.

The remaining wakeups mostly come from the custom-actions job pump, which polls every 120 ms; it is left as is.

Scrolling costs the same as before, within run-to-run noise. Main-thread CPU per wheel notch, three runs each:

| | `main` | This branch |
|---|---|---|
| Columns | 3.80, 3.70, 3.55 ms | 3.80, 3.85, 3.80 ms |
| Icons | 8.05, 7.50, 8.45 ms | 8.20, 7.90, 11.90 ms |

## Visual evidence

N/A: nothing changes visually.

## How to test

1. Open Strata, browse a folder, and leave the window idle for a few seconds.
2. Run `top -H -p "$(pgrep -n strata)"`.
3. Toggle the preview with Space, then resize the window narrower and wider than the width that fits the preview.
4. Open a second tab with Ctrl+T and switch tabs with Ctrl+Tab.
5. In Columns, open enough nested folders that a column is partly scrolled out of view.

**Expected result:**

- After about a second idle, the main thread uses almost no CPU.
- The preview opens, suspends when the window is too narrow, and resumes as before.
- The tab indicator slides to the active tab.
- A partly hidden column still shows its reveal button.

## Related issue

Refs #1671
title: perf(ui): let the frame clock stop while the window is idle

author: l0gicgate
body: ## Description Strata's look could be changed from outside the app, and every corner radius was fixed in the stylesheet. This PR closes both gaps and tidies the status bar: - **Desktop GTK styling no longer reaches Strata.** The GTK theme is pinned to the built-in `Default` theme as an application-sourced value, so the settings portal, `settings.ini`, and `GTK_THEME` cannot swap it (`GTK_THEME` is dropped through the existing startup re-exec). The built-in theme's light or dark variant follows the active Strata theme instead of the desktop color scheme, high contrast is never applied, and Strata's stylesheets load above GTK's user priority so `~/.config/gtk-4.0/gtk.css` cannot override properties Strata defines. - **No more duplicate title bar.** Every Strata window registers a hidden placeholder titlebar, so GTK never adds its default title bar on compositors that leave decorations to the client (GNOME, Weston, WSLg). Strata's header stays inside the content, so overlays and the modal blur still cover it. Client-side decoration keeps only the invisible resize edges plus a hairline border. - **Corner roundness preference.** Settings → Appearance → Shape has a 0–200 percent stepper that scales every pixel radius in the stylesheet, before Settings opens and live across windows, dialogs, menus, and rebuilt views. The radii GTK's theme supplied for buttons, entries, spin buttons, checks, tooltips, popovers, and switches are restated so they scale too; the switch track and thumb share one radius so they keep the same corner shape at every value. - **Status bar inset.** The F1 Shortcuts button now sits the same distance from the left edge as from the top and bottom. Visual baselines were regenerated for that strip only. ## Visual evidence https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d36eafe4-807e-45a3-b4e5-09becd093e3a Fixed F1 button placement ## How to test 1. Under GNOME (or any compositor without the KDE server-decoration protocol), launch Strata: only Strata's own header appears, with no GTK title bar above it. Dragging the header and resizing from the window edges still work. 2. Select a third-party GTK theme in the desktop settings, or launch with `GTK_THEME=Adwaita:dark`, and add `window { color: red; }` to `~/.config/gtk-4.0/gtk.css`: Strata keeps its own fonts, spacing and colors. 3. Open Settings → Appearance → Shape and step **Corner roundness** to 0, then 200: dialogs, groups, buttons, chips, menus, switches and the Settings window itself square off and round up live, in every open window. 4. Hover the **F1 Shortcuts** button in the status bar: the highlight's gap to the left edge matches the gaps above and below. **Expected result:** Strata looks identical on every desktop regardless of GTK theme, user stylesheet, or decoration policy, and the corner roundness setting reshapes the whole interface immediately. ## Related issue Closes #1678 Closes #1679 Closes #1098

issues.body:
### Problem or use case

On Hyprland, Strata presents without a conventional window frame. On other desktops (GNOME, KDE, XFCE, and similar stacking environments) the same build picks up extra window-manager / client-side decoration chrome: a border, shadow, or outer frame around the app.

That extra chrome is the part that should go away. Strata already draws its own header (location bar, actions, custom close) and hides GTK title buttons (`HeaderBar::set_show_title_buttons(false)`). The request is to keep that in-app header and drop the surrounding OS/CSD window border and decoration chrome everywhere, not only on Hyprland.

### Proposed solution

Disable window borders and decoration chrome for Strata windows on non-Hyprland distros so the outer frame matches the Hyprland look. Keep Strata's own header and close control. Apply the same treatment to other application windows that currently inherit the same decorations (for example the file chooser), unless a window truly needs a native frame.

Do not key the behavior on detecting Hyprland as a special case if a single undecorated presentation can work on supported desktops.

### Alternatives considered

- Leave decorations to the desktop: keeps a conventional frame on GNOME/KDE/XFCE, which is the gap this request is meant to close.
- A saved preference to show or hide the frame: more flexible, but the requested default is no outer chrome.
- Hide the in-app header as well: that would remove Strata's own controls, which is not the request.

### Visual examples

N/A — no mockup; compare the Hyprland window edge with the same build on a stacking desktop.

### Strata version

N/A — current main window construction (`gtk::ApplicationWindow` plus custom `HeaderBar`). Recheck against current main before implementation.

### Additional context

Searched open and closed lgse/strata issues for window chrome, decorations, borders, CSD, SSD, client-side decorations, Hyprland, titlebar, window frame, and hide chrome. No existing ticket asks to drop the outer window frame on non-Hyprland desktops.

Related but distinct:

- #469 / #497: XFCE toolbar and pane *icon* scale, not the window frame.
- #577 / #579: compact the in-app top bar height.
- #203: marquee from in-app pane chrome, not OS decorations.

Filed from the feature-request form. No P-band; triage can band it later.
issues.title: feat(window): disable window borders and chrome on non-Hyprland desktops

issues.body:
### Problem or use case

Every rounded corner in Strata is a fixed pixel radius in `src/style.css`: dialogs, buttons, settings groups, chips, menus, cards, badges, and the remaining GTK defaults such as switches and popovers. Users who want a squarer interface, or a softer one, have no way to change it without editing the stylesheet.

### Proposed solution

Add a **Corner roundness** preference under **Settings → Appearance**, stored in `settings.toml`, that scales every corner radius in the application. 0 squares every rounded rectangle; 100 keeps today's look; larger values round further. It should apply before Settings opens, live across windows, dialogs, menus, and rebuilt views, and cover elements whose radius comes from GTK's built-in theme rather than Strata's stylesheet.

### Alternatives considered

- A fixed set of named presets (square, default, round): less flexible than a numeric scale and no simpler to implement.
- Per-element controls: far more settings for little benefit; one scale keeps the design coherent.

### Visual examples

N/A — compare the current interface with corners set to 0 and 200.

### Strata version

Current main.

### Additional context

Searched open issues for roundness, radius, corners, and square; no existing ticket.
issues.title: feat(appearance): make corner roundness customizable

issues.body:
### Problem or use case

Strata's look changes under some desktops because GTK applies external styling to it:

- The desktop GTK theme, selected through the settings portal, `settings.ini`, or `GTK_THEME`, replaces GTK's built-in theme and changes button padding, row heights, letter spacing, and ellipsizing.
- `~/.config/gtk-4.0/gtk.css` loads at GTK's user priority, above Strata's stylesheets, so it can recolor or resize Strata widgets.
- The desktop color scheme and contrast settings choose the built-in theme's light, dark, or high-contrast variant under Strata's own CSS.
- On compositors that leave decorations to the application (GNOME Mutter, Weston, WSLg), GTK adds its own default title bar with a centered title and Adwaita window buttons above Strata's header, because the header is never registered as the window's titlebar (#1098 covers the outer chrome).

A user screenshot from a GNOME desktop shows taller rows, wider spacing, and the duplicate title bar.

### Proposed solution

Pin GTK's built-in theme and regular-contrast variant as application-sourced values, follow the active Strata theme's light or dark background for the built-in variant, drop `GTK_THEME` from the environment before GTK starts, and load Strata's stylesheets above GTK's user priority. Register a titlebar on every Strata window so GTK never creates its default decoration, while keeping Strata's header inside the content.

### Alternatives considered

- Documenting that user stylesheets win: leaves the reported breakage in place.
- A preference to show the GTK title bar: nobody wants two title bars; the window-button toggles already cover the controls it duplicates.

### Visual examples

N/A — user screenshot available in the PR.

### Strata version

Current main.

### Additional context

Related: #1098 (outer window chrome on non-Hyprland desktops).

author: l0gicgate
body:
## Description

#1680 put Strata's stylesheets above GTK's user priority, but that only wins for properties Strata's CSS defines. `~/.config/gtk-4.0/gtk.css` could still set everything Strata leaves to GTK's built-in theme, such as button min-widths, label padding, letter-spacing, outlines and icon sizes. Users with a GTK theme installed into their config saw extra padding around the `~` breadcrumb, among other things.

Two providers now sit between the user stylesheet and Strata's:

1. `* { all: unset; }` just above `STYLE_PROVIDER_PRIORITY_USER`
2. GTK's built-in `Default` theme (light or dark, following the active Strata theme), restated above the reset

Strata's stylesheet and tokens stay on top, so the user `gtk.css` no longer decides any property of Strata's widgets. The existing isolation regression now also covers a property Strata does not set itself (`label { color }`). It fails without the reset.

## Visual evidence

**Pending upload**: local captures (headless Xvfb, same folder) still need to be attached through the GitHub editor:

- Before: `gtk.css` with `button { min-width: 60px } button > label { padding: 0 12px } label { letter-spacing: 1px }` widens the `~` crumb and the sidebar rows
- After: same `gtk.css`, identical to running without it
- Before/after with an aggressive `gtk.css` (outlines, serif font, 40px icons, borders)

## How to test

1. Create `~/.config/gtk-4.0/gtk.css` containing:
   ```css
   button { min-width: 60px; }
   button > label { padding: 0 12px; }
   label { letter-spacing: 1px; }
   * { outline: 3px solid red; }
   ```
2. Launch Strata and open any folder.
3. Switch between a dark and a light theme in Settings > Appearance.

**Expected result:** Strata looks exactly as it does without the file in both theme variants. The `~` breadcrumb stays compact and nothing gets red outlines.

## Related issue

Closes #1681

body:
## Description

With the preview pane open, moving the cursor onto an archive stole keyboard focus into the pane: a password-protected archive focused its password field, and in List and Icons a plain archive highlighted its first member as though the preview had been entered. The password prompt now takes focus only when the preview was opened or entered explicitly (Space, Right / l), and no view highlights a member on a passive archive preview. The listing keeps focus and the cursor keeps moving.

Also updates `docs/keyboard-navigation.md` and `docs/10xer-mode.md`. In 10xer mode, **i** on a locked archive now leaves focus in the listing like it does for every other file; **l** hands the keys to the password field.

## Visual evidence

Pending: `gh` cannot upload attachments. After captures are retained locally at `scratchpad/list-b.zip.png` (plain archive, no member highlighted) and `scratchpad/list-d.zip.png` (password prompt shown, listing row still focused).

## How to test

1. Put a plain ZIP, a password-protected ZIP, and a few text files in one folder, sorted so the archives are not first.
2. Select the first text file and press Space to open the preview.
3. Press Down (List / Columns) or Right (Icons) across the plain ZIP, the password-protected ZIP, and the file after each.
4. On the password-protected ZIP, press Right (or l in 10xer mode), type a character, then press Escape.

**Expected result:** Focus never leaves the listing in step 3: the cursor moves to the next file on each press, the plain archive's preview shows its members with none highlighted, and the password prompt appears without a focused field. Arch Linux, Omarchy (Hyprland)

### What happened?

author: JoeJoeflyn
body:
## Description

Pin folders or reorder existing pins through compact sidebar insertion gaps, without changing folder-row transfers. Preserve selection order, skip duplicate new pins, and persist the resulting bookmarks and labels.

Internal folder and pin drags use provider-matched metadata without filesystem probes. Move-only internal offers are supported; external Move-only offers are rejected to avoid requesting source deletion. External folder validation remains asynchronous and bounded, and pending pin drops never fall through to file transfers. Remote pins and directory symlinks are supported without canonicalizing aliases.

## Visual evidence

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5358a968-b3b0-48ea-b73c-dcea7bca2482

## How to test

1. Drag folders from Columns, List, or Icons into an empty Pinned section, then before, between, and after existing pins. Repeat an internal drag with Shift held and a normal folder drag from another file manager.
2. Drag an existing local or remote sidebar pin into those same gaps to reorder it. Restart Strata.
3. Drop an already-pinned folder from the main pane into another gap, try files/mixed selections in a gap, and drop a file onto a pinned folder row.

**Expected result:** New folders pin in selection order and survive restart. Existing sidebar pins reorder through the insertion gaps without changing their labels or folder contents. Dragging an already-pinned folder from the main pane neither duplicates nor reorders it. Files/mixed selections do not pin or transfer through gaps; folder rows retain their transfer behavior.

## Related issue

Closes #1690

issues.body:
### Problem or use case

Folders cannot currently be pinned by dragging them into the sidebar. Dragging a folder from the browser into the sidebar is a faster, more direct way to pin it, and it is how most file managers let users build their sidebar.

### Proposed solution

Let users pin folders by dragging them into the **Pinned** section of the sidebar.

1. **Already pinned is a no-op.** Dropping a folder that is already pinned does not add a duplicate, and does not change the existing order.
2. **Choose the position.** While dragging over the Pinned section, show an insertion indicator between pinned rows (and before the first / after the last). Dropping inserts the new pin at that spot, and the resulting order is persisted like a manual reorder (#184).

Notes:

- Dropping *onto* an existing sidebar folder row must keep its current behavior of moving/copying the dragged items into that folder (#285). Pinning should only happen when dropping into the gaps between pinned rows, so the two targets need to be visually distinct.
- Only directories can be pinned. Dragged files, or a mixed selection, should not show the pin insertion indicator.
- Multi-folder drags should pin each folder that is not already pinned, in selection order, at the drop position.

### Alternatives considered

Pin through the context menu and then drag the new row into place with the existing reorder support. This works but takes two steps.

### Visual examples

N/A

### Additional context

Related: #184 (reordering pinned folders), #285 (sidebar drop targets for moving files).

comments.author: JoeJoeflyn
comments.body:
Implemented in draft PR #1692, commit `0d7f7fe7`. GitHub's full CI jobs currently skip draft PRs; they have not passed for this PR and remain required before merge.

### Approach and related performance opportunities

The agreed scope is to finish #1690, not redesign all filesystem access. Pinning now uses dedicated gaps, separate from folder-row transfers. Internal drags reuse provider-matched directory metadata; external drags validate asynchronously once across that sidebar's gaps, with one metadata query in flight and a two-second deadline including payload loading. Insertion resolves its anchor against freshly loaded bookmarks, deduplicates in a batch, and preserves selection order and path aliases. Directory symlinks are supported. Cancellation/timeout never falls through to a transfer.

**Recommended next target: Send to device discovery.** `src/ui/window/devices.rs::destination_for_mount` synchronously queries writability/type and then `is_dir()` while `src/ui/browser/context_menu/actions.rs` builds the menu. Move discovery/eligibility off the GTK thread, publish cached results, and revalidate the chosen device at dispatch. This is a concrete blocking-call finding, not a measured runtime regression.

**Next after that: remaining synchronous transfer-volume probes.** `src/adapters/volume.rs` already handles recognized remote mounts, autofs and symlink aliases asynchronously, with timeout coverage. Audit its native prefix probes and synchronous filesystem-identity fast path before adding more driver exceptions. Mount/URI names should determine scheduling at most, not whether two locations are the same filesystem.

For follow-up work, use deterministic delayed/failed/cancelled lookups first, then a small representative real-driver matrix: native/bind aliases; kernel NFS/CIFS; SSHFS/cloud FUSE; local symlinks into remote mounts; autofs parents with nested mounts; and USB removal/reinsertion/read-only transitions. Test source and destination independently rather than multiplying every combination blindly. Existing synthetic mount-table tests do not prove behavior on actual disconnected drivers. GIO cancellation cannot guarantee interruption of kernel-blocked I/O, so globally bounded admission remains a separate resilience question.

### Validation scope

The affected callers are shared drag-content creation, pin-gap lifecycle/eligibility, bookmark insertion/persistence, and coexistence with normal sidebar/file transfers, pin reordering and spring navigation. No transfer engine, mount classifier, dependency, build runner or preferences schema was changed. Targeted execution is therefore used; full Rust/E2E suites are left to unchanged CI. All GUI execution uses the canonical private displays/buses, never the desktop.

Rust commands (67 selected tests total):

```sh
./scripts/test-headless.py ui::browser::clipboard::tests       # 42 passed
./scripts/test-headless.py adapters::directory_validation::tests # 1 passed
./scripts/test-headless.py ui::window::pinned_drop::tests      # 4 passed
./scripts/test-headless.py ui::window::tests::sidebar          # 6 passed
./scripts/test-headless.py ui::window::tests::bookmarks        # 2 passed
./scripts/test-headless.py i18n::                             # 12 passed
```

The expired-provider regression was observed failing against the original working-tree implementation before fixing it. A new Columns E2E initially selected the child pane after folder navigation; source-pane addressing was corrected and that exact scenario passed on its scoped rerun.

Canonical affected E2E command (69 passed):

```sh
STRATA_CONTAINER_ENGINE=podman ./scripts/e2e.sh \
  tests/e2e/scenarios/test_sidebar_pinning.py \
  tests/e2e/scenarios/test_sidebar_file_drops.py \
  tests/e2e/scenarios/test_sidebar_reordering.py \
  tests/e2e/scenarios/test_drag_and_drop.py \
  tests/e2e/scenarios/test_visual_baselines.py --keep-artifacts
```

After the final pin-only payload/style refinements, the affected pinning and visual cases were rerun (**21 passed**):

```sh
STRATA_CONTAINER_ENGINE=podman ./scripts/e2e.sh \
  tests/e2e/scenarios/test_sidebar_pinning.py \
  tests/e2e/scenarios/test_visual_baselines.py --keep-artifacts
```

All pre-push checks passed:

```sh
STRATA_CONTAINER_ENGINE=podman ./scripts/quality.sh fmt
STRATA_CONTAINER_ENGINE=podman ./scripts/quality.sh clippy
git diff --cached --check
```

Pinned checks use Rust 1.98.1 / GTK 4.22.5 and the existing verified base/cache. No environment rebuild or baseline replacement was needed. No actual NFS/CIFS/FUSE outage, hot-unplug test or numeric performance benchmark was run; deterministic pending/cancel/timeout tests and real external GTK drag tests cover this change without claiming driver-level certification.

### Visual evidence pending upload

Please upload these sanitized captures through the PR description/comment editor and embed its GitHub-hosted attachment URLs in the PR's Visual evidence section:

- `target/1690-evidence/before-columns.png` — Before: existing Columns baseline, with no empty Pinned drop section.
- `target/1690-evidence/after-insertion.png` — After: three selected folders dragged above an existing pin, showing the themed insertion line. This is a real private-display capture; the separate capture hook remains ignored under `target/`, not in the test suite.

author: mvanhorn
body:
## Description

On GTK 4.14, choosing an action from a file's context menu, such as Open With..., can crash the app. GTK logs `gtk_widget_get_parent` / `gtk_widget_get_first_child` criticals and the process segfaults inside libgtk. Two separate GTK bugs cause this. Upstream fixed both by 4.22, which is why neither shows up on newer GTK or in E2E. This PR works around both in `src/ui/browser/context_menu/actions.rs`.

1. Use-after-free in `GtkMenuSectionBox`. GTK 4.12 to 4.16 connect `notify::position` on the popover to each section box with a raw pointer (4.22 switched to `g_signal_connect_object`). `ActionMenuSection::new` built the popover from an empty model and then cleared it, which freed one section box and left its handler connected. The next Top/Bottom change from `set_position`, for example a menu opened low in the window, ran `update_popover_position_cb` on freed memory. The popover is now created with no model through `gtk_popover_menu_new_from_model_full(NULL, NESTED)`, since gtk4-rs has no safe constructor for that. The lazily attached root model is the only one it ever builds.

2. NULL surface in `gtk_window_native_layout`. The menu unparents its popover in an idle after closing. On 4.14, pointer events delivered in between can leave the main window's pointer focus on the hidden `GtkPopoverMenu`. When the chooser closes, the window lays out and calls `gdk_surface_request_motion(NULL)` (4.22 added a NULL check there). Toggling the popover's sensitivity just before unparenting runs GTK's `update_pointer_focus_on_state_change`, which moves the pointer target back onto the main window. Both the close idle and `Drop` now go through the same `release_popover` helper.

Neither fix is enough alone. Across `test_open_with.py` and `test_dialogs_and_menus.py` (57 scenarios) on GTK 4.14.5:

| build | failed |
|---|---|
| `main` | 28 |
| original PR commit | crashes in the open-with cases, like `main` |
| pointer-focus fix only | 7 |
| constructor fix only | 22 |
| both (this branch) | 3 |

The remaining 3 are `test_submenu_arrows_return_keyboard_control_to_the_parent`. It fails the same way on `main` with the app still running, so it is a pre-existing 4.14 keyboard-submenu difference, not a crash.

The first version of this PR cleared the menu model on every close. It did not fix the crash (7 of 9 runs still segfaulted, the same rate as `main`) and it added about 40 `Gtk-WARNING: Broken accounting of active state` lines per run. That approach and its `test_open_with.py` extension are gone. CI pins GTK 4.22, which cannot hit either bug, so that test could not fail there. Reopening a menu after an item action and checking for criticals is already covered by `test_the_entry_context_menu_offers_named_actions_and_accelerators`. A real regression guard would need a GTK 4.14 CI lane, which is a separate infrastructure change.

## Visual evidence

No visual change. The fix stops a crash. The manual check below shows the window staying up.

## How to test

Verified by @l0gicgate:

- GTK 4.14: Ubuntu 24.04 container with the reporter's GTK (`libgtk-4-1 4.14.5+ds-0ubuntu0.10`) and the toolchain the release archive is built with. Results in the table above.
- Manual, on GTK 4.14.5: right-click a file, choose Open With..., pick an app. The window stays up and the chooser opens again. Passes 3 of 3 runs. `main` and the original commit crashed.
- GTK 4.22/4.24: `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -D warnings` are clean. Full headless Rust suite: 2767 passed, 9 ignored. Full canonical E2E suite: 1088 passed. Two `test_rename_visibility` List cases timed out waiting for the browser's working state under load. Both pass alone, and the whole file passes (20/20).

## Related issue

Closes #1642

AI was used for assistance.

issues.body:
### Strata version

1.0.0

### Installation method

GitHub release archive

### Linux distribution and desktop environment

Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS, GNOME on X11, GTK 4.14.5 (libgtk-4-1 4.14.5+ds-0ubuntu0.10), glibc 2.39

### What happened?

Choosing any action from an item's context menu — for example **Open With…** — makes the whole window close and nothing else happens. The journal shows two GTK assertion failures at the moment the menu item is activated, and ~7 seconds later the kernel logs a SIGSEGV inside `libgtk-4.so.1.1400.5`. The Open With dialog never appears.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Launch Strata (native binary from the release archive) on Ubuntu 24.04 with GTK 4.14.5.
2. Right-click a file in the browser.
3. Choose **Open With…**.
4. The menu closes, the application window closes, and no dialog appears. `journalctl -k` shows a segfault in libgtk.

### Expected behavior

The Open With dialog opens; the application keeps running.

### Screenshots or video

None

### Relevant logs

```
journalctl --user (application messages):

16:43:54 strata[3122954]: gtk_widget_get_parent: assertion 'GTK_IS_WIDGET (widget)' failed
16:43:54 strata[3122954]: gtk_widget_get_first_child: assertion 'GTK_IS_WIDGET (widget)' failed
16:44:02 systemd[2293]: app-gnome-io.github.lgse.Strata-3122954.scope: Consumed 7.057s CPU time.

journalctl -k (kernel):

16:44:01 kernel: strata[3122954]: segfault at 77 ip 00007d2094294e34 sp 00007ffe655acfd8 error 6 in libgtk-4.so.1.1400.5[7d2093eb0000+49b000] likely on CPU 9 (core 3, socket 0)
```

`coredumpctl list strata` shows no stored coredump for this crash.

### Additional context

This looks like the same code path as #1569 (the after-paint idle that unpairs the item PopoverMenu once it closes, `src/ui/browser/context_menu/actions.rs:171`): there, on GTK 4.22, the teardown logs GLib/GTK CRITICALs but the app survives. On GTK 4.14.5 the widget is already disposed when unparented, so `gtk_widget_get_parent` / `gtk_widget_get_first_child` dereference a dead widget and the process segfaults.

The README states GTK 4.12 or newer is supported, so 4.14 should be in range. Reproduced twice in a row today; it seems deterministic on this system. Happy to run further diagnostics (e.g. `G_DEBUG=fatal-criticals` with a debug build) if that helps.

comments.author: mvanhorn
comments.body:
After the menu closes, an after-paint idle looks up the popover's parent and unparents it, and the same unparent runs when the menu section is dropped. On GTK 4.14 the generated menu children are already disposed while that popover is still parented, so those parent and child queries hit a dead widget, trip the assertions, and crash.

Teardown now watches destroy on the popover and its child.

author: ogarza
body:
## Description

RAW previews went through the generic image path, which broke two formats in different ways:

- **Fuji RAF (all variants, including lossless compressed):** nothing reads the RAF container, so ImageMagick demosaics the full 40 MP sensor data. In the browser worker (`MAGICK_THREAD_LIMIT=1`, 10 s CPU limit) that takes about 20 s against the 12 s wall limit, so every preview timed out.
- **DNG:** GdkPixbuf's TIFF loader reads the 160×120 IFD0 thumbnail and reports that as the image size, so the preview was rendered at 160 px. The Pentax files embed a full 6016×4000 JPEG.

A `PreviewRaw` operation, chosen for RAW file names, renders the camera's embedded preview at preview size (800 px), as RAW thumbnails already did. If `dcraw` and `simple_dcraw` can't extract it and GdkPixbuf only sees a thumbnail-sized image such as a DNG's IFD0, the preview tries ImageMagick before falling back to that thumbnail. Thumbnails keep the cheaper GdkPixbuf decode. Embedded previews follow their EXIF orientation, so portrait shots are upright in previews and thumbnails. RAW thumbnails that an older build cached sideways in the shared thumbnail cache are rendered once more and replaced: Strata now tags the RAW thumbnails it stores and treats untagged RAW entries as stale.

The icon caption's size probe now reads RAW files with the same LibRaw/dcraw and EXIF reader as the RAW details panel, so a DNG no longer reads 160×120 there.

The RAW list also covers the other still-camera formats LibRaw-based tools read: ARI, ARQ, BAY, CRW, DC2, FFF, GPR, IIQ, K25, KC2, MDC, ORI, PXN, QTK, RDC and RWZ. A listed name counts as an image even when shared-mime-info doesn't know it, in the preview, the Type column, custom-action matching and chooser filters. Camera import uses the same list. `.ptx` (also Pro Tools sessions) and `.crf` (not a LibRaw extension) are left out.

Oversized JPEGs, such as the reporter's 42374×10529 panorama (about 1.8 GB decoded against the 512 MB budget), used to render only from an EXIF thumbnail, so the panorama had no preview. They now use the EXIF thumbnail only when it covers the requested size; otherwise ImageMagick decodes them at reduced scale through a `jpeg:size` hint. ImageMagick also gets the decoded-frame budget as its pixel-area limit with no disk spill, so a full-size decode of an oversized image fails in milliseconds instead of filling the sandbox.

Measured under the worker's constraints on the reporter's files:

| File | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| X-T5 RAF (lossless) | ~20 s, times out | 0.13 s, 800×533 |
| Pentax KP DNG (portrait) | 160×120, sideways | 0.2 s, 532×800, upright |
| 42374×10529 panorama JPEG | no preview | 0.75 s, 800×199 |

## Visual evidence

Pending: before/after captures will be added through the GitHub editor.

## How to test

1. Open a folder of Fuji `.RAF` files (for example X-T5 lossless compressed) and select one with the preview pane open.
2. Select a Pentax `.DNG` taken in portrait orientation, then switch to Icons view.
3. Select a very large JPEG panorama (for example 40000×10000 px).
4. Open a RAW folder that an earlier build already thumbnailed.

**Expected result:** the RAF preview appears right away instead of timing out. The DNG preview fills the pane and is upright, its thumbnail is upright, and its Icons caption shows the full image size rather than 160×120. The panorama shows a thumbnail and a preview. Previously sideways RAW thumbnails are replaced with upright ones.

## Related issue

Closes #1666

issues.body:
## Summary

Strata already has several strong security properties, especially around untrusted preview parsing and local filesystem operations. The Bubblewrap preview sandbox, resource limits, `openat2`-based local operations, archive path validation, and release provenance infrastructure are all good foundations.

After reviewing the current code and release flow, I think there are a few areas where the security model could be tightened further, particularly around installation and self-updates.

This issue is intended as a hardening proposal rather than a report of known active compromise.

## Main areas to consider

### 1. Avoid recommending `curl .../main/install.sh | bash`

The current interactive installation path uses a mutable script from the default branch:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lgse/strata/main/install.sh | bash
```

The installer itself later performs SHA-256 and GitHub attestation verification on the Strata release artifact, which is good.

The remaining bootstrap issue is that the installer script is executed before the script itself has been authenticated.

If the repository/default branch or maintainer credentials were compromised, a malicious `install.sh` could execute as the user without ever reaching the release verification step.

### Proposed improvement

Prefer an installation flow where the installer itself comes from an authenticated release artifact.

For example:

```text
GitHub release
    ↓
download archive + checksum
    ↓
verify SHA-256
    ↓
verify GitHub attestation
    ↓
extract verified archive
    ↓
run verified installer
```

Alternatively, document a pinned release/tag or commit-based installation method rather than executing mutable `main` directly.

---

### 2. Verify build provenance in the in-app updater

The release workflow already generates GitHub build-provenance attestations, and the interactive installer verifies them.

The in-app updater currently appears to validate the downloaded archive using its published SHA-256 value but does not perform equivalent provenance verification.

A checksum protects against corruption, but if an attacker gained control of the release publishing path, they could theoretically publish both a malicious archive and the matching checksum.

### Proposed improvement

Require provenance verification before replacing the running executable.

Conceptually:

```text
download release
      ↓
verify expected release URL
      ↓
verify SHA-256
      ↓
verify GitHub build provenance
      ↓
verify source commit
      ↓
install
```

A first implementation could use:

```bash
gh attestation verify <archive> --repo lgse/strata
```

and fail closed if verification cannot be performed.

Longer term, Strata could perform Sigstore/GitHub attestation verification directly without depending on the GitHub CLI.

---

### 3. Restrict updater download URLs

The update installer currently accepts a download URL through its install request.

It may be useful to explicitly validate that update artifacts originate only from the expected Strata release location.

For example, require:

```text
https://github.com/lgse/strata/releases/download/<expected-tag>/<expected-asset>
```

and reject unexpected hosts, repository names, tags, asset names, or schemes.

This adds another defense layer if malformed or unexpected release metadata ever reaches the installer.

---

### 4. Add hard limits to update downloads

The update download path should ideally have a maximum accepted archive size.

A compromised or malfunctioning server could otherwise stream a very large response and potentially exhaust disk space.

Suggested approach:

```rust
const MAX_UPDATE_ARCHIVE_BYTES: u64 = 64 * 1024 * 1024;
const MAX_CHECKSUM_BYTES: u64 = 8 * 1024;
```

The exact values can be tuned based on normal Strata release sizes.

Both `Content-Length` and streamed bytes should be checked, since `Content-Length` cannot be assumed to always be present or trustworthy.

---

### 5. Verify `SOURCE_COMMIT` before installation

Strata release archives already contain `SOURCE_COMMIT`.

It would be useful to compare this value with the commit expected for the selected release before replacing the installed binary.

Example:

```text
release tag → expected commit
                  │
archive SOURCE_COMMIT
                  │
                  ▼
                match?
              /        \
            yes        no
             ↓          ↓
         install      reject
```

This would tie together release metadata, provenance, and the actual artifact being installed.

---

### 6. Consider extracting update archives in-process

The self-update path currently invokes the system `tar` executable.

Since Strata already depends on Rust archive libraries, update extraction could potentially be performed inside Strata.

This would allow the updater to explicitly reject unexpected archive contents before writing anything.

For example, reject:

```text
absolute paths
..
symlinks
hardlinks
FIFOs
devices
sockets
unexpected filenames
unexpected nesting
```

The updater only needs a very small known set of files, so an allowlist could be practical.

Example expected layout:

```text
strata-VERSION-ARCH/
├── strata
├── SOURCE_COMMIT
├── README.md
├── LICENSE
├── THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md
├── io.github.lgse.Strata.desktop
└── io.github.lgse.Strata.svg
```

Anything outside the expected layout could fail closed.

---

## Additional hardening ideas

### 7. Add dependency-vulnerability checks to CI

The current CI already performs formatting, compilation, Clippy, and tests.

It may also be useful to add:

```bash
cargo audit
cargo deny check
```

This would provide automated coverage for newly disclosed RustSec advisories and unexpected dependency sources.

A `deny.toml` could be used to define the project's dependency security policy.

---

### 8. Add extraction resource limits

The archive traversal vulnerability reported in #109 appears to have been addressed, and current path validation is significantly stronger.

A separate concern is resource exhaustion from archive bombs.

Possible limits:

```text
maximum number of entries
maximum single extracted file size
maximum total extracted size
maximum archive nesting/depth
maximum filename/path length
```

The exact limits could be generous enough for normal file-manager use while preventing pathological archives from consuming unlimited disk space or resources.

---

### 9. Complete the filesystem-race audit

Issue #8 is still open, although recent work in #253, #254, and #255 appears to have implemented most or all of the intended descriptor-relative hardening.

It may be useful to perform one final security-focused review against the original acceptance criteria and then either close #8 or document any remaining edge cases.

Particularly valuable regression tests would include:

```text
source directory replaced with symlink during copy
nested directory replaced during traversal
destination replaced during overwrite
directory replaced during permanent delete
file ↔ directory type changes during operation
parent path replacement during operation
```

The desired behavior in each case should be failure rather than following the substituted path.

---

### 10. Document a hardened configuration

Strata's preview sandbox is one of its strongest security features.

It may be worth documenting a conservative configuration for users who prioritize security over hardware acceleration.

For example:

```text
Release channel: Stable
Automatic updates: Verified only
Preview sandbox: Enabled
Media preview backend: Software
Remote locations: Explicit user action only
```

Software media decoding avoids exposing GPU render devices to sandboxed parsers, which slightly reduces the available attack surface.

---

## Things that already look strong

This proposal is not meant to overlook the security work already present.

Current Strata includes several good defenses:

* Bubblewrap sandboxing for untrusted thumbnail/preview parsing
* no general network access inside the preview sandbox
* private sandbox home/environment
* CPU, memory, runtime, and output limits
* process-group termination on timeout/cancellation
* `openat2` with `RESOLVE_BENEATH`
* `RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS`
* `RESOLVE_NO_MAGICLINKS`
* file-type revalidation for sensitive local operations
* archive path validation
* Rust `unsafe_code = "deny"`
* SHA-pinned GitHub Actions
* GitHub build-provenance attestations
* source commit metadata in release archives
* release workflow checks against default-branch changes during release

The main goal here would be to extend that same defense-in-depth philosophy to the installation and update paths.

---

## Suggested priority

### P0 / security-sensitive

* [ ] Stop recommending execution of mutable `main/install.sh` directly
* [ ] Verify GitHub build provenance during self-update
* [ ] Validate updater repository/tag/asset URL
* [ ] Add hard update download limits
* [ ] Verify `SOURCE_COMMIT`
* [ ] Harden/allowlist update archive extraction

### P1

* [ ] Add `cargo audit`
* [ ] Add `cargo deny`
* [ ] Add archive resource-exhaustion limits
* [ ] Complete/review the remaining scope of #8

### P2

* [ ] Add/document a hardened user configuration
* [ ] Consider native attestation verification instead of requiring `gh`

## Expected outcome

The desired trust model would become:

```text
                    Strata
                      │
        ┌─────────────┼─────────────┐
        │             │             │
        ▼             ▼             ▼
 File operations   Previews       Updates
        │             │             │
     openat2       Bubblewrap     HTTPS
        │             │             │
RESOLVE_BENEATH   no network     URL allowlist
NO_SYMLINKS       resource caps      │
NO_MAGICLINKS         │            SHA-256
        │             │              │
        ▼             ▼          provenance
  local files     parsers            │
                                  source commit
                                      │
                                safe extraction
                                      │
                                atomic install
```

I think these changes would complement Strata's existing security architecture and substantially reduce supply-chain and update-path compromise risk without requiring a major redesign.

comments.author: spandan11106
comments.body:
Thanks for the thorough writeup — this lines up with where I want the update path to go.

I went through the current tree against the list. Confirming what is still open:

- **2–6 (P0)** all hold. `src/services/update_install.rs` downloads the archive, verifies the SHA-256, and then shells out to `tar`. There is no attestation check, `download_url` arrives as an unvalidated string on the install request, `content-length` is read only to drive the progress bar rather than to cap the transfer, and `SOURCE_COMMIT` is never compared against the tag being installed.
- **1 (P0)** holds too. `install.sh` itself does verify — `sha256sum --check` plus `gh attestation verify` — so the gap is purely the bootstrap: the README still pipes the script off `main` before anything has authenticated it.

One item is already done: **7**. `deny.toml` is in the repo, `cargo-deny-action` runs in `ci.yml`, and `scripts/check.sh` runs `cargo deny check` locally. Since the advisories check there already covers RustSec, adding `cargo audit` on top would be redundant — I would drop that one from the list.

On sequencing, I would split this rather than take it as one change. The URL allowlist, the download size limits, and the `SOURCE_COMMIT` comparison are self-contained and testable on their own. Provenance verification and in-process extraction are each large enough to want their own issue and discussion — in particular whether we are willing to make `gh` a hard runtime requirement of the updater, or whether we hold that until native Sigstore verification lands.

comments.author: spandan11106
comments.body:
Following up on the overlap: most of this list is already tracked in existing issues, so I want to get the boundaries straight before anyone starts work.

**#148 — harden in-place update safety and recovery** covers essentially the whole P0 block here, and predates this issue. Its authentication and input-validation section already asks to authenticate the archive with trusted provenance or a signed manifest rather than a checksum fetched from the same release (item 2 here), bind verification to the expected release version, architecture, asset name and trusted source (item 3), and reject malformed metadata, unexpected redirects or assets, oversized downloads and unexpected archive layouts (items 4 and 6). It also carries a fair amount this issue does not mention: install eligibility detection, cancellation, an application-wide install lock, mode-0700 staging, rollback retention until a successful restart, and the test matrix for all of it.

Item 5 — comparing the archive's `SOURCE_COMMIT` against the commit expected for the selected release — is the one part of the P0 block I do not see covered anywhere. That is a good addition and I would fold it into #148 rather than track it separately, since it belongs to the same verification chain.

**#479 — archive extraction has no size, ratio, or entry-count limits** is item 8. It is filed with more precision than the summary here: it identifies `copy_with_big_buf` in `src/adapters/local_operations.rs` as the shared unbounded loop behind the zip, tar and 7z extraction paths, and proposes a ceiling derived from free space at the destination via `statvfs` alongside a fixed maximum.

**#8 — harden recursive file operations against symlink and TOCTOU races** is item 9, which this issue already links. Work is live there: the acceptance criteria have been walked back through against what #253, #254 and #255 actually landed, so the closing review you are asking for is in progress in that thread.

That leaves this issue with item 1 (the `curl | bash` bootstrap, which is a docs and release-packaging change rather than an updater change), item 5, and item 10 (documenting a hardened configuration). Items 2, 3, 4, 6, 8 and 9 have homes already, and 7 is done.

@l0gicgate — two ways to go. Either narrow this to items 1, 5 and 10 and let #148, #479 and #8 carry the rest, or keep it as the umbrella and close out the duplicated checkboxes with pointers. I lean towards the first, mainly so that whoever picks up #148 is not working against two overlapping specifications of the same verification chain.

@theaxlklo — none of this is a knock on the writeup, it is a good survey and the `SOURCE_COMMIT` idea is worth having. If you want to take a piece of it, item 1 is the most self-contained: it is a change to how we publish and document the installer, with no updater code involved.

author: spandan11106
body:
## Description

Two test fixtures depended on the host:

- `open_with_hides_recently_used_for_uninstalled_applications` removed its only fake text/plain application and then expected the chooser to open again. Without another installed text/plain handler, Strata correctly reports that no compatible application exists, so the test timed out. The fixture now installs a second fake handler that is never launched or removed.
- `release_tar_format_extracts_long_prerelease_portal_paths` generated its archive through the production `trusted_command` lookup, which only searches fixed system directories. It now runs `tar` from `PATH` for fixture generation only; production helper resolution and trust checks are unchanged.

Assertions, timeouts, and the GNU/USTAR cases are unchanged.

## Visual evidence

N/A: test-only change.

## How to test

1. Hide host desktop entries and the system tar while keeping a GNU tar on `PATH`, e.g. with bubblewrap: `bwrap --dev-bind / / --tmpfs /usr/share/applications --ro-bind /dev/null /usr/bin/tar --tmpfs /tmp --setenv PATH "<dir with tar>:$PATH" -- ./scripts/test-headless.py -- open_with_hides_recently_used_for_uninstalled_applications release_tar_format_extracts_long_prerelease_portal_paths`
2. Run the same command on `main` for comparison.

**Expected result:** both tests pass on this branch. On `main` they fail with `keyboard fixture did not settle` and `tar was not found in a trusted system directory`.

## Related issue

Closes #1694

issues.body:
### Strata version

Current main, `52b8ad9c7ee9ee82cb0495055dcdfe87316ab8a4` (1.0.0).

### Installation method

Built from source; test executables only, with no application installation.

### Linux distribution and desktop environment

NixOS, x86_64-linux: Rust/Cargo 1.98.1, GTK 4.22.4, GLib 2.88.3, GNU tar 1.35. Reproduction used private Xvfb and D-Bus, disposable HOME/XDG directories, and an isolated view of system applications and helper directories.

The proposed changes were also checked in the upstream pinned Arch Linux test image: Rust/Cargo 1.98.1, GTK 4.22.5, GLib 2.88.3 and GNU tar 1.35 at `/usr/bin/tar`, using the existing headless runner. No host display, session bus or Nix libraries were mounted into that container.

### What happened?

While maintaining the Nix package, I found two test fixtures that depend on the host layout or installed applications:

1. **Open With:** `open_with_hides_recently_used_for_uninstalled_applications` creates and launches one fake text/plain application, deletes its desktop entry, then waits for the chooser again. If no other compatible application is installed, the chooser correctly stays closed and the test times out. An unrelated installed editor can mask the missing fixture.
2. **Release tar:** `release_tar_format_extracts_long_prerelease_portal_paths` uses the production `trusted_command::command("tar")` resolver to generate a fixture. In a non-FHS build environment, GNU tar can be available on PATH while absent from the resolver's fixed system directories. The test then fails before exercising extraction.

These currently need two downstream test patches. Could we address both in one small test-only PR?

### Steps to reproduce

1. Use the main commit above in an isolated, provisioned build environment with the required GTK resources and MIME database. Use a private Xvfb display/session bus, set `STRATA_REQUIRE_GTK_TESTS=1`, and use disposable HOME/XDG directories.
2. For Open With, make sure no host text/plain applications are visible, then run:

   ```sh
   cargo test --locked --all-targets --all-features \
     ui::window::tests::keyboard_dispatch::file_verbs::open_with_hides_recently_used_for_uninstalled_applications \
     -- --exact --test-threads=1
   ```

   On NixOS, HOME/XDG isolation alone may leave system/user profile applications visible through GLib; those profiles were hidden in the reproduction namespace.
3. For release tar, provide GNU tar on the test PATH without also installing it into one of the production resolver's fixed directories, then run:

   ```sh
   cargo test --locked --all-targets --all-features \
     services::update_install::archive::tests::release_tar_format_extracts_long_prerelease_portal_paths \
     -- --exact --test-threads=1
   ```

### Expected behavior

The Open With fixture should provide the compatible applications it needs. The archive fixture should be able to use the GNU tar supplied by the build's test environment. Both should retain their existing assertions and work on normal FHS distributions too.

### Screenshots or video

N/A: test fixture defects; no user-visible behavior or layout change is proposed.

### Relevant logs

Unmodified main, one exact test per run:

```text
Open With:
keyboard fixture did not settle
test result: FAILED. 0 passed; 1 failed; 0 ignored

Release tar:
tar was not found in a trusted system directory
test result: FAILED. 0 passed; 1 failed; 0 ignored
```

### Additional context

The minimal local candidates are:

- Add one additional text/plain recorder application to the Open With fixture. It is neither launched nor uninstalled, so the chooser can still open after removing the history entry.
- Use `std::process::Command::new("tar")` only when generating this test archive. GNU tar remains a test prerequisite. Production helper discovery and its trust checks remain unchanged, including the protections introduced by #1045 / #1055.

The original assertions, timeouts, GNU/USTAR cases and archive safety checks are preserved. There are no new dependencies or distribution-specific branches in either candidate.

Targeted results for the candidates, with all features enabled:

| Environment | Open With and keyboard routes | Update archive tests |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Isolated Nix environment | 12 passed, 0 failed, 0 ignored | 14 passed, 0 failed, 0 ignored |
| Upstream pinned Arch image | 12 passed, 0 failed, 0 ignored | 14 passed, 0 failed, 0 ignored |

GTK tests were required to run, with no silent skips. Full Rust/E2E suites and pre-push formatting/lint checks have not been run for these candidates. No PR has been opened; this issue is to discuss the approach first, especially whether PATH lookup is appropriate for this test-only tar fixture or a test-specific override would be preferred.

If this approach is welcome, could you assign the issue to me for a follow-up PR?

Prepared with assistance from Codex (GPT-6).
