author: l0gicgate
body:
## Description

Adds **Settings → Diagnostics**, so users and maintainers can find out why previews, thumbnails, network locations, drives or desktop integration don't work. Nothing runs until **Run** is selected, and no check changes or installs anything.

Where possible a check runs the feature itself instead of looking for a binary. It renders a sample image through a one-shot bubblewrap sandbox and through the pooled workers, a sample PDF and a one-second video through the same thumbnail path as the file list, and reads FFprobe metadata for a sample WAV. It also tests the HTTPS connection to the update server through `api.github.com/rate_limit`, which doesn't count against the rate limit. The remaining checks cover sandbox helper tools (looked up on the sandbox's build-time `PATH`, not the user's), GStreamer audio elements and sink, GVfs and the SFTP/SMB/FTP/WebDAV/MTP/AFC/gphoto2 backends, UDisks2 and the volume monitor, xdg-desktop-portal, Secret Service, folder monitoring and the inotify limit, the terminal, GtkSourceView language data, the MIME database, RAR support and custom actions.

Results stream in as each check finishes, below a compact **System** box with the version and environment details. Each result is marked passed, warning or problem, says what is affected and, when it knows the package, shows an install command for the distribution detected from `os-release`. The command can be copied or run in the user's terminal with its play button; the words are passed as arguments rather than through a shell, and the terminal stays open until Enter is pressed. **Copy report** copies everything, with version, installation method, toolkit, GStreamer, kernel, desktop, display server and renderer, for bug reports. The bug report form gets an optional field for it.

Developer notes are in `docs/diagnostics.md`. All strings are translated into the 11 supported languages.

## Visual evidence

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/264a5a68-023c-4c8f-8e58-a27fbc6b6884

## How to test

1. Open Settings and select **Diagnostics** in the sidebar.
2. Select **Run**.
3. Uninstall an optional tool such as `ffmpegthumbnailer` or `squashfs-tools` (or start Strata with `GIO_USE_VFS=local`), then select **Run** again.
4. Select the play button in the install command for the missing tool.
5. Select **Copy report** and paste it into a text editor.

**Expected result:** Every row moves from "Checking…" to a result within a few seconds, and the summary shows the counts. On a complete install, the sandbox, worker, PDF, video and audio rows pass. A missing tool shows a warning with an install command for your distribution, and `GIO_USE_VFS=local` shows the GVfs problem, with the remote backends reported as unavailable. The play button opens your terminal running the install command, which waits for Enter before closing. The pasted report lists the environment details shown in the System box and every result grouped by section.

## Related issue

Closes #1734

author: l0gicgate
body:
## Description

- Moves the E2E jobs (`E2E build and plan`, `E2E shard N`, `End-to-end GUI suite`) out of `ci.yml` into a new `.github/workflows/e2e.yml` that only runs on `workflow_dispatch`, with the existing `require_published_environments` input. PRs and pushes no longer run E2E.
- `Warm E2E dependencies` no longer triggers on pull requests, since nothing on PRs consumes that cache. It still runs daily, on main dependency changes, and on dispatch.
- Splits the Rust tests into four shards instead of two (`SHARDS = 4` in `scripts/quality_ci.py`, matrix `[0, 1, 2, 3]`). The `quality_ci` mechanism tests pin their two-shard fixture explicitly.
- Updates `docs/e2e-testing.md` and the workflow structure tests.

**Ruleset change needed at merge:** `End-to-end GUI suite` is a required status check in the `Protect main` ruleset. Remove it there, or this PR and every later PR will wait on a check that never reports.

## Visual evidence

N/A — CI configuration only.

## How to test

1. Open this PR's checks: `Rust tests shard 0`–`3` run, and no E2E jobs appear.
2. After merge, go to **Actions → E2E → Run workflow**, pick a branch, and run it (or `gh workflow run e2e.yml --ref <branch>`). Dispatch only becomes available once `e2e.yml` is on `main`.

**Expected result:** PR CI passes without E2E (once the ruleset is updated), the quality gate verifies four shard receipts, and the manual E2E run builds, shards, and aggregates as before.

## Related issue

Closes #1736

issues.body:
## Problem

The end-to-end GUI suite runs on every non-draft pull request as part of the CI workflow. It is the most expensive part of CI (a build job plus several sharded 4-vCPU runners) and gates every PR.

## Proposal

Move the E2E jobs out of `ci.yml` into a dedicated `E2E` workflow that runs only through `workflow_dispatch`, so it can be launched on demand against any branch. Stop warming the E2E dependency cache on pull requests, since nothing on PRs consumes it any more.

The "End-to-end GUI suite" required status check must be removed from the `Protect main` ruleset when this lands, or PRs will wait on a check that never reports.

author: l0gicgate
body:
## Description

The action editor builds its toggles with the same `settings_option` builder as Settings, but the Settings look was in `.settings-dialog switch` rules, which the separate editor dialog doesn't match. That style is now the global `switch` style and the Settings-only override is gone, so every toggle looks the same.

The knob's radius is now 5/6 of the track's, the same ratio as their heights. Corner roundness scales both together, so both are full circles from 50% up (including the 60% default) and square off together below that. Toggles are 2px wider so the knob is square.

The action editor's General/Script/Behavior tabs use natural case and no longer get a background on hover. Inactive tab labels sit at reduced opacity and fade to full opacity on hover. The focus ring now has room around the text. The underline is drawn by the label, so it stays as wide as the text.

The action editor's footer no longer has its own background, button styles or Cancel override. Cancel is outlined and Create action/Save changes uses the shared confirm style, like every other dialog.

Arrow keys can now reach the editor's tabs. Modal arrow navigation only collected buttons, check buttons, switches and entries, so the tab strip was never a target. The current tab is now a candidate: Up/Down treat the strip as spanning the page, and Left/Right on a focused tab are left to GTK, which switches tabs.

## Visual evidence

Pending: the owner will upload before/after captures of the action editor and Settings toggles at several corner-roundness values, and of the action editor's tabs (hovered and focused) and footer.

## How to test

1. Open Settings → Actions → **New action** → **Behavior**, then compare the **Confirm** toggle with any Settings toggle.
2. Hover the **General**, **Script** and **Behavior** tabs in the same dialog, press Tab to focus the tab strip, and compare the footer with another dialog such as Delete.
3. On the **Behavior** tab, focus **Whole selection** and press Up, then Left/Right, then Down.
4. In Settings → Appearance, move **Corner roundness** through 0%, 40%, 60% and 200%.

**Expected result:** All toggles share one style. The knob is a circle whenever the track is fully rounded, and below 50% the knob and track square off together. Hovering an inactive tab shows no background; its label fades in to full opacity. The keyboard focus ring clears the tab text. The footer has no background and matches other dialogs. Up from the page focuses the current tab, Left/Right switch tabs, and Down returns into the page.

## Related issue

Closes #1738

author: l0gicgate
body:
## Description

External file providers can now place root actions inside the **Send to…** submenu instead of their own heading section, by adding `"placement": "send-to"` to a menu reply. Destinations such as paired KDE Connect devices sit next to removable drives, in a group labelled with the provider's registered name, so the labels can be bare device names.

**Send to…** now appears whenever any destination exists, removable or provider-supplied, including entries that arrive while the menu is open, and disappears when the last one is withdrawn. Provider destinations may carry `children` with the usual tree bounds; their leaves activate, refresh and retire exactly like section leaves. `placement` is read on root actions only, ignored on background menus and in menus without Send to…, and unrecognized values keep the section, so providers using it degrade to a heading section on older Strata versions.

Host changes: a `Placement` field in the protocol, the renderer splits placed actions into labelled sections of a second model, and the context menu keeps a persistent Send to… model whose first group is the removable-drive list and whose later groups mirror provider sections live. `docs/file-providers.md` documents the field.

## Visual evidence

Pending upload: captures are retained locally and will be attached through the GitHub editor.

## How to test

1. Register a provider under `~/.config/strata/providers/<id>/` (see `docs/file-providers.md`) whose `menu` reply returns `{"id":"pixel","label":"Pixel","placement":"send-to"}` for files, and restart Strata.
2. With no removable drive attached, right-click a file. **Send to…** should be present; hover or click it to see a group labelled with the provider name containing **Pixel**. The provider's other actions stay in its own section.
3. Plug in a USB drive while the menu is open. The drive group appears first inside **Send to…**, above the provider group.
4. Make the provider emit an `invalidate` event and return a second destination. The open submenu gains it without closing.
5. Choose a destination. The provider receives `activate` with that action id and the whole selection.
6. Make the provider return no placed actions and unplug the drive. **Send to…** disappears; built-in commands remain.

**Expected result:** provider destinations live under **Send to…** alongside drives, update live, and activate like any provider leaf. Providers without `placement` are unchanged.

## Related issue

Closes #1740

issues.body:
### Problem or use case

External file providers (`docs/file-providers.md`) can only contribute actions to their own inline section with a muted provider heading. Some integrations are really *destinations*: KDE Connect devices (#1703, #1704), and in future other device or sharing targets. For those, a separate "KDE Connect" section duplicates what **Send to…** already means, and the provider has to bake "via KDE Connect" into every label. Users expect paired devices next to removable drives, under the single **Send to…** entry.

### Proposed solution

Add an additive, optional `placement` field to root actions in protocol 1 menu replies:

```json
{"version":1,"id":2,"actions":[
  {"id":"pixel","label":"Pixel","icon":"phone","placement":"send-to","context":"…"},
  {"id":"tablet","label":"Tablet","icon":"tablet","placement":"send-to","context":"…"}
]}
```

Host behavior:

- Root actions with `placement: "send-to"` render inside the **Send to…** submenu instead of the provider's heading section. Each provider gets its own labelled section (the registered provider name) below the removable-drive section, so device labels stay clean and the source stays visible.
- **Send to…** appears whenever removable drives *or* provider send-to entries exist, including when entries arrive after the menu is open (the provider model is already live; the Send to… submenu needs the same treatment). The row disappears again when the last entry is withdrawn.
- Children are allowed (a device may offer sub-choices), with the same depth and node bounds. Leaves activate exactly like section leaves: same retirement on refresh/withdrawal, same activation reply, outcome dialog, and `feedback` handling.
- Root actions without `placement`, or with an unrecognized value, keep today's behavior, so a provider that uses the field degrades to a heading section on older Strata versions without a handshake.
- Background (folder) menus never show Send to…, so `placement` is ignored there.

Document the field in `docs/file-providers.md` and extend `file_providers` unit tests, the context-menu Send to tests, and `tests/e2e/scenarios/test_file_providers.py`.

### Alternatives considered

- A dedicated `send-to` method or device-list response: more host code and a second tree model for no gain over reusing the action tree.
- Building KDE Connect into Strata natively: contradicts the opt-in provider model and the planned integrations catalog.
- Keeping a separate provider section (current #1704): works, but duplicates Send to… and needs provider-side label suffixes.

### Visual examples

```text
Send to…  ▸  USB drive        ▸
             ── KDE Connect ──
             Pixel
             Tablet
```

### Additional context

First step of the integrations plan; the catalog issue is #1741. #1704 will switch its menu reply to flat `placement: "send-to"` leaves once this lands.

## Description

Adds a full Traditional Chinese (zh-TW) locale to Strata, translated from the English source with Taiwan terminology (not converted from zh-CN). Implements the Option A routing decided in #1613: `zh_TW`, `zh_HK`, `zh_MO`, and `zh-Hant…` locales resolve to `zh-TW`; `zh_CN`, `zh_SG`, `zh-Hans…`, and bare `zh` stay on `zh-CN`. Also updates catalogs, counts/dates, desktop entry, typos config, tests, and docs.

## Visual evidence

N/A — this is a non-visual i18n/catalog change; no UI layout or styling is modified. Language selector gains a 正體中文 entry.

## How to test

1. Build and run Strata, open Settings → General → Language, choose 正體中文, restart.
2. Verify the UI renders in Traditional Chinese with Taiwan terminology.
3. Set `LANG=zh_TW.UTF-8` (or `zh_HK`/`zh-Hant`) and confirm auto-detect picks zh-TW; `zh_CN` stays Simplified.
4. Run `./scripts/test-headless.py i18n::`, `language_`, `util::tests`, `ui::settings::tests::general`, `ui::settings::search::tests`.

**Expected result:** all listed tests pass; UI fully translated with no missing keys or placeholders.

Closes #1613

issues.body:
## Summary

I'm a Traditional Chinese (zh-TW) translator and I'd like to contribute a zh-TW locale to Strata. Before starting the ~939-message translation, I wanted to confirm direction and check your preferred approach for the locale-routing question.

## What I've already understood about the i18n setup

Reading `src/i18n.rs`, `build.rs`, and the `data/locales/` layout:

- Catalogs are generated at build time by `build.rs` via `rust_i18n_support::load_locales("data/locales", ...)` and embedded as static tables — so a new locale is picked up automatically just by adding files under `data/locales/`
- Per-locale message files live in `data/locales/messages/<locale>.json` as flat `{msgid: msgstr}` maps (English msgid as key)
- `counts.json` and `dates.json` use a single-file multi-language format (`{"counts.items.one": {"en": ..., "zh-CN": ...}}`)
- `plural_category()` currently routes `zh-CN` to `"other"` only — zh-TW behaves the same way (no plural distinction), so no logic change needed there
- Number/date formatting (`decimal_separator`, `group_separator`) treats `zh-CN` like `en`; zh-TW needs the same treatment

## The one thing I want your input on

`supported_locale()` currently collapses all Traditional Chinese into the Simplified catalog:

```rust
// Traditional Chinese locales also use the Simplified catalog.
"zh" => Some("zh-CN"),
```

For zh-TW users this means Simplified Chinese UI. I see two ways to introduce a real zh-TW:

**Option A — full locale split**

```rust
"zh" => match value.split('-').nth(1) {
    Some("hant") | Some("tw") | Some("hk") | Some("mo") => Some("zh-TW"),
    Some("hans") | Some("cn") | Some("sg") => Some("zh-CN"),
    _ => None,  // or a default, your call
}
```

More correct, but changes auto-detection behaviour for existing users.

**Option B — manual choice only**

Add `zh-TW` to the language dropdown, leave `"zh" => "zh-CN"` routing untouched. Zero risk to existing users, but auto-detect still shows Simplified to zh_TW users who don't open settings.

I'm leaning toward **A** (correct behaviour), but B is safer if you want to minimise the blast radius. Which would you prefer?

## Proposed scope

1. `data/locales/messages/zh-TW.json` — 939 messages, translated from English source with Taiwan terminology (not a zh-CN conversion)
2. `data/locales/zh-TW.json` — locale-specific extra strings
3. `counts.json` + `dates.json` — add `"zh-TW"` entries to each item
4. `src/i18n.rs` — `TraditionalChinese` variant, `CHOICES` entry ("正體中文"), `locale()` mapping, and the `supported_locale()` change per your choice above
5. `src/i18n/tests.rs` — coverage for the new locale

## Translation quality note

I'll translate from the English source (not convert from zh-CN) to ensure proper Taiwan terminology — e.g. 文件/檔案, 網絡/網路, 默認/預設 — so it reads naturally for Taiwan users rather than looking like machine-converted Simplified.

Happy to follow whichever direction you prefer — just let me know.

comments.author: ogarza
comments.body:
@a-lang thanks for waiting. Please go ahead with the translation. Here are the decisions.

**Routing: option A.** Auto-detect sends Traditional Chinese locales to zh-TW:
- `zh_TW`, `zh_HK`, `zh_MO`, and any `zh-Hant…` locale or `LANGUAGE` entry go to `zh-TW`.
- `zh_CN`, `zh_SG`, `zh-Hans…`, and bare `zh` stay on `zh-CN`.

Hong Kong and Macau get the Taiwan catalog unless someone contributes a zh-HK one later.

**Keyboard.** #1714 checked Traditional Chinese input on the XKB `tw` layouts and with these input methods:
- Zhuyin through fcitx5-chewing and ibus-chewing
- Cangjie, Quick, Array30 and Boshiamy
- Rime bopomofo

Typing worked in every text field, and no key started a Strata command mid-syllable. The check found two bugs, which #1714 fixes:
- The F1 search swallowed fcitx5's Ctrl+Space.
- Switching IBus engines with Super+Space during a rename committed the rename.

One problem is upstream, tracked in #1715: with fcitx5 through GTK's input-method module (`GTK_IM_MODULE=fcitx`, as on X11), the first key of a composition replaces selected text as a raw character. A rename preselects the name, so typing 八 gives `阿ㄅ.txt`. Press Backspace (or End) before composing. IBus is not affected.

Taiwan keyboards need no locale-specific key logic. Shortcut key names (`keys.name.*`) and the F1 shortcut descriptions are ordinary catalog entries, so you translate them with everything else. That PR adds no user-facing strings, so there is nothing of ours to fix.

**Your PR.** The catalog tests require every key in every listed language, so zh-TW needs all of these:
1. `data/locales/zh-TW.json`: the main interface catalog, with **1,281 strings** (menus, Settings, dialogs, Settings search keywords). Despite the name, it is the largest file, not "extra strings".
2. `data/locales/messages/zh-TW.json`: 939 strings, covering messages and shortcut descriptions.
3. `data/locales/counts.json` (65 entries) and `data/locales/dates.json` (35 entries): a `"zh-TW"` value in each entry.
4. `src/i18n.rs`:
   - a `TraditionalChinese` variant (`#[serde(rename = "zh-TW")]`) with its `locale()` arm;
   - a `CHOICES` entry, with the autonym your call (繁體中文 pairs with 简体中文, and 正體中文 works too);
   - the routing above in `supported_locale()`;
   - `"zh-TW"` next to `"zh-CN"` in `plural_category`, `decimal_separator` and `group_separator`.
5. Tests:
   - add `zh-TW` to `LOCALES` in `src/i18n/catalog_tests.rs`;
   - in `src/i18n/tests.rs`, update the `zh_TW`, `zh_HK` and `zh-Hant` routing rows, and add zh-TW rows wherever zh-CN has one;
   - add zh-TW date rows in `src/util/tests.rs` and `src/ui/settings/tests/updates.rs`, and a Han query row in `src/ui/settings/search/tests.rs`.
6. `data/io.github.lgse.Strata.desktop`: `GenericName[zh_TW]`, `Comment[zh_TW]` and `Keywords[zh_TW]`.
7. `typos.toml`: `zh-TW` next to each `zh-CN` entry.
8. Docs and rules:
   - `docs/internationalization.md`: the locale list; a short zh-TW style paragraph (quotation marks, full-width punctuation, Han/Latin spacing); a font note on Noto Sans CJK TC, with `PANGO_LANGUAGE=zh-tw` giving Traditional glyph forms on a non-Chinese locale.
   - `docs/preferences.md`: the auto-detect description.
   - `AGENTS.md`: change "eleven" to "twelve" and add the language to the list.

Validate with `./scripts/test-headless.py i18n::`, plus the other commands in `docs/internationalization.md#validation`.

Translating from English with Taiwan terminology, as you proposed, is exactly what we want.

author: l0gicgate
body:
## Description

Two packaging gaps kept Strata's sandbox from working on NixOS without a source rebuild or a system-profile install; both are about where trusted paths come from, so they land together.

**Host helper discovery (#1702).** `trusted_command` searched only the fixed FHS and NixOS/Guix system directories, so a package whose bubblewrap lives only in its runtime closure failed with "bwrap was not found in a trusted system directory". A new build-time `STRATA_TRUSTED_COMMAND_PATH` appends colon-separated directories after the fixed roots. The fixed roots keep priority so `/run/wrappers/bin` still wins, the build fails on empty or relative entries, each configured directory is searched only when it canonicalizes under an existing trust root, and the helper found there must still canonicalize under a trust root. Inherited `PATH` and `HOME` stay out of the lookup, and missing helpers still fail closed.

**Sandbox runtime paths (#1599).** `STRATA_SANDBOX_PATH`, `STRATA_SANDBOX_ROOT`, `STRATA_SANDBOX_PRLIMIT`, and `STRATA_SANDBOX_GDK_PIXBUF_MODULE_FILE` were `option_env!` constants, so a prebuilt release could not be pointed at a Nix runtime. They now resolve once at launch through `sandbox::runtime`, with precedence launch-time value, then embedded build-time value, then default, and apply uniformly to one-shot previews, pooled browser workers, media sessions, RAR extraction, and the Diagnostics page. Launch-time values are validated: every path must be absolute without `..`, and a launch-time root must be `/usr`, `/nix/store`, `/gnu/store`, or a directory inside one, so `/` or user data can never be bound into the sandbox. Invalid values are logged and ignored in favour of the embedded configuration. The sandbox still starts with a cleared environment, so the variables are read by the host only.

Docs: `docs/preview-sandbox.md` gains a host-helper section and a launch example, and `docs/hardened-configuration.md` and `docs/diagnostics.md` are updated to match.

## Visual evidence

N/A: packaging and runtime configuration with no UI changes.

## How to test

1. Build with a configured helper directory and confirm priority and validation:
   ```sh
   STRATA_TRUSTED_COMMAND_PATH=relative/bin cargo build --release   # fails: entry must be absolute
   STRATA_TRUSTED_COMMAND_PATH=/nix/store/<bubblewrap>/bin/ cargo build --release
   ```
   On a NixOS host without bubblewrap in the system profile, Settings → Diagnostics should report the preview sandbox as available and render the PDF thumbnail sample.
2. Launch a prebuilt binary with runtime overrides and open a folder with images, PDFs, a video, and a RAR archive:
   ```sh
   STRATA_SANDBOX_ROOT=/nix/store \
   STRATA_SANDBOX_PATH=/nix/store/<ffmpeg>/bin:/nix/store/<imagemagick>/bin \
   STRATA_SANDBOX_PRLIMIT=/nix/store/<util-linux>/bin/prlimit \
   strata
   ```
3. Launch with `STRATA_SANDBOX_ROOT=/home/<user>` or `STRATA_SANDBOX_ROOT=/usr/../home`, then check the log and Diagnostics.

**Expected result:** Step 1 fails the build on the relative entry and, with the store directory, finds bubblewrap without a system-profile entry. Step 2 renders thumbnails and previews and extracts the archive through the Nix runtime without rebuilding Strata. Step 3 logs `ignoring an invalid launch-time sandbox override`, keeps the embedded `/usr` root, and previews keep working. On an FHS host with all variables unset, behaviour is unchanged.

## Related issue

Closes #1599
Closes #1702

issues.body:
### Problem or use case

The v1.0.0 x86_64 release starts on NixOS once its ELF dependencies are packaged, but native previews cannot use the Nix runtime. `STRATA_SANDBOX_ROOT`, `STRATA_SANDBOX_PATH`, `STRATA_SANDBOX_PRLIMIT`, and `STRATA_SANDBOX_GDK_PIXBUF_MODULE_FILE` use `option_env!`, so exporting them when launching the release binary has no effect. Rebuilding the application merely to change these paths defeats installing a prebuilt release.

Environment: NixOS 26.11, x86_64, Wayland/Niri; GTK4 and Bubblewrap 0.12.0 installed. This is separate from Bubblewrap discovery: installing Bubblewrap in the system profile fixes discovery, but not the sandbox's baked-in `/usr` runtime and `/usr/bin/prlimit` paths.

### Proposed solution

Allow explicit runtime `STRATA_SANDBOX_*` overrides, retaining existing build-time values and FHS defaults when unset. Apply them consistently to one-shot previews, pooled browser workers, media helpers, and RAR extraction. Keep namespace isolation, trusted Bubblewrap discovery, resource limits, and fail-closed decoding unchanged; prevent runtime root overrides from mounting private user data or `/`.

### Alternatives considered

Compiling v1.0.0 with Nix store paths works but requires a source rebuild. An FHS compatibility wrapper adds more packaging machinery than a runtime-path override.

### Visual examples

N/A: runtime packaging configuration, with no UI changes.

### Strata version

1.0.0 (`0a086aa3bdb251842a1e8413e2a6b35970d0b409`)

### Additional context

Runtime overrides should be documented with a launch example and their precedence over embedded build-time settings. The release binary installed on the reporting machine should not be replaced by a source build as part of preparing this change.

issues.body:
### Problem or use case

I maintain a Nix source package for Strata. It includes Bubblewrap and the other required helpers as runtime dependencies, with their store directories on the packaged launcher's PATH. These dependencies need not be separately installed into the user's system profile.

Strata's host helper resolver correctly avoids inherited PATH, following #1045 / #1055. Its fixed search directories include the NixOS system profile, and its canonical trust roots already include `/nix/store`, but it cannot discover a helper that is present only in the package's runtime closure.

On current main, this leaves the native PDF thumbnail path reporting `The bubblewrap sandbox is not available` even though both an absolute store invocation and `bwrap --version` through the packaged PATH succeed. Configuring the documented `STRATA_SANDBOX_*` build settings does not resolve this host-side lookup step.

### Proposed solution

Would a small, optional build-time setting for additional host helper search directories be welcome? For example, a colon-separated `STRATA_TRUSTED_COMMAND_PATH`, with the final name and validation policy open to discussion.

The intended scope is narrow:

- Keep all existing search directories first, especially `/run/wrappers/bin`, so NixOS security wrappers retain priority.
- Append only explicitly configured absolute directories from trusted package locations. Do not accept empty or relative components, and do not use runtime PATH or HOME.
- Preserve the existing canonical target checks and trust roots. The configured lookup directory must also be safe from runtime user replacement; the Nix case uses immutable store directories.
- Preserve the search hit's execution path for profile wrappers and multicall argv0 behavior.
- Keep existing behavior when unset, and continue failing closed when a required trusted helper cannot be found.

This would complement the existing sandbox runtime configuration without changing sandbox isolation or introducing runtime path overrides. It could replace our downstream `trusted-helper-path.patch` once the capability is accepted and included in the packaged version.

### Alternatives considered

- Ask every user to install Bubblewrap into the system profile separately. This works, but makes a package's declared runtime dependency insufficient on its own.
- Keep the downstream source patch. This works for the Nix package but adds code and test context to maintain on every update.
- Search inherited PATH. This would undo the security boundary established by #1045 / #1055 and is not the requested behavior.
- Use the existing `STRATA_SANDBOX_*` settings or the runtime overrides discussed in #1599. Those configure the environment inside the sandbox; host Bubblewrap discovery must succeed before that sandbox can start.

### Visual examples

N/A: a packaging capability with no new UI proposed.

### Strata version

Main commit `1921fbdf1f1a71c89dcb67862303e02108548969` (1.0.0), tested on NixOS x86_64-linux with Rust 1.98.1, Cargo 1.98.0, GTK 4.22.4, GLib 2.88.3 and Bubblewrap 0.12.0.

### Additional context

Downstream packaging work: [NixOS/nixpkgs#570118](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/pull/570118) (`strata: init at 1.0.0`). The package currently carries the helper-search patch described above; this request would let that patch be retired in a future package update.

I reproduced the failure and a system-profile workaround in private namespaces. Both runs used the same binary, PDF fixture, store dependencies, runtime PATH and compiled sandbox settings:

| Environment | Host resolver | Existing PDF thumbnail path |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Bubblewrap available in the store and on PATH; no fixed system entry | `bwrap was not found in a trusted system directory` | `The bubblewrap sandbox is not available` |
| Same setup, with a private system-profile symlink to the same Bubblewrap | Resolves `/run/current-system/sw/bin/bwrap` | Produces a valid 64×36 PNG |

The reproduction used a temporary diagnostic entry point calling `trusted_command::resolve` and `sandbox::parse` with `ThumbnailPdf`. The production resolver, sandbox and helper source files were unchanged from the main commit above. This exercises the actual sandboxed renderer rather than a mocked helper. It is not a full GUI/E2E test. No host profile, desktop session or system configuration was changed.

These original runs establish the discovery gap and the existing system-profile workaround. A focused companion implementation has since been prepared locally. It validates both the canonical fallback directories and the final helper targets against the existing trust roots, preserving system priority and helper basenames. Its final build renders the same PDF without a system-profile entry, and launch-time changes do not override the compiled configuration. One settings-text-size test timed out in a full E2E run; the clean base and final candidate passed that exact test, so the earlier timeout cause remains unconfirmed and will be disclosed in the companion PR.

Related work: #1329 / #1357 cover sandbox-internal build-time paths. #1599 concerns launch-time sandbox configuration for prebuilt releases. This request concerns only discovering the trusted host helper before starting that sandbox.

I plan to prepare a focused companion PR. I could not self-assign this issue with my current repository permissions; could a maintainer assign it to me?

Prepared with assistance from Codex (GPT-6).

body: ## Description Adds the home for opt-in integrations that #1741 describes, so providers such as KDE Connect (#1704) and Nextcloud (#1670) can live in this repository and users can find them in the app. - **`integrations/` catalog.** One directory per integration with a `catalog.toml` (id, name, description, category, maintainer, runtime, entry, icons, requirements) beside the program. `build.rs` embeds the directory, so releases carry the catalog without packaging changes. `integrations/README.md` documents the layout, the manifest, the maintainer rule and the review policy. `STRATA_INTEGRATION_CATALOG=` replaces the bundled catalog while developing an entry. - **Settings → Integrations.** Lists entries by category (Cloud, Devices, Version control, Other) with maintainer, description and a requirement check per entry: the runtime and each declared command are looked up in trusted system directories, Python modules are asked of the interpreter without importing them, and missing ones show the install command for the detected distribution. - **Install / Remove / Update.** Install copies the files into `~/.config/strata/providers//`, writes `provider.json` with the interpreter and script paths resolved on this machine, and records a content hash per file in `catalog-install.json`. When the bundled files change, installed copies show **Update available**; nothing updates on its own. Local edits are detected from the recorded hashes and confirmed before they are replaced. Registrations without a record are listed under **Installed manually** with their registered icon and Remove only, which also confirms first. Install, Update and Remove are icon buttons in the row heading, like the custom action rows. - **Enable switch.** Every installed registration has a switch that writes or removes an empty `disabled` marker beside `provider.json`; discovery skips marked directories, so an integration can be turned off without removing it and an update keeps the choice. - **No restart.** The provider hub can stop its running providers and discover the registrations again. The page does that after every install, update, removal or switch change, and a **Refresh** button does it after edits made by hand, so providers take effect at once. - **Open folder.** A button in the page intro closes Settings and shows the providers directory in the browser. - **Agent guidance.** `AGENTS.md` no longer asks agents for PR screenshots or recordings, which they cannot upload. - **CI.** A path-filtered `Integrations` workflow compiles each bundled entry with its runtime and runs its `tests/` with unittest, installing the apt packages a provider's tests declare. The Rust suite checks that every bundled entry parses, respects the manifest bounds and has its name and description in all twelve catalogs. The catalog ships empty in this PR; the page shows its empty state. Moving #1704 into `integrations/kdeconnect/` and inviting the Nextcloud author back are the next step from #1741. Validation was scoped to the new service and page, the provider registry helpers they share, Settings search registration and the i18n catalogs: `test-headless.py integration_catalog` (7), `settings::integrations` (4), `file_providers` (42, including the hub reload), `package_manager` (2), `search::tests` (104), `i18n::` (12); `e2e.sh tests/e2e/scenarios/test_integrations.py tests/e2e/scenarios/test_settings_search.py` (3 passed); `python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts -p 'test_*.py'` (246); `quality.sh fmt` and `clippy`; `typos`. The full Rust and E2E suites were not run locally. ## Visual evidence ## How to test 1. Create a catalog directory with one entry, for example `catalog/example/catalog.toml` and `catalog/example/provider.py`, following `integrations/README.md` (any Python program that reads stdin is enough). 2. Run `STRATA_INTEGRATION_CATALOG=$PWD/catalog cargo run` and open **Settings → Integrations**. 3. Select **Install**, then check `~/.config/strata/providers/example/` for `provider.json`, the copied files and `catalog-install.json`. 4. Change `provider.py` in the catalog directory, close and reopen Settings, and select **Update**. 5. Edit the installed `provider.py`, change the catalog copy again, reopen Settings and select **Update**; confirm with **Replace**. 6. Turn the switch off and check that `~/.config/strata/providers/example/disabled` exists; turn it back on. 7. Select **Remove**. Then create `~/.config/strata/providers/handmade/provider.json` by hand, reopen Settings and remove it from **Installed manually**. 8. Select **Open folder**: Settings closes and the browser shows `~/.config/strata/providers`. **Expected result:** the row moves through Not installed, Installed, Update available and Update available · Modified locally; the installed files match the catalog after each install or update; the local edit is only replaced after confirmation; the switch shows **Disabled** and the marker file; removal deletes the directory; the provider's context-menu action appears right after Install and disappears when disabled or removed, with no restart. Searching Settings for "add-ons" or "plugins" opens the page. ## Related issue Closes #1741

issues.body:
### Problem or use case

Integrations with external services (Nextcloud #1670, KDE Connect #1704, and candidates such as Dropbox, ShareFile and Cirrove) currently have nowhere to live. Closing them and sending the author to their own repository means users never discover them, and contributors have to maintain a separate repo, releases and install scripts for a few hundred lines of Python. Strata already has the opt-in provider protocol (`docs/file-providers.md`); it is missing a home for provider code and an in-app way to install, remove, and update it.

### Proposed solution

**1. A `providers/` directory in this repository**, one provider per subdirectory, bundled with releases:

```text
providers/
  README.md              contributing guide, policy, template
  kdeconnect/
    catalog.toml         id, name key, description key, category, maintainer,
                         requirements, runtime, entry script, icons
    provider.py
    messages.json
    tests/
```

- Each provider names a **maintainer**. An unmaintained, broken provider is marked unmaintained in the catalog and removed after a release or two.
- Provider tests run in a **separate path-filtered CI job** (lint plus the provider's own tests), not in the Rust shards or the E2E suite. One host-side Rust test checks that every bundled entry parses and respects manifest bounds (icon count/size, name length, slug ids).
- Fixed categories: Cloud, Devices, Version control, Other.
- Catalog names and descriptions are Strata-owned UI text and go through `rust-i18n` in all eleven languages; a provider's own runtime messages stay with the provider.

**2. Settings → Integrations page**, modelled on the Actions Library:

- Lists catalog entries with name, description, category, maintainer, and a **requirements check** reusing the Diagnostics dependency checks (for example `kdeconnectd`, `python3-gi`) so missing dependencies are visible before installing.
- Shows the trust statement from the provider docs: providers run with the user's permissions.
- **Install** copies the bundled files into `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/strata/providers/<id>/`, writes `provider.json` with the absolute interpreter and script paths resolved at install time, and records the installed catalog version. Shows the existing restart notice.
- **Remove** deletes that directory and shows the restart notice.
- **Update**: each bundled provider carries a version (or content hash computed at build time). An installed provider whose recorded version differs from the bundled one shows **Update available** with a one-click refresh that re-copies the files. No automatic updates; locally modified installs are detected and the user is warned before overwriting.
- Providers installed by hand (not from the catalog) are listed as "manual" with Remove only.

**3. Policy and contributor path**

- `providers/README.md` with a template, the maintainer rule, test expectations, and what reviewers check.
- Invite the Nextcloud author back once the directory exists; move #1704 into it.

### Alternatives considered

- Catalog pointing at external repositories with pinned hashes: solves discoverability but adds release ceremony for every contributor and makes review a hash rather than code.
- Keeping providers purely external (current state): users do not find them and contributors are turned away.
- Shipping providers enabled by default: rejected; integrations stay opt-in.

### Visual examples

```text
Settings → Integrations
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Devices                                                │
│  ⌂ KDE Connect   Send files to paired devices          │
│     Requires: kdeconnectd ✓  python3-gi ✓   [Install]  │
│ Cloud                                                  │
│  ☁ Nextcloud     Share links and sync status           │
│     Requires: nextcloud-desktop ✗          [Install]   │
│  ☁ Dropbox       …   Installed · Update available      │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### Additional context

Depends on the Send to placement hook (#1740, first PR). Candidate entries need a committed maintainer and a working local client or API on Linux before being listed.

author: l0gicgate
body:
## Description

A cross-volume move verifies a file modified within one coarse clock tick by its contents, because a same-size rewrite leaves its times unchanged. Only the first name of a hard-linked file was read, though. Its later names had no digest, so a later name rewritten within the tick was deleted, while the first name was kept.

- Later names now take the first name's digest, and the deletion compares them by content.
- SMB refuses to open another name of a file it recently opened (`closetimeo`), so there such later names are kept as changed rather than deleted unverified.
- `moves_off_mounts_without_stable_inodes_keep_only_what_changed` flaked on CI's 6.8 kernel, where tmpfs times are coarse; it failed on #1745, #1741 and #1738. It is about stat-based detection, so its files now get settled times and it is deterministic on every kernel. The new `later_names_rewritten_within_the_tick_are_kept` test covers the within-tick case for ext4 and SMB with the coarse-clock seam. It fails without the fix.
- `docs/filesystem-compatibility.md` notes the behaviour under "Racily clean files".

## Visual evidence

N/A: copy-engine behaviour with no UI change.

## How to test

1. Run `./scripts/test-headless.py later_names_rewritten_within_the_tick_are_kept`.
2. Revert the `copy_engine` changes and run it again.

**Expected result:** the test passes with the fix. Without it, the ext4 row fails because `sub/n` is missing from the kept items.

## Related issue

Closes #1750

issues.body:
### Strata version

1.0.0 (main at d390a660)

### Installation method

Built from source

### Linux distribution and desktop environment

Any distribution on a kernel without multigrain timestamps (before 6.13), or a filesystem stamped by a coarse clock. Seen on the CI runners (Ubuntu 24.04, kernel 6.8, tmpfs).

### What happened?

A cross-volume move verifies each source entry before deleting it. If a file was modified within one clock tick of the copy, a stat cannot show a same-size rewrite, so the engine also compares a contents digest taken during the copy. Only the first name of a hard-linked file is read, though. Its later names are recorded through `Pending::new` without a digest, so the deletion judges them on size and modification time alone.

If a hard-linked file is rewritten to the same size within that tick, the move keeps the first name (its digest no longer matches) but deletes the later name, which still holds the rewritten bytes. The report also leaves that name out of the kept items.

This makes `adapters::local_operations::tests::moves::moves_off_mounts_without_stable_inodes_keep_only_what_changed` fail intermittently on CI (`left: ["b.txt", "q"]`, `right: ["b.txt", "n", "q"]`). It failed on #1745, #1741 and #1738, but passes on hosts with kernel 6.13+, where tmpfs has fine-grained timestamps.

### Steps to reproduce

1. In `moves_off_mounts_without_stable_inodes_keep_only_what_changed`, emulate a coarse tick: `let tick = SystemTime::now() - Duration::from_secs(1); let _clock = ClockGuard::set(tick);` and `coarse_clock: Some(tick)` in its `Quirks`.
2. Run `./scripts/test-headless.py moves_off_mounts_without_stable_inodes`.

### Expected behavior

Every name of a rewritten hard-linked file is kept and reported as changed, whatever the clock granularity.

### Additional context

The deterministic repro fails on every run, with the same assertion as CI.

author: JoeJoeflyn
body:
## Description

Fix scrollbar jumps during thumb drags and touchpad/content scrolling while retaining GTK's native input handling and virtualization. The indicator follows document positions rather than changing pixel-height estimates. Cancel stale momentum when GTK changes either the estimated range **or the pixel origin**, then synchronize GTK's next input origin. A flick may end early when newly measured rows invalidate its trajectory.

Defer intermediate/prefetched rendered-row construction and qualify Settings tab-label CSS to avoid unrelated preview style invalidation. Keep Source binding eager for thumb seeking. Retain the earlier shared hit-testing, source-memory, and event-driven table improvements. Browser and picker document previews share the component; file/folder-list scrolling is unchanged.

Ignore GTK's integer quantization when detecting pixel-origin corrections so valid native momentum remains active. The owner confirmed that the real-touchpad candidate no longer jumped before the latest `main` merge; the merged result has not been manually retested. Initial-loading speed and actual battery-life improvements remain unverified.

## Visual evidence

N/A. The thumb no longer jumps to stale positions during touchpad momentum. No intentional content-layout change.

## How to test

1. Open the long mixed Markdown fixture from #1749. Scroll over content with a touchpad in both directions, pause, and release fast flicks into momentum without grabbing the scrollbar.
2. Repeat in Source and with a large plain-text file. Momentum may stop when GTK re-anchors newly measured rows, but the indicator must not jump backward during forward input.
3. Drag/hold the thumb at interior positions and both ends, release outside it, then continue with wheel/keyboard input. Try find, copy, wrapping, view switches, and close/reopen.
4. Repeat from Open/Save picker previews. Check table sorting, selection/copy, resizing, and live theme colors, plus Settings action-editor tabs.

**Expected result:** Content and scrollbar follow input direction without stale-momentum jumps; thumb dragging and existing preview actions remain usable.

## Related issue

Refs #1749.
title: fix(preview): stabilize scrolling and reduce preview resource usage

author: l0gicgate
body:
## Description

The aarch64 release build failed in `Build release binary` with `expected u64, found u32` at the `st_nlink` field of `legacy_stat`, the `fstatat` fallback used when `statx` is unavailable. The `rustix::fs::Stat` field is `u64` on x86_64 but `u32` on aarch64, so the direct copy only compiled on x86_64.

The fix converts through a small generic helper, `link_count`, so the widening is valid on both targets. A plain `u64::from` or `as u64` fails clippy on x86_64 (`useless_conversion` / `unnecessary_cast`), and `expect` attributes would be platform-conditional, so the generic keeps the code lint-clean everywhere.

## Visual evidence

N/A: build fix with no user-visible change.

## How to test

1. Run `cargo check --target aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu` (or the release workflow's aarch64 job).
2. Run `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` on x86_64.

**Expected result:** both succeed. Before this change, step 1 failed with the mismatched-types error at `fs_ops.rs:252`.

Verification done locally: fmt and clippy on x86_64 pass; `./scripts/test-headless.py -- adapters::local_operations::` passed 680 tests (5 ignored). A full aarch64 cross-check of the crate is not possible on the host (no aarch64 C++ cross compiler for a native dependency), so a minimal probe crate pinned to the same `rustix 1.1.4` was checked for aarch64 instead: it reproduces the original error for a direct `u64` assignment and compiles with the helper. The release workflow's aarch64 job remains the authoritative check.

## Related issue

Closes #1753

issues.body:
## Strata version
main at a02d3afd (release workflow)

## Installation method
Release workflow build (`cargo build --release --locked --target aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu` on ubuntu-24.04-arm)

## Environment
GitHub Actions `ubuntu-24.04-arm` runner, aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu

## Reproduction steps
1. Run the release workflow (or `cargo build --target aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu`).
2. The `Build release binary` step fails while compiling `strata`.

## Expected behavior
The aarch64 release binary builds like the x86_64 one.

## Logs
```
error[E0308]: mismatched types
  --> src/adapters/local_operations/fs_ops.rs:252:16
   |
252 |         nlink: stat.st_nlink,
   |                ^^^^^^^^^^^^^ expected `u64`, found `u32`
```

`legacy_stat` copies `st_nlink` straight into the `u64` field of `EntryStat`. `st_nlink` is `u64` on x86_64 but `u32` on aarch64, so the fallback `fstatat` path only compiles on x86_64.

author: l0gicgate
body:
## Description

Adds LocalSend to the Integrations catalog. **Send to… ▸ LocalSend** runs the installed LocalSend app with the selected files and folders. A running instance takes them over and shows its Send tab with them selected; otherwise LocalSend starts with them. The device is chosen in LocalSend, which handles acceptance, progress and errors. The provider uses only the Python standard library. It binds the selection to a single-use token and starts LocalSend in its own session, so quitting Strata never closes it.

Two changes were needed to make this work:

- **`send-to-entry` placement.** Providers can now choose how their Send to… item looks. A root action with `placement: "send-to-entry"` is drawn directly in Send to… as one entry, while it is the provider's only Send to… action and has no children. `send-to` keeps the provider submenu, so KDE Connect with one device still shows **KDE Connect ▸ Pixel**. Strata never collapses a submenu on its own. Older Strata builds put the unknown placement in the provider section.
- **Finding packaged programs.** Every LocalSend package puts a `/usr/bin` symlink to a binary under `/opt` or `/usr/lib` (`/usr/lib/localsend`, `/opt/localsend`, `/opt/localsend_app`). Strata's trusted-command rule rejected all of them. Integration **requirement checks** now also accept such a target when root owns it and every directory above it, none writable by group or others, and the provider runs that resolved target, never the link. A requirement can also list `alternatives`; the upstream .deb names the program `localsend_app`. Helper resolution elsewhere (bwrap, archive tools) is unchanged.

Also included, two small visual fixes: the file view footer's right inset now matches the text inset of the F1 Shortcuts button on the left, and segmented controls (such as the Settings click-to-open switches) only brighten the text on hover, without a background highlight.

Not supported: Flatpak, Snap and AppImage installs of LocalSend. Their launchers are outside the trusted directories, and a Flatpak would need document-portal forwarding.

## Visual evidence

N/A — agents cannot attach captures. The entry appears as a single **LocalSend** row inside **Send to…**, drawn with the Devices category icon and without a submenu arrow.

## How to test

1. Install LocalSend from the AUR, Omarchy, or the upstream .deb.
2. Open **Settings → Integrations**. LocalSend's `localsend` requirement shows as available. Install the integration.
3. Select a few files and a folder, then right-click and choose **Send to… ▸ LocalSend**. Try it once with LocalSend closed and once with it already running, including from the tray.
4. Install KDE Connect with one paired device and open **Send to…**.
5. Select one folder and compare the footer's right edge with its left. Then hover the options of the click-to-open switches in **Settings → General → Opening items**.

**Expected result:** At step 3, Send to… shows **LocalSend** as a single entry, not a submenu. LocalSend opens on its Send tab with exactly the selected items, and Strata shows no dialog. Closing Strata leaves LocalSend running. At step 4, KDE Connect still appears as a submenu holding its one device. At step 5, "1 folder selected" sits as far from the right edge as "F1 Shortcuts" does from the left, and hovering a switch option changes only its text color.

Closes #1754

issues.body:
### Problem or use case

LocalSend is a common way to move files between a Linux desktop and nearby
phones and computers, and Omarchy ships it. Sending a file from Strata today
means opening LocalSend and picking the same file again in its own file dialog.
#1169 was closed because a custom action could cover this; now that the
Integrations catalog exists (#1748, #1704), it can ship as an opt-in entry
instead.

### Proposed solution

Add a `localsend` entry to the integrations catalog:

- **Send to… ▸ LocalSend** for selected files and folders: a single entry, not a submenu. Providers choose this with a new `send-to-entry` placement.
- Activation runs the installed LocalSend app with the selected paths. LocalSend
  passes them to an already running instance (or starts one) and opens its Send
  tab with them selected, so the user chooses the device there. LocalSend still
  handles PINs, the receiver's acceptance, progress, and errors.
- Bind the selection into a short-lived context token and check it again on
  activation, as the KDE Connect provider does. Start LocalSend in its own
  session so that quitting Strata never closes it.
- Requirements: `python3` and `localsend` in a trusted system directory. The
  provider uses only the Python standard library.

### Alternatives considered

- Implementing LocalSend protocol v2 inside the provider, so devices are listed
  in the menu. That would make Strata announce itself as a peer that cannot
  receive files on every LocalSend device on the network. The transfer would
  also have to run inside the provider beyond the 8-second activation limit and
  would stop when Strata quits.
- `localsend-cli` from 1.18 is interactive only (`-f` opens a device picker in a
  terminal) and binds LocalSend's port, so it conflicts with the running app.

### Visual examples

N/A

### Strata version

main (after #1704)

### Additional context

Flatpak and AppImage installs of LocalSend are outside this entry's scope. Their
launchers are not in trusted system directories, and Flatpak would need
document-portal file forwarding.

## Description

Adds an opt-in user stylesheet, as discussed in #1710. When `~/.config/strata/style.css` exists, Strata loads it through its own CSS provider above every stylesheet Strata ships, so user rules have the final word and can use the active theme's `@strata_*` colors. Without the file the provider stays empty and nothing changes.

The file is watched the same way as custom themes: edits apply to open windows after a short debounce, deleting the file restores the default look, and rules GTK cannot parse are skipped and logged as warnings. `~/.config/gtk-4.0/gtk.css` remains ignored, as before. `docs/themes.md` documents the file and notes that class names are not a stable interface.

The implementation was written with the help of an AI coding assistant; I reviewed and tested it and the commit is my own.

## Visual evidence

N/A. This adds an opt-in file and changes nothing by default. With the file present, the rules in it restyle the interface: for example, `.sidebar-shell { margin: 8px; border-radius: 16px; }` turns the sidebar into a floating rounded card, as described in #1710.

## How to test

1. Start Strata, then create `~/.config/strata/style.css` with `.sidebar-shell { margin: 8px; border-radius: 16px; background: alpha(@strata_accent, 0.25); }`.
2. Without restarting, change the alpha to `0.5`, then add an invalid rule such as `.sidebar { color: nope; }` and save again.
3. Delete the file.

**Expected result:** the sidebar turns into a rounded, accent-tinted card as soon as the file is saved and follows each edit; the invalid rule is skipped with a `invalid rule in user stylesheet` warning in the log while the valid rules keep applying; after deleting the file the sidebar returns to the default appearance. Switching themes keeps the override and updates its `@strata_*` colors.

## Related issue

Closes #1710

issues.body:
### Problem or use case

Custom themes cover the nine color tokens, and translucent colors already work well: with `#rrggbbaa` backgrounds a compositor blur shows through the window. Layout-level styling is still out of reach, though. For example, I'd like the sidebar to be an inset, rounded, translucent panel, like Nautilus/libadwaita sidebars under a glass theme. Since #1679/#1681, `~/.config/gtk-4.0/gtk.css` can't touch Strata (which I agree with), and `style.css` is compiled in, so the only way today is to patch and rebuild.

### Proposed solution

Load an optional `~/.config/strata/style.css` above Strata's own stylesheets (`STYLE_PRIORITY`/`TOKEN_STYLE_PRIORITY` + 1), re-read on change like the themes directory. It only exists if the user creates it, so the default isolation from desktop GTK styling stays intact. Advanced users take responsibility for it, and the `@strata_*` tokens are available inside it.

### Alternatives considered

- A **Floating sidebar** toggle under Settings → Appearance: inset margins, rounded corners and its own surface. It's narrower, but it fits the settings-first approach used for corner roundness (#1678).
- Rebuilding from source with a patched `src/style.css`: works, but every update has to be re-patched.

### Strata version

1.0.0 (strata-bin, AUR)

### Additional context

Arch Linux (CachyOS), niri-based compositor with blur, custom theme "Umbrella Corporation · Liquid Glass".

## Description

The Integrations catalog left a gap after the last card when it showed two cards per row. Its `FlowBox` allowed up to three columns and was not homogeneous, so GTK laid out an empty third column and gave it a share of the spare width.

The grid now uses equal-width columns and caps the column count at the number of cards currently shown (1–3), updated on every catalog rebuild and category filter change. Two cards each take 50% of the row.

With equal-width columns GTK also gives every row the height of the tallest card, so with more than one row, expanding a card's requirements leaves space below cards in the other rows.

author: Cha1000000
body:
## Description

Opens Ghostty through `ghostty +new-window`, so **Open in Terminal** starts in the selected folder when Ghostty runs as a single instance.

With `gtk-single-instance = true`, a plain `ghostty --working-directory=<folder>` launch is handed to the running Ghostty, which ignores the folder and opens the window in the home folder. `+new-window` is Ghostty's command for opening a window in a running instance; it applies `--working-directory` and `-e`, and it starts Ghostty through its D-Bus service when no instance is running. The same arguments apply to Ghostty set through `$TERMINAL`, so extra words there, such as `--class`, still follow `+new-window`.

One trade-off: `+new-window` needs that D-Bus service (`com.mitchellh.ghostty.service`, shipped by Ghostty's Linux packages). A Ghostty binary installed without it would fail to open a window when no instance is running; I left the launch unconditional rather than probing for the service, but I am happy to add a fallback if you prefer.

The change was written with the help of an AI coding assistant; I reviewed and tested it and the commit is my own.

## Visual evidence

N/A. The fix changes the arguments Strata passes to Ghostty; nothing in Strata's interface changes.

## How to test

1. Set `gtk-single-instance = true` in `~/.config/ghostty/config` and start Ghostty.
2. Run Strata with Ghostty as its terminal, for example `TERMINAL=ghostty strata` without `xdg-terminal-exec` installed.
3. Right-click a folder other than home and choose **Open in Terminal**; repeat with Ghostty not running.

**Expected result:** each time, the new Ghostty window opens a shell in the selected folder.

## Related issue

Closes #1762

issues.body:
### Strata version

1.0.0 (also reproduced from source at a70fb72)

### Installation method

AUR package

### Linux distribution and desktop environment

CachyOS, niri 26.04, Ghostty 1.3.1

### What happened?

With Ghostty as the terminal and `gtk-single-instance = true` in the Ghostty config, **Open in Terminal** opens a new window in the home folder instead of the selected folder.

Strata runs `ghostty --working-directory=<folder>`. With single-instance enabled, that launch is handed to the already running Ghostty, which opens a window but ignores `--working-directory` and the launcher's current directory. Ghostty's documented way to open a window in a running instance is `ghostty +new-window`, which does apply `--working-directory` and `-e`.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Set `gtk-single-instance = true` in `~/.config/ghostty/config` and start Ghostty.
2. Make sure Strata uses Ghostty (for example `TERMINAL=ghostty`, without `xdg-terminal-exec`).
3. In Strata, right-click a folder other than home and choose **Open in Terminal**.

### Expected behavior

The new Ghostty window starts in the selected folder, as `ghostty +new-window --working-directory=<folder>` does.

### Additional context

Running `ghostty +new-window --working-directory=/some/folder` by hand opens the shell in `/some/folder`; `ghostty --working-directory=/some/folder` opens it in `~`. Ghostty's Linux packages ship the D-Bus service `com.mitchellh.ghostty`, so `+new-window` also starts Ghostty through D-Bus activation when it is not running yet.

author: adamcbrewer
body:
## Description

Audio, video and model previews repeat their headers, navigation buttons and badge construction. I've pulled those common pieces into shared components so we can change them in one place and keep the previews consistent.

The shared UI now lives in two files under `src/ui/preview`:

- `components.rs` contains the details header, previous/next button builder, navigation row, badge row and badge label builders. It also holds the common spacing and minimum panel width values.
- `player_layout.rs` contains the video/model layout, moved out of `video/layout.rs`. Each preview supplies its content, details and controls, with optional badges and timeline sections. The model badges now have their own named area instead of occupying a slot called `timeline`.

Their common appearance is defined in `src/style.css`, using neutral classes such as `preview-details-title` and `preview-details-badge`.

Audio uses the shared header and navigation, while keeping its larger title, artwork, spectrum and responsive layout. Video and models also use the shared badges and player layout. Each preview supplies its centre widget: a playback button for audio/video, or the camera indicator for models.

The waveform and volume controls were already shared. Playback, seeking, metadata loading and camera animation stay in their existing preview implementations. The loaded previews keep their existing appearance, with one implementation to edit when we change a common header, navigation button or badge.

Mesh previews now also show their filename, listing position and file format during the first load, with the triangle count appearing as soon as parsing provides it. Camera controls become active once the first image is ready. When changing angles, the current mesh dims and the spinner in the preview header shows progress until the next view is ready. Failed angle changes keep the previous image and allow a retry. Next rotates the camera clockwise around the model; Previous rotates it anticlockwise. The dot follows the rendered view.

Starts from upstream `main` at `e0f73973`, after #1644 was confirmed merged.

## Visual evidence

N/A. The loaded previews retain their existing typography, theme styling and narrow, wide and tall arrangements. Mesh loading shows the available file details with the loading spinner in the preview header.

## How to test

1. Preview audio, video and STL/3MF files. Resize the window through narrow, wide and tall shapes, including audio's side-by-side arrangement.
2. Open an uncached STL/3MF mesh. During the first render, check that the filename and format are visible, the triangle count appears when available, and the camera buttons remain inactive until the image is ready.
3. Cycle model camera views. Next should move the camera dot clockwise and Previous anticlockwise, matching the rendered view. Check that the header spinner appears while the retained image is dimmed. Check keyboard focus, loading/retry feedback, thumbnail preference, live themes and reduced motion. Step between tracks and videos and exercise playback, seeking and volume too.

**Expected result:** Loaded previews keep their existing appearance and behaviour. Mesh previews show useful details from the start and the header spinner while generating an image or changing angle.

## Related issue

Closes #1659

issues.body:
## Problem or use case

**Please only pick this up once [#1644](https://github.com/lgse/strata/pull/1644) has been merged into `main`. Closing the PR without merging it does not satisfy this prerequisite.**

While adding model camera views in [#1633](https://github.com/lgse/strata/issues/1633), we brought the mesh preview closer to the audio and video UI. I think there's now enough useful overlap to extract a few shared components. At the moment, changes to the headers, buttons and spacing still need to be repeated across the previews, which makes it easier for them to drift apart. 

In my mind, it makes sense to make any kind of media use the same UI controls and primitives.

Some of this is already shared. Audio and video use the same waveform and volume controls, and video and mesh now use the same `PlayerLayout`. The mesh puts its badge row into the area that the video layout calls `timeline`, so the shared layout would benefit from clearer roles.

## Proposed solution

I'd extract small, composable components within `ui::preview`, using the merged camera-view implementation as the starting point:

1. **Details header:** share the filename/title and folder/results position, with optional areas for artist/album information, volume and badges. Keep the existing typography choices, ellipsising and accessible text.
2. **Navigation row:** share the previous/next button builders and row arrangement. Let each preview supply its centre widget, optional elapsed/total labels, actions, keyboard bindings and accessible names. Audio/video keep their playback button; mesh keeps its passive camera indicator.
3. **Badge row:** share badge construction and theme styling for video and mesh, using neutral names rather than making mesh depend on video CSS classes. Keep metadata formatting, video loading placeholders and HDR treatment with the relevant preview.
4. **Layout areas:** move the shared video/mesh layout into a neutral preview module and give it explicit content, details and controls areas, with optional sections where needed. Share the common spacing and width constraints. Audio should keep its own artwork/spectrum sizing and responsive side-by-side arrangement.

The main reason for doing this is to make the common UI easier to change consistently, while keeping the differences between the previews clear. Renderers, playback and seeking, camera animation, asynchronous loading and cancellation should remain owned by their respective previews.

I'd consider this done when:

- [ ] #1644 is confirmed as merged into `main` before assignment or implementation starts. Start from the merged code and check for subsequent changes.
- [ ] The three previews use the shared header and navigation components where their UI overlaps, and video/mesh use the shared badge row and explicit layout areas.
- [ ] Current appearance and behaviour are preserved, including audio's wide layout, model centring, thumbnail preference, loading/retry feedback, keyboard focus, accessibility, live themes and reduced motion.
- [ ] Existing behavioural regression owners cover the affected actions and lifecycle. Compare narrow, wide and tall layouts manually with before/after captures; follow `AGENTS.md` and do not add layout or pixel-placement assertions.

## Alternatives considered

Keeping shared CSS with separate widget builders would leave the repeated assembly and layout assumptions in place. A single universal player would also need to account for quite different artwork, spectrum, playback and camera behaviour. I think a few composable components are a better fit for the overlap we actually have.

## Visual examples

Use the final UI from [#1644](https://github.com/lgse/strata/pull/1644) as the baseline. This is a refactor that should preserve the appearance. Capture the three previews before and after the extraction when implementing it.

## Strata version

Source reference: `395af5e24647c960e6e120d2f8f9da420ca372c1`, the current head of #1644. Recheck the final merged implementation before starting.

## Additional context

- Related camera-view issue: [#1633](https://github.com/lgse/strata/issues/1633).
- Required merge prerequisite: [camera-view PR #1644](https://github.com/lgse/strata/pull/1644). Work can start only once this PR is merged into `main`.
- I couldn't add GitHub's native blocked-by link with the current account. A maintainer can add #1633 as the blocking issue. The merge prerequisite above applies regardless.
- Starting points: `src/ui/preview/audio.rs`, `audio/layout.rs`, `video.rs`, `video/layout.rs`, `model.rs`, `media_layout.rs` and the preview styles in `src/style.css`.
- Keep the existing waveform, volume bindings and `ListingPosition` caption reuse. Any new application-owned strings must follow the eleven-language localisation requirement.

This should be a separate follow-up PR after the camera views have landed.

author: wmfeht
body:
## Description

Adds an in-process QA harness. It drives Strata through a feature-gated `--qa` JSON protocol instead of AT-SPI, and every Python E2E test now has a QA scenario running beside it.

- **Harness:** `strata --qa <dir>` (and `--portal`), behind the `qa` Cargo feature. Input is injected with XTEST, and widget state is read from the app's own widget tree. The default build is unchanged.
- **Scenarios:** 402 scenario files under `tests/qa/scenarios/`, one per Python test function, covering 1049 runs.
  - 4 runs of the large-table test stay Python-only.
  - `settings-text-size-keeps-switches` is skipped by default until its app race is fixed.
- **Runner:** `tests/qa.rs` uses a small custom harness that makes each run its own test and starts the costliest first. Run costs are benchmarked, recorded in each header, and refreshed with `scripts/qa_cost.py`.
  - A full `./scripts/qa.sh` takes about 103 s at 24 threads and about 63 s at 48.
- **Parity:** `scripts/qa-parity.sh` compares each QA scenario with its Python twin: pass/fail, input logs and final state, plus mutation patches for 20 core scenarios. It is a local tool; CI does not run it.
- **Agent skills:** `.agents/skills/qa-scenarios`, `qa-drive` and `qa-quality`, linked from `.claude/skills/`.
  - `qa-scenarios`: writing and managing scenarios.
  - `qa-drive`: checking a change by hand with the new `scripts/qa-drive.sh`.
  - `qa-quality`: a rubric whose scores are recorded in each scenario's `quality` header field and checked by the runner.
- **Twin-less scenarios:** a scenario's `twin` is now optional, so QA-only scenarios can be written.

## Visual evidence

N/A: test tooling, scripts, skills and docs only. The app changes are accessibility labels that match the existing tooltips, and code behind the `qa` feature.

## How to test

1. Run `./scripts/qa.sh`.
2. Run one scenario by name, for example `./scripts/qa.sh copy-leaves-source`.
3. Drive a session by hand:
   - `./scripts/qa-drive.sh start`
   - `./scripts/qa-drive.sh send '{"query":"prefs"}'`
   - `./scripts/qa-drive.sh screenshot shot.png`
   - `./scripts/qa-drive.sh stop`
4. Optionally, check one pair against its Python twin: `./scripts/qa-parity.sh --baseline copy-leaves-source`.

**Expected result:**
- The full run passes, with one SKIPPED line for `settings-text-size-keeps-switches`.
- A named run passes only that scenario's runs.
- `qa-drive.sh` prints a reply for each command and leaves no container behind after `stop`.

## Related issue

No issue; the owner chose to open this without one.
