body:
## Description

When `settings.toml` has a value that fails to deserialize, `salvage_preferences` rebuilds the settings one top-level key at a time and reverts any key that fails. Serde rejects a whole list or map when a single element is invalid, so the unit that got reverted was the entire collection: one unrecognized value in `[omarchy_variants]` emptied every variant, one bad name in `list_hidden_columns` emptied the list, and so on. Startup doesn't write the file, but the next successful save serialized those defaults over the user's data.

A malformed list or table is now salvaged one level down, and again for nested lists (each device's destinations under `send_to_recent_destinations`), keeping every entry that still deserializes. Affected: `omarchy_variants`, `list_hidden_columns`, `list_column_order`, `search_exclusions`, `sidebar_order`, `send_to_recent_destinations`, `device_labels`, `folder_colors`, `custom_icons`.

Unchanged: a scalar of the wrong type, a value of the wrong shape (a string where a table belongs), and a record that is missing a required field still fall back to the default as a unit. That includes `chooser_list_columns` and `browser_list_columns`, whose widths are all required, so one bad width resets that record rather than inventing defaults for the others.

## Visual evidence

N/A: no UI change; this only affects which settings survive loading a partly invalid file.

## How to test

1. Put one unrecognized value next to valid ones in `settings.toml`, for example:
   ```toml
   [omarchy_variants]
   catppuccin = "lighter"
   broken = "not-a-variant"
   ```
   and `search_exclusions = [".venv", 12, "/tmp/skip"]`.
2. Start Strata, change any setting so it saves, and read `settings.toml` again.

**Expected result:** Only the bad entries are gone. `catppuccin`, `.venv` and `/tmp/skip` are still in the file; before this change both tables were erased.

No QA scenario covers malformed collection contents, and the QA runner needs the pinned container, which wasn't available here, so it was not run.

## Related issue

Closes #1844

comments.body:
## Technical details

### Reproduced

Yes, on upstream `main` at `2218357c`. When a list or map in `settings.toml` has only valid entries, it loads intact. One bad entry empties the whole collection:

- `[omarchy_variants]` with `catppuccin = "not-a-variant"` next to two valid entries loads as an empty map.
- `list_hidden_columns = ["size", "not_a_column", "mode"]` loads as an empty list.
- `list_column_order = ["name", "size", "bogus", "modified"]` loads as the default order.
- `search_exclusions = [".venv", 12]` loads as an empty list.
- `[send_to_recent_destinations]` with one bad path drops every device.

Startup doesn't touch the file. The next successful save erases those keys. On Xvfb, `PreferenceManager::load` followed by `set_folder_peeking(true)` and `storage::writer::settle` rewrote a mixed fixture with all of these keys removed: `omarchy_variants`, `list_hidden_columns`, `list_column_order`, `search_exclusions`, `send_to_recent_destinations`, `chooser_list_columns`, and `device_labels`. `sidebar_order` was written back as the built-in default. Valid keys such as `show_hidden` and `[folder_colors]` survived.

### Root cause

`parse_preferences` (`src/ui/preferences.rs:1989`) decodes the whole `Preferences` struct. If that fails, it logs `settings file has invalid entries; keeping the valid ones` and falls back to `salvage_preferences` (`preferences.rs:2004`).

`salvage_preferences` starts from defaults and re-inserts one top-level key at a time. When a key fails to deserialize, it puts the default back (`preferences.rs:2010-2011`). Serde rejects a whole `HashMap` or `Vec` when any one element fails, so the unit that gets reverted is the entire collection.

`save_preferences` (`preferences.rs:1910`, `1924`) serializes the whole struct. The empty map and empty vec are skipped by `skip_serializing_if`, and a default `list_column_order` is skipped by `is_default_list_column_order` (`preferences.rs:247`). So the next save removes the tables from disk.

The doc comment at `preferences.rs:2001` says salvage keeps the entries that still deserialize. In practice it only does that per top-level key.

### Suggested fix direction

When a top-level value that is a table or array fails, run the same insert-and-revert loop one level down, keeping the children that deserialize and dropping the ones that don't. Go one level deeper for nested arrays, such as each device under `send_to_recent_destinations`. A value of the wrong shape entirely, like a string where a table belongs, can stay on the default.

`sanitize_list_column_order` and `sanitize_list_hidden_columns` (`preferences.rs:695`) already repair partial lists. `FolderViews::parse` (`src/ui/preferences/folder_views.rs:417`) already skips one bad entry and keeps the rest, so it can serve as a model.

Keep `a_malformed_preference_does_not_discard_the_others` (`src/ui/preferences/tests/preferences.rs:200`) and add a mixed-entry case next to it.

### Related code

The same key-level revert affects every collection on `Preferences`. The fields marked reproduced were checked in the same run.

- `list_column_order` (reproduced)
- `search_exclusions` (reproduced)
- `sidebar_order`: reproduced. It is replaced by `default_sidebar_order` and written back.
- `send_to_recent_destinations` (reproduced)
- `device_labels` (reproduced)
- `chooser_list_columns`: reproduced. `mode = "wide"` drops the whole width record. `browser_list_columns` uses the same struct.
- `folder_colors` and `custom_icons` have the same type as `device_labels`, so they're exposed the same way.

### Checks run

Temporary tests `repro_1844_one_unrecognized_value_drops_the_rest_of_each_list` and `repro_1844_next_settings_save_erases_the_lists_from_disk` were run with `cargo test --bin strata --all-features repro_1844` under Xvfb. Both passed, confirming the bug, and they have since been removed. The E2E suite, QA scenarios, and `quality.sh` were not run.

author: pdwaldrop
body:
## Description

Extracting a TAR that contains a hard link onto vfat, exFAT, exfat-fuse or an SMB mount stopped at that member: `link()` answers `EPERM`, `ENOSYS` or `EOPNOTSUPP` there, `create_hard_link` turned every error into a fatal one, and the `?` in `extract_member` ended the loop. Every later member was never extracted, and the message didn't say so. Symbolic links the mount can't hold already degrade without stopping the extraction; hard links had no equivalent.

`create_hard_link` now reports those three errors the way `create_symlink` reports a mount that can't hold a link (`Unmade::Unheld`), using the same definition of "no hard links" as the copy engine's placement probe (`EPERM`, or unsupported/`ENOSYS`), and not when the name is simply taken. `extract_member` then re-dispatches the member as a regular file read from the already-extracted target, opened without following links. Because that goes through the normal file path, the copy honors the declared size, the free space left at the destination, cancellation, and the member's mode and time, and a later link to the copy resolves like any other member. On a mount that can hold hard links nothing changes.

A failure that isn't a missing capability (`ENOSPC`, I/O errors) still aborts, as does a target that can't be reopened as a regular file; those keep the existing "Could not link" message, now with the reason after it instead of a bare errno text.

**Not changed:** later hard links still try `link()` once each instead of remembering the mount has none (`learn_mount_type` could record `hard_links = Some(false)`); and an abort still doesn't list the members that were never written. Both are separate from the silent-stop bug here.

## Visual evidence

N/A: no UI change. The visible difference is that the extraction completes.

## How to test

1. Make a TAR with a hard link: `echo data > a.txt && ln a.txt b.txt && echo more > c.txt && tar cf bundle.tar a.txt b.txt c.txt`.
2. Extract it with Strata onto a FAT or exFAT drive (or a loop-mounted `mkfs.vfat` image).

**Expected result:** `a.txt`, `b.txt` and `c.txt` are all extracted and `b.txt` has the same contents as `a.txt` (a copy; it takes space of its own). Before this change extraction stopped at `b.txt` with "Could not link", and `c.txt` was missing.

Covered by `a_hard_link_the_destination_cannot_hold_is_copied_and_the_rest_still_extracts`, which uses the existing filesystem quirks (vfat `EPERM`, exfat-fuse `ENOSYS`, and an `EOPNOTSUPP` mount) plus an ext4 control that must still produce a real hard link, and includes a link to the copied member. It fails on the old code. Not exercised here: a real FAT/exFAT mount, and the QA scenarios (none cover hard links; the runner needs the pinned container, which wasn't available).

## Related issue

Closes #1848

comments.author: wmfeht
comments.body:
## Technical details

### Reproduced

Yes, on upstream `main` at `2218357c`. The kernel vfat and exfat drivers weren't available on the test machine, so I tested on a live exFAT mount through FUSE (exfat-fuse 1.4.0 on a loop device) and with the `Quirks::vfat()`, `Quirks::exfat()`, and `Quirks::exfat_fuse()` presets. On the FUSE mount, `link()` returns `EPERM` and `symlink()` returns `ENOSYS`.

The test archive was a TAR with three members, in order: `a.txt` (a regular file), `b.txt` (a hard link to `a.txt`), and `c.txt` (a regular file).

| Destination | Result |
| --- | --- |
| ext4 | Completes. `a.txt` and `b.txt` share an inode, and progress reaches 3. |
| Live exFAT-FUSE | Stops after one member. Only `a.txt` exists, and `skipped` is empty. |
| vfat and exfat presets (`EPERM`) | Same abort. |
| exfat_fuse preset (`ENOSYS`) | Same abort. |

The error message is `Could not link "b.txt" to "a.txt": Permission denied. Extracted entries remain in "bundle".` With `ENOSYS` it says "An unexpected system error occurred." Neither message mentions `c.txt`.

### Root cause

- In `extract_tar` (`src/adapters/local_operations/archive/decoders.rs:487-504`), a hard link becomes `MemberContent::HardLink`, and `session.extract_member(...)?` exits the loop on the first error. The `remaining` list is filled only when the user cancels (`decoders.rs:441-448`).
- `create_hard_link` (`destination.rs:538-561`) calls `linkat`. Any errno that isn't a refused name becomes `Unmade::Failed` (`destination.rs:672-677`). `refuses_name` (`copy_engine.rs:1527-1532`) doesn't cover `EPERM` or `ENOSYS`, so the error goes back up as `ArchiveError::Failed` (`extraction.rs:334`).
- The `Failed` arm of `finish` (`extraction.rs:575-579`) never reports the remaining names. Those are only read for `Cancelled` (`extraction.rs:540-543`).
- `ENOSYS` has no case in `io_error_reason` (`src/services/file_source.rs:166-200`), which is why the message is the generic one.

### Suggested fix direction

When `link` fails because the mount can't hold hard links, copy the target's bytes into the new member and keep extracting. The copy engine already does this (`copy_engine/links.rs:311-323`).

Treat `EPERM`, `ENOSYS`, and `EOPNOTSUPP` as "no hard links", which matches what `placement::probe` stores as `hard_links = Some(false)` (`placement.rs:807-811`). `ENOSPC`, `EDQUOT`, and fatal I/O errors should still abort.

`learn_mount_type` (`mount_profile.rs:131-146`) already marks symlinks as unsupported on FAT but leaves `hard_links` unset. Setting it there would let later hard links skip calling `link` at all.

If a hard-link failure still has to stop the extract, the error should name the members that weren't written. That means the `Failed` arm of `finish` has to use the remaining-name list, and `extract_tar` has to supply the unread names.

### Related code

- Symlinks on these filesystems are already skipped gracefully: `create_symlink` returns `Unheld`, and `extract_member` turns that into `LeftOut` (`destination.rs:503-505`, `extraction.rs:302-315`). Only hard links to regular files that were already extracted abort the extract.
- The test `links_the_destination_cannot_hold_are_left_out_with_hard_links_to_them` covers hard links to skipped symlinks, but not hard links to regular files.
- ZIP (`decoders.rs:390`), 7z (`decoders.rs:603`), and RAR (`decoders/rar.rs:53-63`) also stop on the first member error. Because the `Failed` arm ignores remaining names, the report leaves out later members for those formats too.
- FIFO and device members refuse on purpose (`decoders.rs:490-500`), but they still leave later members unnamed.
- Update extraction rejects hard links on purpose (`src/services/update_install/archive.rs:92-97`). That should stay.

### Checks run

- `link()` and `symlink()` on the live exfat-fuse mount.
- A temporary test, `tar_hard_link_on_vfat_and_exfat_aborts_before_later_members`, run with `STRATA_EXFAT_MOUNT` set: 1 passed. It was removed afterward.
- E2E, the QA scenarios, and `quality.sh` were not run.

## Description

In List and Icons, Shift+arrow after a Ctrl+click extended the selection from the previously selected item instead of the Ctrl+clicked one, so the next action could hit the wrong files. Columns was already correct.

The two views leave Shift+arrow to GTK, which extends from its own range origin. The row gesture claims modified clicks, so GTK's click handling never runs and the origin stays on the old item. `list.select-item` is the only way to move it, and it replaces the selection, so the Ctrl+click handler now calls it on the clicked row and then puts the selection back. The change is limited to Ctrl+click.

**Not changed:** the marquee, inline search and programmatic selection updates also write the selection without moving the origin. They are listed in the technical notes on the issue and need their own fixes.

## Visual evidence

N/A: no visual change. The difference is which items Shift+arrow selects.

## How to test

1. Open a folder with at least five files in List or Icons view.
2. Click the first file, Ctrl+click the third, then press Shift+Down (List) or Shift+Right (Icons).

**Expected result:** the third and fourth files are selected, as in Columns. Before this change the first four were.

`control_click_moves_the_shift_range_origin_to_the_clicked_row` covers the GTK behavior and the new helper in a List and a Grid view. The real Ctrl+click wiring is covered by the new QA scenario `control-click-sets-shift-anchor`: in the pinned container it passes in all three modes, and with the `move_range_origin` call removed it fails in Icons and List (selection `archive, documents, pictures, readme.md`) while Columns still passes.

## Related issue

Closes #1851

## Technical details

### Reproduced

Yes, on upstream `main` at `2218357c`. In List and Icons, Shift+arrow extends the selection from the item that was selected before the Ctrl+click. Columns extends from the Ctrl+clicked item, which is correct.

Setup: five files, `a.txt` through `e.txt`, group-by-type off, single-click previews off. Steps: click `a.txt`, Ctrl+click `c.txt`, then press Shift and the arrow key toward `d.txt` (Down in Columns and List, Right in Icons).

Results after the Shift+arrow:

- Columns: `c.txt` and `d.txt` are selected.
- List and Icons: `a.txt` through `d.txt` are selected.

In all three views, the app's own anchor is `c.txt` after the Ctrl+click, and it is still `c.txt` after the Shift+arrow.

A separate probe against GTK 4.14.5, with no Strata code, shows the same rule. Writing the `GtkMultiSelection` bitset doesn't move GTK's extend origin. Only `list.select-item` with extend false moves it.

```text
bitset {0,2} without select-item: 0 2
extend select-item 3 from untouched origin: 0 1 2 3
ctrl-style select-item 2, then extend 3: 2 3
```

### Root cause

List and Icons leave Shift+arrow to GTK. Columns handles it itself, starting from `selection_anchor`.

- **Which handler runs:** `single_pane_arrow_action` (`src/ui/window.rs:526`) returns `SinglePaneArrow::Native` for List and Icons (`:542`). `native_selection` then lets GTK's shortcut run (`src/ui/window/keyboard/items.rs:250`, `:271`). Columns goes to `browser.extend_selection` instead (`items.rs:328-339`, `src/app/navigation.rs:1803`).
- **Ctrl+click sets the app anchor:** Ctrl+click sets the app anchor in every view (`src/ui/collection_interaction.rs:45`, `src/ui/browser_modes.rs:4899-4902`, `src/ui/browser/columns/rows.rs:521`).
- **GTK's origin is never moved:** The click gesture runs in the capture phase and claims modified clicks (`src/ui/collection_interaction.rs:62`, `:83`, `src/ui/browser_modes.rs:4828`). That cancels GTK's own click handling (`gtk_list_factory_widget_click_gesture_released`, `gtk/gtklistfactorywidget.c:469`), so `list.select-item` never runs. GTK's `priv->selected` therefore stays on `a.txt`. Shift+arrow extends from it (`gtk/gtklistbase.c:374-445`, binding at `:1172`). The code already notes this at `reset_native_range_origin` (`src/ui/browser_modes.rs:5342`).

### Suggested fix direction

After a non-Shift pointer selection in List and Icons, move GTK's extend origin to the clicked row, then restore the Ctrl+click bitset. `restore_selection` (`src/ui/browser_modes/navigation.rs:470`) already does this: it calls `reset_native_range_origin`, then `set_selections`.

1. In the click handler, keep `anchor_at` and the `set_selection` of the final bits.
2. With `section.syncing` set, activate `list.select-item` on the clicked position with modify false and extend false. Keeping `syncing` set stops the exclusive select from echoing into the app model.
3. Restore the bits, then clear `syncing`.

GTK has no action that only moves the origin, which is why the bits have to be restored afterward.

Keep List and Icons Shift+arrow on the GTK binding. `extend_selection` walks source order, which is wrong for sorted, filtered, and grouped views.

### Related code

These List and Icons paths also write bits without `list.select-item`, so a Shift+arrow after them can start from a stale origin:

- Marquee `apply_selection` (`src/ui/marquee.rs:830`)
- `SelectionUpdate::Positions` (`src/ui/browser_modes/events.rs:430`, `src/ui/browser_modes.rs:5312`)
- Inline search (`src/ui/inline_search/collection.rs:472`)

These paths already move the origin correctly:

- `restore_selection` and `restore_reloaded_selection` (`navigation.rs:470`, `:489`)
- `resume_native_selection` (`src/ui/browser_modes.rs:1529`)
- Space and plain clicks

### Checks run

- A temporary GTK test, `ctrl_click_then_shift_arrow_uses_each_view_anchor`, run under Xvfb. It passed with the results above and was then removed.
- The GTK 4.14.5 `list.select-item` probe shown above.

E2E, the QA scenarios, and `quality.sh` were not run. No code was changed.

## Description

Extracting an archive with a member such as `names/c:notes` stopped at that member: the drive-prefix check ran on every path component, so the name was refused as an unsafe path, the refusal aborted the extraction, and every later member was never extracted.

`sanitized_archive_path` now applies the check only while the sanitized path is still empty, after `.` components are skipped and `..` components are popped. A leading drive prefix stays refused, including one reached through `..` (`safe/../c:notes`) or `./`, and a colon in a later component is an ordinary name. The one check covers ZIP, TAR, TAR.GZ, 7Z and RAR members and hard-link targets. Absolute and UNC paths still go through the separate check. `docs/archives.md` now says a *leading* drive prefix is invalid.

On a destination that cannot store `:` the existing name fixing still rewrites it.

## Visual evidence

N/A: no UI change. The visible difference is that the extraction completes.

## How to test

1. Make a ZIP with `before.txt`, `names/c:notes` and `after.txt`, for example with `zip notes.zip before.txt 'names/c:notes' after.txt`.
2. Extract it with Strata.

**Expected result:** all three files are extracted, with `c:notes` inside `names`. Before this change extraction stopped at `names/c:notes` with "Refusing unsafe archive path" and `after.txt` was missing.

Covered by `archive_paths_are_sanitized_to_confined_relative_paths`, which now accepts the later-component cases and still refuses `C:marker`, `C:/evil.txt`, `./c:notes` and `safe/../c:notes`, and by `a_colon_after_the_first_component_is_a_name_and_a_leading_drive_prefix_is_refused`, which extracts the member plus a hard link to it and checks that a leading `c:notes` still fails. Both fail on the old code with the issue's error. No QA scenario covers archive member names, so none was run.

## Related issue

Closes #1855

## Technical details

### Reproduced

Yes, on upstream `main` at `2218357c`. I extracted a zip named `notes.zip` with the members `before.txt`, `names/c:notes`, and `after.txt` through `extract_zip`. It failed with:

`Refusing unsafe archive path: names/c:notes. Extracted entries remain in "notes".`

`before.txt` was written. `names/c:notes` and `after.txt` were not, so the error aborts the whole extraction.

| Member | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `names/c:notes`, `names\c:notes`, `folder/c:notes.txt`, `safe/C:/marker`, `safe/../names/c:notes` | refused (wrong) |
| `c:notes`, `C:marker`, `C:/evil.txt`, `./c:notes`, `safe/../c:notes` | refused (intended, leading drive prefix) |
| `names/10:00` | accepted |

The repro was a temporary test, run with `cargo test --bin strata -- destination::tests::repro_1855_later_component_drive_prefix` under Xvfb. It was removed afterward.

### Root cause

`sanitized_archive_path` in `src/adapters/local_operations/archive/destination.rs` converts `\` to `/`, splits on `/`, and runs the letter-plus-colon drive check inside the loop for every component (`destination.rs:125-127`). So `names/c:notes` gets refused on its second component.

The error is a hard failure. `ExtractionSession::extract_member` returns it (`extraction.rs:270`), and `From<String> for ArchiveError` turns it into an abort (`archive.rs:485-488`), so every later member is skipped.

`docs/archives.md` says "Absolute paths and Windows drive prefixes remain invalid" without saying the prefix has to lead the member path.

### Suggested fix direction

Only apply the drive check while the sanitized path is still empty, meaning after `.` components are skipped and `..` components are popped. That keeps a leading prefix refused, including `safe/../c:notes`, which sanitizes to `c:notes`. Checking only the first raw segment would let that one through.

Update `archive_paths_are_sanitized_to_confined_relative_paths` in `destination/tests.rs:85-91`, which currently expects `safe/C:/marker` to fail, and add `names/c:notes`. Absolute and UNC paths go through the separate check at `destination.rs:114` and stay refused.

In `docs/archives.md`, say that a *leading* drive prefix is invalid and that a colon in a later component is an ordinary name. Destinations that can't store `:` already rewrite it (`names/fix.rs:165-169`).

### Related code

All of these go through the same predicate, so the one fix covers them:

- ZIP, TAR, TAR.GZ, and 7Z (`decoders.rs:390`, `504`, `604`), and RAR (`decoders/rar.rs:53-54`).
- Hard-link targets (`extraction.rs:243-256`). A target like `names/c:notes` is currently treated as missing.
- The not-attempted list on cancellation (`extraction.rs:540-542`).

### Checks run

The targeted `cargo test` above, using a temporary probe that has since been removed. The E2E suite, QA scenarios, and `quality.sh` were not run.

## Description

With `RUST_LOG` unset the log defaults to INFO, and the open-target warning wrote the location with `display_path`. That keeps the user name, query and fragment once the password has been stripped, and an SMB domain is stored as the user, so it was logged too. The same event also logged the raw GIO error, which can repeat the URI.

The warning now logs `diagnostic_path` (scheme, host and path only) and passes the error text through `sanitize_failure_message`. Three other events that logged a location or URI the same way get the same treatment: opening in a new tab or window, recording a file in Recent history, and removing a Recent entry. The URI redaction behind `diagnostic_path` is now a shared `diagnostic_uri`. `display_path` is unchanged for the UI.

**Not changed:** the lane key built in `mount_lanes::authority` still holds the full user info, but nothing logs it, and `Location::parent` still copies credentials into the parent. Both are listed in the technical notes on the issue and are separate changes.

## Visual evidence

N/A: no UI change.

## How to test

1. Run `strata 'sftp://alice@host.example/some/file?token=abc#frag'` with `RUST_LOG` unset, with no SFTP server at that host.
2. Read the "target location unavailable" warning in the log.

**Expected result:** the warning shows `sftp://host.example/some/file`, with no user name, query or fragment, and the error text carries none either. Before this change it showed `sftp://alice@host.example/some/file?token=abc#frag`.

Covered by `an_unavailable_target_logs_no_user_query_or_fragment` and `recent_removal_logs_keep_credentials_out_of_the_default_log`, which read the captured log, and by `diagnostic_uris_drop_user_domain_query_and_fragment` for the SMB domain forms. The two log tests fail on the old code. No QA scenario covers log output, so none was run.

## Related issue

Closes #1846

comments.body:
## Technical details

### Reproduced

Yes, on upstream `main` at `2218357c`. When `RUST_LOG` is unset, logging defaults to INFO, so WARN lines go to the default log.

I wrote a temporary unit test that passes URIs through `location_for_file` and logs `display_path` in the same form as the open-target warning. The password never appeared in the output. The username, query, fragment, and SMB domain did:

```text
sftp://alice:s3cret@fileserver.example/private?token=abc#frag
  warn: sftp://alice@fileserver.example/private?token=abc#frag
smb://alice:s3cret;domain=CORP@fileserver.example/share?token=abc#frag
  warn: smb://alice@fileserver.example/share?token=abc#frag
smb://CORP;alice:s3cret@fileserver.example/share?token=abc#frag
  warn: smb://CORP@fileserver.example/share?token=abc#frag
```

For comparison, `diagnostic_path` already reduces every one of these to `scheme://host/path`.

### Root cause

`location_for_file` (`src/adapters/gio_location.rs:22-30`) stores the result of `sanitize_uri_credentials` (`src/services/file_source.rs:307-357`). That function rebuilds the URI without the password or auth params, but keeps the user, the query, and the fragment (lines 339-350).

`display_path` (`src/model/mod.rs:361-376`) only hides the userinfo while `uri_contains_credentials` is true. Once the password has been stripped, that check is false, so the user field is printed in full. In the GVfs SMB form `CORP;alice:pw`, GLib stores the domain as the user, which is why `CORP` shows up.

The default-log site is `src/ui/window/open_argument.rs:133-136`:

```rust
tracing::warn!(location = %location.display_path(), %error, "target location unavailable");
```

`%error` there is the raw GIO error, and it is not passed through `sanitize_failure_message`.

### Suggested fix direction

For logging, use `Location::diagnostic_path` (`src/model/mod.rs:344-359`), which already hides userinfo, query, and fragment. Pass GIO error text through `sanitize_failure_message` (`file_source.rs:360-377`) before logging it. Keep `display_path` for the UI.

### Related code

- `src/ui/window/composition/tabs.rs:252`, `259` log the same `display_path` string at DEBUG.
- `src/ui/open_with.rs:522-525` logs raw `file.uri()`, which still includes the password on GLib 2.80.
- `src/adapters/local_files.rs:1391`, `1394`, `1401` (DEBUG) and `1402-1406` (WARN) print recent-registry URIs unchanged. I did not reproduce this one, because recent enumeration is unsupported in this environment.
- `authority` in `src/adapters/volume/mount_lanes.rs:597-610` builds the lane key with the full userinfo, including the password. Nothing logs that key today.
- `Location::parent` (`src/model/mod.rs:228-241`) copies the user, password, auth params, query, and fragment into the parent.
- These sites already do it correctly: `browser/location.rs:629-631`, `local_files.rs:2524-2534` and `2907-2912`, `browser/desktop.rs:171-179`, `browser/clipboard.rs:688-691`, and `app/browser.rs:4221-4225`.

### Checks run

- The temporary test `adapters::gio_location::tests::default_log_shape_keeps_user_query_fragment_and_smb_domain` passed. It has since been removed.
- GLib 2.80 check: `G_URI_HIDE_PASSWORD` drops only the password.
- This VM has no GVfs SFTP/SMB backend, so I did not do a live open.
- E2E, the QA scenarios, and `quality.sh` were not run.

## Description

In Columns with hidden files off, renaming a folder whose child column is open to a dot name left the cursor on the renamed folder and the child column open. The listing never shows that row, so F2 did nothing.

A rename with an open child column took a different path from one without: `publish_rename` moved the row and the open columns to the new hidden path, while a folder with no child column was left to the directory monitor, which reports the old name as removed, moves the cursor to a visible neighbor and closes the columns. `publish_rename` now returns early when the renamed entry is hidden and hidden files are off, so both cases go through the monitor. With hidden files on, or a rename to a visible name, the move is unchanged.

**Not changed:** like the case without a child column, this relies on the directory monitor reporting the removal.

## Visual evidence

N/A: no layout change. The difference is that the child column closes and the cursor moves to a visible item.

## How to test

1. In Columns with hidden files off, select a folder so its contents show in the next column.
2. Rename the folder to a name that starts with a dot, then press F2.

**Expected result:** the child column closes, the cursor moves to a visible neighbor, and F2 starts a rename on it. Before this change the child column stayed open and F2 did nothing.

Covered by `renaming_an_open_folder_to_a_hidden_name_closes_its_column_and_keeps_rename_working`, which fails on the old code with the child column still open. The existing rename tests and QA scenarios still pass.

## Related issue

Closes #1852

2. Press F2.

## Expected

comments.author: wmfeht
comments.body:
## Technical details

### Reproduced

Yes, on upstream `main` at `2218357c`, with hidden files off, in Columns view. The test directory held `a.txt`, `c.txt`, and `folder/child.txt`. I selected `folder` so it was open in the next column, then renamed it to `.hidden-folder` with the inline rename editor (`begin_rename`, which F2 calls).

I checked the state after the rename settled (about 800ms, past the directory monitor's 100ms flush):

- The cursor stayed on `.hidden-folder` (`is_hidden` true, depth 0, position 0, selected `[0]`).
- Column 0 still listed `.hidden-folder`, `a.txt`, and `c.txt`.
- Column 1 stayed open on `.hidden-folder` and listed `child.txt`.
- `begin_rename()` returned false, so F2 opens no editor.
- With `a.txt` selected, `begin_rename()` opened an editor, so the rename operation itself had finished.

The same rename with no child column open works as expected. After the monitor flush, the folder is gone from the model, focus moves to `a.txt`, and `begin_rename()` starts.

### Root cause

`Browser::rename` marks the new entry hidden when its name starts with `.` (`src/app/browser.rs:2616`). With hidden files off, the directory monitor reports a rename from a visible name to a dot name as a removal of the old name and never reports the new one (`src/adapters/local_files.rs:2586-2593`). That removal moves the cursor to a visible neighbor (`src/app/navigation.rs:983-994`). This is what happens when no child column is open, and it matches how files behave.

An open child column takes a different path:

1. `publish_rename` returns early unless an open column is inside the renamed folder (`src/app/browser.rs:4025-4029`). `Location::is_within` uses `Path::starts_with` (`src/model/mod.rs:314-316`), so the open child column counts.
2. `publish_rename` then applies `DirectoryChange::Move` to the parent (`src/app/browser.rs:4037-4044`) and moves the deeper columns to the new path (`src/app/browser.rs:4048`, `4058-4090`).
3. The Move arm keeps the selection, anchor, and load cursor on the new location (`src/app/navigation.rs:1021-1037`). It adds the hidden entry and calls `retain_selected_locations(false)` (`src/app/navigation.rs:1045-1052`), which keeps hidden rows.
4. `apply_live_directory_change` skips `restore_path` for a Move (`src/app/browser/directory_changes.rs:408-412`) and calls `relocate_open_columns` again (`417-429`).
5. When the monitor later reports the old name as removed, nothing matches, because the row and the child column already use the hidden path.

F2 opens the editor only when `begin_rename` returns true (`src/ui/window/keyboard/commands.rs:60-68`). Here the cursor is still on the hidden folder. Columns rename looks up the row in the filtered view (`src/ui/browser/inline_edit.rs:1207-1217`). With hidden files off, `ViewMap::view_position` has no row for that entry (`src/ui/browser/collection.rs:695-710`; the filter is in `src/ui/browser/entry.rs:129-130`), so the editor never opens.

### Suggested fix direction

When a rename gives the folder a dot name and that column isn't showing hidden files, handle it the same way the monitor removal does:

- Remove the old row.
- Move the cursor with `visible_neighbor`, the same rule `set_show_hidden` uses (`src/app/navigation.rs:1140-1156`).
- Close the child columns with `restore_path` instead of `relocate_open_columns`.

Both places that relocate columns need the same change: the Move branch in `apply_live_directory_change`, and the extra `relocate_open_columns` call at the end of `publish_rename`. The hidden entry can stay in the model as long as the cursor and the child columns move off it. The filtered view has no row for that entry, which is why F2 stops working.

### Related code

- `visible_monitor_change` already handles a rename to a dot name correctly (`src/adapters/local_files.rs:2570-2598`). Watches are started with `show_hidden` (`src/app/browser.rs:4162-4164`).
- When a row is removed, the cursor falls back to a neighbor (`src/app/navigation.rs:975-994`). Turning hidden files off also moves the cursor off a hidden row (`src/app/navigation.rs:1136-1158`).
- `path_after_external_change` moves child columns to the new path on a Move and cuts them off on a Remove (`src/app/navigation.rs:430-449`). Only a Remove closes the child column.
- `note_pending_rename_splices` treats a rename to a dot name as done once the old row disappears (`src/ui/browser/inline_edit.rs:143-149`, `481-490`). That only clears the pending rename and doesn't move the cursor. The repro shows the pending rename isn't what blocks F2.
- List and Icons use the same filtered-row lookup in `ModeViews::begin_rename` (`src/ui/browser_modes.rs:946-958`). They never open a child column, so `publish_rename` returns early and the monitor removal moves the cursor first.

### Checks run

- Headless tests under Xvfb with `./scripts/test-headless.py`, built with `CC=gcc CXX=g++ LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/lib/gcc/x86_64-linux-gnu/13`.
- `a_rename_to_a_hidden_name_lets_the_next_rename_start` passed. It covers renaming a file to a dot name in Columns and List.
- A temporary GTK test covered the folder rename to `.hidden-folder` with and without the child column open. It gave the results above and was then deleted.

E2E, the QA scenarios, and `quality.sh` were not run.

author: pdwaldrop
body:
## Description

Format Drive let you enter an exFAT label of up to 32 characters, but `mkfs.exfat` and libblockdev accept 11 UTF-16 code units. A label of 12 to 32 characters passed the check that runs before the unmount, the drive was unmounted, and UDisks then refused the label, leaving the drive unmounted.

`FilesystemType::max_label_len` now returns 11 for exFAT, and label length is counted in UTF-16 code units (`FilesystemType::label_len`) instead of characters, so six emoji, which are 12 units, no longer pass. The entry limit, the Continue button, the summary step and the check before the unmount all use the same limit and measure. FAT32 and NTFS keep their limits; characters in the basic plane count the same as before.

**Not changed:** `label_character_error` still rejects `*?:/\|<>"` for exFAT, which `mkfs.exfat` accepts; that stricter check is a separate question.

## Visual evidence

N/A: no layout change. The label field stops accepting more than 11 characters for exFAT and Continue is disabled for labels over the limit.

## How to test

1. Open Format Drive on a removable drive and choose exFAT.
2. Type a label of 12 or more characters.

**Expected result:** the field stops at 11 characters, and a label of six emoji (12 UTF-16 units) disables Continue. Before this change a label of 12 to 32 characters was accepted, the drive was unmounted, and formatting then failed.

Covered by `filesystem_label_limits_match_backends`, `label_length_counts_utf16_code_units`, `format_filesystem_selection_updates_label_limit_and_validity` and `a_label_over_the_backend_limit_in_utf16_units_blocks_continue`. The first, second-to-last and last fail with the old limit. No QA scenario covers Format Drive, so none was run, and I did not format a real drive.

## Related issue

Closes #1849

Format Drive accepts exFAT labels of 12 to 32 characters, but mkfs.exfat only takes 11. The volume is unmounted first, then formatting fails.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open Format Drive on a removable drive.
2. Choose exFAT and enter a label of 12 to 32 characters.
3. Start formatting.

## Expected

The UI limits exFAT labels to 11 characters, or validates before unmounting.

## Actual

- Installation: Nightly build

comments.author: wmfeht
comments.body:
## Technical details

### Reproduced

Partially, on upstream `main` at `2218357c`. I confirmed the backend limit directly. Format Drive was not run in the app, because the test machine has no system bus or UDisks.

- With exfatprogs 1.2.2 on a 32 MiB image, `mkfs.exfat -L` accepts labels of 0, 1, and 11 characters. It rejects 12, 15, and 32 characters (exit 249, `input string is too long`, `exFAT format fail!`). `-n` fails the same way.
- `exfatlabel` accepts 11 characters and rejects 12 (exit 255). The old label is kept.
- The limit is 11 UTF-16 code units, not 11 characters. Five emoji (10 units) work, and six emoji (12 units) fail.

### Root cause

`src/ui/window/drive_ops.rs:31-37`, `FilesystemType::max_label_len`, returns 32 for exFAT, the same as NTFS. It was set in `84fde94b` (#1331). exfatprogs defines `VOLUME_LABEL_MAX_LEN` as 11 (22 bytes of UTF-16).

The dialog uses that 32 everywhere:

- `refresh_format_selection` (`src/ui/window/drive_dialogs.rs:243-256`) sets the entry's `max_length` and keeps Continue enabled.
- The entry is created with that limit at `drive_dialogs.rs:969-971`.
- The first Continue click checks it again at `drive_dialogs.rs:1054-1056`.

`format_volume` (`drive_ops.rs:324-332`) runs the length and character checks before `unmount_for_exclusive_access` (`drive_ops.rs:296-311`). Labels of 33 or more characters are rejected before the unmount. Labels of 12 to 32 characters pass, the volume is unmounted, and `format_device` (`drive_ops.rs:361-394`) calls UDisks2 `Block.Format` with a `label` option (`format_options`, `drive_ops.rs:72-76`).

With udisks 2.10.1 and libblockdev 3.1.1, `format_pre_checks` runs `bd_fs_exfat_check_label`, which rejects UTF-16LE labels over 22 bytes (`Label for exFAT filesystem is too long.`). That check runs before wipe and mkfs, so the existing filesystem is not erased. The volume is just left unmounted.

### Suggested fix direction

Set the exFAT limit to 11 UTF-16 code units. The entry, the Continue button, the summary step, and the pre-unmount check in `format_volume` all use that one constant. Measure the length in UTF-16 units (`encode_utf16().count()`) instead of `chars().count()`. Otherwise six emoji (6 characters, 12 units) still get through. Also update `filesystem_label_limits_match_backends` in `src/ui/window/drive_ops/tests.rs:174-178`, which currently expects 32 for exFAT.

### Related code

- The FAT32 limit of 11 matches `mkfs.fat` 4.2 and libblockdev.
- The NTFS limit of 32 is tighter than the backend. libblockdev allows 128, and `mkntfs` stored 32, 33, and 128 characters. So NTFS can't hit the unmount-then-fail path.
- `label_character_error` (`drive_ops.rs:39-61`) also runs before the unmount. It rejects `*?:/\|<>"` for exFAT, but `mkfs.exfat` 1.2.2 accepted each of those, so that check may be stricter than it needs to be.
- There is no separate relabel action, so exFAT labels are only sent from this format path.

### Checks run

The `mkfs.exfat`, `exfatlabel`, `mkfs.fat`, and `mkntfs` commands above, on `upstream/main` at `2218357c`. No GUI run, no UDisks `Format` call, and no cargo tests. The E2E suite, QA scenarios, and `quality.sh` were not run.

## Description

`gdbus --timeout` applies to the method call, which starts only after the bus connection is made. A session bus socket that accepts the connection and never answers the handshake left `gdbus` blocked, so the installer's `ReloadConfig` call never returned: the service file was written, but file chooser setup, the Omarchy keybinds, udiskie and the finished message never ran. The same call in `reload_dbus` and `refresh_portals` runs on a worker thread, so a silent bus left the Settings row on "Completing setup..." with the setup flag still set.

The installer now runs the call under `timeout 5` (and requires `timeout`, like its other helper commands), so a failure falls into the existing "log out and back in" branch. In Rust, both calls share one `reload_dbus_config`, which passes `--timeout 5` and kills the process after five seconds (`succeeds_within`). The other portal commands, such as `systemctl restart`, are unchanged.

**Not changed:** the manual `gdbus` commands in `docs/portal-file-chooser.md` stay as they are, since a person at a terminal can interrupt them.

## Visual evidence

N/A: no UI change.

## How to test

1. Create a Unix socket that accepts connections and never replies, and point `DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS` at it.
2. Run the installer's file manager step, or enable the file chooser in Settings.

**Expected result:** the installer prints the "log out and back in" warning after about five seconds and finishes, and the Settings row stops spinning. Before this change both waited forever.

Covered by `test_file_manager_service_continues_when_the_bus_never_replies`, which stubs `gdbus` with a command that sleeps for 20 seconds and fails on the old script (the call takes the full 20 seconds), and by `a_helper_that_never_exits_is_stopped_at_the_deadline`, which checks the Rust deadline with `sleep`, `true`, `false` and a missing command. The existing installer tests, which now link `timeout` into their stub `PATH`, still pass. No QA scenario covers the installer, so none was run, and I did not test against a real silent bus.

## Related issue

Closes #1850

comments.author: wmfeht
comments.body:
## Technical details

### Reproduced

Yes, on upstream `main` at `2218357c` with `gdbus` from GLib 2.80.0.

1. Create a Unix socket that accepts connections and never writes anything back.
2. Point `DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS` at that socket.
3. Run `gdbus call --session --timeout 5 --dest org.freedesktop.DBus --object-path /org/freedesktop/DBus --method org.freedesktop.DBus.ReloadConfig`.

After the client sends the D-Bus handshake `\0AUTH\r\n`, `gdbus` stays blocked in `poll`. It was still running after 8 seconds.

Running `install_file_manager_service` from `install.sh` (with `STRATA_INSTALLER_TESTING=1` and a throwaway `HOME`) against the same socket hangs the same way. The service file gets written, but the function never returns and the relogin warning never prints.

The same `gdbus` against other peers:

- Missing socket: fails immediately.
- Socket that accepts, then closes: fails immediately with broken pipe.
- Real `dbus-daemon` with a method that never replies: times out after 2s as expected.
- `timeout 5 gdbus call ...` against the silent socket: exits 124 after 5s.
- `dbus-send --reply-timeout` and `busctl --timeout`: also hang in the handshake.

### Root cause

`install.sh:1545-1552` runs `gdbus ... ReloadConfig` in the foreground. `main` calls it at `install.sh:1752`, after `CORE_INSTALLED=yes` and outside `run_task`. If `gdbus` gets stuck, file chooser setup, the Omarchy keybinds, udiskie, and the finished message never run.

`--timeout` only applies to the method call, which starts after the connection exists. In GLib 2.80.0 `gio/gdbus-tool.c`, the `--session` connection uses `g_bus_get_sync(G_BUS_TYPE_SESSION, NULL, error)` with no cancellable (line 461). That means connect, SASL auth, and Hello have no deadline. A peer that accepts and never answers `AUTH` never lets the timer start. The call was added in #1728 for #1699.

### Suggested fix direction

Wrap the process: `timeout 5 gdbus call --session --timeout 5 ...`. The existing `if` already sends any non-zero status to the `reveal_relogin` branch, so the installer continues. Keep `--timeout 5` so a connected bus that stalls on the method still fails inside `gdbus`. `dbus-send` and `busctl` hang the same way, so the deadline has to be on the process.

### Related code with the same pattern

- `src/portal_setup.rs:367-380`, `reload_dbus()`, runs the same `gdbus` with no `--timeout` and no process deadline. It's called from `install_file_manager` (line 85) and `uninstall_file_manager` (line 101), on a `spawn_blocking` worker (`src/ui/portal_preferences.rs:253-260`). A silent bus leaves the Settings row stuck on "Completing setup..." with `SETUP_RUNNING` still set.
- `src/portal_setup.rs:1140-1151`, `refresh_portals()`, used by portal install, uninstall, and stale-portal refresh (lines 49, 61, 458). The `systemctl restart` that follows waits on `gdbus` too.
- `docs/portal-file-chooser.md:134-137` and `303-306` show the same untimed manual command.
- `scripts/test_installer.py` (`test_file_manager_service_uses_the_installed_binary`) stubs `gdbus` with a script that exits immediately, so it can't catch this case.

### Checks run

Manual repro commands on `upstream/main` at `2218357c`. No code changes. No Rust tests, because the hang is in the shell installer and `gdbus`. The E2E suite, QA scenarios, and `quality.sh` were not run.

author: pdwaldrop
body:
## Description

The browser and the portal file chooser are separate processes that share `settings.toml`. Each loads it once at startup, and each save wrote the whole file from the process's own in-memory copy, so a change the other process made in between, such as 10xer mode or the hidden list columns, was overwritten with the old value on the next save.

A save now writes only the keys this process changed since a save last succeeded, over the file as it is on disk, and keeps everything else, including keys this version does not know. The read, merge and rename happen on the writer thread under the directory lock that `folder-views.toml` already uses (`lock_saves`), through a new `writer::save_locked` that holds the lock until the file is replaced. A file that was repaired at startup (invalid entries dropped, values clamped) is still rewritten whole by the first save, and the retired `omarchy_variant` key is dropped once it has been migrated. `docs/preferences.md` says what a save keeps.

**Not changed:** there is still no live sync between processes, as `docs/preferences.md` already says, so the other process's values reach this one on its next launch. If both change the same setting the later save wins. The case where an external change arrives while a local save is in flight, which the issue also mentions, is separate.

## Visual evidence

N/A: no UI change.

## How to test

1. Start Strata, and start a second process that saves settings, such as the file chooser from another application with Strata as the portal backend.
2. In the second process, change a setting such as 10xer mode, and in the first, change another, such as the preview text wrap.
3. Open `settings.toml`.

**Expected result:** both changes are in the file. Before this change the second save put the other process's setting back to the value it had at startup.

Covered by `a_save_keeps_the_settings_another_process_wrote`, which edits the file as another process would, saves an unrelated setting twice (the second change back to the starting value), and checks the other process's value and an unknown key survive; it fails on the old code. The existing preferences tests, including the ones that check a repaired file is rewritten, pass. A full QA run on this machine fails an unstable set of unrelated scenarios under load, `main` included; the settings restart scenarios pass when run on their own.

## Related issue

Closes #1845

comments.author: wmfeht
comments.body:
## Technical details

### Reproduced

Yes, on upstream `main` at `2218357c`. I ran two processes under Xvfb that share one `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`. Both use `PreferenceManager` the same way the browser and `strata --portal` do.

1. Process A starts and its `settings.toml` watch connects.
2. Process B turns on 10xer, hides the Size column, sets the default sort to size/descending, and flushes.
3. Process A picks up the sort change. 10xer stays off in A, and the Size column stays visible.
4. Process A turns on preview text wrap and flushes.
5. The file now has `tenxer_mode = false`, no `list_hidden_columns`, `preview_text_wrap = true`, and `sort_key = "size"`. B's 10xer and column changes are gone.

### Root cause

Both processes load the same `settings.toml` once at startup (`src/ui/preferences.rs:664-666`, `2091-2092`; `src/main.rs:242-255`, `315-317`).

When the file changes, `adopt_defaults_saved_elsewhere` (`src/ui/preferences/folder_view_settings.rs:392-404`) rereads it, but `adopt_defaults` (`407-426`) only copies `sort_key`, `sort_direction`, and `icons_thumbnail_size`. `tenxer_mode`, `list_column_order`, and `list_hidden_columns` keep the values the process started with. Windows bind to those through the local manager only (`src/ui/browser/preferences.rs:68-93`).

On the next save, the process writes out its whole in-memory `Preferences` (`preferences.rs:1910-1927`), and the writer replaces the file (`src/storage/writer.rs:111-127`). There is no lock and no merge, so the other process's keys get overwritten with stale values.

### Intended scope

Separate per-process settings are not the design: there is one `settings.toml`. `docs/preferences.md:160-162` (from #518) says cross-process live sync is unsupported and that external edits are read on next launch. #519 (full sync) was closed as wontfix. The only exception is per-folder sort from #1565, which follows default sort and icon size (`docs/preferences.md:214-217`).

So under the current docs, the missing live sync for 10xer and list columns is expected. The overwrite is still a bug, though: a save has to leave the other process's keys alone, or the next launch can't read them. `folder-views.toml` already does this correctly.

### Suggested fix direction

On save, take the same directory lock that folder views use (`folder_view_settings.rs:110-129`), reread `settings.toml`, and write back a merge that overlays only the keys this process has changed since it last adopted the file. Unknown keys should be kept.

If live sync for 10xer and list columns is wanted, copy those fields in `adopt_defaults` and send a notify, since the existing bindings already handle notifications. If not, document the limit next to those settings rows, but still stop replacing the whole file.

There's also a related gap. If a local save is in flight when an external change arrives, `adopt_defaults_saved_elsewhere` drops the reread after `writer::reread` has already recorded the new stamp (`folder_view_settings.rs:396-402`, `writer.rs:164-179`). That can lose even the sort and icon size changes.

### Related paths

Every `PreferenceManager` setter goes through `save_preferences`, so this full-file replace also affects column widths, folder colors, custom icons, device labels, and send-to recents. `save_folder_views` (`folder_view_settings.rs:569-604`) already locks, rereads, and merges, so it can serve as the model.

### Checks run

I ran a temporary test, `repro_1845_browser_misses_portal_settings_then_overwrites_them`, under Xvfb. It passed with assertions that expect the bug, so the bug is confirmed. The test has been removed. E2E, the QA scenarios, and `quality.sh` were not run.

## Description

Integrations > Refresh reloads the file providers. The reload dropped each provider and cleared the hub's pending requests, so the reply to an action still in flight was never matched, and dropping the provider's client made its worker stop reading and kill the provider. A "Link copied" notice, or a rejection dialog, never appeared.

`Hub::reload` now keeps a provider that still owes an answer to an activation in a `retiring` list. Each tick reads its updates: a reply is presented exactly as a normal activation reply is (notice or dialog, through the shared `present_activation`), and an offline or closed provider gets the existing "provider disconnected" dialog. The provider is dropped, and its process ended, once every waiting activation is settled or after 30 seconds. The tick timer keeps running while a provider is retiring. Pending queries and menus are still discarded, as before.

**Not changed:** the transport. Keeping the client alive is enough, so a closed host queue still ends a provider immediately.

## Visual evidence

N/A: no layout change. The difference is that the notice or dialog for an interrupted action appears.

## How to test

1. Install a file provider whose action takes a moment to answer and shows a notice, such as one that copies a link.
2. Start the action from the file's context menu, then open Settings > Integrations and press Refresh before it answers.

**Expected result:** the provider's notice or dialog still appears when it answers. Before this change nothing appeared.

Covered by `a_reload_still_shows_the_outcome_of_a_pending_activation`, which holds a scripted provider's reply until after the reload and fails on the old code. The other hub tests and the Integrations page tests pass. No QA scenario covers provider activation, so none was run.

## Related issue

Closes #1857

## Summary

Pressing Integrations > Refresh while a provider activation is pending drops the activation's result.

## Expected

comments.author: wmfeht
comments.body:
## Technical details

### Reproduced

Yes, on upstream `main` at `2218357c`, using a temporary GTK test under Xvfb.

Integrations > Refresh calls `file_providers::reload` (`src/ui/settings/integrations.rs:151-155`). The test provider answered `activate` with the message `Link copied`.

- With no reload, the reply showed up as an overlay notice.
- When the reply was already queued and `reload()` ran before the next tick, `pending` and `providers` were cleared and no notice appeared within 400ms.
- When the provider had read the request but not yet replied, `reload()` ran first and then the provider answered. Its log shows it printed the reply, and still no notice appeared.

### Root cause

`Hub::reload` (`src/ui/file_providers.rs:227-231`) clears `providers` and then `pending` before the reply is shown.

Dropping `Client` drops `Requests`, which sets `closed` (`src/services/file_providers/transport.rs:35-38`). The worker sees `closed` and returns `Ok(())` without reading the in-flight reply (`transport.rs:372-374`). It publishes neither the reply nor `Update::Offline` (`transport.rs:480-489`) and then kills the provider process group (`transport.rs:475-479`).

The hub only shows replies whose id is still in `pending` (`file_providers.rs:323-326`, `412-422`). After `pending.clear()` there is nothing left to match against.

The generation check on the Integrations page (`integrations.rs:240-242`, `415-417`) only skips a stale catalog scan, so it doesn't help here.

### Suggested fix direction

Let an in-flight `activate` finish before tearing down:

1. In the transport `run`, when the host closes during an `activate`, keep reading until the reply arrives or the provider exits. If no reply comes, emit `Update::Offline` with the in-flight id.
2. Have `Hub::reload` drain those updates and run the existing `Pending::Activate` presentation before it clears `pending`.
3. If the provider exited without replying, show the existing `Hub::offline` dialog (`file_providers.rs:534-540`).

Query and menu refreshes can still be discarded.

### Related code

Successful install, enable, and remove all call the same `reload` (`integrations.rs:931-933`). The `closed` early return and `pending.clear()` also abandon in-flight `query` and `menu` replies.

### Checks run

The temporary test `refresh_during_pending_activation_drops_its_result` was run with `cargo test --bin strata --all-features` under Xvfb and passed, which confirms the bug. It has been removed. E2E, the QA scenarios, and `quality.sh` were not run.

## Summary

The delete confirmation shows a file symlink's size as the size of its target.

## Expected

comments.author: wmfeht
comments.body:
## Technical details

### Reproduced

Yes, on upstream `main` at `2218357c`.

Fixture: a 100000-byte `payload.bin`, a file symlink `link` pointing to it (`lstat` size 11), and a directory symlink `dirlink`.

Once metadata has loaded, the delete row for `link` shows `100 kB`, and `aggregate_directory_summary` totals 1 item and 100000 bytes. That is the target's size, not the link's. Directory links still show `Folder link` with a 0-byte total, as #1627 intended.

This is the normal case. With name sort, the visible rows get filled, and with size or date sort they're stat'd during listing. Before the fill runs, the link's size is `Unknown` and the total shows 0.

### Root cause

#1627 only special-cases `DirectorySymbolicLink`.

- `entry.rs:362` only recurses into directories.
- `trash.rs:943-944` prints `Folder link` only for directory links.
- A file symlink falls through to `entry.size` in both the delete row (`trash.rs:947-949`) and the subtitle (`trash.rs:1124`, then `entry.rs:380-386`).

That stored `entry.size` follows the link on both listing paths:

- Size and date sorts, and peeks, set `include_metadata`. That path calls `folder_stamp` (`local_files.rs:787-794`), which is `statx` without `SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW` (`fs_ops.rs:854-869`).
- Name sort calls `fill_metadata` with `FileQueryInfoFlags::NONE` (`local_files.rs:2168-2174`). Then `update_from_info` copies the size (`local_files.rs:2464-2471`), and `apply_metadata_update` writes it onto the row (`navigation.rs:2601-2605`).

The delete dialog reuses those rows and doesn't stat again. `query_file_entry` already uses `NOFOLLOW_SYMLINKS` (`local_files.rs:500-506`) and returns 11, but the dialog never calls it.

### Suggested fix direction

In the delete row and in `aggregate_directory_summary`, measure each `FileSymbolicLink` with a no-follow stat. That could be `symlink_metadata`, `statx` with `SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW`, or the existing `query_file_entry`. Use that size in both places, otherwise the subtitle will still show the target's size.

Leave the size column in the file list on the followed value. `parallel_fill_follows_symlinks_like_enumeration` in `local_files/tests.rs` locks that behavior in.

### Related code

- `shortcut_footer.rs:1966-1972` sums `entry.size` for the selection, so a selected file symlink adds its target's size to the status text.
- `properties.rs:831-842` replaces the seeded size with a `NOFOLLOW_SYMLINKS` query, so Properties already shows the link's own size.
- Remote listings also follow links (`local_files.rs:1578-1581`, `585-596`).
- Separately, `directory_summary.rs:233-239` adds sizes only for regular files, so symlinks inside a real folder count as 0. That's a different under-count, not this bug.

### Checks run

- A GIO probe on the fixture: `NOFOLLOW` gives 11 and a symbolic link type, and following gives 100000 and a regular file type.
- A temporary test, `repro_1853_file_symlink_delete_prompt_sizes_the_target`, run under Xvfb. It passed, which confirms the bug. It has since been removed.
- The E2E suite, the QA scenarios, and `quality.sh` were not run.

author: wmfeht
body:
## Description

With single-click file previews enabled, clicking a file in a filtered folder opened it. An unfiltered row already selects that file and shows a preview, and opens it on double-click (or on a single click only when that type's click count is one).

GTK single-click activation is already disabled, and filter-model positions already map back to the directory model. The filtered click handlers never consulted the preview setting:

- A native folder replaces the listing with search results, and that result view's pointer release always opened a file.
- A location without a native path filters in place. A non-empty query made one click activate the row, including files.
- Columns queued that same open for every filtered row.

A filtered file now follows the unfiltered rules. One click previews when previews are enabled and the file supports them, one click opens only when the file click count is one, and a double-click opens once. A filtered folder still opens on one plain click, matching #681. Chooser and trashed files never open from a pointer click; one click previews them instead, even with file clicks set to one. A filtered row does not start a slow-click rename. All three filtered paths (search results, the in-place filter, and Columns) share one click rule, so they cannot drift apart again.

## Visual evidence

N/A. This changes which action a click takes on the existing file rows, not layout or styling.

## How to test

1. Enable Settings → Single-click file previews. Leave file clicks at two (the default for List, Icons, and Columns files).
2. Open a folder that contains a previewable file and a subfolder. Repeat in List, Icons, and Columns.
3. Filter the folder so only that file remains, then click it once.
4. Double-click the same file.
5. Filter to the subfolder and click it once.
6. Clear the filter and click the same file once, then double-click it.
7. Open a file chooser (for example File → Open in a portal-using app), filter it to a file, and click the file once.

**Expected result:**

- The single click selects the file and shows the quick preview. It does not launch the file.
- The double-click launches the file once.

comments.author: wmfeht
comments.body:
## Technical details

### Reproduced

Yes, on upstream `main` at `2218357c`. On a filesystem where Trash is refused, replacing a file removes its row after the new contents are already in place. Refreshing with `reload_active` (F5) brings the row back. The same replace on a filesystem where Trash works keeps the row.

I used a tmpfs mount at `/mnt/notrash`, where `access::can-trash` is FALSE. A headless browser listed `note.txt` there, then copied another `note.txt` in with `TransferConflict::ReplaceExisting`:

```text
notrash:   +0ms model=["note.txt"]  +200ms model=["note.txt"]  +800ms model=[]
           after reload_active: model=["note.txt"]
           splice depth=0 @0 -1 +[]   file contents: new
trashable: model=["note.txt"] throughout, no splice, file contents: new
```

When the replace swaps the files, the directory monitor reports this within one batch:

```text
+10ms MOVED_OUT .strata-copy-stage
+10ms MOVED_IN  note.txt
+10ms MOVED_OUT note.txt
```

### Root cause

1. Without Trash, `displacement_without_trash` picks `Displacement::Exchange` on tmpfs, ext4, XFS, btrfs, f2fs, bcachefs, ZFS, and vfat (`src/adapters/local_operations/placement.rs:1266`).
2. `replace_through_stage` then calls `exchange_through` (`src/adapters/local_operations/replacement.rs:690`, `placement.rs:1205`). That moves the staged copy into `.strata-originals-*` and swaps it with the visible file using `RENAME_EXCHANGE`.
3. The folder monitor doesn't watch that hidden directory, so it never sees the two halves of the swap as a pair. GLib delivers `MOVED_IN` and then `MOVED_OUT` for the same visible name.
4. `visible_monitor_change` turns these into an `Upsert` and then a `Remove` (`src/adapters/local_files.rs:2586`), both keyed by the visible path (`:2034`).
5. `merge_pending_change` keeps only the last event (`:2857`), so the `Remove` wins and `flush_monitor_changes` emits only that (`:2893`). The existing check that rescans when a name is both moved and recreated (`:2879`) never fires, because by then the two events have already merged into a single `Remove`.

The copy holds back monitor events until the transfer finishes (`src/app/browser/directory_changes.rs:112`, `src/app/browser/operation_events.rs:508`). That's why the row is still there at 200ms and gone by 800ms.

### Suggested fix direction

When one batch has the same path both arriving and leaving, keep the `Upsert` instead of the later `Remove`. `query_monitored_entry` already emits `Remove` when the follow-up lookup finds nothing (`src/adapters/local_files.rs:2939`). So a real create followed by a delete still drops the row, while a swap just refreshes it. Forcing a rescan for this pair, like the existing recreate check, would also work.

### Related code

- Replacing inside an archive without Trash uses the same `exchange_through` (`src/adapters/local_operations/archive/compression.rs:326`, `:371`), so it should drop the row the same way.
- When the filesystem refuses the swap, the replace falls back to moving the original aside. That gives a different monitor sequence: `MOVED_OUT note.txt`, then about 150ms later a `RENAMED` from the hidden stage to `note.txt`. The rename lands as an `Upsert` in a later batch, so the row should come back. This wasn't run through the browser.

### Checks run

- A GIO probe of `RENAME_EXCHANGE`, and of the move-aside path with `RENAME_NOREPLACE`, on the tmpfs mount.
- A temporary test, `replace_without_trash_drops_the_listed_row_until_reload`, run under Xvfb with `--all-features`. It was not committed.

Full E2E, the QA scenarios, and `quality.sh` were not run.

title: fix(browser): preserve replaced rows and rename navigation

Context menus are real `xdg_popup`s, but Strata clamps their position and height to the window. In a small window the menu is squeezed into a scroll area or pushed away from the click, even when the screen has room.

author: pdwaldrop
body:
## Description

#1860 lists icon-only buttons that only get a name from their tooltip. A tooltip is not an accessible name, so a screen reader announced these as unnamed buttons. The new `accessibility::set_tooltip_and_label` sets the tooltip and the accessible name together, and it is applied to every such button I found:

- the path bar's copy button, which also changes between "Copy path" and "Path copied" and now keeps its name in step
- Back, Forward and Parent folder in List and Icons, and the List view's Columns menu button
- the folder color swatches in Customize (default and custom), and its Back to palette button
- the install command copy button (also changing), the media Play/Pause and Mute buttons, the archive preview's up button, the chooser's cancel button, the theme search clear button, and the sidebar eject and lock buttons

I found them by walking the widget tree in Columns, List and Icons, the location editor, Customize and Settings, and by listing every `tooltip_text` call that had no name next to it. The media, archive, chooser and sidebar buttons need states I could not reach in the test window, so those are covered by reading the code only. The inner buttons of a `SpinButton` stay unnamed; they belong to GTK.

This is the buttons half of the accessible names item. The unnamed text fields and sliders from the same list are a separate change.

## Visual evidence

N/A: no visual change.

## How to test

1. Open the widget tree (`./scripts/qa-drive.sh send '{"query":"tree"}'`), or a screen reader, in List or Icons view.
2. Look at the buttons left of the folder name and the one at the end of the path.

**Expected result:** they are named `Back (Alt+←)`, `Forward (Alt+→)`, `Parent folder (Alt+↑)` and `Copy path`. Before this change they had no name.

Covered by the QA scenario `icon-only-buttons-named`, which fails in every mode on the old code. The other accessibility scenarios and the affected Rust suites pass.

## Related issue

Part of #1860

body:
## Description

Global search (Ctrl+K) now matches space-separated terms across filenames and paths, so `duck txt` finds `ducks_in_the_pool.txt` and `subfolder txt` finds `nested/subfolder/notes.txt`. It reuses the folder filter's allocation-free substring and typo matcher from #1768. Typo checks compare character-aligned UTF-8 suffixes directly instead of repeatedly decoding them.

Match tiers keep contiguous filename hits ahead of contiguous path hits, then all-in-filename term matches, path-only term matches, and the existing fuzzy fallback. Path length, depth, and fuzzy bonuses cannot reverse those tiers. Fuzzy fallback is preserved, so multi-word queries are not a strict filter.

## Visual evidence

N/A. Matching and ranking change only; the search palette layout is unchanged.

2. Open global search with Ctrl+K and type `duck txt`.
3. Replace the query with `subfolder txt`. Repeat with matching files under long or deeply nested paths.

**Expected result:**
`duck txt` finds the phrase match before the scattered filename match. `subfolder txt` finds `notes.txt`. Stronger match tiers remain first regardless of path length or depth; any fuzzy-only results rank below term matches.

## Related issue

Closes #1889

Keep keyboard focus in the visible file pane after dialogs close and views change, and preserve an open modal's focus when a background operation finishes. Settings now refuses to open underneath Properties.

Reuse the shared modal focus restoration and heading-drag finalizer, including the chooser. Escape cancels heading reordering without clearing file selection or saving a new order; later drags still work. Preserve startup and renamed-row focus while discarding obsolete keyboard refocus work.

author: JoeJoeflyn
body: ## Description Fix all three preview problems in #1861: - Prefer whitespace when splitting long rendered paragraphs, preserving words, styled spans and copied text while keeping the 2 KiB limit for pathological tokens. - Decode RTF UTF-16 surrogate pairs with the standard decoder, retaining their style and replacing malformed units instead of silently losing text. - Recognize `.h264` through the shared filename classifier so preview, navigation, Properties and printing agree. Reuse the existing byte-content guards and sandboxed decoder, and retain valid videos with dimensions but no reported duration in navigation. The H.264 fast path avoids the platform MIME lookup and redundant uncertain-type query; no additional file reads or decoder implementation are introduced. Existing validation fixtures now establish playback for each keymap and scroll a long context menu before clicking Properties, without removing their assertions or pointer route. Initial full local runs had environment-sensitive/baseline failures; the final scoped reruns pass. CI's dependency audit is currently blocked by four pre-existing advisories in the unchanged zstd dependency chain; no exceptions have been added. The exact validation history and performance limitations are recorded in #1861. Opened ready for review at the owner's request. ## Visual evidence Before: After: ## How to test 1. Open a DOCX or ODT containing a single paragraph longer than 2 KiB and press Space. Inspect the continuation of words around the former chunk breaks. 2. Save `{\rtf1\ansi\uc1 A [\u-10179?\u-8704?] B}` as `emoji.rtf` and preview it with an emoji-capable font. 3. Generate two raw streams, for example with `ffmpeg -f lavfi -i testsrc2=size=320x180:rate=24:duration=3 -c:v libx264 -pix_fmt yuv420p -an alpha.h264`, and repeat as `beta.h264`. Preview one, step to the next video, and open Properties with Alt+Enter. Also check that plain text named `notes.h264` still previews as text. **Expected result:** ordinary words are not split across virtual rows; the RTF text is `A [😀] B`; both raw streams display video, participate in navigation and show source dimensions in Properties. Misnamed text is not handed to the media decoder. ## Related issue Closes #1861

## Items

- [ ] RTF emoji written as surrogate-pair `\uN` escapes are dropped.
- [ ] A bare .h264 stream shows "No visual preview", because Arch types it as application/octet-stream. Related: #1333.

comments.author: JoeJoeflyn
comments.body:
Reproduced **all three items** on `main` (`be3343a5`) in the pinned QA container using ordinary input files, without fault injection:

- A valid DOCX and ODT each containing one 2,553-byte paragraph display `uninterrupted` as `uninterrupt` / `ed` across virtual rows. Both Office extractors return the original paragraph intact; the cut happens in shared document chunking.
- A valid RTF containing `A [\u-10179?\u-8704?] B` displays `A [] B`. The UTF-16 surrogate units were being interpreted independently as Unicode scalar values and discarded.
- A valid FFmpeg-generated raw `.h264` stream is typed as `application/octet-stream` and shows “No visual preview”. Remuxing the same encoded frames to MP4 displays video, confirming that the decoder already supports the data.

The fix is in **#1901**, commit `c9569acf`, opened ready for review at the owner's request. It keeps the existing 2 KiB document-row bound, uses the standard UTF-16 decoder and existing escaping path, and shares the H.264 filename hint across preview callers rather than adding a decoder. Related raw-video navigation/Properties gaps are included, including valid video dimensions with an unknown duration. Plain text and empty files named `.h264` still take the existing text path.

Before/after captures were checked locally and preserved under `target/issue-1861-before/` and `target/issue-1861-after/`. The after images show intact words and an actual decoded H.264 frame. RTF now retains `A [😀] B` in the preview text; the pinned container lacks an emoji font, so its screenshot shows a fallback glyph rather than a rendered face. No screenshots or one-off probes are committed.

### Validation

Shared document chunking and content classification affect multiple formats, adapters and views, so both complete local suites were selected rather than inferring coverage from the changed filenames. GUI checks used the pinned container, private Xvfb/D-Bus and disabled accessibility bridging, never the desktop session.

- New RTF/H.264 regressions failed on the old implementation and pass with the fix. Targeted checks also covered malformed/signed/unsigned UTF-16 units, fallback lengths, styles/groups, uppercase/misleading filenames, empty/text guards, provider routing, document bounds, and unknown-duration video navigation.
- `./scripts/quality.sh test`: **3,556 passed, 9 failed, 11 ignored** in the initial complete local run. These failures were isolated, not hidden behind another full run. Three passed on the first exact rerun; five more passed with the project's clean private-session environment. The remaining playback-handoff test also failed on unchanged `main`: it now explicitly starts/waits for the current player for each keymap, retaining both resume-position assertions. The final exact nine-test selection passed using `HeadlessDisplay`, `TestEnvironment` and the compiled test binary (`--exact --nocapture --test-threads=1`). The corrected video test also passed under the original minimal Xvfb/D-Bus environment.
- `./scripts/qa.sh`: **607 passed, 3 failed** initially. Exact selection `./scripts/qa.sh replace-without-trash-keeps-row/list media-details-properties-only/icons markdown-equations-keep-prose/columns` passed the replacement and Markdown cases. Properties reproduced on unchanged `main`: the scenario tried to click below a scrollable menu's viewport. It now scrolls the menu before clicking, retaining the pointer route and metadata assertions; final `./scripts/qa.sh media-details-properties-only/icons` passed.
- Targeted `./scripts/qa.sh video-preview-badges-next-video rendered-document-word-selection` coverage passed for MP4/H.264 and DOCX/Markdown/RTF variants.
- `cargo fmt --all`, `./scripts/quality.sh fmt`, `./scripts/quality.sh clippy` and `git diff --check` completed successfully on the final code.
- Full local suites were not repeated solely to obtain a green summary, following the scoped-rerun policy. The original failures and scoped results remain in ignored `target/1861-*` logs.
- **GitHub CI's build/lint and all four Rust test shards passed** on #1901. The PR's GUI job is skipped by the existing workflow; the local GUI results above are not being represented as a clean full run.

### Performance

The filename-only H.264 classification microbenchmark measured approximately **2.514 → 0.298 µs/call**; this is not a playback-speed claim. The existing sample read and decoder are reused, with no additional file reads.

Word-boundary scanning is not free. An optimized, paired standalone benchmark of the actual range-selection functions measured **14.179 → 17.009 µs** for 112 KiB of ordinary prose, and **11.380 → 132.260 µs** for a pathological 96 KiB unbroken Unicode token. ASCII-unbroken and Unicode-prose cases also showed overhead. The 1 MiB input and 2 KiB unit bounds remain. Whole-document development-build timings were noisy, including the unchanged MP4 control; no overall document-rendering speedup is claimed.

### Separate CI blocker

The dependency audit reports four published advisories in the **unchanged baseline** zstd chain: RUSTSEC-2026-0391, RUSTSEC-2026-0398, RUSTSEC-2026-0403 and RUSTSEC-2026-0410. The PR and `main` have byte-identical `Cargo.lock` files. Reported patched minimums are zstd 0.14.3, zstd-safe 8.2.0 and zstd-sys 2.1.2. No advisory exceptions or policy relaxations have been added. This remains a CI failure, not a passed check, and expanding #1901 to update these dependencies needs a scope decision.

This is not yet a merged or released fix.

issues.title: Preview and document rendering issues from QA sweep

title: fix(preview): preserve words, RTF emoji and raw H.264 playback

author: l0gicgate
body:
## Description

`cargo deny check` fails on main and every open PR (e.g. #1899) because of four new RustSec advisories against the locked zstd crates. This updates them to the patched releases and raises the `zstd` requirement in `Cargo.toml` to 0.14.3 so that a lockfile resolution cannot fall back to an affected version:

- `zstd` 0.14.0 → 0.14.3 (RUSTSEC-2026-0391)
- `zstd-safe` 8.0.0 → 8.2.0 (RUSTSEC-2026-0398, RUSTSEC-2026-0403)
- `zstd-sys` 2.1.0 → 2.1.2 (RUSTSEC-2026-0410)

These are patch-level releases with no API changes, so no code changes were needed.

## Visual evidence

N/A — dependency update with no user-visible change.

## How to test

1. Run `cargo deny check`.
2. Install a zstd-compressed update package or open a zip that has zstd entries.

**Expected result:** `advisories ok, bans ok, licenses ok, sources ok`; updates and zip archives decompress as before.

## Related issue

Closes #1903

## Description

#1906 gave the confirmation dialog file list a 6px radius, but the corner roundness preference scales radii up to 200%, so it could reach 12px. The base radius is now 3px, so the list follows the setting from square at 0% through 1.8px at the 60% default to 6px at the 200% maximum.

N/A — agent-authored; the change halves the base corner radius of the dialog file list box.

1. Set Settings → Appearance → corner roundness to 0, select a file, and press Shift+Delete.
2. Repeat at the default and at the maximum roundness.

**Expected result:** The file list is square at 0, subtly rounded at the default, and no rounder than 6px at the maximum.

## Related issue

Closes #1907

author: JoeJoeflyn
body: ## Description 1. On uncomposited X11 displays (without a compositing window manager), transparent pixels cannot be alpha-blended and render as solid black `#000000`, causing popovers and context menus to display black shadow padding frames and clipped black corner tips. This change detects `!display.is_composited()` via a dynamic CSS provider and sets `box-shadow: none; border-radius: 0;` so popovers are crisp with squared borders. 2. When submitting a file path directly in the path/location bar, the browser reveals the file inside its parent directory and now automatically dispatches a Quick Preview request so the user can immediately view its contents. ## Visual evidence https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/186ab6e5-06fa-4577-8ae7-0998d82015c3 ## How to test 1. Launch Strata on an uncomposited X11 display (or in a bare Xvfb / openbox session without picom/compton). Right-click on a file or folder. 2. Confirm the context menu has square right-angle corners without any black borders or clipped black corner artifacts. 3. In the path bar (Ctrl+L), paste or type an exact file path (e.g. `/path/to/image.png`) and press Enter. **Expected result:** Popovers and menus on uncomposited X11 render clean square borders without black frames or pixel clipping. Submitting a file path navigates to the parent directory, focuses the file, and immediately opens Quick Preview for it. ## Related issue Closes #1911

issues.body:
### Strata version
commit 7c9d883cdb528ba8d15f85460fea9d852371d146

### Installation method
Built from source

### Linux distribution and desktop environment
Arch Linux, uncomposited X11 (e.g. i3, AwesomeWM without Picom, Xvfb)

### What happened?
1. On uncomposited X11 environments, context menus and popover dropdowns are surrounded by a thick black layout frame caused by subsurface alpha box-shadow padding falling back to solid black without an X11 compositing manager.
2. Pasting and submitting an absolute file path into the path bar navigates to and selects the file inside its parent directory, but does not trigger Quick Preview to show its contents.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Start Strata on an uncomposited X11 display.
2. Right-click any file to open the context menu. Observe the black border frame surrounding the menu.
3. Paste an image or file path into the path bar and hit Enter. Observe that the file is selected, but Quick Preview remains closed.

### Expected behavior
1. On uncomposited X11 displays, popover subsurfaces strip box-shadow and square borders (border-radius: 0) so override-redirect window bounds display cleanly without solid black frames.
2. Submitting a file path into the path bar should reveal the entry and automatically request preview to display its contents.
